start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A battered Independent freighter hails you on short-range comms. "Hey friend, I've got surplus fuel cells -- 30 credits a pop, no questions asked."

bought.speaker: Merchant
bought.text: "Pleasure doing business. Safe travels, captain." He loads the cells into your hold and warps away with a friendly wave.

decline.speaker: Merchant
decline.text: He shrugs. "Suit yourself. Someone'll buy 'em." The freighter powers up its warp drive and disappears.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, I'm picking up a small shuttle drifting with no power signature. One life sign, fading fast. She won't last much longer out there.

rescue.speaker: Medic
rescue.text: We pulled her out just in time -- a Castellan courier, badly dehydrated and carrying sealed diplomatic correspondence. She's grateful beyond words. "I owe you my life, captain. If you'll have me, I'd like to serve on your ship."

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: We stripped the shuttle clean. Got about 40 credits worth of usable components. The life sign... stopped during the operation. Nobody's talking about it.

leave.text: You pass by the drifting shuttle. The life sign fades from your sensors. Your crew exchanges uncomfortable glances.

start.speaker: Pirate Leader
start.text: Three Fringe corvettes drop out of warp in a triangle formation around you. "Hand over your cargo or we paint the void with your hull," their leader growls.

fight.text: You power up weapons and target the lead ship. Three on one -- not great odds, but you've faced worse. The pirates spread into attack formation.

surrender.speaker: Pirate Leader
surrender.text: "Smart choice." They take a hefty cut of your credits and a chunk of your resources, then warp away laughing. Your crew looks disgusted but alive.

intimidate.text: You power all weapons and angle toward the lead corvette, engines at full burn. The pirates hesitate -- your ship looks meaner up close. They exchange nervous chatter on their encrypted channel.

intimidate_success.speaker: Pirate Leader
intimidate_success.text: "...Alright, this one's not worth it. Break off, boys." The three corvettes peel away and warp out. Your crew cheers.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: An enormous bioluminescent organism drifts across our path -- translucent, pulsing with violet light. Tentacles spanning hundreds of meters. Scans say it's a void jellyfish, feeding on interstellar radiation.

choices.label: Admire the view and keep distance.
Fly closer for a better look.

admire.text: The crew gathers at viewports, watching the creature pulse and shimmer. It's profoundly beautiful -- a reminder that even the void holds wonders. The moment stays with everyone.

closer.speaker: Sensor Officer
closer.text: You drift too close to its tendrils. A mild shield drain pulses through the ship -- nothing dangerous, but your shields flicker. Still, the view is magnificent up close.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Fascinating readings. The creature's bio-electric field is unlike anything in our databases. This data would be worth a lot to Xenoculture researchers.

choices.label: Log the data and move on.

start.speaker: Gambler
start.text: A gold-painted yacht pulls alongside. A flamboyant pilot appears on screen. "I bet you 200 credits I can guess your ship's tonnage within 5%. Deal?"

bet1.speaker: Gambler
bet1.text: He squints at your ship, mutters calculations, and names a figure. He's... shockingly close. "Pay up, friend!" He grins. "But wait -- double or nothing. I bet there's a stowaway in your cargo bay RIGHT NOW."

bet2.text: You check the cargo bay. No stowaway. "Damn!" the gambler laughs. "Can't win 'em all." He transfers 400 credits with a bow.

pay.speaker: Gambler
pay.text: "Better luck next time, captain!" He salutes theatrically and peels away in a burst of golden engine wash.

decline.speaker: Gambler
decline.text: "Your loss! The void is dull enough without a little action." He winks and warps away, engine trail sparkling like tinsel.

start.speaker: Comms Officer
start.text: Captain, we're picking up a repeating distress signal using a 200-year-old encryption protocol. The voice is calm, almost conversational: "This is the CSV Wanderlust. We've found something down here. It's looking back at us. Please don't come looking."

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: The signal is broadcasting from a point in empty space. No ship, no debris, nothing on any scanner. Just... a voice from nowhere. Then it changes. It starts using our ship's name.

listen.speaker: Comm Channel
listen.text: "We know you're listening. We've been listening to you for so long. Come find us. Come find the Wanderlust." The signal cuts out. Dead silence. Your crew looks pale.

record.text: You log the signal and its coordinates. Something about the voice makes your skin crawl. The crew is unsettled.

cut.text: You kill the channel. The bridge falls silent. Nobody speaks for a long moment. Whatever that was, you want no part of it.

flee.text: You hit full burn. The signal fades behind you, but not before one last transmission: "See you soon." Your crew doesn't sleep well that night.

start.speaker: Lead Merchant
start.text: A convoy of six COTAC trade vessels passes through, escorted by two frigates. "Welcome, traveler. Care to browse our exotic wares? We have alien spices, hull plating schematics, and a crate of... surplus power cells."

spices.speaker: Lead Merchant
spices.text: "Excellent taste! These spices will lift any crew's spirits." The fragrant crate is loaded aboard. Your crew is already eyeing it hungrily.

cells.speaker: Lead Merchant
cells.text: "A wise investment. Don't mind the Castellan serial numbers -- they're refurbished, totally legitimate." He avoids eye contact while saying this.

more.speaker: Lead Merchant
more.text: "We also have hull plating schematics for 120 credits, if your ship needs toughening up."

schematics.speaker: Lead Merchant
schematics.text: "Pleasure doing business. May COTAC winds fill your sails -- metaphorically, of course." The convoy resumes its journey.

leave.text: The caravan moves on, a glittering procession of commerce through the void.

start.speaker: Young Pilot
start.text: A sleek, absurdly over-engined shuttle pulls alongside. "You there! Race me to the next system beacon! 500 credits to the winner!" She's grinning ear to ear.

choices.label: I'll pass. Too rich for my blood.

race.text: You slam the throttle forward. The two ships tear through the void side by side, engines screaming. Your crew braces as you push the ship to its limits.

choices.label: Hit the boost. Everything we've got.

win.speaker: Young Pilot
win.text: You cross the beacon first by a hair. "Incredible! I haven't lost in months!" She transfers 500 credits, laughing. "Rematch next time, captain!" She warps away trailing engine sparks.

lose.speaker: Young Pilot
lose.text: She edges past you at the last second. "Better luck next time!" She pays you 50 credits anyway "for being a good sport" and warps off trailing engine sparks. Your crew enjoyed the show.

decline.speaker: Young Pilot
decline.text: "Aww, no fun! Catch you next time, slowpoke!" She hits her boost and vanishes in a streak of light.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We're entering a field of twisted metal and frozen atmosphere crystals -- the remains of a battle. Fragments from both Union Militia and pirate vessels. There could be salvage here.

scavenge.speaker: Engineer
scavenge.text: We pulled in some usable components -- hull scrap, a damaged power conduit, and some ammunition. Not bad for a graveyard.

survivors.speaker: Medic
survivors.text: Wait -- there's a cracked escape pod wedged in the wreckage. One life sign, faint. We pull them out: a militia soldier, badly wounded. He's babbling about 'the thing that came after both sides stopped fighting.'

choices.label: Get him to medbay. Scavenge what we can.
Stabilize him and drop him at the next station.

survivors_after.speaker: Medic
survivors_after.text: Found a cracked escape pod. Survivor inside -- a militia soldier. He keeps muttering about 'something that came after both sides stopped fighting.' Unsettling.

rescue_and_salvage.text: You save the soldier and strip what you can from the wreckage. A productive, if grim, stop.

stabilize.text: The soldier will live. He murmurs a thank you as the sedatives kick in. Your crew marks the nearest station on the nav chart.

leave.text: You skirt the debris field. Whatever happened here, you'd rather not get involved.

start.speaker: ISD Officer
start.text: An ISD enforcement cruiser drops from warp and scans your ship without permission. "Vessel, you are carrying untaxed goods through ISD-administered void space. Remit 15% of cargo value immediately or face seizure."

choices.label: Dump cargo to show empty holds.

pay.speaker: ISD Officer
pay.text: "Your compliance is noted." He issues you an official receipt granting passage through ISD space for 30 days. Not entirely useless.

argue.speaker: ISD Officer
argue.text: "Jurisdiction is not up for debate, civilian." He pauses, reviewing your transponder data. Your ISD reputation might make a difference here.

choices.label: Press the point. This is neutral space.

argue_success.speaker: ISD Officer
argue_success.text: He scowls but waves you through. "Don't let me catch you again without proper documentation." The cruiser powers up warp and vanishes.

fight.speaker: ISD Officer
fight.text: "Hostile action detected. All units, weapons free." The cruiser's weapons light up. This won't be easy -- ISD ships are well-armed.

dump.speaker: ISD Officer
dump.text: You jettison some cargo into the void. The officer rescans your holds. "...Hmm. Appears to be in order. Move along." He eyes the floating cargo hungrily as you depart.

start.speaker: Comm Officer
start.text: Captain, the hull is vibrating at a specific harmonic frequency. The crew is reporting... music. Everyone hears something different. Scans show nothing unusual.

choices.label: Let it play. Enjoy the moment.
Run full diagnostics. Find the source.

enjoy.text: The Choir, some spacers call it -- a known void phenomenon that nobody can explain. The music lasts several minutes, different for each listener but beautiful for all. Some spacers spend their whole lives chasing this sound.

choices.label: Savor the silence when it ends.

diagnose.speaker: Science Officer
diagnose.text: Diagnostics show nothing wrong. The harmonic appears to be a natural resonance phenomenon -- the crew calls it 'the Choir.' It's not dangerous. It's... actually quite lovely. Even I have to admit that.

start.speaker: Fringe Captain
start.text: A Fringe raider hails you with surprising professionalism. "We're expanding operations in this sector. Your ship has potential. Join us -- we offer profit sharing, dental, and a generous retirement package."

choices.label: Tell me more about this... dental plan.
I'd rather eat my own hull plating.

dental.speaker: Fringe Captain
dental.text: He sighs heavily. "It's... it's a pair of pliers, honestly. Look, the profit sharing is real though. We pulled in 20,000 credits last quarter. Minus expenses."

choices.label: You had me at pliers. I'm in.

accept.speaker: Fringe Captain
accept.text: "Welcome to the family! Here's your share of last week's haul. We'll be in touch with job opportunities." Your crew exchanges nervous glances.

decline_polite.speaker: Fringe Captain
decline_polite.text: "Shame. Well, if you change your mind, broadcast on frequency 7-7-3. Good flying, captain." He warps away without incident.

decline_rude.speaker: Fringe Captain
decline_rude.text: His expression hardens. "Wrong answer." Weapons power up on his ship.

start.speaker: The Collector
start.text: A massive ornate vessel covered in trophies and artifacts hails you. "Greetings, traveler! I am a connoisseur of the extraordinary. Do you carry anything... interesting? I pay handsomely for the unusual."

choices.label: I might have something. What are you looking for?

shopping.speaker: The Collector
shopping.text: "Artifacts, alien specimens, unusual cargo -- I pay triple market value for rare items. And if you ever find a void pearl... I'll pay 5,000 credits. Here's my frequency. Find me something extraordinary."

nothing.speaker: The Collector
nothing.text: "Pity. Well, take my frequency regardless. The void is full of wonders for those with open eyes. I pay triple for anything truly rare."

whoami.speaker: The Collector
whoami.text: "I am a curator of the impossible. Xenoculture aligned, but my interests transcend faction politics. The universe is full of things that shouldn't exist, and I want them all. Especially void pearls -- 5,000 credits, no questions."

choices.label: Interesting. I'll keep you in mind.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Warning klaxons blare -- micro-fracture in the reactor shielding! We're venting radiation into engineering. Crew in there are taking exposure. We need to act fast, captain.

choices.label: Evacuate engineering and seal it off.

patch.speaker: Engineer
patch.text: "If we've got someone with warpsmithing experience, they can seal it in minutes. Otherwise we're looking at a slow, dangerous manual repair."

patch_success.speaker: Engineer
patch_success.text: The leak is sealed. Minor radiation exposure to the repair crew, but nothing the medic can't handle. Close call, captain.

reroute.speaker: Engineer
reroute.text: Power rerouted. We're running at reduced output but the radiation has stopped. Going to take a couple hours to stabilize fully. Could have been much worse.

evacuate.speaker: Engineer
evacuate.text: Engineering sealed off. The leak will burn itself out but it's going to chew up some systems in there. Hull integrity took a hit. Everyone's alive though.

start.speaker: Refugee Leader
start.text: A desperate fleet of civilian ships -- shuttles, converted cargo haulers, even a repurposed school bus with welded-on engines -- begs for help. "Please, we're fleeing a Fringe raid. We need food, fuel, anything you can spare."

choices.label: I'm sorry. I can't spare anything.

help.speaker: Refugee Leader
help.text: "Bless you, captain. You've saved lives today." A grizzled engineer steps forward from the crowd. "Captain, I owe you. If you'll have me, I'd like to repay this with honest work on your ship."

credits.speaker: Refugee Leader
credits.text: "Thank you. This will buy us supplies at the next station. You're a good person, captain." Your crew looks proud.

refuse.speaker: Refugee Leader
refuse.text: "I... I understand. Times are hard for everyone." The flotilla limps away. Your crew is quiet.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... something enormous just eclipsed the stars behind us. Tentacles of dark matter unfurling -- each one hundreds of meters long. It's a void kraken. An apex predator of deep space.

choices.label: Target the bioluminescent nodes. All weapons!
Full boost. Get us out of here!

fight.speaker: Gunner
fight.text: Conventional weapons barely scratch it! But the glowing nodes on its tentacles -- those react to our fire. Concentrating all firepower on the nodes!

fight_win.speaker: Science Officer
fight_win.text: The kraken shudders and releases us, retreating into the void. We salvaged exotic biological material from the damaged tentacles -- this is worth a fortune. Your crew will talk about this for the rest of their lives.

flee.speaker: Pilot
flee.text: Full burn! The kraken's tendrils lash at us as we pull away -- one clips the hull, tearing through plating. But we're faster. Barely. The creature recedes into the darkness behind us.

hide.text: You cut everything. Drift in silence. The kraken's tentacles sweep past the hull, close enough to touch. It pauses. Searches. Then slowly, impossibly slowly, it moves on. Nobody breathes for a full minute after it's gone.

start.speaker: Dex
start.text: An Independent shuttle broadcasts on all frequencies: "Is this thing on? So I was flying through the Castellan sector the other day -- what's the deal with their customs forms? 'Declare all sentient cargo.' I barely consider my crew sentient before coffee!"

more_jokes.speaker: Dex
more_jokes.text: "A Bulwark miner, a COTAC diplomat, and a Fringe pirate walk into an airlock -- the pirate says 'I knew this job interview was going too well!' Thank you, thank you! You've been a great audience!" He's beaming.

heckle.speaker: Dex
heckle.text: "Tough crowd! Story of my life. Look, I know I'm no comedy legend, but somebody's gotta keep the void entertained. Here -- 20 credits for your time. Tell your friends about Dex!"

suggest.speaker: Dex
suggest.text: "Wait, your crew has suggestions? This is gold! I'm writing these down. You know what, you've earned this." He sends 20 credits and a terrible comedy holotape. Your crew is in stitches.

tip.speaker: Dex
tip.text: "You're too kind! Here, take 20 credits -- for being a great audience. If you see me out there again, flag me down. I'll have new material!" He warps away, broadcasting rim-shots.

leave.text: You cut the channel. Dex's broadcast fades. A crew member mutters, "I thought the airlock joke was pretty good, actually."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Proximity mines -- hundreds of them, seeded across our flight path! Old Union Militia ordnance, probably from a forgotten conflict. We need to decide how to get through.

navigate.speaker: Pilot
navigate.text: "Threading the needle, captain." The pilot weaves through the mine field with white-knuckle precision. A few close calls, but you emerge on the other side intact. Barely.

blast.speaker: Gunner
blast.text: You open fire. The first mine detonates, triggering a chain reaction. Shrapnel peppers the hull as explosions bloom across the field. It clears a path, but not gently.

detour.speaker: Navigator
detour.text: We plot a course around the minefield. Safe, but it costs fuel and time. At least the hull is intact.

start.speaker: The Aperture
start.text: Five identical black ships arranged in a pentagram pattern block your path. Their speaker addresses you in unison: "Traveler, the Aperture opens. Have you seen the Signal? The Signal sees you."

choices.label: What signal? What are you talking about?
I want nothing to do with this.

explain.speaker: The Aperture
explain.text: "The Signal is the truth beneath the void. It speaks in frequencies older than stars. We are its voice. We offer you a fragment of its awareness -- a crystal that hums with coordinates only the worthy can follow."

accept.speaker: The Aperture
accept.text: They extend a small crystalline device through the airlock. It hums faintly in your hand, warm despite the void. The five ships disperse silently, vanishing one by one. The crystal occasionally whispers coordinates...

refuse.text: The five ships disperse in perfect synchronization, vanishing like shadows. No threats, no aggression. Just silence. Your crew breathes again.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A burst cargo container has scattered trade goods across a wide area -- fabrics, electronics, canned food, and... is that a live animal in a stasis crate?

collect.speaker: Engineer
collect.text: We spent some time hauling it all in. Got a decent haul of general goods, plus that exotic pet in the stasis crate -- a Xenoculture specimen worth good credits to the right buyer.

quick_grab.speaker: Engineer
quick_grab.text: Grabbed the high-value items and moved on. Efficient, if not thorough.

merchant_check.speaker: Comm Officer
merchant_check.text: Captain, an angry merchant just dropped out of warp demanding we return their cargo. "That's MY shipment you're picking through!"

choices.label: Finders keepers. It was floating in open space.

return.speaker: Merchant
return.text: "Hmph. At least you're honest." He pays you a small finder's fee.

keep.speaker: Merchant
keep.text: "You'll regret this! I know people!" He warps away fuming. Your crew shrugs. Space law is vague at best.

split.speaker: Merchant
split.text: "...Fine. Half is better than nothing." He takes his share and nods grudgingly. "You're alright, captain."

leave.text: You pass by the floating debris. Probably wise -- could have been a trap.

start.speaker: ISD Inspector
start.text: An ISD patrol frigate signals you to halt for routine inspection. The officer looks bored and by-the-book. "Standard cargo scan. Won't take long. Please hold position."

choices.label: Try to talk your way past.

clean.speaker: ISD Inspector
clean.text: "Everything checks out. You're clear to proceed. Safe travels, civilian." She stamps your digital manifest and waves you through.

talk.speaker: ISD Inspector
talk.text: "Sir, regulations require -- " She pauses, checks your transponder record. "Actually, your record is clean enough. Move along. I've got twelve more ships in queue."

refuse.speaker: ISD Inspector
refuse.text: "Refusal to comply with lawful inspection is a class-3 violation." Her tone sharpens. "I'm calling backup. Hold position or face interdiction."

flee.text: You hit the engines and burn away from the checkpoint. The patrol frigate doesn't pursue, but you can bet they logged your transponder.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... there's a capital ship out here. Easily ten times our size. Dead in the void. No faction markings, no known design language. Hull looks ancient. Shall we investigate?

choices.label: No. Something feels wrong. Leave it.

board.speaker: Marine
board.text: The interior is frozen, dark, and vast. Empty corridors with strange murals depicting unknown star systems. One room where gravity still works despite no power. The crew refuses to go past deck three.

choices.label: Take what we found and leave.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Readings are... inconsistent. The hull material doesn't match any known alloy. There are energy readings from deep inside -- impossible for a dead ship. Something is still active in there.

choices.label: We have to see what's inside.

vault.speaker: Marine
vault.text: Deep inside -- a sealed vault. The door is covered in warning symbols from no known language. The vault hums with a low, almost musical vibration. Your crew stares at you.

choices.label: Don't open it. Seal the way back.

open_vault.text: The vault opens with a hiss of pressurized atmosphere impossibly still fresh after centuries. Inside: a single artifact, pulsing with dim light, shaped like no tool or weapon you've ever seen. It feels warm. It feels alive. Your crew wants to leave. Now.

choices.label: Leave it. Some things should stay sealed.

leave_with_loot.speaker: Engineer
leave_with_loot.text: We grabbed some hull samples and data recordings on the way out. Valuable to researchers, and nobody had to die. The murals will haunt your crew's dreams, though.

leave.text: You pull away from the ancient hulk. It drifts on, as it has for who knows how long. Some doors are best left closed.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain! Fuel gauge is dropping fast -- something's latched onto the hull! It's a parasitic siphon device. And there's a pirate ship decloaking 500 meters out. "Thanks for the top-off, friend," he sneers.

choices.label: Fight. Take our fuel back and then some.
Pay 100 credits to remove the siphon.
EVA a crew member to detach it manually.

fight.speaker: Pirate
fight.text: "Whoa, whoa! No need to get hostile!" But he's already powering weapons. Too late for diplomacy.

pay.speaker: Pirate
pay.text: "Smart move." He remote-deactivates the siphon. "No hard feelings, yeah? Business is business." He warps away before you can change your mind.

eva.speaker: Engineer
eva.text: Our crew member scrambles across the hull, tools in hand. The pirate watches nervously -- he didn't expect this. The siphon is detached before the pirate can drain much. He curses and warps out.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Captain, we're passing through a stellar nursery -- new stars being born in swirling clouds of gas lit from within. Sensors are going haywire from the EM interference, but the view is... spectacular.

choices.label: Spend some time here. Worth the detour.
Beautiful, but we have places to be.

linger.speaker: Science Officer
linger.text: We spent time analyzing the region. Unusual readings suggest a rare element deposit in one of the proto-stellar clouds. The crew is in high spirits -- it's not every day you watch a star being born.

readings.speaker: Science Officer
readings.text: Got some excellent data. A Xenoculture research station would pay well for these readings. The crew watches the glowing clouds as we pass through.

leave.text: You pass through the stellar nursery without stopping. The crew watches the infant suns glow through the viewports.

start.speaker: The Forger
start.text: A nondescript ship pulls alongside. The pilot's face is half-shadowed. "I offer... documentation services. Transponder codes, trade licenses, bounty papers. All indistinguishable from the real thing. Interested?"

choices.label: I also deal in intel. Got any?

menu.speaker: The Forger
menu.text: "Fake transponder codes -- avoid faction hostility for a time. 500 credits. Forged trade license -- better prices at stations. 500 credits. Falsified bounty papers -- frame anyone you like. Also 500 credits. Quality work isn't cheap."

choices.label: Too rich for me. Got any free intel?

transponder.speaker: The Forger
transponder.text: "Smart investment. These codes will let you pass through hostile space undetected. Don't get scanned too closely, though." He hands over the data chip.

license.speaker: The Forger
license.text: "This license will get you preferential pricing at most stations. Just don't flash it at ISD -- they check the watermarks." He grins.

intel.speaker: The Forger
intel.text: "Free of charge, to build goodwill. Fringe raiders have been hitting the lanes between Castellan and COTAC space hard this month. Militia patrols are spread thin. Stay sharp out there."

leave.speaker: The Forger
leave.text: "Your loss. If you change your mind, I'm on frequency 4-4-1. Discreetly." The ship vanishes -- you're not even sure which direction it went.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, rear sensors are tracking a contact matching our speed exactly. Constant distance -- 2,000 meters. It mirrors every course and speed change we make.

hail.speaker: Sensor Officer
hail.text: No response on any frequency. Deep scan returns nothing -- it reads like a sensor ghost, but ghosts don't persist for twenty minutes straight. Whatever this is, it's not showing up on any known spectrum.

power_down.text: You kill all power. The ship goes dark and silent, drifting. Sixty seconds pass in the blackness. Exactly sixty. Then the contact vanishes from passive sensors. When power comes back, it's gone. Your crew is rattled.

ignore.text: You fly on. After thirty minutes, the contact fades on its own. But the feeling of being watched lingers. Your crew keeps checking the rear sensors for days afterward.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A brawny Bulwark freighter captain fills the screen, flexing one massive arm. "Fifty credits says none of your soft-handed void rats can beat me at arm wrestling! Put your best up or admit defeat!"

win.speaker: Comm Channel
win.text: Your crewmate steps up to the cargo-crate table. After a tense thirty seconds, the Bulwark captain's arm slams down. He stares in disbelief, then roars with laughter. "Ha! Fair and square! Here's your credits, you earned 'em. Name's Brek -- call me if you need a hauling contact."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: The captain shrugs his enormous shoulders. "No shame in knowing your limits. Tell you what -- next time we're docked at the same station, drinks are on me. You seem like good people."

choices.label: We'll take you up on that.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Warp drive just stuttered out, Captain. We're between systems with depleted warp fuel. I can jury-rig a fix if we've got someone with warpsmithing know-how, or we send a distress signal and hope for the best.

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: Took some doing, but we've got the drive limping along. Half speed until we reach a station for proper repairs, but we're moving. Could've been a lot worse out here.

choices.label: Good work. Get us to port.

distress.speaker: Sensor Officer
distress.text: Signal's out. Got a response -- a Union Militia patrol heard us. They're diverting to assist. ETA twenty minutes. They've got spare fuel cells aboard.

choices.label: Thank the void for the Militia.

wait.text: Hours pass in the dark between stars. Your crew grows restless. Eventually the drive cools enough for a cold restart, but the fuel reserves are nearly gone.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark mining barge bristling with drill arms hails you. The foreman grins through a dust-caked visor. "Just cracked open a beauty of an asteroid. Got more ore than we can haul -- want to buy raw materials at cost? Sixty percent market price."

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: The foreman's crew loads your hold with practiced efficiency. As they finish, he leans in conspiratorially. "Between us? We've been getting strange readings from the deeper void lately. Sensor returns that don't match anything natural." He won't say more.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Suit yourself, friend. We'll find a buyer." The barge powers up its drills and lumbers back toward the asteroid field.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A lone pilot in a heavily modified fighter locks weapons on you. His voice is calm, almost bored. "I am Kael Voss. Forty-seven ships destroyed in single combat. You will be forty-eight. Do you accept the duel?"

accept.text: The fight is brutal. Voss is every bit as skilled as his reputation suggests -- but so are you. His fighter breaks apart under your final volley. As his escape pod ejects, a tight-beam transmission arrives: "Well fought. Forty-seven was a good run."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: Voss stares at the screen for a long moment. "Coward." The word hangs in the silence. His fighter banks away and vanishes into warp without another word. Your crew says nothing, but you can feel their judgment.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, we've picked up void barnacles -- little organisms that latch onto hulls during long flights. Harmless alone, but we've got enough to cut engine efficiency by ten percent. I can scrape 'em off, or... apparently Xenoculture researchers buy these things.

choices.label: Scrape them off and sell them.

sell.speaker: Engineer
sell.text: Fifty kilograms of void barnacles, scraped, bagged, and ready for sale. Two credits a kilo from the Xenoculture types. "They're not bugs, they're a cash crop," your helmsman observes with a straight face.

scrape.speaker: Engineer
scrape.text: Hull's clean. Engines are back to full efficiency. I'll set up a regular inspection schedule so we catch them earlier next time.

leave.speaker: Engineer
leave.text: Your call, Captain. But if they keep multiplying, we'll be crawling through space before long.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A civilian transport broadcasts a medical emergency. Their cook ate something from an unmarked alien container and is now turning blue and speaking in frequencies below human hearing. They need someone with medical or cooking knowledge to synthesize an antidote.

choices.label: Send a crew member to help.

help.speaker: Medic
help.text: Took some creative chemistry with whatever was in that galley, but the antidote worked. Cook's color is returning to normal, though he still has a faint subsonic hum when he talks. The captain is enormously grateful.

decline.text: The transport limps toward the nearest station, broadcasting increasingly desperate calls. Your crew watches them go in uncomfortable silence.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A heavily armed Independent merchant vessel opens a trade channel. "Looking for firepower, friend? Autocannons, missile racks, shields -- and one pristine Castellan lance battery that, ah, fell off a truck."

lance.speaker: Comm Channel
lance.text: "Excellent taste." The merchant transfers the lance battery with a wink. "Word of advice -- if a Castellan patrol asks where you got that, you never met me."

standard.speaker: Comm Channel
standard.text: "Good choice. Reliable hardware, no questions attached." The merchant loads a crate of weapon components into your hold.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss, friend. I'll be around." The merchant's ship powers up and drifts away, bristling with enough armament to outfit a small fleet.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- sensors just lit up. Two hundred plus contacts in tight formation, crossing our path at extreme velocity. Visual shows... nothing. The echo lasted eight seconds. Gone now.

analyze.speaker: Sensor Officer
analyze.text: The formation matches a pre-war Castellan battle group -- the 14th Expeditionary Fleet. They disappeared sixty years ago during a deep-void patrol. All hands lost. No wreckage ever found. Until now, apparently, they were still... traveling.

log.text: Your sensor officer logs the anomaly with shaking hands. Nobody on the bridge speaks for a long time. Some things are better left unexamined.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, security found a stowaway in the cargo bay. A teenager -- no ID, no money, just a bag of encrypted data chips. Kid's terrified. Says: "Please don't turn me back. They'll kill me for what I know."

choices.label: Turn the kid over to ISD.

listen.text: The teenager claims to have evidence of ISD corruption -- weapon deals with Fringe pirates, falsified patrol reports, missing people. The data chips are encrypted but the headers are damning. This is either a treasure trove or a very elaborate trap.

choices.label: Turn the kid over to ISD.

isd.text: An ISD patrol collects the stowaway within the hour -- suspiciously fast. The lead officer thanks you curtly and hands over a "finders fee." The teenager's eyes as they're led away are impossible to forget.

shelter.text: The kid stays. The data chips, once decrypted, contain intel that several factions would pay handsomely for. Your new passenger is quiet, helpful, and clearly haunted by something.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Gravitational anomaly dead ahead! The ship lurches sideways, instruments are spinning, and anything not bolted down just became a projectile.

choices.label: Ride the eddy -- use it for a slingshot.

ride.speaker: Engineer
ride.text: Your pilot catches the current perfectly -- the ship whips around the eddy and catapults out the other side with a massive speed boost. Fuel gauges actually ticked UP from the gravitational assist. Brilliant flying.

choices.label: Mark this spot for future reference.

brace.speaker: Engineer
brace.text: We pushed through. Some hull stress and a few bruised crew members, but nothing critical. Navigator's already mapping the anomaly for future avoidance.

reverse.speaker: Engineer
reverse.text: Emergency burn ate through fuel reserves, but we're clear. That was close -- the eddy nearly had us. Plotting an alternate route now.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An ancient, wheezing shuttle broadcasts nonstop sermons about "the Holy Engine, blessed be its combustion." The preacher, Brother Ignatius, offers to bless your reactor. He also buys engine components at above-market prices, calling them "sacred relics."

bless.speaker: Comm Channel
bless.text: Brother Ignatius intones a prayer over your reactor via comms, invoking "the sacred spark of ignition" and "the holy torque of the crankshaft." Your reactor performs exactly the same. But somehow, your crew feels better about it.

sell.speaker: Comm Channel
sell.text: "A genuine power coupling! Blessed be the conductors!" Ignatius pays generously and cradles the component like a newborn. Your engineer is mildly disturbed.

leave.text: You pull away as the sermons continue to broadcast behind you. "...and on the third ignition cycle, the Engine did TURN OVER, and there was combustion, and it was GOOD..."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two Fringe pirates drop from warp and immediately collide with each other. Your comms fill with their unencrypted argument: "Dammit Reg, I told you to come in from the LEFT!" "MY left or YOUR left?!"

attack.text: One pirate surrenders instantly. The other tries to flee but flies into his partner's debris. You salvage what's left of both ships. It's not much, but it's honest work.

listen.speaker: Comm Channel
listen.text: The argument escalates: whose mother-in-law is worse, who forgot to refuel, and whether Reg's navigating or his "backseat flying." Eventually they notice you. "Oh. Right. Um... give us, like, some credits or whatever?"

choices.label: Toss them 20 credits out of pity.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Thanks! See Reg? THAT'S how you do piracy -- politely!" They limp away arguing about how to split twenty credits. Your crew is in tears laughing.

choices.label: Best twenty credits we ever spent.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Fair enough. We, uh, we're gonna go. Reg, start the-- REG DON'T TOUCH THAT BUTTON--" The comms cut to static. They warp away, barely.

leave.text: You slip away while they're still arguing. Their voices fade: "...and ANOTHER thing, your ship smells like wet dog..."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A deep vibration just passed through the hull -- frequency so low you feel it in your bones. Sensors show an immense biological signature moving at .02c, already past us and receding. Captain... that was a void whale. It sang as it passed.

choices.label: Let it go. Savor the moment.

follow.speaker: Sensor Officer
follow.text: You chase the whale's trail for an hour, burning fuel, until the void opens into something impossible -- a bioluminescent nebula, lit from within by organisms that shouldn't exist. Your crew watches in stunned silence. The whale sings again, distant now, as if saying goodbye.

stay.text: Your crew stands at viewports, watching the vast shape recede into the dark. Nobody speaks. The vibration lingers in the deck plating for minutes after. Some moments don't need words.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A fast, well-armed ship drops from warp and locks weapons. "This is Mara Ghent, licensed bounty hunter. You match a warrant description. Hold position for verification or I open fire."

choices.label: Transmit transponder records to prove identity.

prove.speaker: Comm Channel
prove.text: Ghent reviews your records in silence, then unlocks weapons. "Clean. My apologies, Captain -- mistaken identity. As compensation, here's intel on pirate activity in this sector. Their patrol routes and safe harbors. Professional courtesy."

choices.label: No harm done. Thanks for the intel.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Payment received. Bounty cleared." Ghent is all business. The comms cut and her ship vanishes into warp. Efficient. Cold. Your crew grumbles about the cost.

fight.text: Ghent is good -- very good. But you're better today. Her ship takes critical damage and she disengages. "This isn't over, Captain." The threat is professional, not personal. She'll be back.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two merchant ships are arguing on an open channel and they want you to arbitrate. "This idiot says Castellan brandy is better than COTAC reserve!" one shouts. The other: "Anyone with functioning taste buds knows I'm right!" They've each bet 100 credits.

cotac.speaker: Comm Channel
cotac.text: "HA! A captain of refined taste!" The COTAC supporter collects his winnings and shares a bottle with your crew. The Castellan supporter grumbles but pays up and departs. Your crew enjoys the drink.

castellan.speaker: Comm Channel
castellan.text: "Finally, someone with SENSE!" The Castellan supporter collects and shares a glass of brandy with your bridge crew. Rich, smooth, undeniably good. The COTAC supporter departs muttering about barbarians.

refuse.text: Both merchants boo you and resume arguing as they drift away. Some battles aren't worth fighting.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Magnetized plasma wave incoming! Probably ejected from a distant star months ago. It's going to hit us in seconds. We can raise shields to absorb it or try to harden the electronics before impact.

shields.speaker: Engineer
shields.text: Shields absorbed the worst of it. Some power fluctuations and the nav data corrupted slightly, but we're intact. Could've been a lot worse without shields.

harden.speaker: Engineer
harden.text: Electronics are hardened just in time. The plasma wave washes over us and the hull crackles, but our systems hold steady. Good call, Captain.

brace.speaker: Engineer
brace.text: The wave hit us full force. Electronics are flickering, navigation data is scrambled, and we've got minor hull scoring from charged particle impacts. We'll be sorting this out for hours.

choices.label: Get us back up and running.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Small probe drifting past us, Captain. Broadcasting a single message on loop: "42." Analysis shows it's of unknown origin and impossibly old -- the message has been repeating for approximately six million years.

capture.speaker: Engineer
capture.text: Probe secured in the cargo bay. Still broadcasting. The collector's market should pay well for this -- six-million-year-old alien tech with a sense of humor.

hail.speaker: Sensor Officer
hail.text: We hailed it. It responded -- once. "You're welcome." Then resumed broadcasting "42." I... have no idea what to do with that information, Captain.

choices.label: Let it go. Some mysteries are better unsolved.

leave.text: The probe drifts on, broadcasting its eternal answer to a question nobody remembers asking. Your crew watches it go with a mix of wonder and confusion.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: COTAC customs frigate requesting a routine cargo scan. "Civilian vessel, heave to for inspection. We're checking for smuggled xenotech. Standard procedure -- shouldn't take long."

clean.speaker: Comm Channel
clean.text: The inspector runs her scan in minutes. "All clear. Thank you for your cooperation, Captain. We appreciate law-abiding citizens out here." She looks exhausted -- clearly just wants her shift to end.

hide.speaker: Engineer
hide.text: Your crew scrambles to stash anything questionable. The inspector's scan comes up clean -- barely. She narrows her eyes but waves you through. "Move along, Captain."

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Refusal is noted and will be reported. You're now flagged for enhanced screening at all COTAC stations." The frigate's weapons track you as you depart. Not hostile, but pointed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Picking up a tiny habitat module deep in the void -- orbiting nothing. Literally nothing. One life sign. The occupant is hailing us.

talk.speaker: Comm Channel
talk.text: An old man's face fills the screen -- bright-eyed and smiling. "Visitors! I'm Aldric. Lived here thirty years. The void is honest, you know. Stars lie." He offers navigation advice about a shortcut between systems. He asks for nothing in return but conversation.

stay.speaker: Comm Channel
stay.text: You spend an hour talking with Aldric about philosophy, space, and the nature of solitude. He's perfectly sane -- more so than most people you meet in ports. Your crew finds the visit profoundly unsettling, but in a way that makes them think.

thanks.speaker: Comm Channel
thanks.text: "Of course. Safe travels. The void provides, if you know how to listen." His signal fades as you pull away. Your navigator plugs in his shortcut coordinates -- they check out.

leave.text: You pass the tiny habitat in silence. One man, alone in the infinite dark, choosing to stay. Your crew watches until it fades from sensors.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: FIRE IN THE ENGINE BAY! A fuel line cracked during our last hard maneuver. Flames are spreading fast. I need orders, Captain!

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: Our warpsmith got in there with a patching kit and sealed the fuel line in under a minute. Fire's out, damage is minimal. That skill saved us a fortune in repairs.

vent.speaker: Engineer
vent.text: Compartment vented. Fire's out instantly, but we lost atmosphere in the engine bay. Took an hour to re-pressurize. Engine's intact but we burned through oxygen reserves.

manual.speaker: Engineer
manual.text: The crew fought the fire by hand -- extinguishers, wet blankets, sheer stubbornness. Took twenty minutes and two crew got minor burns, but the fire's out. Engine took a beating though.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You've stumbled into an illegal deep-space race. A Fringe pilot waves you down: "Entry fee's 200 credits, winner takes the pot -- 2,000 credits! Course runs through the asteroid cluster ahead. You in or out?"

choices.label: Pay the entry fee and race.

race.text: Your pilot threads through the asteroid cluster like a needle through fabric -- dodging, weaving, engines screaming. You cross the finish line in first place. The Fringe pilots howl with respect. "You fly like one of us!"

watch.text: You watch from a safe distance as pilots tear through the asteroid field. Two ships collide spectacularly. The winner does a victory barrel roll. Your crew enjoys the show and you pick up some gossip about local pilot networks.

choices.label: Entertainment value alone was worth it.

leave.text: You pull away from the racing cluster. Behind you, engines flare and cheering fills the comms. Your crew looks wistfully at the receding lights.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Distress beacon from a sealed cargo pod -- no ship attached. Inside our scans show preserved biological samples, research notes in an unknown script, and what appears to be a star map marking three locations in deep void.

choices.label: Leave it. Could be a trap.

recover.speaker: Engineer
recover.text: Pod's aboard. The biological samples are in perfect condition -- Xenoculture would pay well for these. The star map coordinates are intriguing but lead deep into unmapped void. Whatever destroyed the ship that left this pod... it didn't get the research.

leave.text: The beacon continues its lonely pulse as you pull away. Whatever secrets that pod holds, they'll wait for a braver captain.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Union Militia patrol wing scanning the area. "Civilian vessel, report any pirate activity in this sector. We've got increased Fringe activity warnings ahead."

intel.speaker: Comm Channel
intel.text: "Good intel, Captain. We'll adjust our patrols. The Militia appreciates citizens who look out for the sector. Watch yourself out there -- Fringe has been aggressive lately."

nothing.speaker: Comm Channel
nothing.text: "Understood. Stay alert -- we've confirmed pirate staging areas in the next two systems. Avoid uncharted routes if you can. Militia out."

escort.speaker: Comm Channel
escort.text: "We can spare a fighter to shadow you to the next system. No charge -- protecting civilians is what we're here for." The wing commander sounds almost pleased to have something useful to do.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, crew's reporting scratching sounds inside the hull -- between the interior walls and the outer plating. Sensors show nothing, but the sounds are moving. Something is crawling through the ship's structure.

chemical.speaker: Engineer
chemical.text: Our smelter cooked up a chemical repellent and pumped it into the wall cavities. Void mites -- a whole colony of tiny organisms that eat hull metal. The repellent drove them out through the exhaust vents. Hull integrity is intact. Close call.

choices.label: Good work. Run a full hull scan.

vent.speaker: Engineer
vent.text: Vented three sections to vacuum. The scratching stopped. Hull inspection shows minor scoring from void mite feeding -- the colony was bigger than we thought. But they're dead now.

ignore.speaker: Engineer
ignore.text: The scratching got worse over the next day. Hull integrity readings started dropping -- void mites, eating through our plating. We had to do an emergency purge. Should've acted sooner, Captain.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cluster of parked ships is running a Void Poker game via video link -- five captains around a virtual table. They wave you in. "Buy-in's 100 credits! Pull up a chair, friend!"

play.speaker: Comm Channel
play.text: Three hours of bluffing, betting, and banter later, you walk away up. "Lucky" Pham, the info broker at the table, trades gossip between hands -- pirate routes, trade deals, faction politics. Worth more than the pot.

watch.text: You watch a few hands. The players are colorful characters -- a Bulwark miner, a COTAC socialite, and the legendary "Lucky" Pham. The banter alone is worth the stop.

leave.text: The players shrug and deal another hand as you pull away. The game will be there next time -- it always is.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A convoy of battered civilian ships fleeing a solar flare disaster. They're trading personal possessions for fuel and food at desperate prices. Family heirlooms, handcrafted goods -- even a functional module.

help.text: You hand over food and fuel at no charge. The convoy leader weeps with gratitude. Your crew stands a little taller afterward. Sometimes doing the right thing is its own reward.

trade.text: You exchange supplies at fair prices. The refugees are grateful for honest dealing. Among their goods is a cosmetically damaged but functional module -- yours at a steep discount.

exploit.text: You buy their valuables for a fraction of their worth. The refugees have no choice but to accept. Your crew watches in silence. Whispers about your character circulate for days.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... sensors are showing a ship matching our exact specifications. Same hull, same modules, same energy signature. It's approaching from dead ahead. And it's -- it's hailing us with our own voice, played backwards.

hail.text: Your last three transmissions play back to you in reverse. The ship mirrors every movement you make, perfectly synchronized. Your crew is frozen with horror. This thing is wearing your face.

fire.speaker: Engineer
fire.text: Weapons hit the mirror ship -- and your own hull shudders with identical damage. Every shot you fire hurts you both equally. The mirror doesn't flinch, doesn't retaliate. It just absorbs and reflects.

power_down.text: The ship goes dark. Ninety seconds of absolute silence and darkness. Your crew barely breathes. When power returns, the mirror ship is gone. Sensors show nothing. But the crew will be checking the viewports for weeks.

choices.label: Resume course. Don't talk about this.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You spot a derelict at the same time as another salvager. "I was here first!" she shouts across comms. "My beacon tagged it!" There is definitely no beacon. Her name is Renko, and she looks ready to fight.

split.speaker: Comm Channel
split.text: Renko eyes you warily, then grins. "Fair's fair. Fifty-fifty." You work the derelict together. She's competent and tells good stories. "You're alright, Captain. I'll remember this -- got leads on better wrecks if you're interested."

fight.text: Renko doesn't back down easily, but your ship outguns hers. She retreats, cursing. "This isn't over!" You strip the derelict alone. Full haul, but you've made an enemy of a well-connected salvager.

defer.speaker: Comm Channel
defer.text: Renko blinks, surprised. "Huh. A captain with manners. Tell you what -- I know where three better wrecks are. Here are the coordinates. Consider us square." She tips an invisible hat and docks with the derelict.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A COTAC socialite in a luxury yacht is broadcasting restaurant reviews of ship galleys. She's spotted you. "You there! I demand to taste your ship's cuisine. My audience of 50,000 awaits my verdict."

good.speaker: Comm Channel
good.text: Your cook puts together the best plate they can. The critic chews slowly, deliberately. Then her eyes widen. "Seven out of ten! A hidden gem in the void!" She broadcasts a rave review. Your next port visit should be interesting.

choices.label: Tell the cook they did well.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Refusing a review? What are you hiding?" She broadcasts speculation that your galley is a health hazard. Your crew doesn't appreciate the publicity.

no_kitchen.speaker: Comm Channel
no_kitchen.text: "No kitchen?! You feed your crew with -- what, reconstituted protein bars?" She broadcasts a scathing expose on "the inhumane conditions aboard void-class vessels." Your crew rolls their eyes.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We just hit an invisible dark matter concentration! Gravity is fluctuating wildly -- crew floating, then slamming to the deck. Electronics are glitching. For thirty seconds the ship exists in a state of uncertain physics.

careful.speaker: Engineer
careful.text: We're through. Running diagnostics... interesting. One of our systems is actually performing better than before -- the dark matter seems to have had a beneficial effect on the power couplings. Could've gone the other way.

push.speaker: Engineer
push.text: Punching through at full power rattled everything loose that wasn't welded down. Some minor damage, but we're clear. The dark matter pocket is behind us. Sensors flagging it for future avoidance.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A converted cargo hauler serves as a mobile library. The Librarian, an elderly Xenoculture scholar, hails you warmly. "Knowledge is the only cargo that grows heavier with use. What can I teach you today?"

train.speaker: Comm Channel
train.text: The Librarian spends an hour with your crew member, teaching with patience and clarity. "Remember -- every skill is a door. Walk through enough doors and you'll find rooms you never knew existed."

maps.speaker: Comm Channel
maps.text: The Librarian transfers detailed charts of uncharted regions. "These took me forty years to compile. Use them wisely, Captain. Some of those regions are uncharted for good reason."

chat.speaker: Comm Channel
chat.text: You spend a pleasant hour discussing void philosophy and alien linguistics. The Librarian's knowledge is staggering. She asks nothing in return but the pleasure of conversation. Your crew is quietly inspired.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: HULL BREACH DECK TWO! All hands, pressure suits NOW! ...Wait. Wait. False alarm. Someone microwaved something they shouldn't have and the pressure sensor misread the steam burst.

choices.label: At least we know the drills work.

who.speaker: Engineer
who.text: A sheepish crew member steps forward. "I just wanted to heat up my lunch, Captain." The crew's relief after the scare pushes morale above where it started. Your engineer is recommending microwave safety training.

choices.label: Carry on. No more unauthorized microwaving.

drills.text: The crew's response time was excellent -- everyone suited up in under ninety seconds. The scare turned into an impromptu drill assessment. Silver linings.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Xenoculture science ship studying void organisms hails you. The lead researcher is eager to trade data and buy biological samples at double market value. Her assistant behind her looks terrified about something.

sell.speaker: Comm Channel
sell.text: "Excellent specimens! These will advance our understanding of void ecology tremendously." She pays generously. As the transaction completes, her assistant whispers something. The researcher's smile falters briefly before she waves goodbye.

ask.speaker: Comm Channel
ask.text: The researcher's eyes light up. "We've detected organized patterns in void organism migration -- as if something is herding them. Directing them." She's excited. Her assistant pulls her aside urgently. She returns with a strained smile. "Just academic curiosity. Nothing to worry about."

leave.text: The research vessel returns to its work as you depart. Through the viewport, you catch a glimpse of something massive in the distance that the researchers seem to be studying. Then it's gone.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two armed ships block your path. "This is a toll zone. 150 credits for safe passage." They're unaffiliated thugs with big guns and small ambitions.

choices.label: Bluff with a fake military transponder.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Pleasure doing business." They pocket the credits and drift aside. Your crew grumbles about paying off thugs. At least nobody got hurt.

fight.text: The thugs are tough but disorganized. One breaks and runs when their shields drop. The other fights to the end. You salvage what's left and add "toll zone enforcer" to your resume.

bluff.text: You broadcast a Castellan military transponder code. The thugs' bravado evaporates instantly. "We, uh -- didn't see you. Free passage. Always." They scatter like startled fish.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's... a painting floating in the void. Oil on canvas, ornate frame, perfectly preserved in vacuum. It depicts a star system that doesn't match any known charts -- three suns with a single green planet.

choices.label: Recover it and sell to a collector.

collector.text: An art dealer at the next station pays 500 credits without hesitation. "Void paintings are extremely rare. This one is... particularly interesting." She examines the pigments with a magnifier and goes very quiet. She doesn't share what she found.

xeno.text: A Xenoculture historian examines the painting and nearly falls off her chair. "These pigments contain minerals found only in the Karath system -- which was supposedly sterilized centuries ago. Someone painted this AFTER the sterilization." She pays handsomely for the find.

leave.text: The painting tumbles slowly through the void, catching starlight on its surface. Three suns. One green planet. A mystery for someone else to solve.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Captain, one of the crew has developed void psychosis. Paranoid, insisting the stars are rearranging themselves. The rest of the crew is getting tense. We need to handle this before it spreads.

choices.label: Ignore it -- they'll snap out of it.

treat.speaker: Medic
treat.text: Treatment is effective -- sedatives and cognitive therapy over a few hours. The crew member recovers, mostly. But later, quietly, they pull you aside: "Did you check, Captain? Did anyone actually check if the stars moved?"

confine.speaker: Medic
confine.text: Confinement calms them eventually, but the paranoia spread to two other crew members first. Tensions are high for days. The affected crew member recovers but refuses to look out viewports anymore.

ignore.speaker: Engineer
ignore.text: The crew member sabotaged the navigation console overnight, insisting it was "telling lies about where the stars are." Repairs cost time and parts. Other crew members are rattled. Should've acted sooner.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A massive COTAC merchant convoy -- twenty ships strong -- passes through. Their commodore hails you. "Care to travel with us? Safety in numbers, friend. We've also got bulk goods at eighty percent market price."

join.speaker: Comm Channel
join.text: You fall into formation. The convoy is slow but safe -- twenty armed escorts and strength in numbers. The commodore shares trade gossip and your crew relaxes for the first time in days.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: The convoy's quartermaster offers bulk supplies at a discount. Good prices on fuel, food, and raw materials. "Can't beat convoy pricing," he says with a merchant's pride.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: The commodore nods, visibly disappointed. "Suit yourself. Safe travels, Captain. Safety in numbers, remember." The convoy rumbles on without you.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- we just dropped out of warp and there's a ghostly image of our own ship arriving. It looks damaged. Hull scoring, a missing engine nacelle. The timestamp on the echo reads... six hours from now.

choices.label: Change course to avoid whatever caused that.

avoid.speaker: Sensor Officer
avoid.text: Plotting a detour now. It'll cost fuel and time, but if that echo is accurate, whatever's ahead nearly destroyed us. Some fates are worth avoiding.

prepare.speaker: Engineer
prepare.text: Six hours. We use every minute -- shields charged, weapons hot, damage control teams on standby. Whatever hit us in that echo, we'll see it coming this time.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Multiple contacts dropping from warp in an encirclement pattern! Four pirate ships -- coordinated, well-equipped. Their leader is broadcasting: "Captain Nix sends regards. Hand over your cargo or we take everything."

choices.label: Fight -- we knew this was coming.

fight_ready.text: Thanks to the warp echo, you're positioned perfectly. First strike tears through their formation before they can coordinate. Captain Nix is good -- but not good enough when you see the punch coming. Two ships down, two fleeing. Nix's voice crackles: "Next time, Captain."

surrender.speaker: Comm Channel
surrender.text: Nix's crew strips your cargo hold efficiently. "Smart choice. Live to fly another day." They warp away with your goods. Your crew is furious but alive.

break.text: You punch through the weakest point in their encirclement, taking fire from all sides. Hull alarms scream. But you're through, and they can't match your speed in open void. Your ship is battered but free.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Captain, we've recovered a stasis pod drifting in the void. Inside is a healthy infant. No ship, no debris, no explanation. Medical scans show human with unusual genetic markers. Every faction will claim this child.

choices.label: Take the baby to the nearest station.

station.speaker: Medic
station.text: The station accepts the child with a mix of gratitude and barely concealed excitement about those genetic markers. Three different faction representatives attempt to "claim" the infant within the hour. You leave before it becomes a diplomatic incident.

keep.speaker: Medic
keep.text: The crew adopts the baby with startling enthusiasm. Tough spacers fighting over who gets to hold it. Someone rigs a crib from spare parts. Morale has never been higher. You now have a baby on a spaceship. What could go wrong?

leave.text: You leave the stasis pod drifting. Your crew stares at you in disbelief. Some won't speak to you for days. The silence on the bridge is deafening.

choices.label: We couldn't take on that responsibility.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Rogue asteroid on intercept course! Sixty seconds to impact. It's big, Captain. We need to evade, shoot it, or brace for impact.

evade.text: Emergency burn pushes the crew into their seats as the asteroid screams past, close enough to see individual craters. Your pilot lets out a breath they've been holding for thirty seconds.

shoot.speaker: Engineer
shoot.text: Direct hit! The asteroid shatters into fragments. Most pass harmlessly by, though a few smaller pieces pepper the hull. Your weapons officer looks satisfied -- target practice doesn't usually come with stakes this high.

brace.speaker: Engineer
brace.text: Direct impact. The ship rings like a bell. Hull breach warnings on three decks. Structural damage is significant -- we're going to need a station for repairs. But we're alive.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Hey, it's my favorite audience!" Dex the void comedian is back, broadcasting on all frequencies. "Check out my new material! Also, I picked up some useful gossip about pirate patrol routes if you're interested."

choices.label: Let's hear the jokes AND the intel.

full.speaker: Comm Channel
full.text: His jokes are marginally better -- one actually gets a genuine laugh from the bridge. The intel is solid: pirate patrol routes, safe corridors, and a rumor about a Fringe supply depot. Dex is more useful than he looks.

intel.speaker: Comm Channel
intel.text: "All business, huh? Fine." Dex shares detailed pirate patrol routes and safe corridors. He's heard things from dozens of ships. The information is genuinely valuable.

tip.speaker: Comm Channel
tip.text: "A tipper! You beautiful human!" Dex dedicates his next broadcast set to you by name. Independent traders who catch the show remember you favorably. Plus the intel. "This one's on the house, friend."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, we've found it -- the CSV Wanderlust. Intact but running on minimal power, drifting. Bridge is empty. Crew quarters look recently lived in -- meals half-eaten. And there's a massive sealed container in the cargo bay covered in warning symbols from no known language. The container hums.

choices.label: Salvage the ship but leave the container.

open.text: The container opens. Inside is... nothing. Absolute nothing -- a void within a void, darker than space itself. And then something looks back. Not with eyes. With attention. Your crew screams. The container seals itself. The hum stops. Whatever was inside is gone. Or is everywhere now.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Good haul from the Wanderlust -- intact systems, fuel reserves, personal effects. We left the container sealed. The crew wanted nothing to do with it. Smart. As we undock, the container's hum gets louder briefly, then stops. Like it noticed us leaving.

leave.text: You leave the Wanderlust drifting. Your crew watches it recede on sensors. Nobody questions the decision. Some ships are lost for a reason.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A passing ship hails you on frequency 69.0. The entire message is a single word: "Nice." Your comms officer logs it with a straight face. A crew member chuckles.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An Independent master shipwright operates a mobile workshop from a converted carrier. "Your ship has character," she says approvingly. "I can repair, install, or modify. What do you need?"

repair.speaker: Comm Channel
repair.text: The shipwright's crew patches your hull with practiced efficiency. "Good as new. Well, better than new -- I use Bulwark-grade welding." The work is flawless.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: She has hull plating, electronics, and composites in stock -- quality materials at fair prices. "I only sell what I'd use on my own ship," she says. That's a high bar.

browse.speaker: Comm Channel
browse.text: "No pressure. I'll be in this sector for a few more days. Come back if you change your mind." She gives your ship one more appraising look before returning to work.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: An alien vessel just emerged from -- that wasn't a warp jump. That was a dimensional fold. The hull is organic, shifting, covered in what might be eyes. Communication attempts produce static... wait. It's trying to speak. Slowly: "WE. LOST. WHICH. STAR. HOME?"

choices.label: Help them navigate -- share star maps.

help.text: Hours of patient communication follow -- pointing at stars, sharing data, learning to understand each other through mathematics and light patterns. Finally, recognition. The alien ship shudders with what you interpret as joy. A module detaches from their hull and drifts to yours -- a gift. It generates power beyond anything human-made.

observe.speaker: Sensor Officer
observe.text: The alien ship waits, pulsing with bioluminescent patterns. After an hour of no response, it slowly folds back into whatever dimension it came from. The crew is silent. Something extraordinary just passed through your life, and you let it go.

retreat.text: As you pull away, the alien ship emits a low tone -- almost sad. It folds back into its dimension and vanishes. Your crew watches the empty space where it was for a long time.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A panicked comm: a merchant captain's crew has mutinied. He's locked on the bridge while armed crew demand the ship. The mutineers claim he cheated them on six months' wages. Both sides are offering you 200 credits to help.

captain.text: You intimidate the mutineers into standing down. The captain is grateful, but as you help secure the crew, you find their pay records. They really haven't been paid in months. The captain avoids your eyes.

mutineers.text: The mutineers take control with your backing. They're not violent -- just desperate workers who want what they're owed. The deposed captain is put in an escape pod with supplies. Your crew watches and draws their own conclusions about fair wages.

neutral.text: You pull away from the standoff. Both sides broadcast increasingly desperate pleas. Eventually the comms go silent. You never find out what happened. Your crew is divided on whether you made the right call.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: POWER SURGE! Cascade failure in the electrical grid -- systems dropping in sequence! Shields down, weapons offline, life support flickering. If someone can isolate the cascade before it reaches the reactor, we survive. If not...

choices.label: Get the warpsmith on it NOW.

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: Your warpsmith isolates the cascade at junction fourteen -- barely. The surge dies. Systems come back online one by one. Five seconds later and the reactor would have blown. Five seconds.

shutdown.speaker: Engineer
shutdown.text: Grid's dead. We're floating dark in the void -- no power, no sensors, no weapons. Oxygen for about an hour. Restart sequence takes five minutes. Longest five minutes of your life. But the grid comes back clean.

manual.speaker: Engineer
manual.text: Rerouting manually -- it's like defusing a bomb with a wrench. Three crew take electrical burns before the cascade is contained. The grid stabilizes, but barely. We need a station for proper repairs.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A gold-plated yacht pulls alongside. "Ah, my favorite mark!" The gambler is back, grinning widely. "Double or nothing on everything! I bet 500 credits your cook can't make a souffle in zero-g. I bet 300 credits I can dock with your ship blindfolded!"

souffle.speaker: Comm Channel
souffle.text: Against all odds and physics, your cook pulls it off -- a slightly lopsided but technically valid zero-g souffle. The gambler stares in disbelief, then laughs. "You magnificent lunatic. Here's your credits." Your cook has never looked more proud.

dock.speaker: Comm Channel
dock.text: The gambler actually tries it -- blindfolded, using only instruments. He clips your hull on approach, scratching his gold paint. "That counts! ...It doesn't count? Fine." He pays up with a theatrical sigh.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Coward! Spoilsport! Come back! I'll bet you 100 credits you can't resist one more bet!" His voice fades as you pull away. The man is incorrigible.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Quarantined medical vessel ahead, broadcasting automated warnings: "Do not approach. Biological contamination. All crew deceased." But Captain -- the medical bay may contain data on the pathogen. That data could be worth a fortune.

board.speaker: Medic
board.text: Hazmat protocols, full containment. Our medics navigate the ship's horrors and recover the pathogen data. It's engineered -- someone designed this disease. A Fringe bioweapons program. The data is worth a fortune to Union Militia or ISD.

choices.label: Seal the data. Find a buyer.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Long-range scans pull partial data from the ship's computers. Incomplete, but enough to confirm an engineered pathogen. Someone will pay for even partial data. The full story dies with the ship.

choices.label: Partial data is better than nothing.

leave.text: You leave the plague ship drifting. The automated warning continues its broadcast behind you, patient and eternal. Some knowledge isn't worth the price of acquisition.

start.text: Your entire crew falls asleep simultaneously during a quiet stretch of void travel. Everyone wakes up two hours later feeling inexplicably refreshed. Your navigator's console has a sticky note that wasn't there before: "You all needed that. -- V." Nobody wrote it. Nobody is concerned about this, which is somehow more concerning.

choices.label: Accept the gift. Don't question it.

question.speaker: Sensor Officer
question.text: No unauthorized access detected. No ships on sensors during the blackout. The autopilot maintained course perfectly. The sticky note is standard ship-issue paper. There is no explanation. Your crew shrugs and returns to duty, unusually well-rested.

accept.text: Sometimes the void gives instead of takes. Your crew is rested, refreshed, and inexplicably cheerful. The sticky note goes on the bridge bulletin board. Nobody removes it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark transport carrying sensitive mining equipment needs an escort through a pirate corridor. "400 credits on safe delivery. Don't die and I'll recommend you to the guild." The captain is gruff but the pay is good.

accept.text: The escort runs hot -- two pirate attacks in quick succession. Your guns keep them off the transport while the Bulwark captain maintains course with iron nerve. "Knew I picked the right escort," he grunts as you reach safe space.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: The captain grunts. "Your loss. I'll find someone with backbone." The transport lumbers off alone into the pirate corridor. You hope they make it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We're passing through a region where radio signals bounce endlessly. Comms are flooding with fragments -- ancient distress calls, love letters between stars, a child's voice reciting multiplication tables. And Captain... one message has our transponder ID. A distress call from us. Dated three months from now.

record.speaker: Sensor Officer
record.text: Recorded. The call describes a cascade failure near a binary star. Coordinates included. We now have a date, location, and cause for our own future disaster. Whether we can change it... that's the question.

filter.speaker: Sensor Officer
filter.text: Filters engaged. The voices fade to static, then silence. We pass through the echo chamber and back into clean void. Your comms officer looks shaken but says nothing.

listen.text: A captain's final log, calm and dignified. A trader singing a lullaby across light-years to a child who grew old decades ago. Fragments of lives, preserved in radio echoes. Beautiful and devastating. Your crew is quiet for hours afterward.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- dozens of ships ahead, all docked together. It's a Void Market -- a floating bazaar assembled from ships. Hundreds of merchants, everything from common goods to rare components. The market master broadcasts: "Welcome! Same time next month!"

supplies.text: Fuel, food, and basic materials at fair prices from a dozen competing vendors. The atmosphere is festive -- music, food stalls, even void-brewed ale. Your crew is thrilled at the opportunity to stretch their legs and shop.

rare.text: Deep in the market, specialty vendors offer electronics, alloys, and crystal at competitive prices. One stall sells exotic biological samples. Another has reclaimed military hardware. The selection is remarkable.

browse.text: You wander the market for an hour. The sights alone are worth the stop -- alien crafts, rare artifacts, performers, and the best people-watching in the sector. Your crew enjoys the break from routine.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A single pirate frigate blocks your path. "I've got twenty ships behind that asteroid and they all have their guns on you. 200 credits or we open fire." Sensor sweep shows... one ship. No asteroid. No fleet.

call.speaker: Comm Channel
call.text: "There's no fleet behind the asteroid. There's no asteroid. It's just you." Long silence on comms. "...Okay, fair enough. Can't blame a girl for trying." She powers down weapons and drifts aside, muttering about needing a better script.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Smart move! The fleet thanks you!" She takes the credits and warps away before you can reconsider. Your sensor officer clears their throat. "Captain, there was no fleet." Your crew's opinion of your judgment takes a hit.

attack.text: The pirate's bluff collapses the moment you open fire. She takes one hit to shields and immediately starts running. "Okay okay OKAY! No fleet! I lied! CEASEFIRE!" She limps away at top speed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive ion storm incoming -- a wall of crackling blue energy sweeping through the sector. Shields will absorb most of it, but power systems are going to fluctuate wildly. We can ride it out or try to collect the charged particles for sale.

shields.speaker: Engineer
shields.text: Five minutes of blue hell. Shields held, but power fluctuated enough to reset half our systems. Navigation instruments gave contradictory readings for a while. We're through now.

collect.speaker: Engineer
collect.text: Risky, but we managed to scoop charged ions into our cargo containers. Xenoculture researchers pay well for this stuff. The hull took some scoring from unshielded exposure, but the payload is worth it.

calm.text: Your pilot threads through the storm, finding pockets of stillness between the crackling energy walls. Masterful flying. You emerge on the other side with barely a scratch.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A lone ship drifts in the void, engines off. The pilot, an old ISD retiree, hails you. "I come out here to think. The void doesn't judge. Care to talk?"

talk.speaker: Comm Channel
talk.text: You talk for an hour about consciousness, faction warfare, and whether synthetic coffee counts as real coffee. He gives no quest, sells nothing, wants nothing. Just good conversation. Sometimes that's exactly what you need.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "I understand. The void will be here when you're ready to listen." He settles back in his chair and closes his eyes, drifting peacefully.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: We just passed through an alien spore cloud -- invisible until they coated the hull and started glowing. Life support caught most, but some got through. The crew is sneezing in harmonic patterns. Worse: these spores attract void predators. Hull cleaning is urgent.

choices.label: Use farming crew to identify them.

clean.speaker: Engineer
clean.text: EVA team scrubbed the hull clean in thirty minutes. The glowing fades. Your crew will be sneezing for another day, but at least we won't be attracting anything hungry.

farm.speaker: Engineer
farm.text: Your farmer identifies them as void orchid reproduction spores -- beautiful, harmless to humans, but the bioluminescence is a dinner bell for predators. They process the spores into a useful biological compound before cleaning the hull.

ignore.speaker: Sensor Officer
ignore.text: Captain, we've got something large approaching on sensors -- attracted by the spore glow on our hull. It's moving fast. We should have cleaned the hull when we had the chance.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A smooth-talking merchant hails you with a gleam in his eye. "Friend, I have something extraordinary -- a genuine star map to the legendary Vault of Koss. Treasure beyond imagining! Yours for just 300 credits."
