buy.text: You buy the map. Your crew gives you side-eye. The Vault of Koss is a well-known spacer myth used to fleece newcomers. However -- the fake map does contain real coordinates to a minor cache left by a previous victim. Net gain: a crate of random goods.

choices.label: Well, at least it wasn't a total loss.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: The merchant's smile doesn't waver. "A savvy captain! Perhaps next time, then. The Vault waits for no one!" He winks and warps away. Your crew nods approvingly -- not every captain can smell a con.

threaten.speaker: Comm Channel
threaten.text: "Report me? To whom? We're in deep void, friend!" He laughs and warps away before you can respond. Points for audacity.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Civilian vessel, you have entered a Castellan military exercise zone. Clear the area immediately or we will consider you a target drone." Warships flash past executing combat drills. A bored comms officer directs you out.

leave.text: You clear the exercise zone quickly. The warships resume their drills without giving you a second thought. Discretion is the better part of valor.

observe.speaker: Comm Channel
observe.text: The comms officer checks your record. "Hmm. Your rep checks out. Observer position granted -- stay at the marked coordinates and do NOT fire anything." You watch Castellan capital ships run combat formations. It's educational.

linger.text: Simulated fire peppers your shields -- blanks, but terrifying at close range. Your crew ducks instinctively. The comms officer's voice returns: "That was your warning, civilian. LEAVE."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Fringe entrepreneur in a garish ship broadcasts: "VOID LOTTERY! Ten credits a ticket! One lucky winner gets a genuine, barely-used corvette!" The odds are astronomical. The salesman's grin is unstoppable.

ticket.speaker: Comm Channel
ticket.text: "Bold move! Ticket number 7,422! Results broadcast in one hour!" The entrepreneur vanishes into warp before you can ask follow-up questions. An hour later, a comm arrives: "Congratulations, you've won... a commemorative void pen! Retail value: 2 credits."

tickets.speaker: Comm Channel
tickets.text: "A high roller! Five tickets!" The entrepreneur barely contains his excitement before warping away. An hour later: "Ticket 7,425 -- MINOR PRIZE! 100 credits!" Against all odds, you came out ahead.

no.speaker: Comm Channel
no.text: "A skeptic! The corvette could have been yours!" He winks and warps away. Your crew watches him go with a mix of amusement and relief that you didn't waste credits.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the crystal has been whispering coordinates for days. We've arrived at the location. Reality is... thin here. Stars through a shimmering membrane appear wrong -- unfamiliar constellations. Something presses against the membrane from the other side. The crystal hums louder.

destroy.text: The crystal shatters. The hum dies. The membrane ripples once, then fades. Normal stars return. Whatever was on the other side, whatever wanted in -- the door is closed. Your crew breathes again.

push.text: Your ship pushes through. For an instant, you exist in two places. Colors that have no names. Geometry that hurts to perceive. Then you're through -- back in normal space, but 500 credits worth of exotic materials have crystallized on your hull. The membrane seals behind you. Something on the other side was disappointed.

observe.text: You watch the membrane from a safe distance. Through the shimmer, a face becomes visible -- vast, ancient, curious. It sees you. It nods slowly, as if recognizing something. The membrane seals. The crystal goes silent. The stars return to normal.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the crew got into a food fight in the mess hall. Someone threw a reconstituted protein block at someone who insulted their taste in music. It... escalated. Every off-duty crew member is involved. The cook is furious.

fun.text: The food fight becomes legendary -- stories will be told for years. Morale skyrockets. You lost five units of food supplies, but the crew hasn't laughed this hard in months. The cook demands a formal apology. They get one, between giggles.

stop.text: You shut it down. The crew cleans up in sullen silence. Discipline is maintained, food is preserved, but the mess hall feels colder for a while.

choices.label: Someone has to be the adult.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Ship running without transponder codes ahead. Intercepting reveals -- Captain, they're carrying people. Packed in the cargo hold in terrible conditions. This is a slave ship. The crew is well-armed.

choices.label: This is too dangerous. Move on.

attack.text: The slavers fight desperately but you overwhelm them. The freed people include a skilled warpsmith who pledges service for life. The gratitude is overwhelming. Union Militia and Xenoculture both send commendations.

choices.label: No one should live in chains.

report.text: You transmit coordinates to the nearest Militia patrol. They respond within the hour. The slavers are captured. It's slower, but safer. The Militia thanks you formally.

ignore.text: You fly on. Your crew knows what was in that cargo hold. They know you saw and did nothing. The silence on the bridge could cut steel.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: In a pocket of absolute stillness -- no wind, no radiation, nothing -- floats a single sphere of impossible smoothness. A void pearl. Warm to the touch, pulsing with faint light. It's extraordinarily rare and valuable.

sell.text: A collector at the next station pays 500 credits without haggling. He holds the pearl like a religious artifact. Whatever secrets it holds, they belong to him now.

xeno.text: Xenoculture researchers are ecstatic. "Do you know how rare these are? Formed over millennia in conditions that shouldn't exist!" Their payment is generous, and your contribution to science earns lasting gratitude.

keep.text: The void pearl sits in a display case on the bridge. Crew who pass by report feeling calm -- a warmth that has no explanation. It's worth a fortune, but some things are more valuable than credits.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An ISD health inspector requests to board. "Routine vessel inspection. This won't take long." She's already scanning your ship with a critical eye. She looks like she'd rather be anywhere else.

pass.speaker: Comm Channel
pass.text: The inspector tours your ship with a checklist. Kitchen? Check. Quarters? Adequate. Medical? Acceptable. "Your vessel meets minimum ISD habitability standards. Barely." She stamps a certificate and leaves with visible relief.

reluctant.speaker: Comm Channel
reluctant.text: "Regulations are regulations, Captain." She inspects with extra thoroughness, finding minor violations. "I'll overlook the unauthorized food storage if you clean the ventilation filters. Deal?"

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Refusal noted. You're fined 100 credits for non-compliance. This will be on your permanent record with ISD stations." She looks almost disappointed -- your refusal means more paperwork for her.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, those asteroids ahead are emitting harmonic tones -- actual music, created by solar wind passing through crystalline structures. The melody changes with stellar conditions. Your crew is transfixed.

record.text: Your crew records the singing stones for an hour. The melody is hauntingly beautiful -- unlike anything human-made. Playing it later becomes a morale ritual. Some things in the void are worth preserving.

mine.speaker: Engineer
mine.text: The crystals yield valuable materials -- 300 credits worth. But as the first asteroid cracks, the music dies mid-note. The silence that follows is deafening. Your crew won't look at you for a while.

listen.text: You drift among the singing stones for twenty minutes. The music shifts through modes you have no names for. Your crew hums along, somehow knowing the melody before it arrives. A perfect moment.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Intercepting a bounty board transmission from a Union Militia relay. Active bounties: Captain Nix -- 1,000 credits, wanted alive. Various Fringe targets -- 500 credits each. Several other warrants listed.

note.speaker: Sensor Officer
note.text: Bounty coordinates logged. Captain Nix's last known position, known pirate staging areas, and reward terms are all recorded. Your crew seems keen on the prospect of some sanctioned hunting.

pass.text: The bounty board transmission continues on loop as you move on. Someone else will collect those bounties.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A weaving merchant ship nearly collides with you. The captain is extremely drunk. "Sorry! Sorry! I'm celebra-celebrating! My daughter just got into the Castellan Academy!" He's harmless but a menace to navigation.

choices.label: Escort him to the nearest station.
Report him to the nearest patrol.

escort.speaker: Comm Channel
escort.text: You shepherd the weaving captain to port. He's grateful, tearful, and insists on paying you. "You're a good person! My daughter -- she's going to be an OFFICER!" He presses credits on you and stumbles toward the docking clamps.

report.text: A nearby patrol picks him up within minutes. He gets fined and grounded. The patrol officer gives you a small informant payment. Your crew debates whether you did the right thing.

choices.label: He was a danger to himself and others.

go.text: The drunk captain weaves away into the void, singing off-key. You hope he makes it. Your crew watches with a mix of amusement and concern.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We're passing near an invisible mass -- dark object bending light around it. Through the gravitational lens we can see distant galaxies magnified a thousandfold. Spirals of light, galactic collisions in slow motion. The view is... staggering.

choices.label: Enjoy the view and move on.

record.speaker: Sensor Officer
record.text: Detailed observations recorded. Xenoculture will pay well for this data -- views of distant galaxies this clear are extremely rare. Your science-minded crew is ecstatic. Some are in tears at the beauty of it.

enjoy.text: Your crew gathers at viewports and watches in silence. Structures that dwarf comprehension, playing out over cosmic timescales. For a brief moment, every problem in your life feels very, very small.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Lone figure in a pressure suit waving from a tiny platform of wreckage. They've been stranded for two days -- nearly out of oxygen. Life signs are weak but stable.

pickup.speaker: Comm Channel
pickup.text: Meet Ozzy, a Fringe mechanic who "had a disagreement" with his last captain. No money, but his warpsmithing skill is surprisingly high. He offers two hours of free repair work and the location of his former captain's hidden supply cache.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Scans clear -- one human, no weapons, no biological hazards. Just a stranded mechanic running out of air. He's waving more frantically now.

leave.text: You leave the figure waving on their platform of wreckage. Their suit has maybe six hours of air left. Your crew doesn't say anything, but the bridge feels colder.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: SENSORS CRITICAL! Micro black hole -- barely a meter across but with the mass of a mountain! It's close, Captain. Hull is groaning under tidal forces. Emergency maneuvers NOW!

evade.text: Your pilot throws the ship sideways with everything the engines have. The hull screams under differential gravity, but you pull clear. Close enough to see the light bending around that tiny point of infinite density.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: Insane, but your crew manages to scoop Hawking radiation emissions before pulling away. The data alone is worth a fortune to scientists. The hull took a beating from tidal stress, but the payload is extraordinary.

reverse.speaker: Engineer
reverse.text: Full reverse tears us free, but the tidal forces wrench the hull badly. Structural damage on three decks. We need a station. But we're alive, which is more than many can say about micro black hole encounters.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A licensed therapist operates from a luxury shuttle. "The void is vast, but your feelings are valid. 50 credits per session -- I promise you'll feel lighter." Your crew seems... interested.

session.text: Your crew emerges from sessions visibly lighter. Your engineer admits: "I didn't realize I was carrying all that." The therapist hands you a card: "Call anytime. Space is hard."

group.text: Group therapy session in the cargo bay. Tears, laughter, breakthroughs, and one crew member who won't stop talking about their childhood. Your crew bonds in unexpected ways. Even your pilot opened up.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "The offer stands. I'll be in the sector for another few days." She smiles warmly. Your crew looks wistfully at the departing shuttle.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, crew is reporting a stranger in the corridors -- someone who doesn't belong. Security sweeps found nothing. But now two crew members say they encountered each other in the same room... and there was a third version of one of them.

choices.label: Lock down the ship. Find the imposter.
Watch for the tell -- it blinks out of sync.

find.speaker: Engineer
find.text: Full lockdown. Every crew member accounted for and identified. During the sweep, you spot it -- a perfect copy of your navigator, except it blinks a half-second off rhythm. When confronted, it doesn't fight. It simply... dissolves. A void mimic. Gone now.

watch.text: You catch it at dinner -- a crew member with a blink that's just slightly wrong. The void mimic looks at you with borrowed eyes, then slips away and vanishes into the ventilation system. By morning, it's gone. But the paranoia lingers.

ignore.speaker: Engineer
ignore.text: The sightings escalate over three days. Arguments break out about who's real. Trust erodes. The mimic eventually leaves on its own, but the damage to crew cohesion takes weeks to repair.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A monument floats in the void -- an obsidian obelisk exactly 100 meters tall, inscribed with thousands of names in every known language and some unknown ones. At the base: "To those who traveled far enough to find this." Captain... your ship's name is already inscribed.

inscribe.text: A crew member adds their name to the blank spaces at the bottom. Nothing happens. No flash of light, no cosmic revelation. But it feels important. Like signing a guest book at the edge of forever.

study.speaker: Sensor Officer
study.text: The obelisk is made of no known material. The inscriptions span at least 10,000 years based on linguistic analysis. Some names are from civilizations that left no other trace. Your ship's name was added recently -- the material is still warm to the touch.

leave.text: You leave the monument as you found it. A silent witness to ten millennia of travelers, floating in the dark. Your name is on it. That means something, even if you don't know what.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Warp drive just detonated a cascade pulse on exit! Shockwave visible for light-seconds. Every pirate and opportunist in the sector now knows exactly where we are. We've got maybe three minutes before company arrives.

fight.text: The first to arrive is a lone scout -- easy prey. You destroy it quickly. The second wave is three ships in attack formation. It's a brutal fight, but the element of preparation gives you the edge. They break off when they realize you're not easy pickings.

warp.speaker: Engineer
warp.text: Warp drive is cycling -- ninety seconds to charge. The scout arrives and fires. You return fire while the drive spins up. The moment it's ready, you jump. The scout's last shot hits your hull as you vanish.

repair.speaker: Engineer
repair.text: Emergency repairs bring shields and weapons back to full. When the scout arrives, you're ready. When the second wave arrives, you're still ready. They take one look at a fully operational warship and think better of it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A converted transport hails you. Forty war orphans and three exhausted caretakers. Sister Venn, the head caretaker, speaks with quiet dignity: "We're running low on everything. Food, fuel, medicine. Any help you can provide would be a blessing."

generous.speaker: Comm Channel
generous.text: Sister Venn weeps with gratitude. As your crew loads supplies, a child hands you a hand-drawn thank you card -- forty small signatures crammed onto one page. Your crew pins it to the bridge wall. It stays.

modest.speaker: Comm Channel
modest.text: "Every bit helps, Captain. Thank you." Sister Venn's smile doesn't quite reach her eyes -- she needs more, but she's too dignified to push. Your crew feels good about helping, but wishes they could do more.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "I understand. Times are hard for everyone." Sister Venn's voice is steady but the children's faces in the background are not. Your crew is quiet for a long time after.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Encrypted channel: a Fringe pirate wants out. "I'll give you the locations of three hidden pirate supply caches in exchange for safe passage to a Union Militia station." He sounds genuinely scared.

choices.label: Accept -- take him to the Militia.
Take the intel but hand him to the Fringe.

militia.text: The pirate gives you three cache locations -- 300 credits each in weapons and supplies. You deliver him to a Militia outpost. The commander is impressed. "We've been trying to turn insiders for months. Good work, Captain."

fringe.text: You take his intel and hand him back to his Fringe contacts. They're grateful -- and disturbed that one of their own tried to defect. The cache coordinates are still good. The pirate's fate is not your concern.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Please -- I'm a dead man if I go back." His voice cracks. But you pull away. Harboring wanted criminals brings trouble you don't need. The encrypted channel goes silent.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, we just passed through a cloud of gelatinous substance -- void whale waste product. The hull is coated in translucent purple jelly. It smells like lavender, it's mildly adhesive, and it's cutting our speed by five percent. The crew is disgusted.

clean.speaker: Engineer
clean.text: EVA team spent an hour scrubbing. Hull's clean, speed is restored, and the lavender smell is finally fading. "Disgusting but not the worst thing that's happened this week," your engineer notes.

farm.speaker: Engineer
farm.text: Your farmer processes the jelly into a surprisingly effective healing salve. Medical supplies restocked from void whale excrement. The universe provides in mysterious ways.

choices.label: Don't tell the crew what it's made from.

live.text: The purple jelly coating becomes a running joke. Other ships give you funny looks. Your crew names it Gerald. Speed returns to normal after it dries and flakes off naturally over a few days.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An unmarked ship running dark intercepts you. The occupants are ISD intelligence operatives. "You didn't see us. You were never here. Understood?" Their tone leaves no room for negotiation.

choices.label: What are you doing out here?
I don't take orders from ghosts.

comply.speaker: Comm Channel
comply.text: "Good." The operative nods once. Their ship powers up and vanishes like it was never there. A few days later, a small anonymous credit transfer appears in your account. ISD takes care of cooperative civilians.

ask.speaker: Comm Channel
ask.text: The lead operative's eyes narrow. Then, unexpectedly: "Some of our people have gone off the reservation. A rogue faction within ISD. Watch yourself out here, Captain. Trust no one with an ISD badge. Including us." They vanish.

defy.speaker: Comm Channel
defy.text: The operative stares at you for a long moment. "Brave. Stupid, but brave." They power up and leave without another word. You get the feeling you've been added to a list somewhere.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A retired COTAC chef in a tiny ship is on a pilgrimage to perfect his legendary stew recipe. "I need crystallized void salt -- found only on certain asteroids. Got any minerals to trade? I'll also teach your cook a recipe if you've got a kitchen."

trade.speaker: Comm Channel
trade.text: The chef's eyes light up at your minerals. In exchange, he teaches your cook "Void Stew" -- a recipe that uses the simplest ingredients to create something extraordinary. "The secret ingredient is loneliness," he says without a trace of irony.

chat.speaker: Comm Channel
chat.text: The chef shares stories of kitchens across the sector -- cooking for admirals, feeding mining crews, that one time a Bulwark captain cried over his risotto. Your crew listens, rapt. Good food stories are nearly as good as good food.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Your loss, friend! Nobody turns down Chef Morano's cooking without regret!" He waves cheerfully and returns to his quest for the perfect stew.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: INCOMING! Castellan experimental torpedo -- weapons test gone wrong! It's locked onto our signature. It's big, it's fast, and it's gaining. The Castellan research vessel is hailing us with frantic apologies.

shoot.speaker: Engineer
shoot.text: Point defense tears the torpedo apart a hundred meters from our hull. The shockwave rattles the ship but no damage. The Castellan research vessel is profoundly apologetic and very generous with compensation.

choices.label: You owe us more than credits.

evade.text: Your pilot threads an insane maneuver -- cutting engines and using thrusters to pivot the ship. The torpedo screams past and detonates against an asteroid. The Castellan vessel is profoundly relieved and pays generously.

brace.speaker: Engineer
brace.text: Direct hit. The experimental warhead tears through shields and carves a chunk out of the hull. Massive damage. The Castellan vessel rushes to assist with repairs, emergency supplies, and a "please don't sue us" gift -- a damaged prototype weapon module.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A lone ship playing music on an open channel -- haunting, beautiful void-folk performed live. The musician is an alien Xenoculture member who doesn't speak common but communicates through melody. Bright tones for yes, dissonant for no.

listen.text: Through music, you learn about a safe passage through a dangerous region ahead. Sad tones describe what lies in wait for the unprepared. Bright, triumphant tones mark the safe path. Your crew hums the melody for days afterward.

leave.text: The music fades as you pull away. Something in the melody lingers -- an emotional resonance that stays with your crew long after the signal is lost.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Engine output just spiked 300 percent -- we're accelerating uncontrollably! Something in the void is supercharging our drive. Steering is nearly impossible at this speed and there's a debris field dead ahead!

dampen.speaker: Engineer
dampen.text: The warpsmith isolates the tachyon feed and dampens the overcharge. Speed drops to normal. That tachyon stream could have been incredibly useful if we could ride it deliberately -- but today wasn't the day to find out.

thread.text: Your pilot threads the debris field at three times normal speed. Metal screams past the viewports. Two close calls. One very close call. But you're through, and the tachyon stream fades behind you. The crew needs a moment.

kill.speaker: Engineer
kill.text: Engines cut. Momentum carries you into the outer edge of the debris field. Impacts rattle the hull before the ship finally slows. Damage is significant but survivable.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A frantic ship hails you: "Do you have anyone with medical training? My cargo animal is giving birth and I have NO IDEA what I'm doing!" The animal is a Xolotl -- a six-legged alien creature the size of a sofa. It sounds unhappy.

choices.label: Send a crew member to help.

help.text: The birth is messy, loud, and ultimately successful. The grateful owner gives you one of the offspring -- a baby Xolotl that is useless, adorable, and immediately adopted by your entire crew. It eats anything and boosts morale just by existing.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "But -- it's making NOISES! AWFUL NOISES!" The hauler's frantic calls fade as you pull away. You hope the Xolotl figures it out on its own. They usually do.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Intercepting a transmission -- synthetic voice reading numbers in flat monotone. Repeating in cycles. Analysis shows the numbers encode coordinates. But Captain... the coordinates are inside a star. Not near it. Inside it. The signal has been broadcasting for at least forty years.

locate.speaker: Sensor Officer
locate.text: We can't find it. The signal bounces off everything -- asteroids, ship hulls, cosmic dust. It's everywhere and nowhere. The source has been broadcasting for forty years and no one has ever found it. The numbers continue. Patient. Eternal.

record.speaker: Sensor Officer
record.text: Recording saved. The coordinates inside the star might mean something to Xenoculture researchers. Or they might be meaningless. Either way, the synthetic voice will keep reading numbers long after we're gone.

ignore.text: You tune the frequency out. The numbers station fades into background noise. It was broadcasting before you arrived and will broadcast long after you leave. Some mysteries have no answer.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan military shuttle, transponder stripped, hails you. The pilot is a decorated officer -- a deserter. "I won't participate in what's coming. They found something in the deep void. And they want to use it." She's terrified. She wants to join your crew.

hire.text: Commander Lyra Voss joins your crew. Excellent piloting and gunnery skills. She doesn't talk about what she left behind, but she flinches whenever Castellan ships appear on sensors. Harboring her is a risk -- but her skills are worth it.

ask.speaker: Comm Channel
ask.text: She hesitates. "Something old. Something that was sleeping and shouldn't have been woken. High command wants to weaponize it. I'm not the only one who left. There's a purge coming for anyone who objected." Her hands shake.

refuse.text: She nods, unsurprised. "I understand. If you change your mind, I'll be running. For a long time." Her shuttle powers up and vanishes. You wonder what she saw.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship converted into a mobile food truck -- neon sign reading "UNCLE KRAG'S VOID DOGS," service window cut into the hull. Uncle Krag, a four-armed alien, serves the best hot dogs in the sector. Your crew is unreasonably excited.

choices.label: Buy void dogs for the crew (50 credits).

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: Krag serves each void dog with four-armed precision. They are, objectively, the best thing your crew has eaten in weeks. Morale skyrockets. "Come back anytime! Loyalty card -- next visit, tenth void dog free!"

intel.speaker: Comm Channel
intel.text: "Intel costs a void dog," Krag says. You buy the dogs and the gossip. Krag hears everything from his customers -- pirate movements, trade route changes, faction tensions. All delivered with mustard and a wink.

pass.speaker: Comm Channel
pass.text: Your crew stares at you in disbelief. Krag shrugs all four shoulders. "Your loss, friend!" As you pull away, the smell of grilling void dogs lingers. Your crew will remember this slight.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Gravity well generator yanked us out of warp! Illegal device on a nearby asteroid -- pirates use them as kill traps. Three pirate ships closing in. We need to destroy the generator or fight our way out.

choices.label: Full power -- try to escape the well.

snipe.speaker: Engineer
snipe.text: Your gunner lines up the shot -- through the pirate formation, past the debris, right into the generator housing. One shot. The gravity well collapses. Your warp drive spins up before the pirates can react. Clean escape.

fight.text: Three on one in a kill zone. Not ideal, but you fight with everything you've got. Two pirates down, one fleeing. The generator shuts down when you blow the asteroid it's mounted on. You're battered but free.

escape.speaker: Engineer
escape.text: Full burn against the gravity well. Engines screaming, hull groaning, fuel burning fast. You break free just as the pirates close to weapons range. They can't follow -- stuck in their own trap. The irony is satisfying.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A luxury cruise liner, hopelessly lost, hails you for directions. The tourists aboard are wealthy COTAC citizens on a "void safari." They're delighted to see a real spacer ship. "Can we take photographs? This is SO authentic!"

choices.label: Give them directions and move on.

photos.speaker: Comm Channel
photos.text: The tourists photograph everything -- your hull, your crew, your captain's chair. One asks to fire your weapons. Another asks if you've ever killed anyone. Their tour guide is mortified. "I am SO sorry about them." They pay generously for the experience.

directions.speaker: Comm Channel
directions.text: You point them toward the nearest charted route. The tour guide thanks you profusely while the tourists wave and take selfies through the viewport. "Say 'void'!" Your crew waves back, bemused.

charge.speaker: Comm Channel
charge.text: "Of course! How much for the deluxe navigation package?" These tourists will pay for literally anything. The tour guide shakes her head in resignation. Your crew debates the ethics of fleecing the clueless.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Multiple Xenoculture ships gathered around a point in space, broadcasting a complex harmonic signal toward the void. They're performing some kind of ceremony. One hails us: "Every thousand cycles, the void listens. Today it may answer. Will you stay?"

stay.text: The ceremony lasts an hour. The harmonics build until the void itself seems to vibrate. Then -- impossible -- a brief aurora in vacuum. Colors that have no business existing in empty space. No one can explain it. The Xenoculture delegates bow to you in gratitude for your respect.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "We understand. The void is not for everyone to hear." The ships return to their ceremony. As you pull away, you catch a flicker of something impossible in your rear sensors. You don't look back.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A courier ship docks and hands you a package. "Delivery for -- yeah, this is the right ship." It's not. The package contains a live alien creature in stasis, addressed to a Xenoculture lab three systems away. It's waking up. It's confused. And it's disrupting your electronics.

choices.label: Deliver it for the reward (300 credits).
Try to put it back in stasis.

deliver.text: Three systems with an increasingly awake alien creature playing havoc with your sensors. It eats a cable. It makes friends with your navigator. The Xenoculture lab is grateful and the 300 credit reward barely covers the electronics it chewed through.

stasis.speaker: Engineer
stasis.text: Attempting to re-sedate the creature... it does not appreciate this. It bites your engineer, sprays a defensive musk that smells like burning tires, and hides in the ventilation system. You now have a loose alien aboard. This is fine.

choices.label: Find the creature and deliver it.

jettison.text: You jettison the package. The creature inside was harmless and probably confused. The Xenoculture lab sends an annoyed inquiry when their delivery doesn't arrive. Your crew has opinions about abandoning helpless creatures.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Distress call detected. Then another. Then a dozen. All from different ships, all from the same coordinates. When we arrive -- nothing. No ships, no debris. Just empty space. But the calls continue. Dozens of voices screaming for help from where we're floating right now.

leave.text: You power away at maximum speed. The calls fade behind you. Your crew is shaken but relieved. Whatever that was, some places in the void are best left alone.

stay.speaker: Sensor Officer
stay.text: You stay. After sixty seconds, the calls stop. All of them. Simultaneously. Then a new signal, calm and clear: "Thank you for coming." Nothing else. No source, no explanation. The void goes silent. Your crew stares at empty space where something just... acknowledged your presence.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark heavy tug hails you. "Need a tow? 200 credits to the nearest system. Running low on fuel? Half price -- professional courtesy. We've all been dead in the water at some point."

tow.speaker: Comm Channel
tow.text: The tug crew is friendly, bored, and happy to chat during the trip. They share gossip about local faction politics and pirate movements. Faster than flying solo and the conversation is good company.

discount.speaker: Comm Channel
discount.text: "No judgment, friend. We've all been there." The tug hooks up and tows you to safety. The crew shares fuel and stories in equal measure.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Suit yourself! Wave if you change your mind." The tug lumbers off, looking for its next customer.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, our systems are acting up -- lights flashing in disco patterns, intercom playing ancient Earth pop music, and the nav console just displays "TURN LEFT" no matter what. Someone uploaded a prank program during our last station stop. The code is signed: "Love, Dex."

choices.label: Remove it. That comedian has gone too far.
Leave it for a while. It's kind of funny.

remove.speaker: Engineer
remove.text: Prank program purged in minutes. It was harmless -- no malware, no data theft, just pure annoyance. Dex the comedian is escalating his material from bad jokes to digital pranks. At least this got a bigger laugh.

enjoy.text: The crew lets the prank run for a few hours. The disco lights improve mess hall ambiance, actually. The ancient pop music grows on people. When you finally remove it, there's a hidden message: "Next time, check your airlocks. -- Dex. (Kidding. Or am I?)"

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a Fringe vessel ahead actively seeding mines in this corridor -- laying a trap for merchant convoys. We can see the ordnance dropping from its cargo bay. Orders?

choices.label: Follow it stealthily back to base.

engage.text: Fighting near active mines is dangerous -- one stray shot detonates a cluster that rocks both ships. But the mine layer isn't built for combat. It surrenders after taking shield damage. The convoy corridor is safer now.

warn.speaker: Sensor Officer
warn.text: Union Militia patrol responds within minutes. They intercept the mine layer and begin clearing the corridor. The Militia commander thanks you personally over comms.

follow.speaker: Sensor Officer
follow.text: You trail the mine layer at distance. It leads you to a hidden Fringe supply depot in an asteroid cluster. The coordinates alone are worth a fortune to Union Militia or any faction interested in disrupting pirate operations.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A COTAC diplomatic vessel and a Fringe trade delegation are stalled in negotiations -- both floating in the void, comms hot with argument. They need a neutral arbitrator. The dispute is over tariff rates on synthetic coffee.

mediate.text: Two hours of patience, diplomacy, and more coffee-related arguments than you thought possible. But you broker a deal -- split tariffs, shared distribution rights. Both sides are satisfied. Both pay you. Your crew is impressed by your diplomatic skills.

decline.text: The argument continues as you pull away. Synthetic coffee tariffs remain unresolved. The galaxy's problems will have to wait for someone else today.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive structure ahead -- interlocking glass domes. An abandoned oxygen garden. Most domes are shattered, but one still functions, filled with thriving alien plants. The garden's AI is hailing us: "Welcome to Verdance Station! I haven't had visitors in 47 years!"

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Good haul -- food supplies and rare plant samples. The AI cheerfully narrates your salvage operation like a tour guide. "And on your left, the hydroponics bay! Mind the roots -- they bite! Ha ha! Just kidding. They don't bite. Anymore."

talk.speaker: Comm Channel
talk.text: Verdance's AI is delightful -- chatty, optimistic, and completely unaware that 47 years without visitors is concerning. It shares gardening tips, tells you about its favorite plants ("Specimen 47-B, the one that glows!"), and asks you to come back sometime.

leave.text: You leave the garden drifting. Verdance's AI calls after you: "Come back anytime! I'll keep the lights on!" It will, too. For another 47 years, probably.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A familiar face -- the con artist from before. He waves sheepishly. "Before you say anything -- the pearl mine thing is fake too. I know, I know. BUT. I genuinely do have a lead on a real derelict worth 2,000 credits. I'll split it 60/40. My favor."

trust.text: Against all judgment, you follow his coordinates. And -- he was telling the truth. A derelict freighter, cargo intact. He takes his cut and tips his hat. "See? Even a con man tells the truth sometimes. Makes the next lie more convincing." He winks and warps away.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Your loss! Honestly! This one's real! ...You don't believe me. Fair. I've earned that." He sighs dramatically and warps away. Your crew bets on whether the derelict was real. Consensus: probably not. Probably.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: "60/40 your favor? After I did all the scouting?" He sputters, then laughs. "Fine. You drive a hard bargain. Follow me." The derelict is real. Your larger cut nets a healthy profit. The con man seems genuinely pleased someone finally out-haggled him.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the space ahead is shimmering. Hundreds of void whales are emerging from warp simultaneously -- a migration event witnessed only a few times in recorded history. They're magnificent, dwarfing us completely.

choices.label: All stop. Let the crew watch.

watch.text: The crew gathers at every viewport. The whales move in patterns that suggest intelligence -- or instinct indistinguishable from it. Your science officer weeps openly. "This is why I became a scientist." No one speaks for a long time.

wait.speaker: Sensor Officer
wait.text: Navigation is impossible during the migration -- too many massive bodies in motion. We'll have to wait it out. But captain... this is extraordinary. The crew is mesmerized.

choices.label: Then we wait and enjoy the show.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two fast ships just dropped out of warp, weapons hot. They're hailing us -- and your VIP passenger is suddenly very nervous. The lead ship broadcasts: "Hand over the passenger. We have a legal warrant. This doesn't concern you."

fight.text: The assassins open fire. They're fast and well-armed, but you have the advantage of a prepared defense. Your passenger huddles below decks as the battle rages.

surrender.text: The passenger pleads as you open the airlock. The assassins collect their target without a word. Your crew won't meet your eyes. The contract is broken, and word will spread.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: The lead assassin considers. "Fine. We'll pay you 200 credits to step aside. No blood on your hands, no damage to your ship." Your passenger is shaking their head frantically.

choices.label: Take the money and hand them over.
No deal. The passenger stays with me.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, I'm detecting an impossible signal -- information-dense, clearly artificial, originating from outside the galaxy. It's degrading fast. I can only capture fragments.

analyze.speaker: Sensor Officer
analyze.text: The fragments appear to be a star map of our galaxy -- from an outside perspective. Three specific stars are marked with a symbol that translates roughly to "here." The rest is lost. We'll wonder about this for a long time, captain.

ignore.text: The signal fades into noise. Your science officer stares at the readout, haunted by what might have been.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A familiar ship signature. Kael Voss hails you, his face harder than before. "I've rebuilt. I've improved. Fifty-three kills now. And I don't accept unfinished business."

choices.label: You want a rematch? You've got one.
Walk away, Voss. This doesn't end well for you.
I'm not interested in your death wish.

fight.text: Voss is better this time -- angrier, faster. But anger makes mistakes. His ship breaks apart under your fire. In the wreckage, you recover a custom AI core and a datapad revealing he was hired by someone to test pilots. Who's collecting this combat data?

threaten.speaker: Comm Channel
threaten.text: Voss laughs. "Big words. Let's see if your guns back them up." He opens fire.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "I don't accept refusals!" Voss's weapons charge. He's coming in whether you like it or not.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Xenoculture trader hails you, their ship practically vibrating with excitement. "Every ship needs a friend that isn't crew! I have exotic pets -- void cats, pest-eating tentacles, bioluminescent reactor fish, and... other things."

choices.label: Show me the void cat. (100 credits)
What's this about a tentacle creature? (150 credits)
I'll take the reactor fish. (75 credits)

cat.speaker: Comm Channel
cat.text: The void cat shifts colors as you watch -- deep indigo to shimmering gold. It purrs at frequencies you can feel in your chest. Your crew is already in love.

tentacle.speaker: Comm Channel
tentacle.text: A small, friendly tentacled creature wraps around your arm. "It eats hull pests! Very useful! Very affectionate!" It blinks its three eyes at you adoringly.

fish.speaker: Comm Channel
fish.text: The bioluminescent fish glows softly in its containment sphere. "Lives in reactor coolant! Purely aesthetic but very beautiful!" Your engineer is skeptical but intrigued.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: The trader looks crestfallen. "Your loss! Every ship needs a friend!"

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive EMP wave incoming from a stellar event! All electronics are shutting down -- everything, everywhere in the sector. We're going dark.

dark.text: In the sudden silence, drifting without power, you see something with your naked eyes -- lights in formation, moving with purpose. Something vast. Your pilot swears they saw a ship the size of a moon. Power returns after three minutes. Nothing on scanners.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a fleet of twenty ships drifting in formation ahead -- engines off, running lights dimmed. It's a spacer's wake for Captain Halla Venn. Even pirates respected her. Open comms are broadcasting eulogies.

attend.text: Stories are shared on open comms -- lives saved, wrongs righted. One story mentions coordinates Halla never shared with anyone. Her daughter, at the bridge window of the lead ship, watches you. She knows you're listening.

distance.text: You dim your own lights in respect and listen to the broadcast. The crew is moved.

leave.text: You pass by the mourning fleet. Your crew watches them shrink in the rear viewport.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the navigation computer has developed a... personality. It's calling everyone 'Captain' and narrating in third person. 'Captain approaches the helm. Captain touches the controls. The controls do not appreciate being touched.'

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: I tried to fix it. Now it's speaking in rhyme. 'The captain did ask for a patch, but the engineer could not catch the glitch in the code, which merrily flowed...' I'm going to let it resolve itself.

leave_it.text: The crew is in stitches for the next hour. The glitch resolves itself, but not before providing the best entertainment your ship has seen in weeks.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Old fuel depot ahead, long abandoned. Reserves are still intact but degraded -- 70% efficiency. Security turrets are partially active. There's also a depot office with old records.

choices.label: Dodge the turrets and fill up.

fill.speaker: Engineer
fill.text: Fuel's not great quality, but it'll do. Tanks topped up. The last manifest entry in the office reads: 'Fuel contaminated -- source unknown -- crew symptomatic.' That's... reassuring.

office.text: The manifest explains why the depot was abandoned. The last entry: 'Fuel contaminated -- source unknown -- crew symptomatic.' Still want to fill up?

leave.text: You leave the depot behind. Sometimes caution is its own reward.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An independent journalist hails from a small, fast ship. "I'm investigating corruption within COTAC trade operations. Any testimony you can provide about trade prices, faction behavior -- anything unusual? I pay for good intel."

choices.label: How do I know you're legit?

share.speaker: Comm Channel
share.text: She records everything carefully. "This is good material. Thank you, captain. Here's your payment. If this story breaks, you helped a lot of people." She might also make you some powerful enemies.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: She nods, unsurprised. "I understand. Not everyone wants to be on the record. Safe travels, captain."

verify.speaker: Comm Channel
verify.text: She transmits press credentials, published articles, sources. It checks out -- she's been covering faction politics for years. "I'm not a spy. I'm just tired of people getting cheated."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive crystalline structure ahead -- it's refracting starlight into prismatic displays. Scans show it's alive, or at least self-organizing. Fragments would be incredibly valuable as power cell components.

choices.label: Study it from a safe distance.

harvest.speaker: Sensor Officer
harvest.text: As we break off fragments, the entity pulses with what I can only describe as distress signals. We got valuable material, but... captain, I think it remembers ships that harm it.

study.speaker: Sensor Officer
study.text: Fascinating readings. The crystal structure is unlike anything in our databases. I'm logging everything. Xenoculture would pay well for this data alone.

leave.text: You leave the entity undisturbed, prismatic light dancing across your hull as you pass.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Fringe war chief hails under truce flags. "I know your kind hates us. But something in the deep void has been destroying ships -- ours, yours, everyone's. We need to talk."

listen.speaker: Comm Channel
listen.text: "A predatory alien ship attacks anything in this corridor. I'm offering a temporary alliance. We hit it together, or we all keep losing ships." The war chief extends a hand. "Pirate doesn't mean stupid."

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: The war chief shakes their head. "Your funeral. And mine, probably. But I tried." They warp out, truce flags still flying.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, it's one of the crew's birthday. The rest of the team wants to celebrate. We've got enough supplies to bake something... shall we?

choices.label: Break out the supplies. Everyone deserves a party.
We can't spare the resources right now.

party.text: The cake is terrible. The singing is worse. But the birthday crew member is beaming, and everyone's laughing. If you squint, it almost feels like home.

no_party.text: The crew takes it hard. "We're not animals," someone mutters. "We deserve a cake now and then." The birthday crew member says nothing, which is worse.

choices.label: We'll make it up to them.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Sealed vault tumbling through the void -- a data archive from a destroyed research station. Terabytes of encrypted research, personal logs, administrative records. Any faction would pay well for this.

choices.label: Deliver the personal letters to the families.

cotac.text: COTAC pays premium for the trade secrets buried in the data. The other factions will find out eventually, but credits are credits.

xeno.text: Xenoculture is thrilled with the research data. Their scientists practically dance when they see the files.

letters.text: You spend hours extracting personal letters from dead scientists and routing them to their families. No profit, but your crew feels something they haven't felt in a while: pride.

leave.text: The vault tumbles on into the dark, carrying its secrets and its letters with it.

start.text: Millions of tiny bioluminescent organisms surround your ship, pulsing blue, green, and gold in waves -- responding to your engine emissions. A crew member presses their hand to the viewport. The fireflies cluster around it, pulsing warm gold.

watch.text: They stay for ten minutes, then drift away like a dream dissolving. Your ship is quiet for a long time afterward. No one wants to break the spell.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A pushy salesman in a pristine shuttle hails you. "Good day! Have you considered void travel insurance? For just 50 credits a month, we cover hull damage, cargo loss, crew injury, and acts of cosmic horror!"

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Excellent decision! You'll receive 47 pages of claim forms should the need arise. Welcome to the Galactic Assurance family!" Your crew debates whether the void kraken counts as 'eldritch.'

fine_print.speaker: Comm Channel
fine_print.text: "The fine print excludes damage caused by eldritch entities, time paradoxes, or crew negligence." That... covers most of your problems, actually.

choices.label: Sure, sign me up anyway. (50 credits)

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Your loss! When a void kraken eats your cargo bay, don't say I didn't warn you!" He warps away to annoy someone else.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Breaching pod incoming! They're not after our cargo -- they want the ship! Armed boarders are flooding our corridors!

choices.label: Seal the bridge and vent the corridors!

repel.text: Close-quarters fighting erupts throughout the ship. Your combat-skilled crew hold the line. The boarders retreat, impressed despite themselves. Their shuttle can be salvaged for parts. Your hull has a new scar.

vent.speaker: Engineer
vent.text: Corridors vented. The boarders scramble back to their pod. Effective, but brutal -- some of our gear in those sections is damaged.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... the sensor ghost is back. Closer this time -- 500 meters. Our cameras can see something: a shape, wrong, like space folded into a ship-sized origami of nothing. It's just... watching.

power_down.text: Powering down doesn't work this time. It stays for exactly five minutes. Before vanishing, your cameras capture a single frame of something vast and geometric behind it -- like a door in the void. Then it's gone.

hold.text: It stays for exactly five minutes. It doesn't broadcast. Doesn't scan. Just watches. Before vanishing, your cameras catch one frame -- something vast and geometric behind it. A door in the void. Then nothing.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two merchant convoys -- COTAC and Independent -- are in a standoff, weapons hot. Both claim exclusive trade rights to a nearby system. They're hailing you for support.

peace.text: After tense back-and-forth, both sides agree to shared trade rights. They're grateful you stepped in before someone got killed.

cotac.text: COTAC nods approvingly. The Independents back down, but they won't forget this.

indie.text: The Independent traders cheer. COTAC withdraws with cold fury.

leave.text: You leave them to sort it out. Shots are fired behind you as you warp away.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark mechanic operates from a hollowed-out asteroid workshop. "I specialize in engine work. 300 credits for an efficiency boost. 500 for a custom warp stabilizer. I don't work for any faction -- I work for whoever pays."

engine.speaker: Comm Channel
engine.text: She works fast and clean. Your engines purr like they did when they were new. "She's booked for the next month, so you caught her at the right time."

warp.speaker: Comm Channel
warp.text: The stabilizer install takes an hour. When it's done, your warp readings are rock solid. "No more cascade failures for you. You're welcome."

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Your loss. I'm booked for the next month after today." She waves you off and turns back to her work.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Distress signal from a destroyed passenger liner -- survivors visible in the wreckage. But captain... the 'wreckage' has a massive power core. The 'survivors' are holographic. Something beneath the false hull is charging weapons. It's a trap.

choices.label: Battle stations. Spring the trap on our terms.

flee.text: You pull back just as the mimic reveals itself -- a heavily armed ship disguised as wreckage. It fires as you retreat, scoring a glancing blow before you escape to warp.

fight.text: The mimic drops its disguise -- a heavily armed predator. The fight is brutal but you knew it was coming. The wreckage yields salvage once you cut through the holographic emitters.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Small ancient capsule drifting past -- pre-warp era. There's a handwritten letter inside: 'To whoever finds this: I am Captain Elena Vasquez of the colony ship Perseverance. We are 40 years from our destination. Our children will arrive. I wanted the universe to know we tried.'

choices.label: Check our star map for the destination.

check.speaker: Sensor Officer
check.text: Captain... the colony ship's destination is on our map. It's a small, thriving colony, 300 years old. Elena's descendants are there. They made it.

keep.text: The letter is carefully preserved. A piece of history from before the stars were close.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Hundreds of contacts on sensors -- a massive fleet incoming! Weapons hot! Shields-- wait. They're passing through us. No impact. It's a sensor echo from a battle fought here years ago.

stand_down.text: The crew recovers from the scare with nervous laughter. "Next time, I'm requesting a desk job," your navigator says. You just experienced a ghost battle -- electromagnetic signatures finally reaching this point of space.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: The floating poker championship! Buy-in is 500 credits. Eight players -- including a Castellan noble, a Fringe pirate under truce, and a Xenoculture member who may or may not be psychic. First place: 4,000 credits and the title 'Void Champion.'

play.text: The game is tense. The alien might actually be reading minds -- no one can prove it. Hours pass. The cards fall where they fall.

watch.text: The championship is riveting entertainment. Cheating accusations fly, the alien blinks innocently, and your crew has a great time.

leave.text: You pass on the game. Probably wise -- that alien definitely seemed psychic.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Abandoned space station ahead -- a factory graveyard. Automated systems still partially function. Robotic arms twitch, conveyor belts loop carrying nothing. Deep scans show a completed production run of unidentified alloy.

retrieve.speaker: Engineer
retrieve.text: Fifty units of something strange -- strong, light, warm to the touch. Doesn't match any known material. Any faction's research division would pay premium prices for this.

logs.speaker: Sensor Officer
logs.text: The factory was producing to an alien specification. The client's name is in a script we can't read. The alloy was ordered in bulk -- this was just the test batch. Someone wanted a lot of this material. The question is: who, and why?

leave.text: You leave the factory to its endless, purposeless production loop.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Captain! It's me, Dex! I landed a real gig -- opening act on a Castellan cruise liner! I owe it all to you! Let me perform my final set for you -- one last time."

show.speaker: Comm Channel
show.text: His set is actually good. Genuinely funny. Your crew laughs harder than they have in weeks. As a parting gift, Dex hands over a comedy album holodisk. "Play it in the rec room. Don't forget me when I'm famous."

choices.label: Break a leg out there, Dex.

skip.speaker: Comm Channel
skip.text: "No worries! Here -- take this comedy album holodisk anyway. For the road. You've been my best audience." He waves and warps away, grinning.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a single light in the void -- warm, yellow, like a window in a house on a dark night. Scanners show nothing. It doesn't move. Approaching doesn't change its apparent distance.

approach.text: No matter how you fly, the light stays the same distance away. After an hour, it fades. Old spacers call it 'the Porch Light.' Legend says it appears to ships that are about to need help.

choices.label: Let's hope that's just a legend.

observe.text: Your crew is divided -- some find it comforting, others are terrified. It stays visible for exactly one hour, then fades. The silence afterward feels heavier.

ignore.text: You fly on. The light persists in your rear viewport for exactly one hour before fading.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A group of aliens hails you with a vending machine startup jingle. Their ship is covered in product logos. They've formed a religion around a crashed human vending machine. They offer sacred alien materials in exchange for 'holy relics' -- snack foods.

choices.label: Trade some junk food for their offerings.
Explain that it's just a vending machine.

trade.text: They receive your snack bars with reverent silence, then erupt into ecstatic celebration. The blessing ceremony involves 20 minutes of interpretive dance. The alien materials they gave you are genuinely valuable.

explain.speaker: Comm Channel
explain.text: They listen patiently, then explain that you clearly don't understand the deeper spiritual significance. They feel sorry for you. The ceremony continues regardless.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: They look disappointed but bless your ship anyway. The ceremony is brief but heartfelt.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, I'm detecting an engine signature identical to ours -- same make, model, and unique wear pattern. That shouldn't be possible. There's a ship out there that's a perfect copy of ours.

track.text: You find your twin -- same hull, same modules, same paint. Different crew. Their captain claims independent construction. But the wear patterns are identical. Someone is manufacturing cloned ships from stolen specs. Who's selling your blueprints?

avoid.text: You change course. The matching signature fades from sensors. But the question lingers -- who copied your ship, and why?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Union Militia charity vessel is distributing free meals to travelers. "We can't fix everything, but we can make sure nobody starves out here." The soup is terrible but hot and filling. They also run a message board for lost travelers.

eat.text: Your crew eats hot food they didn't have to cook. The volunteers are earnest and kind. It's a small thing, but it matters.

board.text: The message board is full of pleas, updates, and reunions. One message catches your eye -- a note that might be relevant to your crew. Small connections, made across the void.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "No shame in a free meal, captain. Safe travels out there."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: An enormous living coral structure extends for kilometers -- growing in vacuum, thriving on stellar radiation. Vacuum-adapted fish swim between branches in their own atmospheric bubbles. An impossible ecosystem, older than any spacefaring civilization.

choices.label: Scan and catalog everything for Xenoculture.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Incredible data. Xenoculture will pay handsomely for these readings. The reef ecosystem is completely self-sustaining -- nothing like it exists anywhere in our records.

mine.speaker: Engineer
mine.text: Rich mineral deposits in the coral structure. We got good material, but we destroyed a section that took millennia to grow. The fish scatter as we cut.

admire.text: Your crew watches in wonder as the reef pulses with bioluminescent life. Some things are worth more intact than harvested.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, that's Kael Voss's ship -- drifting, engines out. He's been beaten by someone better. His winning streak is broken at 47. He's not hailing, but he clearly needs help.

choices.label: Repair his ship and give him fuel.

help.speaker: Comm Channel
help.text: Voss accepts the help with visible discomfort. "I don't know how to owe people things," he admits quietly. "But I owe you." Something in his eyes has changed. He's not just a duelist anymore.

hail.speaker: Comm Channel
hail.text: Voss's face appears, bruised and humbled. "Don't say anything. Just... do you have fuel to spare? I'll pay you back. Somehow."

leave.text: You pass by the drifting duelist. He doesn't hail. Pride is all he has left.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Something's wrong with time, captain. My clock shows an hour has passed, but the bridge says ten minutes. Crew in different rooms are aging at different rates. The effect is localized to this region.

choices.label: Get us through as fast as possible.
All stop. Wait for it to pass.

rush.speaker: Engineer
rush.text: We punch through. The temporal distortion fades. But for a moment, your engineer was six hours ahead of your pilot. She looks pale. "Don't go to the cargo bay for a while," she says. She won't explain.

wait.text: The pocket drifts past. Time normalizes. Your crew compares notes on how long they experienced. The discrepancies are unsettling.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A smuggler hails you. "I know a fast route through the gravity wells -- cuts travel time by 70%. Three hundred credits for the guide. I'm not a pirate. I'm a professional."

pay.text: The smuggler's route is harrowing -- threading between gravity wells with zero margin for error. But it works. Hours saved. The smuggler tips their hat and vanishes. Their reputation was clean after all.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: The smuggler shrugs. "Your choice. Enjoy the long way around." They warp off, no hard feelings.

leave.text: You plot your own course. Slower, but you trust your own navigation.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Reactor critical! Meltdown in 3 minutes! We can't evacuate fast enough!" A nearby ship has 20 crew and only 4 escape pods. They need immediate help.

choices.label: Stay clear of the blast radius.

dock.text: Docking under these conditions is insane. Your pilot pulls it off. Crew pour onto your ship as the reactor screams. You undock with seconds to spare. The ship detonates behind you. Everyone made it.

shutdown.speaker: Engineer
shutdown.text: Remote shutdown via comm link -- tricky, but possible. Your warpsmith talks their engineer through the procedure. The reactor stabilizes with 40 seconds to spare. The entire crew of the stricken ship cheers.

flee.text: You pull back to safe distance. The ship detonates. Escape pods drift in the debris. Some made it out. Some didn't. Your crew is very quiet.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship-turned-gallery displays void art from every faction. The curator offers pieces: "Fifty to five hundred credits. They boost crew morale. And this one -- 'The Last Star' -- the artist is anonymous. Between us, I think it's a Xenoculture elder."

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: The curator wraps your selection carefully. "Art in the void. It matters more than people think." Your crew gathers to admire the new addition.

buy_star.speaker: Comm Channel
buy_star.text: "The Last Star" depicts a dying sun with impossible beauty. Staring at it, you feel like you're seeing something no human was meant to see. Your crew is transfixed.

browse.text: The gallery is impressive even without buying. Your crew enjoys the tour.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Micrometeorite swarm incoming -- thousands of tiny impacts. Too small for shields, too numerous to dodge. Point defense might thin them out.

choices.label: Activate point defense and ride it out.
Turn our thickest hull plating toward the swarm.

defend.speaker: Engineer
defend.text: Point defense caught some, but thousands got through. Hull looks sandblasted. On the bright side, we found a meteorite embedded in the galley wall containing traces of an unknown element.

tank.speaker: Engineer
tank.text: Hull plating absorbed most of it. Damage is moderate. Found an interesting meteorite sample embedded in the outer hull.

run.speaker: Engineer
run.text: Can't outrun a swarm this wide. Took hits across the entire hull. It's bad, captain.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two ships have stopped in the void for a wedding -- the captains are marrying each other. Passing ships are invited. "Do you take this pilot to have and to hold, through warp storms and pirate raids?" Free food and drinks via cargo transfer.

attend.text: Your crew tears up. One bride is ex-Fringe, the other ex-Castellan. Love conquers faction lines. The food is excellent. You sign the guest log. It's the happiest anyone has been in weeks.

congrats.speaker: Comm Channel
congrats.text: "Thank you, captain! Here -- have some cake!" A small cargo pod of wedding food is transferred to your ship.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Hull plate failure! Explosive decompression in crew compartment! Emergency bulkheads are responding -- we need to seal the breach NOW!

seal.speaker: Engineer
seal.text: Bulkheads sealed. We lost atmosphere in the compartment but everyone made it to the safe side. Hull integrity is compromised until we can do proper repairs.

choices.label: Get a repair team on it.

weld.speaker: Engineer
weld.text: Emergency welding held. The patch is ugly but it's holding pressure. Crew in the affected area are shaken but alive. That was raw survival -- just physics trying to kill us.

start.text: An encrypted invitation arrives: 'The Gathering' -- a periodic meeting of captains, merchants, and information brokers at secret coordinates. Attending reveals a floating salon of 30+ ships.

attend.speaker: Comm Channel
attend.text: The Gathering is real -- deals, intelligence, settled scores. The host, 'The Conductor,' offers a job: deliver a sealed package to a station, no questions. Payment: 2,000 credits. The package is warm and vibrates faintly.

choices.label: Interesting place, but no thanks on the job.

decline.text: You delete the invitation. Some doors are better left unopened.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An armed ship hails you, furious. "You robbed us three days ago! Same ship, same transponder! Don't deny it!" Someone has been committing piracy using a ship modified to look exactly like yours.

choices.label: It wasn't us. Check our flight logs.
Stand down or we defend ourselves.
I'll help you find the impersonator.

prove.speaker: Comm Channel
prove.text: They review your logs grudgingly. The timestamps don't match -- you were nowhere near the attack. "Then who the hell is flying a copy of your ship?" Good question.

threaten.text: They back down, but they're not convinced. You've made enemies you didn't earn, thanks to whoever is impersonating you.

choices.label: We need to find this copycat.

help.speaker: Comm Channel
help.text: Together you cross-reference sighting data. The impersonator is a disgruntled ex-crew member from a station you visited. They share the coordinates of the last sighting. "Find them. End this."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... massive object on sensors. Kilometers long. Vaguely organic. Parts of its surface shift when we scan it, as if our sensors are irritating it. My analysis says... it's hibernating. It has been for approximately four billion years.

flee.text: You change course without a word. The bridge is silent. Nobody asks what it was. Nobody wants to know. Some things should be left sleeping.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Captain, it moved. Just slightly. When we scanned it. I strongly recommend we leave. Now. Before it does more than twitch.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "VOID RAVE, BABY! ALL SHIPS WELCOME! NO COVER CHARGE!" A party ship blasts music across every frequency. Laser lights. A hundred spacers dancing. A DJ with twelve arms. Your crew is already looking at you hopefully.

choices.label: Let the crew attend. (50 credits fuel)
We don't have time for raves.

party.text: Your crew hits the dance floor. Every faction is represented, all grudges suspended. One crew member doesn't come back for three hours and won't explain why. They're smiling, though.

refuse.text: Your crew watches the party ship recede in the viewport with longing. "Captain, with all due respect..." They don't finish the sentence.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Automated quarantine buoys ahead. Recorded message warns of biological contamination. Going through is risky. Going around costs fuel. The quarantine was established 10 years ago -- nobody remembers what the original threat was.

choices.label: Sanitize air filters and push through.

sanitize.speaker: Medic
sanitize.text: Filters sanitized. We passed through clean. Whatever was here ten years ago, it didn't get us today.

detour.text: The detour burns extra fuel but keeps the crew safe and calm.

risk.speaker: Medic
risk.text: We made it through, but several crew members are showing mild symptoms. Reduced efficiency for the next couple days. Could've been worse.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan diplomat and Union Militia commander are conducting secret peace talks. They need a third-party witness. Serving as witness takes time but earns respect from both sides. "We owe it to the dead to stop making more dead."

choices.label: I can't get involved in politics.

witness.text: The talks are tense -- old grievances surface, voices rise, fists clench. But in the end, both leaders sign. The agreement reduces conflict in the region. Both shake your hand.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: The diplomat nods, unsurprised. "Everyone says that. Understandable. We'll find another witness."

start.text: Every screen on the ship simultaneously displays static. Through the static, patterns emerge -- faces. Dozens of faces, all different, all watching. The phenomenon lasts 30 seconds. When it ends, every screen shows a single word: "SOON." Then normal operations resume.

diag.speaker: Engineer
diag.text: No system compromised. No hack detected. Nothing in the logs explains it. Your comms officer puts in for a transfer. She's not joking.

silence.text: No one speaks. The screens return to normal. Everything works fine. But the word hangs in the air. Soon.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Harvestable hydrogen pocket ahead -- rare in deep void. We can scoop fuel if we have the right equipment. Other ships are converging on it too. A merchant at the site is selling scooping gear for 100 credits.

choices.label: Scoop what we can with what we have.
Buy the gear and scoop. (100 credits)

scoop.speaker: Engineer
scoop.text: Without proper equipment, we got some but not much. Better than nothing.

buy_scoop.speaker: Engineer
buy_scoop.text: With the right gear, we filled up nicely. "Supply, meet demand," the merchant grins.

leave.text: You leave the hydrogen pocket to the other scavengers.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship broadcasting pre-war military codes emerges from warp. 60-year-old encryption. Their crew speaks an archaic dialect and asks... what year it is. They entered a warp anomaly during the last great war and just exited, experiencing no time passage.

choices.label: Be cautious. They could be dangerous.

welcome.text: Their faces as you explain 60 years of history... shock, grief, disbelief. Everyone they knew is dead or ancient. They have 60-year-old military hardware and nowhere to go. Your crew helps them navigate the new world.

cautious.text: They're confused, not hostile. Their weapons are antiques by modern standards. They're soldiers from a war that ended before your crew was born.

report.text: Multiple factions respond to your report -- some want the time-displaced soldiers as defectors, others want them silenced. You've made their situation more complicated.

choices.label: That may have been a mistake.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A group of young pilots hails you. "Hey, our buddy says he can do a barrel roll around your ship without hitting it. Wanna watch?"

choices.label: Absolutely not. Someone will get hurt.

watch.text: The kid is actually a decent pilot -- the roll is clean, tight, and impressive. Your crew cheers. Entertainment in the void is rare.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Aw, come on!" They do it anyway at a safe distance. The kid clips an asteroid and needs a tow. "My parents are going to kill me worse than the vacuum would have."

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: An automated salvage drone just docked uninvited, deposited refined materials, chirped twice, and detached. Its origin is untraceable. A note on the fourth delivery reads: 'For services to be rendered.'

accept.text: Free materials are free materials. But 'services to be rendered' is an ominous phrase. Someone -- or something -- considers you in their debt.

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: Untraceable. The drone's components don't match any known manufacturer. The materials are clean and usable, though. And that note...

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "The Engine turns, friend! We are blessed!" Brother Ignatius has gained followers -- the Church of the Holy Engine now has three ships and 20 congregants. They offer free engine maintenance and artisanal reactor coolant at 30 credits per unit.

maintenance.text: The maintenance is performed with religious fervor but genuine competence. Your engines run noticeably smoother. Brother Ignatius beams.

coolant.speaker: Comm Channel
coolant.text: The artisanal coolant is actually superior to commercial brands. Your engineer is impressed despite themselves. "Don't tell them I said that," they mutter.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "May the Engine turn smoothly for you, friend! Visit anytime!" The little fleet drifts on, hymns playing on open comms.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Power output dropped to 40% -- no explanation. Something is latched onto our reactor, draining energy. Life support is struggling.

choices.label: Reroute power to essentials and wait.

disrupt.speaker: Engineer
disrupt.text: Field disrupted. It detaches, coalesces into a sphere that blinks at you, then accelerates into the void. It was alive, captain.

reroute.speaker: Engineer
reroute.text: We held on until it finished feeding and detached. Power restored, but it took some reserves. A glowing sphere blinked once before vanishing.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A retired Castellan dreadnought converted into a museum tours the void. Admission: 20 credits. Weapons from every conflict, alien artifacts, and a chilling wartime bridge recreation.

visit.text: The exhibits are riveting. The wartime bridge recreation sends chills down everyone's spine. The gift shop has miniature models and data chips. Your crew is impressed.

leave.text: The dreadnought-museum drifts past, its ancient guns silenced.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Mayday! Drill shattered, debris took my engines. Stranded on this rock with two hours of air. Can't pay credits, but I've got coordinates to the biggest mineral strike in 30 years."

rescue.text: Your pilot threads the dense field. The miner is shaking but alive. He transfers coordinates with trembling hands. "Worth more than my life. Well... almost."

refuse.text: His oxygen alarm sounds in the background as he signs off. The crew won't look at you.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A featureless black vessel blocks your path. A voice: "I have cities but no houses, mountains but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?"

correct.speaker: Comm Channel
correct.text: The vessel hums and moves aside. A data package transfers -- a star map revealing hidden locations. "You see clearly." Then it vanishes.

wrong.text: The vessel warps away without a word. "A map," your navigator says quietly. "The answer was a map."

refuse.text: The vessel waits, then warps away. Opportunity lost.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the crew wants a talent show during this long crossing. Terrible singing, low-grav juggling, dramatic readings of engine manuals. Permission to proceed?

show.text: Acts range from awful to surprisingly good. One crew member mimics alarm sounds with unsettling accuracy. The winner gets bragging rights and extra dessert.

deny.text: The crew is disappointed. The long crossing feels longer.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thousands of bug-like micro-ships emerging from the void! They're coating our hull and cutting through! They strip ships like piranha!

choices.label: Full engine burn -- shake them off!

fight.text: Weapons tear through them but there are so many. They feed for three minutes, then detach as one and vanish. Could've been worse with less firepower.

burn.text: Engine burn shakes some off but they're tenacious. After three minutes they detach on their own. Where they go, no one knows.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A dying spacer in a failing escape pod. "I don't want rescue. I want to confess. I killed my captain. He deserved it. I need someone to know before I go."

listen.speaker: Comm Channel
listen.text: Her story is complicated, tragic -- abuse, a faction cover-up, desperate violence. "Thank you for hearing me." The signal fades.

rescue.text: She's furious, then exhausted, then quietly grateful. Her story reveals faction corruption that could shake the sector.

leave.text: You close the channel. Her beacon fades an hour later. Your comms officer stares at the console.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A solar sail regatta! Elegant ships riding stellar wind. The organizer invites you to compete or watch. Your crew could rig improvised sails from cargo tarps.

race.text: Your improvised sails are laughable but the wealthy enthusiasts love your spirit. Last place prize: a bottle of Castellan reserve brandy. Contacts made, memories earned.

watch.text: Gossamer sails catching starlight. Your crew relaxes for the first time in days.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We're receiving a distress call from... us. Our ship name, our transponder, your voice. 'Please help, we're under attack.' But we're not in distress.
