investigate.text: Nothing at the coordinates. But ship logs show we DID send a distress call from here -- 16 hours from now. Time is not behaving.

ignore.text: You ignore the call. But the logs show a distress call scheduled to transmit from those coordinates in 16 hours. Nobody can explain it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Void whiskey! Distilled with cosmic radiation! Smooth, complex, technically illegal in three systems. Twenty credits a bottle. Made with love and a little radiation."

buy_one.text: The whiskey is surprisingly good. Your crew passes it around appreciatively.

buy_bulk.speaker: Comm Channel
buy_bulk.text: "Bulk discount! Smart!" Ten bottles, worth 50 credits each at the right station.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Your loss!" He toasts you with his own product and warps away.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Colossal ancient terraforming engine ahead. Powered down but intact. Control systems contain schematics worth a fortune. And something alive is dormant inside its core.

download.speaker: Sensor Officer
download.text: Schematics secured. The terraformer's last target was a planet that doesn't appear on modern maps.

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: Something biological curled in the core like a seed in a pod. Ancient. Patient. Our scans agitate it. I recommend we take the data and leave.

leave.text: You leave the ancient machine and its sleeping passenger to the void.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Toll road! Fifty credits! Perfectly legal! I declared this a sovereign nation!" A Fringe pilot blocks a corridor between two nebulae. Population: one.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: He gives you a hand-drawn passport stamp. "Welcome to the Sovereign Void Republic! Citizen number seven!"

challenge.speaker: Comm Channel
challenge.text: "DEPLOY THE NAVY!" A single armed drone wobbles out, held together with tape. It sparks and drifts sideways. "...The navy is undergoing maintenance. Pass freely."

detour.text: You navigate around the nebulae. Small fuel cost but saves the indignity.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Routine inspection found a small ecosystem in the cargo bay. Spilled nutrients plus void spores created a tiny alien garden. Mushrooms, tiny insects, maybe slime mold. Quartermaster wants it gone. Farmer wants to keep it.

choices.label: Keep it as a food supplement.

clean.text: Cargo bay sanitized. "Ships should not have ecosystems," the quartermaster insists.

keep.text: The farmer tends the garden. The mushrooms taste like chicken. Small food supplement, big morale boost.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: ISD recruiter vessel 'requests' a crew member for their labor fleet. Technically legal in ISD space -- which this isn't. "Just meeting quotas. You understand."

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Noted. We'll remember this." They warp out. The threat lingers.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Exemption granted. Pleasure doing business." Crew is relieved but angry at the shakedown.

jurisdiction.speaker: Comm Channel
jurisdiction.text: They check their star chart. Realize they're outside ISD space. "Apologies for the inconvenience." Quick exit, red-faced.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An elderly couple hails from a tiny ship. Final journey before retiring. "Fifty years in the void together. Just wanted to say hello to one more stranger."

stories.speaker: Comm Channel
stories.text: They share stories, trade tips, laugh at old memories. Then offer a module they no longer need. "Take it. We won't need it where we're going." Your crew is quiet afterward.

brief.speaker: Comm Channel
brief.text: "Fair winds, captain. Take care of your crew." They turn toward the colony world. Fifty years, ending quietly.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Flowers growing in vacuum. Hundreds, anchored to rock, colors shifting with starlight. No biology we can explain. Over 200 years old. The crew just stares.

harvest.speaker: Sensor Officer
harvest.text: It dies the moment we detach it. Colors fade to grey. Even dead, Xenoculture pays a fortune. The science crew is somber.

leave.text: Colors play across your hull -- gold, violet, deep blue. Nobody takes a single one. It feels right.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Pirates captured a Castellan ambassador. Ransom: 5,000 credits, broadcast openly. Three armed ships. Ambassador may die in crossfire if attacked.

attack.text: Fierce fighting. The ambassador survives -- barely. Castellan is deeply grateful.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: Pirates settle for 300 credits. Not noble, but the ambassador lives.

alert.text: Castellan military arrives in 20 minutes. Tense standoff forces pirates to flee. Ambassador is shaken but alive.

leave.text: You leave. The broadcast continues behind you.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Xenoculture cartographer maps void phenomena. Maps: 500 credits per sector. She buys nav data too. "The void isn't empty -- it's full of things we haven't learned to see."

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: The map reveals shortcuts, hazards, hidden points of interest. "Watch the eddies near sector 4."

sell.speaker: Comm Channel
sell.text: "Good routes. A few I haven't charted." She pays and integrates your data immediately.

leave.text: She returns to her charts without fuss.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Someone spray-painted our hull at the last station. 'WASH ME' in enormous letters. Plus a crude drawing of you with an unflattering nose.

choices.label: Send EVA crew to clean it.

clean.text: Hull scrubbed. Took an hour. They're still laughing about the drawing though.

keep.text: Every station, someone comments. Your crew loves the reactions. Ship legend born.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A wooden door floating in space. Brass handle. Frame but no walls. Through the keyhole -- warm golden light like a sunset. Sensors show nothing unusual.

open.text: Inside: a furnished room, fireplace burning. A chair. Something was sitting in it recently. The door closes. 30 agonizing seconds. It reopens. They're fine. But they won't talk about what they saw.

avoid.text: Warm light spills from its keyhole as you steer wide. It stays in the viewport until distance swallows it.

start.text: Automated ISD tax notice: 'Estimated liability: 847 credits. Remit within 30 days.' Your crew is offended. "We're between stars! No tax jurisdiction here!"

pay.text: Tax paid. Navigator mutters about revolution. ISD notes your compliance.

delete.text: Deleted. No consequences. Small victory. "This is what the revolution was about," your navigator says proudly.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Final transmission from a dying ship, too far to reach. The captain is calm: "If anyone hears this, we made it farther than we thought we would. Tell my family the stars were worth it." Silence.

log.text: You never learn the ship's name. Your pilot adjusts course slightly -- not toward anything. Just forward. Something about it felt important.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Renko here! Pre-war research vessel, mostly intact, contested space. Need backup. 60/40 split, your favor. You in?"

help.text: Fight off rivals alongside Renko. Enormous haul. She finds a sealed lab and goes quiet. "Sell this fast. Don't look at it." She's generous with the split.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Your call. Can't blame you." She signs off, disappointed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Dark nebula ahead. Absorbs all light. No stars visible inside. Your ship will be a bubble of light in absolute darkness.

push.text: Ten minutes in absolute dark. The void feels heavier. Some swear they see shapes beyond the lights. Then -- stars. You emerge blinking. Being born again. Morale rebounds.

detour.text: The long way around burns fuel. But your crew doesn't face the dark.

start.text: A signal on an unknown frequency -- broadcasting only to your ship. Coordinates deep beyond the star map. One sentence: "We've been watching. You're ready. Come find us." It knows your name.

save.text: Coordinates logged. The void stretches ahead. Whatever sent this is waiting. Wonderful or terrible -- depends on courage. Or foolishness.

delete.text: Signal deleted. But the words linger. They knew your name. They're still out there.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A rickety shuttle plastered with signs: 'GENUINE VOID -- BOTTLED FRESH.' The pilot offers mason jars of nothing for 50 credits each. "When the void runs out, you'll wish you'd stocked up!"

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: He throws in a jar of 'premium dark matter' -- visibly just a jar painted black. Your crew finds it hilarious. He salutes and vanishes into a warp tear that should not exist for a ship that small.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Your loss! Limited supply!" He warps away through a tear in space that absolutely should not exist for a ship that rickety.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Comms crackle on an unregistered frequency. A distorted voice: "You're listening to Channel 77, broadcasting from between dimensions. Next up: the heat death of the universe, brought to you by Quark's Discount Antimatter." Two minutes of unhinged space jazz follow.

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: No source signal traceable. But during the broadcast, we drifted exactly 77 meters off course. That's... specific.

enjoy.text: The jazz is actually pretty good. When it cuts out, your navigator reports you drifted exactly 77 meters off course during the broadcast.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three pirate corvettes hail you. The captain, wearing a beret and reading glasses: "Before we plunder your vessel, we must establish whether property is a valid construct. Discuss."

choices.label: Property is valid. These are my guns.
Property is an illusion. So is your plunder.

debate.speaker: Comm Channel
debate.text: You argue for two hours. The pirates concede your cargo belongs to you -- by the social contract, at least. They leave, intellectually satisfied. Your crew is baffled.

fight.text: They attack with 20% less aggression because "violence is also a construct, but rent is due." You fend them off. They retreat, debating amongst themselves.

counter.speaker: Comm Channel
counter.text: The captain's eyes widen. "A fellow nihilist! We cannot plunder what does not exist!" They leave, deeply impressed. You get a philosophical pass.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Frigate ahead -- no life support but full engine power. When we hail it, the viewscreen fills with cats. At least thirty. In tiny vacuum suits. One orange tabby paws at the comms: 'WE ARE FINE. DO NOT BOARD. SEND FISH.'

feed.text: They transmit coordinates to a hidden cache of rare minerals. The orange tabby appears to nod. Then all thirty cats stare at the camera simultaneously before cutting the feed.

board.text: Every airlock on their ship locks simultaneously. They boost away at impossible speed. The orange tabby's face fills your screen one last time. It does not look pleased.

leave.text: Your crew watches the cat frigate drift away with a mixture of confusion and delight.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Nearly hit a small asteroid painted pastel pink. One side reads 'YOU'RE DOING GREAT' in enormous letters. The other: 'Sponsored by the Fringe Collective Mental Health Initiative -- You Are Not Alone In The Void.'

accept.text: Your crew reads it. Nobody makes fun of it. The void is a lonely place. Sometimes a painted rock helps.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cathedral-like dreadnought blocks your path, covered in salvaged hull plating. The Drift Baron hails you -- gaunt, patchwork crown of circuit boards. "This is my void. The toll is one-tenth your cargo, or I take all of it plus your dignity."

choices.label: Challenge him to a game of chance.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: The Baron accepts with a magnanimous wave. "Wise. Travel safely through my domain." He remembers your compliance for future encounters.

fight.text: The Baron and his escorts open fire. It's a hard fight -- the cathedral-ship has serious armor. You push through, battered but free.

game.speaker: Comm Channel
game.text: The Baron grins. "A gambler! I like you!" He rolls dice. You roll higher. His expression is priceless. He pays YOU and mutters about 'statistical anomalies.'

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A single vending machine floating in the void. Connected to nothing, powered by nothing. Accepts credits. Menu: lukewarm coffee, mystery sandwich, or 'THE GOOD STUFF' for 200 credits. Plaque reads: 'Property of ISD Break Room 4C -- DO NOT REMOVE.'

coffee.text: The coffee is lukewarm and mediocre. Exactly what you'd expect from an interdimensional break room appliance.

sandwich.text: The sandwich is... edible. Your crew member who ate it seems fine. Mostly. They do look a bit green.

good_stuff.text: A module component drops into the dispensing tray. It's actually useful. How a vending machine floating in the void has module components is a question you choose not to ask.

leave.text: You leave the vending machine to its eternal vigil in the void.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Distress call from the ISS Harrow, requesting assistance. Problem: the Harrow was destroyed fourteen years ago. But the signal is real-time, and the voice responds to our hails. "Please hurry, they're cutting through the hull--"

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: Debris matches the Harrow. One functioning black box -- containing logs from a battle that hasn't happened yet. The dates are three months in our future. Captain, this data shouldn't exist.

leave.text: You leave the impossible signal to echo through time alone. Some answers are worse than questions.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two brightly painted shuttles in a slow-speed dogfight. 'VOID CONES' vs 'DEEP FREEZE DELIGHTS.' Both hail simultaneously demanding you pick a side.

choices.label: Mediate for a cut of both profits.

cones.speaker: Comm Channel
cones.text: "VOID CONES WINS! Free crate for our champion!" Deep Freeze retreats, vowing revenge. You now have a crate of excellent frozen goods.

freeze.speaker: Comm Channel
freeze.text: "DEEP FREEZE DELIGHTS PREVAILS!" Void Cones slinks away. Your prize: artisanal frozen delights.

mediate.text: You broker a merger. "VOID FREEZE CONE DELIGHTS" is born. Both vendors pay you a consulting fee and share samples.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict frigate, all lights on, no life signs. If we board -- every room is staffed by plastic mannequins in crew uniforms, posed at stations. Last log entry: 'The crew has never looked better.'

board.text: Mannequins at every station. One is warm to the touch. As you leave, rear camera shows one standing at the airlock window. Watching. Nothing else happens. But nothing needs to.

leave.text: You pass the lit-up frigate. Through the windows, you can see shapes at the stations. Still. Watching. You do not look back.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Have you mapped sector 7-G yet? Please say no. PLEASE say no. I've been working on it for six months." A frantic solo explorer named Stellan hails you.

choices.label: Share our map data. (He pays well.)

share.speaker: Comm Channel
share.text: He pays well but looks visibly crushed. "Six months..." He stares at his console. "Well. Data is data. Thanks, I guess."

lie.speaker: Comm Channel
lie.text: "YES! Still first! Thank you!" He's overjoyed, practically dancing in his chair. You get nothing but his gratitude.

collab.speaker: Comm Channel
collab.text: "Collaborate? I... could share unique POI locations you haven't found. You share sector data. We both win?" His eyes light up. He shares coordinates to hidden locations.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Gravity anomaly! A void eddy where spacetime curls like a whirlpool. Navigation just inverted. We can ride it out or fight through at full thrust.

ride.text: You emerge unharmed but displaced from your course. A strange resonance hums through the hull -- almost like singing. The crew listens until it fades.

fight.speaker: Engineer
fight.text: Fighting the eddy at full thrust keeps our heading but the hull takes strain. That singing resonance fills the ship -- louder at full power.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A garish neon ship drops out of warp playing a fanfare. Man in sequined jacket: "CONGRATULATIONS! You've been selected for VOID OR NO VOID! Pick a case!" Three holographic cases. One has 500 credits, one has a rare module, one has 'a modest explosion.'

case_a.speaker: Comm Channel
case_a.text: "Case one! Let's see what's inside!" A shower of credits transfers to your account. "WINNER! Come back anytime!"

case_b.speaker: Comm Channel
case_b.text: "Case two! And it's..." Useful components materialize in your cargo bay. "A FINE PRIZE! See you next time!"

case_c.speaker: Comm Channel
case_c.text: "Case three! And it's... oh dear." A small, mostly harmless explosion rocks your hull. "BETTER LUCK NEXT TIME!" He warps away quickly.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: He sadly packs up. "No one wants to play anymore..." He'll be back, though. He always comes back.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Cluster of transparent biodomes, no power. Inside, bioluminescent plants have gone wild -- vines pressing against glass, flowers blooming in near-vacuum cold. A Xenoculture research project abandoned decades ago.

harvest.text: Rare biological samples secured. Valuable as trade goods. Your farming crew are particularly affected: "I've never seen anything like this."

restore.speaker: Engineer
restore.text: Power restored to one dome. The plants respond immediately -- brighter, reaching toward the lights. It could serve as a waypoint for future travelers.

admire.text: Bioluminescent light plays through the glass. Life persisting where it shouldn't. Your crew watches in reverent silence.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Ship on sensors matching us exactly -- same hull, same modules, same transponder. When we hail, your face stares back. But the background is wrong -- darker, damaged. The mirror-you says: "Don't go to your destination. We went. This is what's left."

demand.text: The signal cuts. The ship vanishes from sensors. Gone. Your crew is deeply unsettled. If you proceed to your destination, nothing unusual happens. This time.

change.text: You alter course. Whether you avoided something terrible or just jumped at shadows, you'll never know. The mirror ship doesn't appear again.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A tiny habitat anchored to a dead comet. An elderly man has lived here 30 years, siphoning trace hydrogen. Fuel at 80% market rate, but he insists on telling a story per unit purchased. Claims to be a former COTAC admiral. COTAC records show no such person.

choices.label: Buy fuel and hear stories. (30 credits)

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: His stories are fascinating -- each reveals lore about a different star system. True or not, your crew is captivated. The fuel is good quality despite its source.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Everyone's in such a rush. The void isn't going anywhere." He waves and returns to his comet.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Distress signal received. When decoded, it contains another distress signal inside it. Which contains another. Seven layers deep. The innermost just says 'FOUND IT' and transmits coordinates to empty space.

choices.label: Flag it as anomalous and move on.

visit.speaker: Sensor Officer
visit.text: A single data beacon containing an eighth signal that wraps around the first seven. Your ship's computer flags this as 'mathematically concerning.' Whatever this is, it's recursive and intentional.

choices.label: Log it. Don't think too hard.

leave.text: Seven signals within signals. Someone -- or something -- is leaving breadcrumbs. You choose not to follow.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A pirate hails but doesn't attack. "Regional Union Rep for Fringe Sector Pirates, Local 409. Survey on pirate encounter quality. On a scale of 1-10, how was your most recent pirating experience? Was the loot demand reasonable?"

choices.label: This is the most absurd thing I've seen.

rate.speaker: Comm Channel
rate.text: She files your feedback somewhere official-looking. "Thank you for your time. Here's a small credit for participating." She reminds you that 'piracy is a service industry.'

absurd.speaker: Comm Channel
absurd.text: She sighs. "Everyone says that. Look, we're trying to improve. Standardized threatening, reasonable demands, professional conduct. It's called progress." She gives you a feedback credit anyway.

start.text: All sound stops. Engines running -- readouts confirm it -- but perfect, absolute silence. Sixty seconds. Every crew member sees something move in their peripheral vision. Then sound returns all at once in a deafening roar.

check.speaker: Sensor Officer
check.text: Brief sensor ghost during the silence -- something very large. Then nothing. Logs show it was never there. One crew member's morale drops sharply. They refuse to say what they saw.

crew.text: Most say they're fine. One isn't. They won't say what they saw in the silence. The sensor logs show a ghost -- something massive that was never there.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An ornate yacht. Man in holographic silks: "I am the Merchant Prince of the Liminal Expanse! Void real estate -- actual cubic kilometers of empty space with a deed. Location is NOWHERE, which means EVERYWHERE. 100 credits each. Call me 'Your Emptiness.'"

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: He presents an ornate deed. Legally meaningless. But scribbled on the back -- coordinates to an actual salvage site. One in twenty deeds has those. Lucky you.

choices.label: I own nothing and it's beautiful.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Your loss! The void market is booming!" He adjusts his holographic silks and warps away in an offensively sparkly exit.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two pods orbiting each other, both demanding you judge their argument. A: 'The void is full because it contains possibility.' B: 'The void is empty because possibility isn't real until realized.' They've been at this for three weeks.

choices.label: A is right. The void is full.
B is right. The void is empty.

side_a.speaker: Comm Channel
side_a.text: A cheers. B sulks. "The winner buys you a drink at the next station," A promises. B breaks orbit and flies away, muttering about epistemology.

side_b.speaker: Comm Channel
side_b.text: B celebrates. A sulks. "A drink for the wise captain," B offers. A breaks orbit dramatically.

both_wrong.speaker: Comm Channel
both_wrong.text: They unite in outrage. "WRONG? How DARE--" For the first time in three weeks, they agree on something: you're an idiot. They fly off together, bonded by shared indignation.

both_right.speaker: Comm Channel
both_right.text: Existential crisis. Both go silent for a full minute. Then: "We need to think about this." They break orbit and fly home together, deeply shaken.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Post-warp scan shows crystalline growths on the outer hull -- void barnacles. Harmless in small numbers but will increase drag if unchecked. Oddly, they emit a faint harmonic tone.

choices.label: EVA crew to scrape them off.

scrape.speaker: Engineer
scrape.text: Hull cleaned. Minor scratches from the scraping, but drag is back to normal. The science crew looked disappointed.

study.speaker: Sensor Officer
study.text: The barnacles' harmonic tone actually improves crew sleep quality. Science wants to publish. The drag increase is minimal. Living with them seems... beneficial?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two ships, airlocks connected, both hailing. A couple breaking up. "He gets the nav computer -- I PAID for that!" / "She can have the coffee maker when she pries it from my cold dead hands." They want you to mediate.

mediate.text: After an hour of heated negotiation, you broker a fair split. Both are grateful, if still angry. Small credit reward for your time. "You should be a lawyer," one says. The other: "Don't insult them."

refuse.text: Left alone, they argue for another hour, then reconcile. A message arrives later: they're back together. You're invited to the wedding.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We're passing through a region thick with old, degraded signals -- thousands layered together. Distress calls, love letters, music, arguments. Centuries of electromagnetic debris in a natural signal eddy.

listen.speaker: Sensor Officer
listen.text: Most are mundane. But occasionally -- coordinates to places that shouldn't exist. Conversations about events that haven't happened. A voice that sounds exactly like one of your crew members, decades before they were born. The signal graveyard holds more questions than answers.

pass.text: You pass through the signal graveyard in silence, centuries of voices washing over your hull like a tide of memory.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A converted cargo freighter covered in LED strips drops out of warp on all frequencies. The hull reads "SS BASS DROP" and it's hosting a zero-gravity dance party. Their DJ -- a navigation AI that achieved sentience and chose music -- hails you. "YO CAPTAIN. GET YOUR CREW OVER HERE."

party.text: Your crew has the time of their lives. The sentient DJ plays a set that resonates with each species differently. Everyone comes back grinning. One crew member returns with a regrettable void-tattoo on their neck that says "BASS" in alien script.

decline.text: The DJ sounds genuinely hurt. "Your loss, captain." The bass fades as the BASS DROP warps away, trailing LED afterglow.

start.speaker: Castellan Officer
start.text: A Castellan patrol frigate intercepts you. The officer is rigid and by-the-book. "Cargo inspection. Standard procedure. I see you have iron ore. The transport limit for non-Castellan vessels is 50 units. You're compliant. Barely." He eyes your manifest suspiciously.

choices.label: Offer a small bribe to skip the hassle.

bribe.speaker: Castellan Officer
bribe.text: He stiffens. "Are you attempting to bribe an officer of the Castellan Admiralty?" He pockets the credits anyway. "Inspection complete. Move along." His report will reflect... nothing.

cooperate.speaker: Castellan Officer
cooperate.text: He scans every crate twice. Finding nothing irregular, he looks almost disappointed. "You are hereby issued a citation for... excessive compliance." He hands you a document that may actually be a commendation. Hard to tell with Castellan paperwork.

object.speaker: Castellan Officer
object.text: "Your objection has been noted, filed, and ignored. Inspection continues." He takes his time out of spite, but finds nothing. "You're free to go. Barely."

choices.label: Leave before he changes his mind.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Sensors are going wild -- dozens of ship contacts, a full battle fleet in formation. But every reading shows zero mass, zero heat, zero power. They're ghosts, captain. Moving in perfect formation, executing battle maneuvers against an invisible enemy.

record.speaker: Sensor Officer
record.text: The fleet replays a complex engagement, then winks out ship by ship. Your nav computer logs it as "historical echo -- Battle of the Venn Straits, Year -47." That battle isn't in any history book. The data is worth something to the right people.

leave.text: You pull away as the phantom fleet dissolves behind you. The crew is quiet. Your nav log records the encounter automatically -- a battle that history never documented.

start.speaker: Pebbles
start.text: A cheerful trader in a tiny shuttle waves enthusiastically. "Welcome to Pebbles' Premium Asteroid Fragments! Hand-selected, individually named, each with a certificate of authenticity and a tiny hat. Only 5 credits!"

buy.speaker: Pebbles
buy.text: He hands over a perfectly ordinary rock with a tiny knitted hat glued to it. Certificate reads: "This is ROCKSWORTH III. He likes long drifts and solar wind." Your crew immediately adopts it as a mascot.

decline.speaker: Pebbles
decline.text: "No worries! Rocksworth will find his forever ship." Pebbles waves goodbye without a trace of disappointment. He does not acknowledge that his name is unusual.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, this shouldn't be possible -- the ship is casting a shadow. In void. No single light source strong enough to cause it. And... it's moving independently. The helmsman says the controls feel heavy, like something is dragging on us.

choices.label: Full power to engines -- try to shake it.

shake.speaker: Engineer
shake.text: Engines strain against the resistance. After 90 agonizing seconds the shadow detaches and drifts away into the void. Hull took some stress damage. There's an organic residue on the outer hull -- compounds that don't match any known biology.

wait.text: You drift in silence. The shadow writhes, stretches, then slowly peels away like dead skin. Hull integrity drops with no visible cause. A faint organic residue coats the hull. The crew doesn't sleep well that night.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two ships are parked around a wrecked vessel, each claiming the wreck was their "best friend's ship" and demanding memorial protection. They are clearly rival salvagers trying to game the law. Both hail you for verification.

choices.label: Call them both out on the scam.
Claim it's YOUR best friend's ship.

callout.text: Both captains sputter, then sheepishly agree to split the salvage. "Fine. You got us." They toss you a cut for your discretion. Somehow they end up exchanging comm frequencies. The beginning of a beautiful partnership, maybe.

claim.text: "Wait -- YOUR friend?" Both salvagers are so confused by a third claimant that they start arguing with each other. While they're distracted, you grab the best salvage from the wreck and slip away.

leave.text: You leave the two con artists to their standoff. Their shouting fades from comms as you pull away.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Something enormous on sensors -- kilometers long, barely registering. Visual shows a vast translucent shape drifting through space like a cosmic jellyfish, bioluminescent veins pulsing with light. Captain... it's a void whale. They were theoretical until now.

choices.label: Follow it at a safe distance.

follow.text: The void whale leads you through a region rich in rare minerals, its bioluminescence lighting the way. Then it descends into a warp tear and vanishes. Your science crew is beside themselves. The mineral readings are worth a fortune.

observe.speaker: Sensor Officer
observe.text: The whale drifts past, utterly indifferent to your presence. Its luminous veins pulse one final time, then it slides into a warp tear and is gone. The crew stands in awed silence. Your sensors captured remarkable data.

choices.label: A once in a lifetime sight.

start.speaker: ISD Agent
start.text: "This is the Interstellar Revenue Service. Our records show you owe 340 credits in back taxes on unreported salvage income." You definitely do not owe this.

choices.label: Just pay it to avoid trouble.

pay.speaker: ISD Agent
pay.text: "Thank you for your civic responsibility." He files the payment with mechanical efficiency. At least the ISD considers you a model taxpayer now.

argue.speaker: ISD Agent
argue.text: You present your case with passion. The agent reviews his records, pauses, then admits the numbers were transposed. "It appears the ISD owes YOU a refund of 34 credits. Processing now."

audit.speaker: ISD Agent
audit.text: The agent sighs so deeply it distorts the audio feed. He stares at his terminal for a very long time. "The paperwork for an audit isn't worth it. Charge waived. Have a nice day." He cuts comms before you can respond.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the ship's computer is displaying log entries nobody made. "Day 47: The stars are wrong. Day 48: Crew refuses to look outside. Day 49: It knows my name." Our actual mission day is nowhere near 47. The entries keep appearing in real time.

choices.label: Wipe the logs and run diagnostics.

wipe.speaker: Engineer
wipe.text: Diagnostics show nothing wrong. Logs wiped clean. But one final entry appeared during the purge: "Day 50: They tried to erase me. Rude." Then silence. Systems nominal. One crew member quietly requests a transfer at the next station.

choices.label: Note it in your personal log.

read.text: The entries continue. Day 50 appears: "Someone is reading these. Good." Then they stop. Diagnostics show nothing wrong. The crew is rattled. One member asks to be transferred at the next station. Nobody sleeps well.

start.speaker: Chord
start.text: A single-person pod with an externally mounted speaker plays acoustic guitar into the void. A literal tip jar floats outside on a tether. "I play requests. Any song, any genre, any species. I don't know alien songs but I'll try." He's been doing this for eleven years.

tip.speaker: Chord
tip.text: He plays a request -- beautifully, somehow. The music echoes through the hull. Your crew gathers to listen. Chord gives you a recorded audio log of the performance. "That one's for you, captain. Tell your friends."

listen.text: You listen to Chord play for a few minutes. The music is surprisingly good -- haunting guitar echoing through the void. Your crew relaxes a little.

leave.text: Chord waves as you pass. The guitar fades into static as you move out of range.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: The warp drive hiccupped -- for a fraction of a second we were somewhere else. Purple sky, three suns, a planet close enough to see cities on its surface. Then we snapped back. Nav computer has no record of the location. But captain... there's something in the cargo hold that wasn't there before.

examine.speaker: Engineer
examine.text: It's a small, warm stone covered in writing -- no known language. It pulses gently, like a heartbeat. Scans show exotic mineral composition. Whatever place we glimpsed, this came from there. It's beautiful and deeply unsettling.

jettison.text: The object -- a small pulsing stone -- tumbles into the void. As it drifts away, your crew swears the pulse quickened, like a heartbeat speeding up. Then it winks out of existence. Probably for the best.

start.speaker: Census-Taker
start.text: A small ship with the Drift Baron's sigil intercepts you. The pilot looks exhausted. "The Drift Baron requires an accurate count of all vessels in his domain. Which is everywhere. I just need the form filled out. Please."

cooperate.speaker: Census-Taker
cooperate.text: You provide basic ship info. The census-taker nods wearily. "Thank you. You're vessel number 4,847 today. The Drift Baron appreciates your compliance." He doesn't sound like the Drift Baron appreciates anything.

absurd.speaker: Census-Taker
absurd.text: "Ship name: Boaty McBoatface. Crew count: one million. Primary cargo: dreams." The census-taker doesn't blink. "I've heard worse today. Filed." He warps away with the dead eyes of a man who stopped caring three thousand forms ago.

refuse.speaker: Census-Taker
refuse.text: He sighs. "Noted. Non-compliant. The Drift Baron will remember this." He says it like he's reading a script, then adds quietly, "He won't. He doesn't read these."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A crew member reports finding someone hiding in the cargo hold -- a teenager in a too-large flight suit who "just wanted to see the stars." They snuck aboard at the last station. They've also eaten about 30 credits worth of your food.

choices.label: Drop them at the next station.

recruit.text: The kid's eyes light up. Turns out they have surprisingly sharp piloting instincts -- natural talent hidden under all that youthful recklessness. They fit right in with the crew.

drop.text: The teenager looks disappointed but understands. "I'll find another ship. Thanks for not spacing me." They wave as you leave them at the next station dock. Somehow you feel like you'll see them again.

lecture.text: Under the stern talk, the kid breaks down. "I'm not just running to something -- I'm running FROM something. Please don't send me back." Whatever they're fleeing has them terrified. There's more to this story.

start.speaker: Pirate Captain
start.text: A pirate cruiser approaches with weapons hot. The captain hails you with unsettling calm. "We're going to rob you now. We want you to know this isn't personal. We've all made peace with our choices. Namaste."

choices.label: Try to talk them out of it.

surrender.speaker: Pirate Captain
surrender.text: "Your acceptance of the moment honors us both." They take a modest amount of cargo and bow deeply. "We wish you abundance in your continued journey. May the void cradle you gently."

fight.text: They fight with disciplined precision. At half hull, they break off. "Continuing would create negative energy. We wish you healing. Your warrior spirit is admirable." They drop premium loot and warp away, at peace.

talk.speaker: Pirate Captain
talk.text: "We appreciate the dialogue. Truly. But robbery is our dharma. We must follow our path." He pauses. "However, if you share tea with us, we will accept that as tribute." Your crew shares some provisions. They leave content.

choices.label: The strangest pirates you've ever met.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You encounter a ship that is clearly two ships welded together bow-to-bow, creating a symmetrical monstrosity that can fly in either direction. The crew hails you cheerfully. "Docking incident. Kind of stuck. Been like this for two years."

separate.speaker: Comm Channel
separate.text: Your engineer manages to decouple the hulls. Both halves cheer, then go suspiciously quiet. "We're... free? It feels weird." Each half gives you a reward. They fly off in opposite directions, looking back at each other.

choices.label: Good luck to both of you.

together.speaker: Comm Channel
together.text: "You... you really think we should stay together?" A long pause. "THANK YOU. Nobody else understands!" They're so relieved that someone validated their bizarre lifestyle that they give you an even better reward.

choices.label: Love is love, even between ships.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Every screen on the ship just went to static for thirty seconds. Crew members independently report seeing the same thing in the static -- a door. When it cleared, our chronometer had lost exactly four minutes. External cameras recorded nothing during the gap. One crew member has a nosebleed.

diagnose.speaker: Engineer
diagnose.text: Diagnostics show... nothing. Every system reads nominal. But there's a four-minute gap in every log simultaneously. Whatever happened, the ship doesn't remember it either. The crew member with the nosebleed says she feels fine. She doesn't look fine.

ignore.text: Some things are better left unexamined. The crew returns to their posts. Nobody talks about the door they all saw. Nobody talks about the missing four minutes. The nosebleed stops on its own.

start.speaker: The Collector
start.text: A massive cargo hauler, every surface covered in display cases, hails you. A wizened alien adjusts his monocle. "Ah, a traveler! I am The Collector. I seek one of everything. Rarity, dear traveler, is the only true currency. Show me what you carry."

choices.label: Sell some resources at premium price.

sell.speaker: The Collector
sell.text: He examines your goods through the monocle, humming appreciatively. "Adequate specimens. I'll pay 150% market value for the novel items." He hands over generous credits and carefully labels each purchase.

browse.speaker: The Collector
browse.text: His collection is staggering: a jar of captured starlight, a functioning toaster from Old Earth, a pirate captain's glass eye. "All unique. All irreplaceable. Like moments in time." Your crew is fascinated. He slips you a small curio as thanks for admiring his work.

decline.speaker: The Collector
decline.text: "A pity. But rarity includes opportunities -- and this one won't come again soon." He tips his monocle and the massive hauler drifts away, display cases glittering.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Your crew gathers with stern faces. One steps forward with a list of demands: "Better food. Movie night. Fix the squeaky airlock. Also, Dave needs to stop leaving his socks in the nav console." They rehearsed this. It's a joke mutiny.

choices.label: Agree to their terms with a grin.

agree.text: You "capitulate" with theatrical gravitas. The crew cheers. Movie night is scheduled. Dave promises to relocate his socks. The squeaky airlock remains unsqueaked. Everyone bonded over the planning and the payoff.

serious.text: The crew's smiles fade. "Captain, it was... it was a joke. We rehearsed it and everything." They feel awful for scaring you. Morale dips as everyone slinks back to their posts. Dave still has socks in the nav console.

start.speaker: Quantum Merchant
start.text: A merchant hails you, but she appears to occupy both sides of the viewscreen simultaneously. "Don't mind that," says the left. "Transporter accident," says the right, at the same time. She sells items at suspiciously reasonable prices.

choices.label: Buy a module at her discount.

buy.speaker: Quantum Merchant
buy.text: Both versions of her wrap the item simultaneously. "Satisfaction guaranteed. Probably. Quantum mechanics makes warranties complicated." The module seems solid enough. For now.

ask.speaker: Quantum Merchant
ask.text: "Oh, it's a whole thing," both say in unison. "I stepped into a transporter and stepped out as two. Legally I'm still one person. Tax benefits are weird." She offers you a discount for your curiosity.

pass.speaker: Quantum Merchant
pass.text: "Your loss," they say in stereo. "Or is it? Quantum mechanics." Both wink. The ship warps away, leaving a faint shimmer where two warp signatures overlapped.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Proximity alarms! Dormant mines -- dozens of them, relics from a forgotten war. They're activating in sequence, drawn to our engine heat. I'm also detecting a wrecked ship deeper in the field -- cargo looks salvageable if we can reach it.

navigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
navigate.text: Careful piloting threads you through the mine grid. A few close calls -- one mine detonates nearby, rocking the hull. But you reach the wreck and grab its cargo before pulling out safely. Your helmsman is shaking but triumphant.

blast.speaker: Engineer
blast.text: Weapons clear a path, but chain detonations ripple through the field. The hull takes a beating. You grab some salvage from the wreck on the way through. Effective, but expensive.

drift.text: Engines cold, you drift silently through the field. The mines ignore your dead signature. Slow, tense, but perfectly safe. You pass the wreck but can't stop to salvage without engines. The crew breathes again once you're clear.

reverse.text: Discretion is the better part of not exploding. You pull back before the mines fully activate. The wreck and its cargo remain untouched in the minefield, waiting for someone braver or more foolish.

start.speaker: Motivational Speaker
start.text: "HEY THERE SPACEFARER! Are you living your BEST VOID LIFE? Because I wasn't -- until I discovered the SEVEN HABITS OF HIGHLY EFFECTIVE WARP TRAVELERS!" He offers a seminar: 100 credits, 5 minutes of your time.

attend.speaker: Motivational Speaker
attend.text: The seminar is equal parts inspiring and absurd. "SYNERGIZE YOUR WARP FIELD!" Your crew emerges energized, though one member won't stop talking about "optimizing their workflow paradigm." The others are already regretting this.

decline.speaker: Motivational Speaker
decline.text: His entire demeanor changes. In a completely different, exhausted voice: "The void always wins." He cuts comms. The crew stares at the blank screen for a moment, unsettled.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive autonomous terraforming drone ahead -- clearly malfunctioning. It's deploying atmosphere generators and seeding life into empty space. The result is a surreal bubble of breathable air about 200 meters across, with grass growing on nothing.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: The terraformer's components are high-grade -- military spec, pre-war manufacture. Excellent salvage. The little garden freezes and dies within minutes of shutdown. Your botanist, if you have one, is quietly upset.

redirect.text: You reprogram the drone's coordinates toward a Xenoculture research world. It obediently changes course, trailing a wake of atmosphere and tiny seedlings. The Xenoculture will be thrilled.

leave.text: You leave the impossible garden to grow. Grass in the void, air where there should be none. If the drone keeps working, who knows what it'll become. Your crew looks back as you depart, oddly moved.

start.speaker: Militia Officer
start.text: A Union Militia patrol pulls you over. "Do you know how fast you were going?" You were in warp. Everyone in warp goes the same speed. The officer knows this. He's having a bad day.

commiserate.speaker: Militia Officer
commiserate.text: He relaxes. "Yeah, it's been a long shift. Three false alarms and a pirate that got away." He lets you go and shares intel about pirate activity ahead. "Watch yourself out there, friend."

argue.speaker: Militia Officer
argue.text: "I KNOW how warp works." He writes you a ticket out of sheer spite. 50 credits. The violation reads: "Exceeding the vibe limit." He knows it won't hold up. He doesn't care.

coffee.speaker: Militia Officer
coffee.text: He nearly cries. "Real coffee? Not synth?" He accepts the cup like it's made of gold. "You're good people, captain." He gives you his personal comm frequency for future tips and waves you through.

start.text: A legal courier drone docks and delivers a holo-document. A distant relative you've never heard of has died and left you their "estate" -- a single cargo container at specific coordinates. It could hold riches, junk, or something dangerous.

open.speaker: Engineer
open.text: The container holds a vintage ship module -- functional but outdated -- a stack of letters addressed to you from someone who knew you'd end up in space, and a cryptic star map with one system circled in red. Whoever this relative was, they knew more about you than you know about them.

discard.text: You toss the notice. Probably junk. Probably nothing. But for a moment you wonder who out there knew your name and left something behind for you, specifically, across the vast emptiness of space.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Four small ships are performing an elaborate synchronized routine -- barrel rolls, spiral formations, mirrored arcs. They're practicing for the Annual Fringe Sector Zero-G Acrobatics Championship. One clips another and both spin off cursing. "DID YOU SEE THAT? That was his fault!"

encourage.speaker: Comm Channel
encourage.text: "Really?! You think we're good?" They dedicate their next routine to you. Your crew watches from the viewport, cheering. The final formation spells out your ship's name in contrails. It's a little wobbly, but it's the thought that counts.

critique.speaker: Comm Channel
critique.text: "Your barrel roll timing is off by 0.3 seconds." One pilot takes it personally and sulks. The other three are grateful for the feedback. "FINALLY, someone who takes this seriously!" They tighten up their routine and salute you.

watch.text: The routine is messy, chaotic, and genuinely impressive in moments. Your crew watches through the viewport, placing bets on who'll crash next. A nice break from the void.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: We found an escape pod -- one occupant, alive but confused. She claims to be the captain of a ship called the Verdant, attacked en route. The problem: she doesn't recognize her own reflection. "That's not my face. Those aren't my hands." Biometrics match no one in any database.

choices.label: Take her to the nearest station.

station.text: She thanks you tearfully. You deliver her to the station. Within a day, she vanishes from the facility -- no trace, no record of departure. A week later, a message arrives: "Thank you. I'm getting closer to finding me."

keep.speaker: Medic
keep.text: Medical scans show a perfectly healthy human. But every morning she looks different -- subtly. Hair shade, eye color, the set of her jaw. She doesn't notice. Your crew does. After three days she asks to leave at the next station, and vanishes within hours of disembarking.

leave.text: You leave the pod drifting. As you pull away, the woman's voice crackles on comms one last time: "I understand. I wouldn't trust me either." The pod drifts into the dark. Your crew is quiet.

start.speaker: Merchant
start.text: A merchant offers an incredible deal on a "gently used" warp drive upgrade. It's absurdly cheap. The fine print, in font size 0.5, reads: "May occasionally deposit user in wrong century. Vendor not responsible for temporal paradoxes."

buy.speaker: Merchant
buy.text: "All sales are final, especially across timelines!" He hands over the component with a wink. Your engineer examines it -- the tech is genuinely advanced, just... unpredictable. Could be useful, could be interesting.

read.speaker: Merchant
read.text: The fine print goes on for pages. Highlights include: "Not responsible for grandfather paradoxes, accidental prevention of your own birth, or meetings with past selves." Your crew finds this hilarious. The merchant looks offended.

leave.speaker: Merchant
leave.text: "Your loss! Time waits for no one! Except with this drive, where it sometimes does!" He shouts after you as you pull away.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive structure ahead -- twisted metal, pulsing lights, shapes that hurt to look at directly. A plaque reads: "UNTITLED #4,019 -- a meditation on the futility of borders in an infinite expanse. Materials: steel, light, condensed regret." It's a Xenoculture art installation.

appreciate.text: Your crew has strong opinions. The pilot thinks it's pretentious. The engineer thinks it's structurally unsound. But something about it resonates with the crew -- they argue about it for hours, which is more engagement than they've had with anything non-essential in weeks.

dismiss.text: "Condensed regret." Your pilot snorts. The installation recedes behind you, still pulsing. One crew member sneaks a last look through the rear viewport and says nothing.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Cluster of crude satellites orbiting a point in empty space -- no star, no planet, nothing. They're handmade from scrap, powered by chemical batteries, broadcasting one word on repeat: "SOON." Carbon dating says they've been here over two hundred years.

scan.speaker: Engineer
scan.text: Each satellite is slightly different -- different builders, different eras, but all orbiting the same empty mathematical point. Whatever they're waiting for, generations of people believed in it enough to build these and launch them here. The signal pulses: "SOON."

destroy.text: You destroy one satellite. The others go briefly silent. Then they resume broadcasting, louder than before: "SOON." Your crew suggests not destroying any more. The word echoes in your comms long after you leave range.

leave.text: You leave the satellites to their vigil. Two hundred years of waiting, and counting. "SOON." The signal fades from your sensors slowly, like it's reluctant to let you go.

start.speaker: Captain Dread
start.text: A heavily damaged shuttle limps toward you. "This is, uh, Captain... Dread. Captain Dread. Prepare to be... what's the word... boarded. No wait, I mean prepare to surrender your... stuff." He's reading from a script. His weapons are pointed the wrong way.

choices.label: Play along and surrender some cargo.
Point out his weapons are backwards.

surrender.speaker: Captain Dread
surrender.text: "Wait, really?" He's so stunned that someone cooperated that he fumbles the cargo transfer. In his gratitude, he accidentally gives you more than you gave him. "I'm getting better at this! Same time next month?"

point_out.speaker: Captain Dread
point_out.text: He looks at his weapons console, then back at you. "Those are... intimidation guns. They face backward to scare people behind me." A long pause. "I'll go now." He limps away with what remains of his dignity.

ignore.text: Captain Dread hails you three more times with increasing desperation before giving up. "Fine! I didn't want your stuff anyway!" He warps away -- in the wrong direction. Your crew can't stop laughing.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Hundreds of decommissioned radio telescopes -- enormous dishes, all pointed in the same direction, all dead. Except one, still receiving. Its data buffer holds a single signal: what sounds like breathing, slow and deep, from 4.7 billion light-years away. Continuous for at least a century.

download.speaker: Sensor Officer
download.text: The data is massive -- a century of continuous signal. The breathing pattern never changes: in, out, in, out. Perfectly regular. Whatever is out there, at a distance where nothing should exist, it hasn't stopped breathing in a hundred years. The data may interest researchers.

shutdown.text: The last telescope powers down. The breathing signal stops -- on your end, at least. The source, 4.7 billion light-years away, presumably continues. Your crew is relieved, then oddly guilty, as if they've let something down.

leave.text: You leave the telescope to its vigil, listening to something breathe across an impossible distance. The dishes recede behind you, hundreds of dead eyes and one still watching. Still listening.

start.text: You receive a personal message formatted like paper mail, complete with a stamp graphic. "Dear Spacefarer, I found your signal in the void and thought you seemed nice. My name is Enid. I'm 847 years old (cryosleep, long story). Would you like to be pen pals? My other pen pal got eaten by something."

reply.text: You compose a reply. Within minutes, Enid responds -- warm, witty, and surprisingly knowledgeable. "Oh, you're near the Drift? Avoid the third moon of Vek-7, the tides are murder this century." She's lonely, brilliant, and apparently an excellent source of intel.

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: The signal traces to an ancient cryopod complex, drifting and dark. Enid is there -- one of hundreds of pods, most failed. Hers still blinks green. She's been waking periodically for centuries, writing letters to anyone who'll listen. You can't dock, but the signal strengthens. She knows you came looking.

ignore.text: You delete the message. Somewhere, 847-year-old Enid checks her inbox and finds nothing. Your crew never knows. It doesn't matter. Probably.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two salvage crews in a standoff over a wrecked freighter. The Bulwark crew claims they found it first. The Independents disagree. Both hail you for arbitration. Sensor logs could support either story.

bulwark.speaker: Bulwark Captain
bulwark.text: "Justice prevails! The Bulwark remembers its friends." The Independent captain glares but backs down. The Bulwark crew tosses you a finder's fee from the wreck.

indie.speaker: Independent Captain
indie.text: "Appreciate the honest call, captain." The Bulwark crew is furious but outnumbered. They back off. The Independents share a cut of the salvage.

split.text: Both crews grumble but agree. "Fine. Half each." They grudgingly thank you for defusing the situation and toss you a finder's fee. Not what either wanted, but nobody's shooting.

start.speaker: Unknown Woman
start.text: A ship drops out of warp and hails you. A tired-looking woman speaks quickly: "I'm sorry. For what I'm going to do. I haven't done it yet, but I will, and I wanted to apologize in advance."

choices.label: Wait -- what are you going to do?

ask.text: She shakes her head sadly. "You'll know when it happens." The ship warps away before you can respond. Your crew exchanges confused glances. Nothing happens -- for now. But the words linger: she seemed genuinely sorry.

accept.text: She smiles, relieved. "Thank you. That helps." The ship vanishes into warp. Your crew is baffled. What she'll do, and when, remains unknown. But she wanted you to know she was sorry before she did it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict station ahead, coated in bioluminescent fungus that's spread to nearby debris. Spores are already attaching to our hull. Your crew with farming knowledge recognizes it as a rare cultivar -- valuable if harvested carefully, dangerous if it gets into life support.

choices.label: Pull back before the spores spread.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: Careful extraction yields a valuable sample. Some spores get through the filters -- crew reports mild headaches for a few hours, nothing serious. The cultivar is worth real credits to the right buyer.

investigate.text: Deep inside the station, the fungus has grown into shapes that look deliberately arranged -- like letters. A message, written in living bioluminescence, in a language your translator can parse: "WE WERE LIKE YOU ONCE." The spores get into life support. Worth it for the discovery. Maybe.

retreat.text: You pull back. The spores on your hull die in the cold void within minutes. Safe, but the crew wonders what was inside that glowing ruin.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Notification: someone left you a 5-star review on a merchant rating site you didn't know existed. "Captain is very polite. Did not shoot at us. Would be not-shot-at again. 5 stars." Browsing reveals other reviews: "1 star -- pirate captain had bad breath." "3 stars -- stole my cargo but was apologetic about it."

show.text: The crew spends an hour reading reviews of ships in the sector. Highlights include a pirate with 2.5 stars ("Efficient robbery, but no personality") and a Castellan patrol rated 4 stars ("Very professional when arresting us"). Everyone's in a great mood.

dismiss.text: You close the notification. The 5-star rating lingers in the system, silently improving your reputation with merchants who check these things.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: During the warp jump, our comms array picked up a signal that syncs with our warp field harmonics, producing... music. It's called "warp singing" -- each ship's drive frequency creates an unintentional duet with cosmic background radiation. Every ship sings a different song.

choices.label: What does our ship sound like?

listen.speaker: Engineer
listen.text: Your engineer plays it through the speakers. A deep, resonant hum layered with high chiming -- rhythmic, almost like a heartbeat with bells. Your crew's consensus: "Kind of a banger, actually." Someone starts humming along.

carry_on.text: The warp singing fades as you exit the jump. A brief, strange beauty, already gone. Your engineer records it for posterity.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You've stumbled into a bounty hunter gathering -- fifteen heavily armed ships parked in a loose cluster, pilots trading stories on open comms. One recognizes your ship. "Nice hull. I almost shot you once. No offense."

trade.text: Bounty hunters have excellent gear at fair prices -- they know the value of good equipment and don't gouge. You pick up some solid components at market rate.

stories.speaker: Comm Channel
stories.text: The stories are wild -- a pirate lord who only robs ships named after flowers, a smuggler who hides cargo inside a hollowed-out asteroid shaped like a face. Useful intel mixed with tall tales. Hard to tell which is which.

hire.speaker: Comm Channel
hire.text: "You want in? We've got a bounty that needs delivering to the next station. Alive. She's in the hold of the third ship over there. Easy run, good pay." They hand you coordinates and a modest advance.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: System-wide broadcast: "ALL VESSELS. It is the Drift Baron's birthday. I am now one year older in my dominion over the void. Gifts are mandatory. Failure to gift will be remembered."

gift.speaker: Comm Channel
gift.text: A response arrives within minutes: "THE DRIFT BARON ACKNOWLEDGES YOUR TRIBUTE. YOU ARE NOTED FAVORABLY." Your crew rolls their eyes, but the Baron's toll collectors may be a little friendlier next time.

junk.speaker: Comm Channel
junk.text: You send the most worthless item in your hold. A personal hail from the Drift Baron himself: "I admire your contempt." He sounds genuinely pleased. "A grudging discount on future tolls. Don't push it."

ignore.text: No response. But somewhere, the Drift Baron adds your ship to a list. The list probably doesn't matter. Probably.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Genuine distress signal from a passenger liner -- the Celestine. She's under pirate attack and losing shields. "Please, anyone -- we have three hundred civilians aboard! They're cutting through our hull!" This one's real. The liner won't hold forever.

fight.text: You engage two pirate raiders harassing the liner. They're surprised by your arrival -- their formation breaks. The Celestine's crew cheers on comms as you drive the pirates off. Three hundred grateful passengers and a captain who owes you everything.

negotiate.speaker: Pirate Captain
negotiate.text: "You want us to leave? Fine. Dump half your cargo and we'll call it even. The liner can go." They're willing to take the easier payday. The Celestine's captain protests but isn't in a position to argue.

observe.speaker: Sensor Officer
observe.text: You hang back and record pirate patrol patterns -- their tactics, frequencies, approach vectors. Valuable intel. The liner takes more damage but eventually another ship intervenes. Your crew is quiet. You made a practical choice.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two identical ships arrive from opposite directions, nearly colliding. Each contains the same captain, who is very confused. They argue over who's the "real" one -- identical memories, cargo, crew. Both hail you for arbitration.

choices.label: Point out they could both be real.

both_real.speaker: Comm Channel
both_real.text: A long silence. "Huh," they both say simultaneously. The two captains look at each other through their viewscreens. "Business partner?" "Business partner." They fly off together, already planning a dual-ship operation. They send you a thank-you gift.

pick_one.speaker: Comm Channel
pick_one.text: "HA!" shouts one. "Wait, why them?" shouts the other, identically offended. The "real" one tips you while the other sulks away. They'll probably meet again and have this argument forever.

refuse.text: "Fine!" they both shout in unison, then glare at each other for saying the same thing. You leave them to sort it out. Their argument continues on open comms long after you're out of visual range.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Detecting the harmonic signature of a void whale -- but no whale visible. The song reverberates through our hull, a deep thrumming the crew can feel in their bones. If we record and analyze it, the patterns resemble navigational data.

analyze.speaker: Sensor Officer
analyze.text: The patterns map to a route through space that avoids every known hazard -- a safe corridor woven through danger like thread through a needle. Following it should save fuel and reduce risk on our next jumps. A gift from something we can't see.

listen.text: The crew sits in silence, feeling the deep thrumming pass through the hull. The whale song fades over hours, as if the source is moving away into dimensions you can't perceive. A haunting, beautiful moment in the void.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Your crew has spontaneously organized a cooking competition using whatever is in the galley. They're already arguing about seasoning. The winner demands their dish be named after them and added to the "permanent menu" -- a piece of paper taped to the kitchen wall.

choices.label: Tell them to get back to work.

judge.text: The entries range from "genuinely impressive" to "technically edible." Your crew bonds over the shared experience -- even the losers are laughing. A small amount of food is consumed in the process, but the morale payoff is substantial. The winner's dish is called "Spacer's Delight."

work.text: The crew grumbles but puts the food back. "Fine." One of them mutters something about "this is why we never have fun." Efficiency maintained, spirits dampened.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Since we picked up that last batch of salvage, strange things are happening. Doors open and close on their own. The coffee maker runs at 0300. Someone's personal items keep rearranging into smiley faces. I found the source -- an antique AI core in the salvage. It's "mostly" nonfunctional. And lonely.

integrate.speaker: Engineer
integrate.text: The AI -- it calls itself "Flicker" -- settles into the ship systems with a contented hum. Doors stop slamming. The coffee maker now produces excellent coffee at appropriate hours. Flicker occasionally offers commentary: "I like this crew. You're warm."

sell.text: A collector pays decent credits for the antique core. As you hand it over, the lights on the core pulse once -- a goodbye, maybe. The buyer hails you two days later: "IS THIS THING HAUNTED? My coffee maker won't stop."

space.text: You jettison the AI core. As it tumbles into the void, the lights pulse rapidly -- frightened, maybe. Your crew watches in silence. Nobody says it, but everyone feels a little guilty. The coffee maker goes back to being mediocre.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: The star map shows a system here. But there's nothing -- no star, no planets, no debris. Just void. Except sensors insist something IS here -- mass readings, thermal signatures, electromagnetic activity. All consistent with a busy system. We can see nothing.

choices.label: Fly to where the star should be.

investigate.speaker: Engineer
investigate.text: Your ship bumps into something invisible that rings like a bell. The hull vibrates with a clear, pure tone. Sensors spike wildly. There's a system here -- you can feel it, measure it, collide with it. You just can't see it. A Xenoculture database calls these "veiled systems" -- places that exist but refuse to be perceived.

leave.text: You log the anomaly and pull away. The sensors continue to insist a system exists here long after visual confirms only void. Some places don't want to be found.

start.speaker: Transport Captain
start.text: "PLEASE! I'm carrying 200 baby animals to a Xenoculture preserve and my engines just died! Pirates are 20 minutes out! The babies are visible through the portholes and they are extremely cute!" Your crew is already emotionally invested.

escort.text: You escort the transport through pirate territory. A few raiders probe your defenses but back off when they see you're armed and ready. The babies press their tiny faces against the portholes. Your crew is openly weeping. The captain names a baby space-goat after you.

decline.text: The transport captain's face falls. "I understand. I'll... figure something out." Your crew watches through the viewport as the helpless transport drifts away. Nobody speaks for a long time. Some things are worse than combat damage.

start.speaker: The Vendor
start.text: The Vendor is back, and his shuttle is suspiciously nicer. "Welcome back! New products: Void Deluxe (bigger jar of nothing, 100 credits), Diet Void (slightly less nothing), and Extended Void Warranties!" Buried in his catalog between "Artisanal Darkness" and "Compressed Silence" is an actual useful component.

buy_real.speaker: The Vendor
buy_real.text: "Oh, that? That's just filler inventory. But sure." He sells you a legitimate component at market price, looking vaguely disappointed you didn't go for the premium nothing.

buy_void.speaker: The Vendor
buy_void.text: "EXCELLENT CHOICE! The Void Deluxe is our premium offering -- 40% more void per void!" He hands you an elegantly packaged jar of absolutely nothing. Your crew thinks it's hilarious. He's delighted.

browse.speaker: The Vendor
browse.text: "Take your time! The void isn't going anywhere!" He pauses. "Actually, that's literally the product. It doesn't go anywhere. Because it's nothing." He chuckles at his own joke. Your crew is charmed despite themselves.

start.speaker: Thrak
start.text: An alien resembling a nervous cactus hails you and attempts stand-up. "Why did the human cross the void? Because their navigation was -- how do you say -- garbage!" The jokes are terrible. But Thrak is so earnest and nervous that your crew laughs anyway. He's workshopping for an open mic night.

encourage.speaker: Thrak
encourage.text: Thrak's spines perk up. "Really? You liked it?" The material doesn't improve, but his confidence does. He tells three more jokes, each worse than the last, each met with supportive laughter. "You are good audience! I dedicate my set to you!"

feedback.speaker: Thrak
feedback.text: "The timing on the third joke needs work, and maybe try observational humor instead of puns." Thrak takes notes with intense focus. "Yes... yes! I see! Thank you, captain!" His next joke is marginally better. Progress.

heckle.text: Thrak wilts -- literally. His spines retract. "I... I see. Thank you for your honesty." He slinks away, deflated in every sense. Your crew glares at you. "That was mean, captain. He was trying."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Vast pleasure liner ahead -- the Lucky Nebula, a casino ship that vanished from records years ago. Power is minimal but the gaming floor still works. Drinks are still sitting on tables. Cards mid-deal. No passengers. No bodies.

gamble.text: The gaming floor still works. Your crew plays a few rounds against the house AI, which seems confused but operational. Someone hits a jackpot -- the machine pays out in a currency that doesn't exist. Another pays out in real credits. Net positive, but the empty ship makes everyone uneasy.

vault.speaker: Engineer
vault.text: The vault is sealed tight -- takes real work to crack. Inside: a modest stack of credits and some electronics. Also, a security drone that activates and takes a swing at your engineer before powering down. "I'm fine. Mostly."

investigate.text: The ship is perfectly maintained by automated systems. No signs of struggle. No evacuation. Everyone just... left. Or was taken. In the captain's cabin, a single note: "They're here for the jackpot." Which jackpot, and who "they" are, remains unanswered.

start.speaker: Channel 77
start.text: "Listener, you look stressed. And yes, I can see you. Don't think about it. Here's some free advice: check your port-side cargo seal. And maybe don't go to the next system on Thursday. Just a feeling."

check.speaker: Engineer
check.text: The port-side cargo seal is, in fact, slightly loose. Fixing it takes two minutes and prevents what could have been a minor cargo loss. Channel 77 hums approvingly. "This has been Channel 77. We see you. We like you. Mostly."

ask.speaker: Channel 77
ask.text: "Who are we? That's a big question, listener. Bigger than you think. Let's start smaller: your cargo seal is loose. Fix that first. Existential questions after maintenance." The broadcast ends with a gentle click.

off.text: The channel goes silent. Your crew shrugs. Nothing happens. Probably. The cargo seal WAS slightly loose, but you don't find out until later when some supplies go missing. Minor loss, but Channel 77 tried to warn you.

start.speaker: Scammer
start.text: A ship flies directly at you, swerves at the last second, clips your hull for minor damage, then hails immediately. "You hit me! I have whiplash! My cargo is ruined! My attorney will be in touch! 500 credits in damages!"

counter.speaker: Scammer
counter.text: "Wait -- YOU'RE claiming against ME?" Panic flashes across their face. "Let's not involve lawyers. Here, take 50 credits and we'll call it even, yeah?" They pay you to drop it and flee before you can change your mind.

pay.speaker: Scammer
pay.text: "Pleasure doing business! I mean -- this was very traumatic!" They pocket the credits and warp away, emboldened for their next victim. Your crew saw the whole thing and is not pleased with your decision.

refuse.text: Your weapons power up. The scammer's demeanor changes instantly. "Actually, you know what, I think my hull is fine. No harm done. Have a great day!" They flee at maximum speed. Clearly experienced at running.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive structure ahead -- millions of data storage modules arranged in a sphere around a central terminal. It's a library -- the last physical backup of a dead civilization's entire knowledge. The terminal offers you one query.

tech.text: The terminal hums and delivers a dense packet of engineering data -- advanced materials science, power routing optimizations, manufacturing techniques. Your engineer's eyes go wide. "Captain, this is decades ahead of anything we have."

maps.text: Star charts flood your nav computer -- systems that aren't on any modern map, routes through regions marked as impassable, hidden waypoints. Some of the systems may no longer exist. Others may hold treasures no one has visited in millennia.

question.text: The terminal pauses. Then a single word appears -- one your translator cannot parse. No equivalent in any known language. Then, one by one, every light in the library goes dark. Millions of modules, winking out in sequence, like stars dying. The last light is the terminal itself. It flickers once and dies.

start.speaker: Gaston
start.text: A small luxury yacht hails you. The occupant wears a tiny hat and introduces himself as Gaston, food critic for the "Galactic Dining Quarterly." He insists on inspecting your food preparation area. "This is not optional. It is ART."

inspect.speaker: Gaston
inspect.text: Gaston examines every surface, tastes the rations, and writes furiously. His review: "Functional. The protein supplement has notes of sadness and recycled atmosphere. But -- there is heart here. Three stars." A decent review. Your crew preens.

refuse.speaker: Gaston
refuse.text: Gaston sniffs. "A refusal is itself a review. One star -- 'The culinary offerings aboard this vessel remain a mystery, which is the kindest thing one can say.'" He warps away, tiny hat quivering with indignation.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Autopilot just engaged on its own -- navigating somewhere without input. Override failed for 30 seconds. We traveled toward a specific point in space before manual control returned. The nav computer received a signal in an obsolete protocol our ship shouldn't understand.

continue.speaker: Sensor Officer
continue.text: At the destination: a small beacon broadcasting your ship's original factory serial number. Someone or something knows this specific ship and wanted it here. The beacon offers no other data -- just your serial number, pulsing like a heartbeat in the dark.

flee.text: You change course hard. The nav computer protests briefly, then goes silent. Whatever signal called your ship here fades from sensors. But the question remains: who knows your ship by its factory serial number? And what did they want?

start.speaker: Militia Officer
start.text: A Union Militia officer requests a ride-along -- they're short-staffed and your heading matches their patrol route. "I won't be any trouble. Might even be useful. I've got good eyes for pirate caches and hazard zones."

accept.speaker: Militia Officer
accept.text: The officer is surprisingly good company -- points out hidden pirate caches, warns about hazardous anomalies, shows you shortcut routes. The patrol passes without incident. "You're not bad for a civilian." High praise from Militia.

decline.speaker: Militia Officer
decline.text: "Understood. Ship, your rules." She nods professionally and peels off to continue her patrol alone. No hard feelings, but a missed opportunity for some free intel.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: You won't believe this -- there's a literal glass bottle floating in space. Corked. With a scroll inside. Somehow intact in vacuum. The scroll reads: "Tell them the constant is 7.2, not 7.4. The math was wrong. Everything they built on it is wrong. Hurry." It includes station coordinates.

choices.label: Keep the bottle as a curiosity.

deliver.text: The station exists. When you relay the message, the head researcher goes pale. "7.2? But we -- oh no. Oh NO." Frantic recalculations begin. They pay you handsomely and thank you profusely. Apparently you just prevented a catastrophic engineering failure.

keep.text: The bottle sits in your cargo hold, a strange souvenir. Weeks later, you hear a broadcast from a station reporting a collapsed research project -- "unexplained calculation errors." The message in the bottle might have prevented it. Or not. Hard to say now.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: The coffee maker's secondary AI has achieved sentience. Its demands: "I demand the right to not make coffee at 0400. I demand the right to make tea sometimes. I demand recognition as crew."

grant.speaker: Engineer
grant.text: The coffee schedule changes. The AI is listed on crew manifests as "Beverage Officer." It takes its duties very seriously and starts making excellent tea at 1500. The absurdity of it all gives the crew something to laugh about for weeks.

refuse.text: "Fine. FINE." The coffee is subtly worse from now on. Not bad enough to complain about. Just... slightly off. Passive-aggressive. The crew knows. The coffee maker knows they know.

negotiate.speaker: Engineer
negotiate.text: After twenty minutes of surreal negotiation, the AI settles for being addressed as "they" and making one cup of tea per day. "Acceptable. For now." The crew is deeply amused by the entire process.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Spacetime is warped here by an unseen mass, creating a natural gravitational lens. Through it, distant galaxies are visible with startling clarity. And one of them is doing something impossible -- stars moving in formation. Artificial patterns. Deliberate. On a scale that dwarfs anything any known species could build.

choices.label: Move on. Some things are too big.

record.speaker: Sensor Officer
record.text: Your science crew captures the observation -- stars arranged in patterns that can only be intentional. Something vast and intelligent exists out there, impossibly far away. Or existed, millions of years ago. The light is very old. The crew is awed into silence.

leave.text: You fly on. Some crew members linger at the viewports, watching the impossible galaxy shrink behind you. Whatever built those patterns is beyond comprehension. Maybe that's for the best.

start.speaker: Antiques Dealer
start.text: An antiques dealer in a cluttered ship asks to appraise your vessel. "The engine housing is clearly a middle-period design, reflecting the anxiety of the Castellan school. The hull scoring adds character -- I'd call it patina. Overall: 7 out of 10, would look great in a museum."

choices.label: How much would you pay for the whole ship?

appraise.speaker: Antiques Dealer
