appraise.text: His module-by-module commentary is entertaining and occasionally insightful. He identifies a component as rare pre-war manufacture worth more than you thought. "You've got a real collector's piece there. Don't sell it to just anyone."

offer.speaker: Antiques Dealer
offer.text: He squints, calculates, and offers a comically low amount. "I could do... 47 credits? It's more of a sentimental purchase." Your ship is worth thousands. He knows this. He's trying anyway.

decline.speaker: Antiques Dealer
decline.text: "Your loss! That patina won't last forever!" He floats away in his cluttered ship, appraising things that didn't ask to be appraised.

start.speaker: Void Mama
start.text: A pirate broadcast features a DJ calling herself "Void Mama." She plays music and takes calls from pirates across the sector. Her voice is like honey. "Next caller -- and if you request 'Starlight Serenade' one more time I'm aiming the antenna at a sun."

listen.text: Between songs, pirate callers chat about scores, patrol routes, and close calls. Valuable intel mixed with bragging. Your crew enjoys the music while noting down useful information. Void Mama plays a solid set.

call.speaker: Void Mama
call.text: "New caller! What'll it be?" She plays your request flawlessly. "Dedicated to the crew of that ship that just called in. You know who you are. So does everyone else now." Pirates in the area now know your frequency. Worth it for the music.

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: The signal traces to a hidden Fringe station not on any map. A pirate rest stop with a bar, repairs, and Void Mama broadcasting from a converted cargo bay. Useful coordinates to have, if you need to disappear or trade off the books.

start.speaker: Physicist
start.text: A physicist's transport has a sealed container that simultaneously contains and does not contain 50 tons of iron. "It's not a metaphor. I literally cannot determine the contents until someone opens it. And I'm too scared to check."

choices.label: Buy it sealed at a discount.
Suggest selling it to a university.

open.text: You crack the seal. The quantum state collapses. Inside: 50 tons of iron. Also, inexplicably, one perfectly healthy cat who meows indignantly. The physicist is both relieved and disappointed. "I suppose that answers that."

buy.speaker: Physicist
buy.text: "50% off market value. Because it might be nothing. Literally." You take the gamble. The container sits in your hold, its contents both existing and not existing. Your engineer refuses to go near it.

suggest.speaker: Physicist
suggest.text: Her eyes go wide. "A university! Of course! They'd pay a fortune for a macroscopic quantum superposition!" She pays you a consultant fee and warps away, container intact, to the nearest institution. "You've saved my career!"

start.speaker: Castellan Noble
start.text: A lone fighter pilot hails you. "I am Lady Voss of House Castellan. I challenge you to an honorable duel -- ship to ship, no fleeing. I need this victory to restore my family's honor. Will you accept?"

accept.text: The duel is fierce but disciplined. Lady Voss fights with Castellan precision. When her shields drop, she surrenders gracefully. "Well fought, captain. My honor is... deferred, not lost. Take this bounty -- you earned it." She salutes and warps away, dignity intact.

decline.speaker: Castellan Noble
decline.text: Lady Voss's expression doesn't change. "I understand. Not everyone seeks combat. But know this: next time we meet, I'll have found someone else to fight. And I'll be flying a much better ship." She nods curtly and departs.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A small void whale -- barely larger than our ship -- appears to have imprinted on us. It's following our maneuvers, occasionally bumping the hull gently. The crew finds it adorable. Your engineer notes minor hull contact damage. "But look at its FACE."

follow.text: The calf follows for a few minutes, bumping you twice more with enthusiastic affection. Then it gets bored, chirps, and drifts away. In its wake: a trail of rare mineral deposits. Void whale excrement. Disgusting. Valuable.

shoo.text: You attempt to shoo the calf away. It makes a sound your audio systems render as deeply, profoundly sad. Your entire crew turns on you. "CAPTAIN. HOW COULD YOU." The calf drifts away, dejected. Crew morale takes an immediate hit.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, we're detecting our own ship ahead. Damaged -- carbon scoring, breached hull, emergency lights. It's empty. Logs indicate it's from six hours in our future. The crew evacuated after an attack by unknown hostiles at a specific location. We have six hours to change the outcome.

choices.label: Avoid the location in the logs.
Go there prepared for a fight.

avoid.text: You change course, giving the logged coordinates a wide berth. Six hours pass without incident. Behind you, the damaged echo of your ship fades from existence, timeline corrected. Your crew breathes a collective sigh of relief.

confront.text: Forewarned is forearmed. You arrive at the coordinates ready for battle -- a swarm of autonomous drones, exactly as the logs described. But prepared and alert, you dismantle them efficiently. The damaged future ship fades from existence. Timeline rewritten.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three ships in a triangle formation are having a heated book club discussion on open comms. "The captain was CLEARLY a metaphor for institutional corruption--" "No, she was just a bad captain, you're reading too much into it--" "YOU'RE NOT READING ENOUGH INTO IT--"

join.speaker: Comm Channel
join.text: You offer your interpretation. One captain praises your insight. Another calls it "reductive." The third demands you pick a side. Your crew listens in, entertained. The argument continues for another hour.

recommend.speaker: Comm Channel
recommend.text: "Ooh, new blood! Send the title!" They add you to the group chat and schedule next month's read. Your crew is now involuntarily part of a deep-space book club. The reading list is surprisingly good.

choices.label: We're in a book club now.

flythrough.speaker: Comm Channel
flythrough.text: All three ships stop mid-sentence and hail you furiously. "YOU JUST FLEW THROUGH OUR FORMATION! We were building ATMOSPHERE!" The argument shifts from the book to you. Somehow this is worse.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Dozens of escape pods from different ships, eras, and factions -- arranged in a perfect circle. All empty. All opened from the outside. One pod is fresh -- days old. Its log: screaming, then silence, then a sound labeled as "laughter (non-human)." The circle has room for one more pod.

choices.label: Scan the fresh pod for clues.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: The fresh pod's biometrics show its occupant was alive and healthy until the moment the door opened. Then all life signs ceased simultaneously -- not gradually, not from trauma. Just... stopped. Whatever opened these pods, it's been doing this for a very long time.

leave.text: You don't linger. The circle of pods shrinks behind you -- dozens of empty shells, each a person who thought rescue had arrived. The gap in the ring watches your ship like an empty socket.

start.text: A tiny drone approaches and broadcasts: "ATTENTION VESSEL. You have been identified as AESTHETICALLY PLEASING. Your hull configuration rates 8.2 out of 10 on the Castellan Beauty Index. Suggested improvements: more chrome." It scans you (harmlessly) and flies away.

show.text: The crew is unreasonably pleased with an 8.2 rating from an anonymous drone of unknown origin. "We're a beautiful ship!" argues the engineer. "We should frame this." Morale improves for reasons that defy rational analysis.

swat.text: You take a shot at the drone. It dodges with surprising agility, broadcasting: "RUDENESS LOGGED. BEAUTY INDEX REVISED TO 7.1." Your crew is offended on the ship's behalf.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- remember that rogue terraformer we left alone? We're passing through the area again. The Impossible Garden has grown. It's a kilometer across now -- actual trees, a pond, and what appears to be a bench. Small luminous creatures flit between the branches. Someone put up a sign: "WELCOME TO NOWHERE PARK. PLEASE DON'T LITTER."

visit.text: Your crew steps out into breathable air growing from nothing. Trees sway in a breeze that shouldn't exist. The luminous creatures are curious and friendly. Someone sits on the bench and just... breathes. Real air, in the void. Nobody wants to leave.

choices.label: We can stay a few minutes.

admire.text: The garden glows softly in the void -- an impossible oasis. The terraformer chugs away happily. Life persists where it has no right to. Your crew watches through the viewports, oddly moved.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Automated message: "Hello, we've been trying to reach you about your ship's extended warranty. Your current coverage expired on [ERROR: DATE NOT FOUND] and you may be eligible for--"

block.text: You block the frequency. Ten seconds later, the same message arrives in a different voice. And a different accent. Your engineer sighs. "This thing has been spam-calling ships for forty years. It's... persistent."

listen.text: The message is seventeen minutes of increasingly unhinged warranty options. It ends with "press 9 to speak to an operator." You press 9. Channel 77 picks up, laughing hysterically. "Gets them every time. This has been Channel 77."

trace.speaker: Engineer
trace.text: The source is a defunct marketing company's server drifting in orbit around a dead planet. It's been autonomously spam-calling ships for forty years after everyone left. Nobody turned it off. It's oddly sad. Also, extremely annoying.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: There's a painting floating in the void. Oil on canvas, sealed in a protective case. It depicts... our ship. In this exact location. Finding a painting in the void. The detail is extraordinary -- you can see crew members through the painted windows. On the back: yesterday's date. And a signature you can't read.

choices.label: Leave it. This is too strange.

keep.text: The painting hangs in the ship's common area. Crew opinions are split between "beautiful" and "deeply unsettling." The detail really is extraordinary -- and the painted crew members are in the exact positions they were standing when you found it. Nobody can explain it.

leave.text: You leave the painting to drift. As you pull away, one crew member swears the painted ship in the canvas began drifting too, perfectly mirroring your movement. Nobody else saw it. The painting shrinks to a point and vanishes.

start.speaker: Toll Keeper
start.text: Someone built an actual bridge in space -- two pylons with a walkway, spanning nothing over nothing. A grumpy old man sits in a booth. "Five credits to cross. Don't give me that look. It's tradition."

choices.label: Ask why there's a bridge here.

pay.speaker: Toll Keeper
pay.text: He's surprisingly grateful. "Most people just go around. You've got respect for infrastructure." He hands you a homemade cookie. It's terrible. He made it himself. The gesture is genuine.

around.speaker: Toll Keeper
around.text: "COWARD!" he shouts as you fly past. The bridge stands resolute in the void, a monument to stubbornness. It's been here for decades. The old man shakes his fist.

ask.speaker: Toll Keeper
ask.text: "Why is there a bridge? Why is there anything? I built it. I maintain it. People pay. It's honest work." He pauses. "Also, I'm the only registered cultural landmark in three sectors. Try to demolish me. I dare you."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A luxury liner is parked in the void. ISD bureaucrats on a corporate retreat are doing trust falls in zero gravity. One has drifted away from the ship and is spinning, too embarrassed to call for help. The retreat coordinator hails: "Everything is FINE. This is a PLANNED EXERCISE."

rescue.text: You scoop up the spinning bureaucrat, who is profoundly grateful and also nauseous. They hand you their business card with trembling hands. "If you ever need a permit expedited, call me." Small ISD rep boost. Priceless gratitude.

charge.text: "How much?" the coordinator asks, panic barely concealed. You name a price. They pay without hesitation. The bureaucrat is retrieved, dignity in tatters. The retreat coordinator insists this will be "in the report as a valuable learning experience."

watch.text: Your crew watches the bureaucrat spin slowly while the retreat coordinator makes increasingly desperate reassurances. Eventually someone on the liner throws a rope. The whole scene is deeply entertaining.

start.speaker: Ship Whisperer
start.text: A lone traveler in a patched-up vessel hails you. "I'm a ship whisperer. I commune with machine spirits. Your ship is tired. It wants a rest. And it's worried about the port thruster -- says it feels 'tingly.'" The port thruster IS showing micro-fluctuations your engineer hasn't flagged yet.

choices.label: Pay for a healing session (100 credits).

pay.speaker: Ship Whisperer
pay.text: She places her hands on your hull and hums. This should be ridiculous. But a minor systemic issue in the port thruster -- one your diagnostics missed -- resolves itself. "Your ship says thank you. It's happier now." She flies off humming.

refuse.speaker: Ship Whisperer
refuse.text: "Your choice. But listen to your port thruster. It's trying to tell you something." She warps away. Within the hour, the port thruster develops a noticeable wobble. Your engineer finally notices and spends hours fixing it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two explorer ships are fighting over naming rights to a nebula. One wants "The Crimson Veil." The other insists on "Steve." They want you to cast the deciding vote.

crimson.speaker: Comm Channel
crimson.text: "The Crimson Veil it is!" One captain celebrates. The other sulks. "Steve was a perfectly good name." Minor reputation shifts as one explorer remembers your support and the other remembers your betrayal of Steve.

steve.speaker: Comm Channel
steve.text: "STEVE! I KNEW IT!" The Steve captain is ecstatic. The Crimson Veil captain is distraught. "You can't name a nebula Steve." "I just did." Star maps may or may not reflect this.

compromise.speaker: Comm Channel
compromise.text: A long silence. Then both captains simultaneously say: "...Huh." Another silence. "Steve's Crimson Veil. It's... actually perfect?" They agree, name you an honorary cartographer, and promise to send a fruit basket to the next station.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A familiar face appears in your cargo hold -- the stowaway teenager from before. "Look, I can explain--" They've been station-hopping trying to get back to you. The thing they're fleeing has followed them. They have intel on a Fringe smuggling operation that someone wants silenced.

choices.label: Give them a pod and safe coordinates.

protect.text: The kid's shoulders drop with relief. "Thank you. I won't let you down." They turn out to be genuinely skilled at engineering -- all that station-hopping taught them to fix anything. And the intel they carry is worth something to the right people.

authorities.text: The kid looks betrayed. "I trusted you." You hand them over to a Militia patrol. Safe, technically. But the look on their face haunts your crew. The intel dies with the bureaucratic process.

pod.text: You give them an escape pod and coordinates to a hidden station. "It's not ideal, but you'll be safe there." They nod, bravely. "You're still the best captain I ever stowed away on." The pod launches into the dark.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Small monument plaque on a dead satellite: "Halfway Point Between Two Places That Don't Matter -- Placed by the Fringe Collective Absurdist Society." Hundreds of travelers have scratched their names. Some are famous. There's space to add yours. Underneath all the names: "I was here first -- The Vendor."

sign.text: You scratch your name and your crew's alongside admirals, pirates, and legends. No mechanical effect. But it feels oddly significant -- a mark in the void that says 'we were here.' Your crew adds theirs too, grinning.

read.text: The names span centuries. A Castellan admiral. A legendary pirate. A famous explorer. Someone just wrote "HELP" which is either a cry for assistance or a very dark joke. The Vendor's mark is at the very bottom, barely visible.

leave.text: You pass the plaque without stopping. Halfway between two places that don't matter. The Vendor was here first, apparently.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Hull breach alarm! Wait -- false positive. Our hull is vibrating at a frequency that sensors read as structural failure. Actual cause: engine harmonics making the hull 'sing.' I can fix it now, or we could... enjoy it for a bit?

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: Quick adjustment to the engine harmonics. The singing stops. The hull falls silent. Efficient, responsible, and slightly disappointing. Your crew nods approvingly while secretly wishing you'd let it play.

enjoy.text: The crew starts singing along with the hull vibrations. Terrible harmonies echo through the ship. Someone breaks out a makeshift drum. It's the most fun anyone's had in weeks. A small hull stress crack opens. The crew considers this worth it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Tiny single-room station floating in the void. Sign reads: "CONFESSIONS -- ALL WELCOME -- NO JUDGMENT -- NO COST." Inside: one chair facing a dark screen. Speaking produces a warm voice: "I hear you." Scans show no AI, no recording equipment. Nothing.

visit.text: Crew members visit one at a time. Each comes back looking lighter -- like they set something down they'd been carrying. Nobody shares what they said. Nobody asks. The voice behind the screen, whatever it is, listens without judgment.

choices.label: Everyone needs someone to talk to.

investigate.speaker: Engineer
investigate.text: You look behind the screen. Nothing. Empty space. No speakers, no processing units, no hidden compartment. But when you sit in the chair, the warm voice speaks: "I hear you." It comes from everywhere and nowhere. Your engineer can't explain it. Nobody can.

leave.text: The confession booth drifts behind you. The sign faces the void: "ALL WELCOME." Whatever waits behind that dark screen continues to wait, patient and eternal.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A COTAC and Castellan diplomatic vessel are both complaining about each other claiming "the good parking spot." This is empty space. There are no parking spots. The dispute has been going for three hours.

choices.label: Park in the disputed spot yourself.

cotac.speaker: COTAC Ambassador
cotac.text: "Finally, someone with sense!" The Castellan diplomat huffs and repositions 50 meters to the left, which solves nothing but satisfies protocol. The COTAC ambassador tips you for your diplomatic acumen.

castellan.speaker: Castellan Ambassador
castellan.text: "A person of culture!" The COTAC diplomat sends a formal complaint that will take three years to process. The Castellan ambassador rewards your loyalty to proper space etiquette.

park.text: You park directly in the disputed spot. Both diplomats are FURIOUS. They hail you simultaneously, sputtering. Your crew is in tears laughing. Somehow, the Fringe network picks up the story and loves it.

start.speaker: Maz
start.text: A food truck. In space. A converted shuttle with a serving window, string lights, and a chalk menu. The owner, retired Bulwark cook Maz, ladles broth into a zero-G container. "Best ramen in the void. 15 credits. I go where the hunger is."

buy.speaker: Maz
buy.text: The ramen is transcendent. Rich broth, perfect noodles, an egg that has no business being this good in zero gravity. Your crew falls silent -- the silence of pure satisfaction. Maz smiles. "Come back anytime. I'll be somewhere."

pass.speaker: Maz
pass.text: "Suit yourself. The void'll make you hungry eventually." She waves and goes back to cooking. The smell of her broth lingers in your sensors long after she's out of range. Your crew looks at you accusingly.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An ISD automated buoy declares this region "under construction" and requests you reroute. Nothing is being constructed. The work order is seven years old and was never closed. The buoy recommends an alternate route that goes through a sun.

choices.label: Hack the buoy to close the work order.

ignore.text: You fly through. Nothing happens. The buoy logs a formal complaint that nobody will ever read. It has been logging complaints for seven years. Its database of ignored infractions is a monument to bureaucratic futility.

hack.speaker: Engineer
hack.text: Your engineer closes the seven-year-old work order. The buoy goes silent for the first time in its operational life. "Construction complete. Thank you for your patience. Have a nice day." You've done the ISD a favor. They'll never know.

reroute.text: You reroute as the buoy suggests, wasting fuel on a detour around literally nothing. The buoy thanks you for your patience. The alternate route, thankfully, does not actually go through the sun.

start.speaker: Court Poet
start.text: A small ship with the Drift Baron's sigil hails you. The Drift Baron's court poet recites: "O void, so dark and void-like in your voidness / The Baron stands upon it, tall and... moist?" They ask for honest feedback. The Baron's been trying to fire this poet for months.

encourage.speaker: Court Poet
encourage.text: "You really like it?!" They beam and immediately get worse. "O BARON, MOIST AND LORDLY--" The poem devolves. Somewhere, the Drift Baron feels a chill and doesn't know why.

criticize.speaker: Court Poet
criticize.text: "Hmm. 'Moist' is wrong, you say? What about 'damp'?" Over the next hour, the poem improves from terrible to merely bad. The poet is genuinely grateful. "You have the soul of an editor."

rewrite.text: You spend twenty minutes punching up the worst poetry in the sector. The result is passable. The poet transmits it to the Drift Baron, who hails you personally: "Finally. Thank you. I've been trying to fire this poet for months but they have a contract." He sends credits.

start.speaker: Collector
start.text: A quiet, serious woman in a nondescript ship offers to buy flight recorder data. She pays triple market value. When you ask why: "I'm listening to how people die. Not why. How. The last words. The sounds." She's searching for something specific in the recordings.

sell.speaker: Collector
sell.text: She pays generously and immediately begins listening, eyes closed. After a moment she shakes her head slightly. "Not this one either." Whatever she's looking for, it wasn't in your data. But she pays well regardless.

ask.speaker: Collector
ask.text: She hesitates, then: "A voice that matches my own. In a recording from before I was born." She doesn't elaborate. The statement hangs in the air, vast and unsettling. She pays you for your time, whether you sell data or not.

decline.speaker: Collector
decline.text: She nods. "I understand. Not everyone wants to traffic in last words." Her ship pulls away quietly, heading deeper into the void. She'll find another seller.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: SURPRISE! Your crew has organized a birthday party for whoever's birthday is closest -- they don't know yours, so they picked a date. There's cake made from ration bars, decorations from cargo manifests, and a card signed by everyone. Their pooled gift: a polished asteroid fragment, a lucky bolt, and 27 credits.

touched.text: Your crew sees the emotion on your face and cheers. The ration-bar cake is terrible. The decorations are lopsided. It's the best party anyone's ever thrown in the void. Someone cries a little. Nobody mentions it.

awkward.text: You shuffle your feet and mumble thanks. The crew is slightly deflated but rallies. The cake is still terrible. The party is still decent. "Happy birthday, captain. Even if it's not actually your birthday."

start.speaker: Repo Man
start.text: A professional ship marked "GALACTIC RECOVERY SERVICES" hails you. The pilot looks exhausted. "One of your modules is flagged as stolen property. Serial numbers match. I need it back. I'm just doing my job here, captain."

choices.label: Prove the module is legitimately yours.

negotiate.speaker: Repo Man
negotiate.text: "A payment plan? That's... actually the most reasonable response I've gotten all week." He runs the numbers. "12 installments of 25 credits. First payment now. Module stays. Everyone's happy." He looks relieved not to be fighting.

prove.speaker: Repo Man
prove.text: You pull up your trade records and receipts. He cross-references, scratches his head, then sighs. "Checks out. Module was laundered before you got it. Not your fault. Sorry for the hassle." He waves and moves on to his next headache.

refuse.speaker: Repo Man
refuse.text: He pinches the bridge of his nose. "Look, I don't want trouble either. But this goes in my report as 'non-cooperative' and someone nastier than me shows up next time." He backs off, radiating the weariness of a man who chose the wrong career.

choices.label: Take it up with my lawyer.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Dead satellite ahead with luminous graffiti. Three messages: "KILROY WAS HERE" in pre-spaceflight handwriting. Below: "NO HE WASN'T -- KILROY." Below that: "BOTH OF THESE ARE LIES -- ALSO KILROY." Analysis: all three written simultaneously by the same hand. The paint is dated 400 years in the future.

document.text: Your historian crew member, if you have one, goes very quiet. "That's not possible." The temporal dating is confirmed by three independent methods. Kilroy was here, wasn't here, and lied about both -- 400 years from now, in a handwriting style from before spaceflight. The data is unsettling but valuable.

add.text: You add: "[Your name] was here too." The luminous paint you use looks dim next to the original graffiti, which seems to glow brighter in response. As you pull away, your sensor officer swears a fourth line appears: "I KNOW."

leave.text: Kilroy was here. Or wasn't. Or both. You leave the satellite and its impossible graffiti to the void. The paint continues to glow, patient and paradoxical.

start.speaker: Gerald
start.text: An insurance adjuster's ship intercepts you. "Gerald Finch, claims investigation. I've been chasing you for three systems. Someone filed a cargo loss claim under your ship's ID eight months ago. You didn't file this, did you?"

cooperate.speaker: Gerald
cooperate.text: "Thank you. THANK you. You would not believe how rare cooperation is in this job." Gerald tracks down the scammer within days and sends you a cut of the recovered funds. His message: "You restored my faith in spacers. Slightly."

claim.speaker: Gerald
claim.text: Gerald narrows his eyes. "The claim IS in your name..." He processes it, but something in his expression says he knows. The credits arrive. So does a flag on your file. Gerald has seen things in this job. He sees you.

dismiss.speaker: Gerald
dismiss.text: "I'll be back. With questions." He says it like a man who has made this promise thousands of times and kept it every single one. Gerald is patient. Gerald is thorough. Gerald has seen things.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Voices on an unused frequency -- faint, overlapping, in languages that don't exist. They're not transmissions. They originate from the void itself. If you tune in, they become clearer: narrating your ship in real time with a 3-second delay. "The captain looks concerned. They should be."

listen.text: The voices narrate everything -- crew movements, your expression, the hum of the engines. Then they notice you listening. All voices stop except one, which whispers your name. Your actual name. Then silence. Total, complete silence on every frequency.

away.text: You tune away. The voices fade. Your comms officer looks shaken -- she heard them narrating her before you switched off. "They knew my name, captain. They said it like they'd been saying it for a long time."

start.speaker: Merchant
start.text: "Premium ship upgrades! Hull reinforcement, weapon upgrades, shield boosts!" He holds them up. They're stickers. Literally stickers. "REINFORCED" in block letters. A picture of a bigger gun. A shield with a plus sign. 10 credits each. He's completely transparent about it. "It's a sticker. You know it's a sticker. You want the sticker."

buy.speaker: Merchant
buy.text: You buy the stickers. Your crew applies them with irrational enthusiasm. "REINFORCED" now decorates the hull. A sticker gun covers an actual gun port. Nothing has changed mechanically. Morale soars anyway. The crew LOVES the stickers.

decline.speaker: Merchant
decline.text: "Your loss. These are collector's items. Limited edition. I printed them this morning." He floats away, stickers gleaming. Your crew is quietly disappointed. They wanted the stickers.

start.speaker: Convoy Captain
start.text: A passing trade convoy is running a skills challenge -- their crew vs. yours. Categories: fastest engine diagnostic, best zero-G cooking, most creative insult in three languages. "We do this every month. You're welcome to join the circuit."

accept.text: Your crew throws themselves into the competition. Engine diagnostics go well, cooking is debatable, and the insult round is surprisingly creative. Small prizes for each win -- credits, supplies, bragging rights. Win or lose, the crew had a blast.

decline.speaker: Convoy Captain
decline.text: "Aww. Next time, then. The circuit runs monthly -- look for our beacon." Your crew is mildly disappointed to miss the fun, but there's always next time.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Every transmission is reflecting back -- not immediately, but on variable delay. We're hearing our own hails from yesterday, engine noise from an hour ago, and impossibly, a transmission we'll make tomorrow. At the center: a single ancient satellite that shouldn't be capable of this.

listen.text: The future transmission is mundane -- routine status report, coordinates for your next jump. But there's a warning at the end: "Avoid the debris field at bearing 270." That's useful. Deeply unnerving, but useful. The echoes continue around you, fragments of past and future overlapping.

destroy.speaker: Engineer
destroy.text: One shot and the satellite breaks apart. The echoes stop immediately -- past and future fall silent. Normal comms resume. It's quieter now. Your crew is relieved. But you'll never know what tomorrow's transmissions might have warned you about.

leave.text: You exit the echo field. The fragments of past and future transmissions fade. The ancient satellite continues its impossible work, reflecting time back on itself, patient and unexplained.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Castellan nobles are playing golf in space -- launching balls from a yacht with mass drivers at a target beacon. One slices badly and the ball punctures a solar panel on a nearby Independent cargo ship. Both sides hail you to mediate.

settle.text: You broker a deal: the golfers pay for the panel damage plus a little extra. The cargo captain is satisfied. The golfers grumble but pay. Both sides tip you for your mediation. Justice, in its own absurd way.

join.text: You line up a shot with your ship's mass driver. It's wildly impractical and incredibly fun. Your crew cheers. The Castellan nobles are impressed by your enthusiasm if not your aim. The cargo captain is yelling. Nobody cares. Best game ever.

confiscate.text: "You can't do that! Those are antique clubs!" You confiscate the mass driver golf equipment. The golfers are furious. The cargo captain stops yelling. Nobody is particularly happy, but at least no more solar panels will die today.

start.text: Your entire crew falls asleep simultaneously. You're last -- in the seconds before unconsciousness, you see something outside the viewport. A shape, vast and slow, passing like a whale in dark water. You wake eight minutes later. Everyone wakes at the same moment. The ship moved 2000 units in a direction you weren't traveling. Every crew member had the same dream: a door in the void, opening.

check.speaker: Engineer
check.text: Eight minutes of nothing. Systems ran on autopilot -- or something ran them. The ship moved precisely, not drifting, as if guided. The course adjustment points toward empty space. At least, space that's empty on our charts. The crew is scared. You should be too.

ignore.text: Nobody talks about it. The dream fades. The course correction remains in the nav log like a scar. Your crew goes about their duties, but something has changed. The void feels less empty now. More watched.

start.speaker: COTAC Commissioner
start.text: A COTAC trade commissioner offers work: survey a potential new trade route. Fly the path, record hazards. Flat fee plus danger bonuses. "The route passes through low-security space. Moderate pirate risk. Good pay for honest work."

accept.text: The survey is smooth -- a few asteroid clusters to note, one suspicious sensor contact that turns out to be a lost cargo pod. Along the way, you discover a shortcut not on any map. You can report it for a bigger bonus or keep it for yourself.

decline.speaker: COTAC Commissioner
decline.text: "Understood. Can't blame a captain for knowing their limits. If you change your mind, the offer stands for 48 hours." She warps away to find another surveyor.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Several ships are gathered for a space funeral, launching a casket into a star. Mid-eulogy, a captain interrupts: "Wait. That's not my mother." The funeral home mixed up the caskets. Awkward silence. This isn't the right dead person.

choices.label: Offer to host the memorial on your ship.

help.text: A chain of calls across three stations traces the mix-up. The correct casket was accidentally shipped as "agricultural supplies" to a farming colony. The wrong casket's occupant turns out to be a minor celebrity. The funeral home's response: "Our deepest apologies and a 10% discount on future services."

choices.label: Glad I could help sort this out.

host.text: Your ship becomes an impromptu memorial venue. The mourners appreciate the gesture -- it's not about the casket, it's about remembering. Your crew serves refreshments. The eulogy is moving. Someone remarks that the deceased would have found this whole mix-up hilarious.

leave.text: Fair enough. Not your funeral. Literally. The mourners continue their awkward situation as you pull away. The wrong casket continues its journey toward the star, carrying someone else's loved one on an unplanned voyage.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Found the source of the module flickering -- a tiny creature nested in the wiring. A "circuit sprite" -- silicon-based, the size of a mouse. It's not malicious; it's nesting. It chirps when the engines start. It's actually kind of cute.

choices.label: Relocate it to a non-critical module.

relocate.speaker: Engineer
relocate.text: The sprite settles happily into a non-critical module, chirping contentedly. Its body heat actually creates a minor efficiency boost in the module. Your engineer is delighted. "Free heating! Best infestation ever."

adopt.text: The crew names it "Sparky" and it becomes the official ship mascot. It chirps at engine start, purrs near warm modules, and occasionally causes random flickering. The crew loves it. The module flickering is "character."

remove.speaker: Engineer
remove.text: The sprite chirps sadly as your engineer extracts it and releases it near a derelict. The flickering stops. The ship is a little quieter. Your crew watches the tiny creature drift toward the derelict, looking for a new home.

start.speaker: Pirate Captain
start.text: A pirate captain hails you -- not to rob you, but to settle a bet. "Which is better: synthetic coffee or real coffee? We tracked you down because you looked like a coffee person." Her crew is watching, money on the table.

real.speaker: Pirate Captain
real.text: Half the pirate crew cheers. The other half groans. Credits change hands. "Smart captain. Real coffee drinkers know quality." She sends you a small care package of genuine beans as thanks for settling the debate.

synth.speaker: Pirate Captain
synth.text: "SYNTHETIC?" She's appalled. The winning half of her crew celebrates loudly. "I... respect your conviction, even if it's wrong." She shakes her head and warps away, reconsidering her life choices.

tea.speaker: Pirate Captain
tea.text: Five-second silence. Both sides of the bet turn hostile. "TEA?" The pirate captain intervenes before her crew can open fire. "You've got guts. Terrible taste, but guts." She saves you from her crew's wrath and warps away, muttering.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict station ahead -- its atmospheric processors are venting, creating a visible gas cloud. It looks like fog in space. Flying through is disorienting -- sensors go haywire, visibility drops to visual only. Inside the cloud, the station sits like a haunted house in mist. The atmosphere is slowly freezing into glittering ice crystals.

enter.speaker: Engineer
enter.text: Sensors are useless in the cloud. Visual navigation only, feeling your way through freezing fog. The station yields decent salvage -- components, hull plating, a few credits worth of electronics. The ice crystals drift past the viewport like snow. Eerie, beautiful, and profitable.

observe.text: You watch from a safe distance as the fog expands, ice crystals catching distant starlight. The derelict station sits at the heart like a ghost ship in harbor mist. It's genuinely beautiful. The salvage remains untouched for someone braver.

start.speaker: Event Host
start.text: The Love Boat IV is hosting speed dating for spacers! "In space, no one can hear you flirt. But we can! Table four!" Your single crew members are looking at you hopefully.

allow.text: Your crew has a wonderful time. One comes back with a "space pen pal" who sends morale-boosting messages. Another matched with someone who turned out to be a pirate doing recon -- but a charming pirate. Everyone's smiling. Worth it.

refuse.text: Your crew watches the Love Boat IV recede, a floating beacon of romantic possibility, shrinking to a dot. "You never let us do anything," mutters someone. The ship feels a little lonelier than usual.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: ISD filing station ahead -- automated bureaucratic waypoint. It's stuck in an error loop: simultaneously requesting and approving its own demolition permit. This has been going on for three years. The paperwork is physically printing and venting into space, forming a paper asteroid.

reboot.speaker: Engineer
reboot.text: System reboot clears the error loop. The station goes quiet for the first time in three years. The paper asteroid drifts, a monument to bureaucratic entropy. The ISD should be grateful, though they'll never know why their filing station suddenly started working.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: The printer is industrial-grade -- high-quality components, barely worn despite three years of continuous operation. You extract it carefully. The station, now unable to print its contradictory permits, falls silent and begins processing the error correctly. Accidentally fixed.

add.text: You submit a formal request to the station: "Please demolish faster." The station accepts the request, files it, contradicts it, approves the contradiction, and prints twelve new forms. The paper asteroid grows slightly larger. Your crew is in tears laughing.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, an alien vessel just deposited a human on our airlock. There's a note taped to his chest. Translated badly, it reads: 'RETURN TO EARTH PLEASE. VERY SORRY. THOUGHT WAS INTERESTING. ACTUALLY QUITE BORING.'

choices.label: Drop him at the nearest station.

recruit.text: The man blinks in the light. He's been gone twenty years but seems oddly well-adjusted. Alien implants glow faintly beneath his skin -- turns out they make him a surprisingly capable engineer. He mutters something about 'probe calibration' and gets to work.

station.text: You drop him at the nearest station. Within a week he becomes a fixture at the bar, telling increasingly elaborate abduction stories. The bartender confirms he's great for business.

talk.speaker: Rescued Human
talk.text: "They kept me in a habitat pod. Fed me well, actually. I think they were studying me but got bored when I just... watched holovids all day. They called me 'the disappointment' in their language. Twenty years of being an alien's boring pet."

choices.label: Join my crew -- we're never boring.
Let's get you to a station.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark checkpoint blocks the travel lane ahead -- portable security station flanked by two gunships. "All vessels submit to crew scan. We're tracking a fugitive. This won't take long if you cooperate."

scan.speaker: Bulwark Officer
scan.text: The scan takes about a minute. "All clear. One of your crew has an unfortunate resemblance to our target, but biometrics don't match. You're free to go. Safe travels, captain."

vouch.speaker: Bulwark Officer
vouch.text: "Appreciate the cooperation, captain. We'll still need to run biometrics, but your willingness is noted." The scan confirms your crew is clean. The officer nods approvingly.

run.text: You punch the engines and blast past the checkpoint. The gunships give chase briefly but break off -- they're not leaving their post for one ship. Your crew cheers, but Bulwark won't forget this.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the crew has called a... retrospective meeting. About your captaincy. They have an agenda. And a list. It's surprisingly detailed.

graceful.text: You sit through comments ranging from 'the food situation could be better' to 'that time you flew us into an asteroid field was questionable.' Final rating: 7 out of 10, would crew again. Your humility earns genuine respect.

argue.text: You contest every point with passionate counter-arguments. The crew finds this hilarious rather than intimidating. The meeting devolves into a roast. Nobody's morale changes because they're too busy laughing.

fire.text: "You're all fired!" you announce. Silence. Then the realization that you can't actually fly the ship alone. You rehire everyone immediately. Morale improves because now they know you need them.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A man in a tiny pod sits motionless in open space, a sensor tether extending outward like a fishing line. He waves. "Quiet down, you'll scare the catch. ...I'm fishing. In the void. You'd be surprised what you pull in out here."

choices.label: Leave the man to his hobby.

learn.speaker: Void Fisherman
learn.text: "It's all about patience and sensor calibration. Cast your tether, wait for a mass signature, reel it in." He teaches your crew the basics. They're oddly enthusiastic about it. Fifteen years of practice has made this man a master of finding useful debris.

catches.speaker: Void Fisherman
catches.text: He produces a photo album. Most catches are space debris. One photo shows a 40-kilo data buoy. Another shows a live, very confused alien. "Threw that one back," he says proudly. "Catch and release. It's only sporting."

leave.text: You leave the fisherman to his quiet vigil. As you pull away, your sensors ping -- he's caught something. A small, happy whoop echoes over the comms before he cuts the channel.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A wealthy Independent trader named Ren hails you with a slick pitch: "I'm funding a new mining operation -- ground floor opportunity, projected 300% returns. My track record is... mixed. But this one's different. They're always different."

invest.speaker: Ren
invest.text: "Smart move, captain! I'll have your returns wired within the quarter. Probably. Almost certainly." He transfers the investment documents with a flourish. His confidence is either infectious or delusional.

decline.speaker: Ren
decline.text: "No hard feelings. Can't win 'em all. If you change your mind, I'll be around -- I'm always around." He tips an imaginary hat and his yacht glides away.

counter.speaker: Ren
counter.text: He listens to your pitch with growing interest. "You know what? I like your style. Tell you what -- I'll keep you in mind for future opportunities. Here's a little good-faith gesture." He transfers some credits and trade route data.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Mayday! This is Castellan Transport Valen -- we have a passenger in critical condition and our medical bay is offline. We need a ship with medical facilities immediately. The patient is... politically significant."

choices.label: We have medical facilities. Dock up.
We'll escort you to the nearest station.

surgery.speaker: Medic
surgery.text: Your medical crew gets to work. It's touch and go -- the patient is a Castellan noble with internal injuries from a shuttle accident. Hours of careful work, and... the noble pulls through. Their family is profoundly grateful.

escort.text: You fly alongside the transport, pushing hard for the nearest station. It's a tense few hours, but you make it. The station medical team takes over and the patient stabilizes. The transport captain shakes your hand.

refuse.text: The transport's captain curses and cuts the channel, desperately hailing other ships. Your crew is quiet. Someone mutters about the oath of the void.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: The Collector's ship appears, display cases even fuller than before. "Ah, a return visitor! I've acquired new pieces -- a bottled thought from a dying star, the second-best joke ever told on actual paper. I'm also selling duplicates. I don't need two of anything. That's the point of collecting."

buy.speaker: The Collector
buy.text: Among the duplicates you find a useful module at roughly five times market value. "I know the price seems steep," he says, adjusting his monocle. "But can you really put a price on provenance? Yes. This price. Exactly this price."

purchased.speaker: The Collector
purchased.text: "Excellent taste. That piece was on the *Starfall Meridian* when it crossed the Kessler Belt. Or so I'm told." He wraps it with absurd care.

sell.speaker: The Collector
sell.text: He examines your offering with a jeweler's loupe. "Interesting. Not unique, but... characterful. I'll give you a fair price." His definition of fair is actually generous -- collectors pay premiums for novelty.

admire.speaker: The Collector
admire.text: "A fellow appreciator! Most people just want to buy or sell. Sometimes the joy is simply in seeing." He gives you a guided tour. Your crew is fascinated. He slips you a small curio as a parting gift.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a mass signature ahead -- planet-sized, exerting real gravitational pull. But it's invisible across all spectra. It's on no charts. Instruments say it's there. Eyes say it isn't.

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: You approach the coordinates. Nothing visual. But instruments go haywire -- temperature, radiation, gravity, all fluctuating wildly. Your hull groans under shifting gravitational tides. Whatever this is, it doesn't want to be understood.

probe.speaker: Sensor Officer
probe.text: The probe transmits for 4.7 seconds before signal loss. Its final data burst, when analyzed, appears to be a star map of a galaxy that doesn't exist. The coordinates are precise, detailed, and completely impossible. The mass sits where it has always been. It has always been here.

choices.label: Archive the data and move on.

skirt.text: You give the anomaly a wide berth. Smart. Safe. Your crew watches the empty space on sensors as you pass. The gravitational readings spike once -- almost like a heartbeat -- then settle.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, every numerical readout on the ship just flickered to 333. Distance: 333. Fuel: 333. Credits: 333. It lasted exactly 3.33 seconds. A Channel 77 broadcast just activated: 'Three-three-three. Nice. Moving on.' Everything's back to normal.

shrug.text: The universe winks at you and moves on. Your crew exchanges puzzled looks. Nothing is damaged, nothing is changed. Just a moment of numerical synchronicity in the endless void. Your lucky number, apparently.

diagnostic.speaker: Engineer
diagnostic.text: "Diagnostics are clean. No intrusion, no malfunction. The number 333 appeared simultaneously across every system for exactly 3.33 seconds. That's... not supposed to be possible. I have no explanation." She looks genuinely unsettled.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cluster of ships is broadcasting on an open channel: "Welcome to Captains Anonymous. I'm Marcus, and I haven't micromanaged my crew in three days." "Hi Marcus." They're inviting you to join the session.

join.text: Topics include 'Setting Boundaries With Your Engineer,' 'You Can't Fix Everything By Flying At It,' and 'When Your Crew Likes The First Mate Better.' It's played for laughs, but the advice is surprisingly solid. Your crew appreciates a captain willing to learn.

listen.text: You eavesdrop on the session. One captain describes flying into a nebula because 'it looked interesting.' Another admits to naming their ship's systems after ex-partners. It's entertaining and oddly relatable.

pass.text: You fly on. Marcus calls after you: "The offer's always open! We meet weekly!" Your crew looks mildly disappointed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, our warp afterimage from the last jump isn't fading. It's been sitting at the origin point for hours. Other ships are reporting it too. It's not a ship, not a hologram -- just a persistent image of us, frozen in space.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: You return to the origin point. The afterimage is there -- a perfect silhouette of your ship in fading light. Scans show nothing physical. After six hours, it blinks. Once. Like an eye. Then it vanishes. Sensor logs confirm the blink.

ignore.text: You fly on. Six hours later, your sensor officer quietly reports the afterimage vanished. Just before it did, it blinked. She shows you the sensor log. One blink. Like an eye closing.

choices.label: Best not to think about it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A newly commissioned Independent ship is performing its maiden voyage naming ceremony -- champagne bottle, speeches, the works. They invite you to witness. The ship is a tiny cargo shuttle named 'DEATH'S EMBRACE III.' The crew is completely sincere.

choices.label: Say a few words of congratulations.

speech.text: You deliver a short speech about the void, adventure, and the bond between a crew and their ship. The new crew cheers. Their captain wipes away a tear. They press a gift into your hands -- a small good-luck charm and some supplies.

watch.text: The ceremony is earnest and slightly chaotic -- the champagne bottle bounces off the hull without breaking on the first two tries. When it finally shatters, everyone cheers. They send you a small gift as thanks for witnessing.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Automated warning buoys mark a quarantine zone. A Bulwark patrol hails: "Area restricted. Station went dark two weeks ago. Something aboard is still moving but no life signs register. Turn back." The officer sounds scared.

choices.label: Try to sneak past for salvage.

respect.speaker: Bulwark Officer
respect.text: "Smart decision. Whatever's in there... we're waiting for a specialist team. Nobody goes in, nobody comes out. Appreciate your cooperation, captain."

investigate.speaker: Bulwark Officer
investigate.text: "You want to go IN there? ...Actually, we've lost two recon teams. If you're volunteering..." The station interior is dark, wet, and wrong. Walls pulse with organic growth. You grab what data you can and get out fast.

choices.label: Seal it behind us. Burn it all.

sneak.text: You slip past the patrol and dock with the station. The salvage is excellent -- abandoned cargo, intact modules. But the walls are coated in something organic. Something moves in the dark. You grab what you can and run.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A courier drone docks with your ship and deposits a package: fan mail. Apparently your exploits were featured on a Fringe entertainment broadcast. Inside: handwritten letters, a hand-knit sweater in your ship's colors, and a drawing of your ship by 'Ella, age 8.'

choices.label: Read the letters to the crew.
Pin Ella's drawing on the bridge.

read.text: Letters range from heartfelt ('You're an inspiration') to unhinged ('MARRY ME CAPTAIN'). One just says 'COOL' in very large handwriting. The sweater doesn't fit anyone properly. Your crew is delighted. Someone frames Ella's drawing for the mess hall.

pin.text: Ella's drawing goes on the bridge wall. It's genuinely charming -- your ship rendered in crayon, surrounded by stars and a smiling sun. The crew takes turns wearing the sweater ironically. One letter asks for an autograph. Another asks if you're single.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two armed fleets face off over disputed salvage -- Castellan and Union Militia. An Independent diplomat hails you: "Please, they'll listen to a neutral party. Neither wants to fire first but neither will back down. Can you help?"

mediate.text: Hours of tense negotiation. You propose splitting the salvage based on each fleet's proximity when they found it. Both sides grumble but agree. The diplomat sags with relief. Both faction commanders nod grudgingly in your direction.

castellan.text: You throw your support behind the Castellan claim. The Militia captain scowls and withdraws -- outnumbered with you added to the equation. The Castellan commander is grateful. The Militia will remember this.

militia.text: You back the Militia's claim. The Castellan fleet withdraws with cold dignity. The Militia captain claps you on the back over comms. The Castellan won't forget this slight.

leave.text: You leave the standoff behind. Hours later, distant explosions light up the sector. Trade routes in the area will be disrupted for a while.

start.speaker: The Vendor
start.text: The Vendor is different this time. Quiet. His jars are full -- not of nothing, but of light. Actual, warm, visible light in glass containers. "I went somewhere," he says softly. "Between the frequencies. Where the void remembers being a star."

choices.label: Buy a jar of light. (100 credits)

buy.speaker: The Vendor
buy.text: The jar is warm in your hands. The light inside it pulses gently, like a heartbeat. It's real. "Take care of your crew," he says, and for the first time he isn't joking. "The void is getting darker."

ask.speaker: The Vendor
ask.text: "There's a place between radio frequencies where things still glow. I found it by accident. Stayed too long. Brought back what I could." He holds up a jar. The light inside shifts like a living thing. "These are memories. Star memories. They keep a ship warm."

leave.text: You pull away from the Vendor's shuttle. He watches you go with an expression you can't quite read. Something between gratitude and warning.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cargo ship has suffered a catastrophic bay failure, scattering several thousand rubber ducks across a wide area. They float in an expanding cloud, catching starlight like a surreal yellow nebula. The captain is mortified. A passing Xenoculture ship is taking photos.

collect.speaker: Cargo Captain
collect.text: "You're a saint. An absolute saint." It takes hours. Your crew is covered in rubber ducks. The captain pays you generously for your time and your dignity. The Xenoculture ship got some incredible photos.

buy.speaker: Cargo Captain
buy.text: "You want to BUY them? They're for a colony's children but... at this point I'll take what I can get." You acquire several thousand rubber ducks at a steep discount. They have to be worth something to someone.

choices.label: I am now a duck merchant.

enjoy.text: Your crew watches the duck nebula in quiet wonder. It's absurd. It's beautiful. The cargo captain wails in the background. The Xenoculture ship labels it 'Temporary Installation #4,091' in their cultural database.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the crew's been telling ghost stories during the quiet stretch. Ship-specific ones -- 'They say if you walk deck 3 at 0300, you can hear the original crew.' They've spooked themselves pretty good.

choices.label: Join in with your own story.
Tell them to knock it off.

join.text: You tell a story about a captain who flew into the void and never came back -- except the ship did, empty, still running, still warm. Your crew is delighted and terrified. Great bonding. Then someone asks: 'Does anyone remember when the new guy came aboard?' Awkward silence.

fun.text: The stories continue. One tale, from the newest crew member, describes a stowaway from the void who didn't need to breathe. It stops being funny when no one can remember that crew member boarding. They did, of course. Probably.

stop.text: The ghost stories stop. Morale dips slightly from having their fun curtailed. But at least nobody's checking under their bunks anymore. Well, fewer people are.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the Drift Baron's flagship is on long-range sensors. Full escort fleet -- at least twenty ships. A moving city in the void. Comms chatter is fascinating: logistics reports, poetry recitals, an argument about whose turn it is to cook.

monitor.speaker: Sensor Officer
monitor.text: You listen for an hour. The fleet's logistics chatter reveals planned movements -- useful for avoiding future toll zones. Someone in the fleet is reading poetry about 'the loneliness of command.' It's actually quite good.

hail.speaker: The Drift Baron
hail.text: A pause. Then: "Well. Bold. Very few hail me uninvited. I'll remember you, captain -- and I mean that in the way that could go either direction. Carry on. And next time you're in my space... we'll talk tolls." He sounds amused.

hide.text: You cut emissions and drift. The fleet passes within visual range -- enormous, organized, terrifying in its casual power. Nobody notices you. Your crew breathes again once the last ship clears sensors.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the crew insists on a talent show. Acts include a magic trick using engine components, a dramatic reading from the ship's manual, interpretive dance about 'the loneliness of the void,' and someone who makes engine sounds with their mouth. You're judging.

generous.text: You applaud everything enthusiastically. Even the manual reading. The crew glows with appreciation. The winner -- magic trick, hands down -- is insufferably smug for three days but everyone's spirits are high.

choices.label: Best talent show in the void.

harsh.text: "Technical execution: 3. Artistic merit: 2. The interpretive dance was overwrought." Your crew takes it as a challenge. One member practices their act obsessively and is noticeably sharper at their job afterward. Competition breeds excellence.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You intercept a coded signal advertising a pop-up black market -- coordinates, time window, no questions asked. The goods are real, the prices excellent, the risk of a Bulwark raid also real.

shop.text: A cluster of ships in loose formation, selling everything from stolen military hardware to suspicious salvage. Prices are the best you've seen. You shop fast, keep your head down, and leave before any patrols show up.

report.speaker: Bulwark Officer
report.text: "Appreciated, captain. We'll handle it. These pop-ups are a menace. Here's something for your trouble." The Bulwark dispatches a patrol. The market scatters before they arrive, but the gesture is noted.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, swarm of about fifty small mining drones ahead. They've lost their mothership and are executing their last command: 'MINE NEAREST MASS.' The nearest mass is us. They're making sad little beeps.

hack.speaker: Engineer
hack.text: "Kill command sent... and accepted. The swarm powers down. Fifty little drones floating dead in space, each one making one final sad beep." Your engineer looks oddly guilty. "They were just doing their job."

outrun.text: The drones are slow. Painfully slow. You outpace them easily. They follow for a while, confused beeping fading on sensors, then give up and resume wandering. Someone else's problem now.

reprogram.speaker: Engineer
reprogram.text: "Got it! Rewrote their mothership designation to... us. They think we're home now." The swarm forms up around your hull, docile and eager. Fifty tiny miners, ready to work. They still beep, but happily now.

choices.label: Welcome to the fleet, little guys.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: "Captain! That's DAVEN ROKE! From 'Void Justice'!" A famous holovid actor's yacht is hailing you. The actor wants to shadow you for 'research' on a role as a spacer captain. Your crew is star-struck.

choices.label: Sure, shadow us for a while.

agree.speaker: Daven Roke
agree.text: Roke follows for hours, asking annoying questions and getting everything wrong. 'So the warp drive runs on... feelings?' He's genuinely likeable though. At the end, he pays a generous consulting fee. "This is PERFECT material."

choices.label: The resulting holovid will be terrible.

decline.speaker: Daven Roke
decline.text: "Totally understand. Method acting isn't for everyone. Here -- for your time." He sends a small payment and an autographed photo. Your crew is disappointed but the photo goes on the bridge wall.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Long-range comms are picking up a signal that's degrading in real time -- words dissolving into static. "We found... [static]... it's not... [static]... please don't... [static]..." The signal is crumbling apart.

choices.label: Record what we can and move on.

triangulate.speaker: Sensor Officer
triangulate.text: By the time you reach the source coordinates, the signal is pure noise. The location is empty. But the background radiation is slightly elevated -- something used tremendous energy here recently. A single piece of hull plating floats where the signal originated. It's warm.

record.text: You capture what fragments you can before the signal dissolves entirely. The recording is mostly static, but the fragments -- those desperate, broken words -- haunt your comms officer for days.

cut.text: Silence fills the bridge. Your crew looks at each other. Whatever that was, whoever that was -- they're gone now. The void keeps its secrets.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Halt, um, vessel. This is... [paper rustling]... ISD Patrol Ship Vigilant. Please state your, uh, intentions." The voice is young and nervous. A senior officer coaches from off-screen: "Say 'prepare to be scanned.'" "Oh right -- prepare to be scanned!"

cooperate.speaker: ISD Intern
cooperate.text: The scan is routine and finds nothing. "All clear! Thank you for your cooperation and, um, patience." A whisper from off-screen: "Good job, kid." Then, brightly: "You were my first real ship! That was great!" The senior officer sighs audibly.

tease.speaker: ISD Intern
tease.text: "Is this your first patrol?" you ask. Flustered silence. "N-no! I've done... several. Many." More coaching from off-screen. The scan completes. "You're clear! And... yes. It was my first. Please don't tell anyone." Your crew is charmed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a marker in the void. Plain, official-looking, centuries old. It reads: 'HALFWAY.' Navigation confirms we're exactly between two significant locations. But those locations didn't exist when this marker was placed.

examine.speaker: Sensor Officer
examine.text: There's a small compartment in the base. Inside: a coin, ancient, predating space travel. On one side -- your ship. Not your ship type. YOUR specific ship, every detail perfect. The coin is older than the technology to build your vessel. Much older.

note.text: You log the marker's position and continue. Halfway between what and what? Between then and now, maybe. Between asking and knowing. The void doesn't answer questions you're not ready to hear.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain... the crew has been keeping pets. A hamster in engineering, a lizard in navigation, a plant in the galley that someone insists is 'basically a pet.' Regulations technically forbid this. The hamster has a tiny hard hat.

allow.text: The hamster, named Captain Whiskers, becomes an unofficial crew mascot. The lizard keeps navigation warm. The plant in the galley is growing faster than any plant should, but nobody mentions that. Morale soars.

enforce.text: "Regulations are regulations." The crew complies. The hamster goes into storage. The lizard vanishes. The plant... is still there, actually. Nobody can move it. It appears to have grown into the counter. Morale plummets.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An alien hails you and launches into an animated conversation in an unknown language, clearly believing you're someone else. They're excited, gesturing wildly, showing what appears to be baby photos. You have no idea what's happening.

nod.text: After two minutes of confused smiling, the alien pauses, checks their display, and makes a noise your translator renders as 'profound embarrassment.' They disconnect. Thirty seconds later, they hail again: "Sorry. Wrong ship. Nice hull though."

explain.text: Your attempts to communicate only make the alien more enthusiastic -- they think you're agreeing with everything. Eventually they check their display, realize the error, and disconnect in flustered haste. A brief follow-up: "Sorry. Wrong ship. Nice hull though."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We're passing through the remnants of a recent battle -- not wrecks, but unexploded ordnance. Missiles that missed targets, mines that didn't arm, torpedo shells drifting in lazy spirals. Each one individually harmless, but the density is concerning.

choices.label: Clear a path with point defense.

navigate.text: Slow, careful flying through the debris. A few tense moments as you drift past a torpedo that's still spinning, but nothing detonates. You emerge on the other side intact and slightly sweaty.

clear.speaker: Engineer
clear.text: Point defense makes short work of the nearest ordnance. The chain of small detonations is briefly spectacular. "Clear lane established. Nice fireworks show, captain."

scavenge.speaker: Engineer
scavenge.text: "Careful extraction... careful... got it." Your crew pulls apart the unexploded ordnance for raw materials. It's nerve-wracking work but the salvage is decent -- composite casings, electronics, power cells.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Your ship receives a misdirected personal ad: 'Single Castellan pilot, 34, enjoys long warp jumps, candlelit airlocks, and ships that know how to maneuver. No pirates. Serious inquiries only.'

forward.text: Channel 77 broadcasts it immediately. The pilot is mortified but receives hundreds of responses. Channel 77 adds commentary: "We're not a dating service, but we ARE a public service. Good luck out there, lonely pilot."

delete.text: You delete the message. Your comms officer has already screenshotted it for crew entertainment. It circulates the ship for days. 'Candlelit airlocks' becomes a running joke.

respond.text: You send a polite response explaining the misdirection. The pilot is mortified but grateful you didn't broadcast it. They send a small thank-you gift of credits. 'You're the first decent person I've met in the void,' they say. The irony is palpable.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A natural micro-wormhole -- too small and unstable for transit -- has been turned into a tourist attraction by a Fringe merchant. "25 credits to look through! That's light from SOMEWHERE ELSE!" A gift shop sells 'I SAW THROUGH SPACE' data chips.

look.text: You look through the micro-wormhole. You see... the other side, about 30 meters away. "It's about the EXPERIENCE," the merchant insists. Your crew takes photos. Despite everything, morale goes up. It IS technically a wormhole.

souvenir.speaker: Merchant
souvenir.text: "Excellent choice! This data chip contains a full recording of the wormhole from seventeen angles. Premium package!" It costs 15 credits and contains approximately 3 seconds of footage of a tiny shimmer in space.

pass.text: "Your loss! This wormhole won't be here forever! Probably!" Your crew looks wistfully at the attraction as you pass. Someone mutters about never getting to do anything fun.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, a manufacturer's drone delivered a recall notice for our reactor model. Known flaw: 'intermittent temporal displacement of the exhaust manifold.' Free replacement at nearest station. But... I've grown attached to this one.

replace.speaker: Engineer
replace.text: "Fine. But I'm taking photos." You dock and swap the reactor. The replacement is objectively better -- more efficient, more stable, zero chance of temporal hiccups. Your engineer pats it sadly. "It's just not the same."

choices.label: You'll bond with the new one.

keep.speaker: Engineer
keep.text: "I knew you'd understand." She hugs the reactor casing. There's a small chance of temporal hiccups -- briefly experiencing the same 10 seconds twice -- but your engineer's loyalty is unwavering. She's already named it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's an ancient ship on sensors -- documented for centuries, always the same course, same speed, never stopping. Scans show the interior is full of active cryopods. Thousands of them. All occupied. Where it's going, no one knows.

hail.text: No response. The ship doesn't acknowledge your transmission. It doesn't acknowledge anything. As it passes, one light in one window turns on, then off. Your comms officer swears it was timed to your hail. The ship continues its eternal journey.

observe.speaker: Sensor Officer
observe.text: You fly alongside for an hour. The ship is ancient beyond belief -- hull scarred by millennia of micro-impacts. The cryopods inside are functioning perfectly. Who sleeps within has spawned entire academic disciplines. As you break away, one light blinks. Once.

pass.text: The ancient ship drifts past in silence. Your crew watches it go. It will still be traveling when everyone on your ship is dust. One light blinks as it passes. Maybe it was a sensor glitch. Maybe.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Floating debris includes what appears to be a music box -- a mechanical device in a sealed case. When retrieved, it plays a melody everyone finds hauntingly familiar but nobody can identify. It's not in any music database.

listen.text: Every person who hears the melody describes the same image: a blue sun over a silver ocean. No such place exists. The music box has no manufacturer's mark and the mechanism has too few parts to function. It plays anyway. Your crew is quiet for a long time afterward.

study.speaker: Engineer
study.text: "This shouldn't work. There aren't enough gears. The spring is decorative. But the music..." She describes a blue sun over a silver ocean, the same vision every listener reports. The box defies analysis. It simply plays.

choices.label: Some things aren't meant to be understood.

leave.text: You leave the music box floating in the void. As you pull away, your crew hums a melody none of them can identify. A blue sun. A silver ocean. The box plays for no one.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two ships broadcast distress signals simultaneously: "MAYDAY MAYDAY, we're DYING!" / "MAYDAY, we're dying MORE!" They're not dying. They both want salvage priority on a nearby wreck and first-rescued gets first-pick.

both.text: You 'rescue' both ships, which immediately race each other to the wreck at full speed. They were never in danger. Your crew watches the race with amusement. Both captains send you a small thank-you for maintaining the charade.

claim.text: While both ships play dead, you casually fly to the wreck and start salvaging. Outraged sputtering on two channels simultaneously. Both captains abandon their ruse and race over, but you've already grabbed the best parts. Devious. Hilarious.

watch.text: You ignore both signals. After an awkward minute, they stop faking and race to the wreck under their own power, bickering the whole way. Your crew enjoys the show.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A dying ship hails -- engines failing, life support critical. The captain, an elderly Fringe spacer, doesn't want rescue. She wants to confess. "I buried something on a moon thirty years ago. Evidence of a COTAC conspiracy. I was too scared to use it. Maybe you're braver."

listen.speaker: Dying Captain
listen.text: She recites coordinates with practiced precision -- she's rehearsed this moment. "Sealed container, two meters down. Don't let them bury it again." She smiles, cuts the channel, and her ship goes dark. The coordinates are logged.

rescue.speaker: Dying Captain
rescue.text: "I said I don't want--" You dock anyway. She's furious. Then exhausted. Then, slowly, grateful. Over coffee in your mess hall, she provides the coordinates and the full story. It's bigger than she let on.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the ship's OS just initiated a mandatory software update. Systems are going offline one by one -- weapons, shields, navigation. A cheery automated voice keeps saying 'Improving your experience!' We're defenseless for about thirty seconds per system.

ride.speaker: Engineer
ride.text: Systems come back online one at a time. The update provides no noticeable improvement. The changelog reads: 'Fixed a bug where everything worked correctly. Minor stability improvements. Added new loading screen tips.' One tip: 'Try not to die.'

cancel.speaker: Engineer
cancel.text: "I can't cancel it -- it's hardcoded as mandatory. Who designs these things?" The update completes. No improvements detected. The new loading screen tip reads: 'If you're reading this, you survived the update. Congratulations.'

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Captain Dread is BACK! And this time I mean BUSINESS!" It's the Worst Pirate again. He's improved -- marginally. His ship is slightly better, his script memorized, and his weapons point the right direction. He still can't bring himself to actually fire.

encourage.speaker: Captain Dread
encourage.text: "You... you believe in me?" He manages a single warning shot that misses by a kilometer. "DID YOU SEE THAT? I FIRED! I actually fired!" He's so proud. Your crew applauds. He weeps openly.

rob.text: You turn the tables and demand HIS cargo. Stunned silence. Then: "That's... that's not how this..." He has surprisingly decent goods -- turns out he's an excellent pirate when no one is watching. He hands them over, bewildered.

wave.speaker: Captain Dread
wave.text: "Wait! I had a whole speech! I practiced!" You wave and fly past. He sighs on an open channel. "They never let me finish. One day. ONE DAY."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You pick up a private channel between two station operators gossiping: "Did you hear about the ship that brought a void whale calf into dock? Docking clamps couldn't hold it." "No! What about the captain who paid the Drift Baron's toll in rubber ducks?"

eavesdrop.text: The gossip continues -- faction movements, station sales, who's dating who in the patrol fleet. Useful intel mixed with delicious scandal. Then one says: "Wait -- is someone listening?" You hold your breath. "...Nah. Anyway, about that trader..."

announce.text: Embarrassed silence. Then: "Well? Do you have any gossip?" Your crew shares a few stories. The operators are delighted. "Best eavesdropper we've had all week. Come back anytime." They share some useful local intel as thanks.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the warp drive is hiccupping. We're micro-jumping 100 meters in random directions every few seconds. Disorienting but not dangerous. From outside, we apparently look like we're strobing across space.

wait.speaker: Engineer
wait.text: "The warp equivalent of hiccups," she diagnoses. A nearby ship panics: "IS THAT SHIP HAVING A SEIZURE?" Another ship applauds: "DO THAT AGAIN!" After a minute, the jumps stop. Diagnostics clean. Everyone's slightly dizzy.

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: "I'm recalibrating the-- bzzzt --field harmonics and-- bzzzt --" Each micro-jump interrupts her mid-sentence. Finally it stops on its own. "I fixed it," she claims. The drive's log suggests otherwise. Nobody argues.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, we've found a time capsule -- sealed, reinforced, launched exactly one year ago. Addressed to 'whoever finds this.' Inside: a letter from a child on a colony world, a seed for a native plant, and a coin 'for luck.' The child's favorite color is green.

choices.label: Send a reply to the return address.

reply.text: You compose a reply describing the void, your ship, and your crew. You include a small gift. Somewhere on a colony world, a child is going to have the best day of their life. Your crew insists on adding their own messages.

keep.text: The letter goes on the bridge wall, next to the coin. The drawing -- space as imagined by a child, inaccurate but sincere -- becomes a quiet comfort during long watches. Green was a good choice for a favorite color.

plant.text: The seed goes into hydroponics. Within days, a small green shoot emerges -- hardy, determined, growing toward light that isn't quite right for it but making do. Like all of you, really.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship matching a Union Militia patrol demands you submit to inspection. But the codes are expired, the uniform's slightly wrong, the registration doesn't match. This is a pirate impersonating a patrol.

bluff.text: "Nice try. Your codes expired two months ago and that uniform is inside-out." Silence. Then the ship's weapons power down and it bolts, warp drive engaging at full burn. Cowards -- they only prey on the gullible.

report.speaker: Militia Officer
report.text: "Impersonating a Militia vessel? That's a capital offense. We're dispatching a real patrol. Thanks for the tip, captain." The fake patrol sees the incoming signatures and flees. The Militia sends a reward.

comply.text: You play along. They 'confiscate' some cargo -- which is just robbery with extra steps. Your crew is annoyed at the charade. At least nobody got shot.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A small unarmed ship broadcasting a white flag approaches. "I'm on an apology tour. I used to be a pirate -- bad at being a person, not bad at piracy. I stole your..." he checks a list, "...12 units of copper, three years ago? I'm here to make it right."

choices.label: Tell him it's water under the bridge.

accept.speaker: Reformed Pirate
accept.text: He pays double what he stole, plus interest. "That's everyone in this sector. Only forty-seven more systems to go." He's genuine. His list is long. He funded his restitution by going straight -- surprisingly successful courier business.

forgive.speaker: Reformed Pirate
forgive.text: "Really? Just like that?" He looks like he might cry. "Most people take the money. You're... you're good people." He insists on paying something and leaves with a lighter conscience. His list is very long.
