trade.text: Fair prices, rare salvage. These people know their craft -- every bolt identified and catalogued. Professional, if unsettling. Good selection of hard-to-find components.

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: Captain... some of these 'dead' ships still have active distress beacons. Broadcasting from inside the walls. The Ossuary insists the ships were empty when found. But those beacons are still screaming.

confront.speaker: Ossuary Leader
confront.text: "Beacons persist after crews are gone. That's all it is. Echoes. We save what can be saved." Their eyes are steady, but their hands aren't. You're not getting the full story.

leave.text: You pull away from the shipyard of bones. Behind you, the distress beacons continue their silent screams.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: This cargo container -- the goods inside won't exist for another thirty years. Fabrics from materials not yet synthesized, electronics using architectures not yet invented. Manufacturer dates from three decades in the future. Everything is functional.

sell.text: ISD intelligence paid an extraordinary sum. They were very interested in the implications -- and very insistent you tell no one about this transaction.

keep.speaker: Science Officer
keep.text: Fascinating study material, but it raises more questions than it answers. The crew is unsettled by future-goods sitting in their cargo bay.

destroy.speaker: Science Officer
destroy.text: Incinerated. The science part of me is weeping, but the rational part agrees -- some things shouldn't cross the timeline.

start.speaker: Security
start.text: Captain -- hull cameras show something on the outside of the ship. Roughly humanoid, two meters tall, clinging near engine housing. No suit. Not breathing. It's looking directly at the camera.

eva.speaker: Security
eva.text: EVA team found nothing at the location. But when they came back inside... it's on a different camera now. Opposite side of the ship. Same pose. Same stare. The crew is terrified.

shoot.speaker: Security
shoot.text: Fired point defense at the hull section. Direct hit. When we checked the camera -- it's gone from that spot. Now it's on Camera 7. Other side of the ship. Same stare.

wait.text: It stayed for exactly 24 hours, then vanished. No damage, no effect, just... watching. The crew didn't sleep well.

ignore.text: It stays for 24 hours, always visible on one camera or another. Then it's gone. The crew barely slept the whole time.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, that trader -- perfectly ordinary offer, fair prices. But it has no warp signature. Nothing that travels through space lacks a warp signature. Rocks have one. That ship doesn't technically exist.

confront.speaker: Mystery Trader
confront.text: The trader smiles. "Clever crew you've got. Tell you what -- double price for my goods. Call it a premium for shopping at a store that doesn't technically exist." The goods are real. The ship vanishes after the transaction.

trade.text: The transaction is normal. The goods are real, functional, ordinary. After you're done, the ship vanishes -- not warps, not flies away. Just ceases to exist. No trace it was ever there.

choices.label: The goods are real. That's enough.

leave.text: You pull away from the impossible ship. It watches you go with no expression. Then it's gone. Your crew argues about whether it was ever there at all.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Captain, crew member showing symptoms -- iridescent skin patches, euphoria, intense desire for physical contact. Bioluminescent parasite. Spreads through skin contact. Not lethal, but permanently alters neurochemistry. We need to quarantine NOW.

choices.label: Quarantine immediately. Treat at the station.

quarantine.speaker: Medic
quarantine.text: Quarantine successful. We'll need station-grade medical supplies for treatment -- about 300 credits. The infected crew member keeps saying they feel 'wonderful.' That's the parasite talking.

choices.label: Get them treated at next station.

treat.speaker: Medic
treat.text: I managed to neutralize the parasite with our onboard supplies. It was close -- the organism was already integrating with their neural pathways. They'll recover, but they're going to feel 'too normal' for a while.

assess.speaker: Medic
assess.text: Functionally? They'd be fine -- compliant, happy, effective. Just... slightly less themselves. And they'd want to spread it. The parasite is insidious because the hosts genuinely feel better. That's how it propagates.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Encrypted broadcast: Fringe black-market auction in a debris field. Shield generator, alien artifacts, a living creature in stasis, and a 'map to something you shouldn't find.' All bidding starts steep.

choices.label: Bid on the shield generator (500 credits).

shield.speaker: Auctioneer
shield.text: "Sold! Military-grade shield generator to the captain with good taste. Installation instructions included. No warranty, obviously."

artifacts.speaker: Auctioneer
artifacts.text: "Sold! Fine selection of alien artifacts. Provenance unknown, but beauty needs no documentation." The crate contains genuinely fascinating items.

map.speaker: Auctioneer
map.text: "Sold! A map to places best left unfound. Enjoy, captain." The data chip contains coordinates to a weapon cache from a forgotten war.

leave.text: You watch the auction from the edges. Interesting crowd, interesting goods. You file the location away for future reference.

start.speaker: Comm Officer
start.text: We've entered a spherical region where all signals are perfectly reflected. We're hearing our own transmissions -- and fragments from ships that passed through before. Distress calls, love letters, battle commands. Some are centuries old. It's artificial -- a 'memory' designed to capture communications forever.

record.speaker: Comm Officer
record.text: Archive captured -- centuries of communications, perfectly preserved. ISD historians will pay well for this. There are love letters in here that would break your heart, and battle commands from wars nobody remembers.

message.text: You add your own voice to the echo chamber. Ship name, crew roster, date. It'll bounce around in here long after you're gone. The crew finds it oddly moving.

leave.text: You pass through the sphere of echoes, centuries of voices washing over the hull like rain. Then silence. The void feels emptier on the other side.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Cryo-ship drifting in the void. 200 occupied pods, all functioning. Navigation destroyed centuries ago. These people have been sleeping, going nowhere, for longer than most civilizations have existed.

choices.label: Wake them and send a distress beacon.
Raid the cargo. They'll never know.

wake.speaker: Medic
wake.text: First ones are waking up. They're confused, disoriented -- speaking a language we can barely parse. They're from an era before current civilization. We've launched a beacon for pickup.

report.speaker: Comm Officer
report.text: Coordinates transmitted to Union Militia. They'll send a recovery vessel. There's a finder's fee -- modest, but it's something. Those sleepers will wake up in a world nothing like the one they left.

raid.speaker: Engineer
raid.text: Pre-civilization trade goods -- well-preserved, some genuine antiques. Worth a fortune. The sleepers never stirred. They'll keep drifting, dreaming of a home that doesn't exist anymore.

start.speaker: Alien Artist
start.text: An alien in a craft decorated with swirling colors hails you in broken common tongue: "Your ship has a good shape. I would like to paint it. I pay YOU for the honor. 100 credits for 5 minutes of your time."

choices.label: Can you paint crew portraits too?

paint.speaker: Alien Artist
paint.text: The artist works in silence for five minutes, then transmits the holographic painting. It captures something ineffable about your ship -- crew members who view it say it looks like 'home.'

portraits.speaker: Alien Artist
portraits.text: "Yes! Individual portraits -- 20 credits each to you!" The artist paints each crew member with impossible skill. Each portrait captures something deeply personal. Crew members treasure them.

decline.speaker: Alien Artist
decline.text: "A pity. Your shape deserved to be remembered." The colorful craft drifts away, seeking the next vessel worthy of its art.

start.speaker: Comm Officer
start.text: Distress signal. We responded. But this ship responded to a distress signal, and THAT ship responded to one too -- it goes back seven ships. All seven are here in a line. None can leave. Their nav systems lock when they try. Captain -- our nav just locked too.

choices.label: Try to break the causal loop.

override.speaker: Engineer
override.text: Nav override engaged -- burning through the lock with a hard warp pulse. Fuel cost is steep but we're free! The other seven ships are still trapped. Sorry, friends.

break.speaker: Engineer
break.text: I identified the causal loop -- a resonance in the distress beacon frequencies locking nav systems in sequence. Disabled the resonance for all ships simultaneously. Seven grateful captains are hailing us with supplies.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A dying star shedding exotic matter -- materials that only exist in the brief window between stellar death and collapse. Mining ships from three factions are racing to harvest. We could join in.

choices.label: Join the harvest. Risk the radiation.
Sell our shield data to a faction.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: Radiation battering the hull, shields barely holding -- but we're pulling in exotic materials hand over fist. This stuff is worth a fortune. Hull took a beating though.

sell.speaker: Comm Officer
sell.text: Sold our shield frequency data to the nearest faction's mining team. Easy credits, no risk. They're grateful for the edge.

leave.text: You watch the dying star from a safe distance. Beautiful, in a terrible way. The harvest continues without you.

start.speaker: Station Medic
start.text: Ten-year coma patient here. Anonymous account pays for care monthly. The patient talks in their sleep -- coordinates. Every set corresponds to a major spacefaring disaster, 1 to 30 days before it happens. The next coordinates they mumbled... match a system you were planning to visit.

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: We found it -- a bomb on the main station, set to detonate in 72 hours. Disarmed it with help from local security. Hundreds of lives saved. The news feeds are calling us heroes.

avoid.text: You reroute around the system. Days later, news feeds report an explosion at the station there. Hundreds of casualties. Your crew is quiet.

sell.text: Information sold. Someone else's problem now. You never find out what happened at those coordinates.

start.speaker: Xenoculture Scientist
start.text: Welcome to the Augmentation Lab. We offer biological symbiotes -- organisms that bond permanently with crew. Reflexive, Analytical, or Regenerative. 500 credits each. Side effects are... minimal.

buy.speaker: Xenoculture Scientist
buy.text: "Bonding complete. Your crew member may experience mild... personality shifts. Iridescent skin patches are normal. Occasional sleep-talking in unknown languages is also normal. Probably."

decline.speaker: Xenoculture Scientist
decline.text: "Your loss. The symbiotes are quite lonely without hosts. If you change your mind, our frequency is always open."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Light with no source. A soft, warm glow suffusing a region about a kilometer across. No radiation, no energy signature. Just... light. Peaceful light. Ships that pass through report nothing unusual except profound calm.

through.speaker: Engineer
through.text: Warm. Safe. The crew is smiling -- actually smiling, all of them, at the same time. Like remembering something good. Your warpsmithing officer says quietly: 'I think it's a scar. From when something beautiful used to be here.'

study.speaker: Science Officer
study.text: Hours of study, no results. It defies every known physical law. It's just light being light, with no reason to exist. And yet -- the crew watching the instruments seems calmer than they've been in weeks.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Water recycler failure! Contaminated by an unknown spatial chemical absorbed through the hull. We've got 48 hours of reserves. I might be able to fix it.

fix.speaker: Engineer
fix.text: Recycler repaired. Had to flush the whole system -- lost some water reserves, but we're operational again. Close call.

analyze.speaker: Science Officer
analyze.text: The compound is actually beneficial in small doses -- a naturally occurring spatial chemical. The crew's been unknowingly microdosing. Everyone's sharper than usual. I've purged the excess and fixed the recycler.

station.text: You make for the nearest station at best speed. Water rationing makes the trip uncomfortable, but you arrive with reserves to spare. Resupply is quick and cheap.

start.speaker: Militia Officer
start.text: "Your vessel matches a ship involved in piracy in the Kovac system. Sensor logs, witness statements, docking records. Someone spoofed your transponder code."

choices.label: Bribe them to leave us alone (400 credits).

inspect.speaker: Militia Officer
inspect.text: "Inspection complete. You're clear -- our apologies for the inconvenience. We'll update our records. Whoever's using your transponder code is still out there, though."

investigate.speaker: Engineer
investigate.text: Found it -- a device attached to our hull, cloning our transponder signal. Someone's been using our identity for piracy. I've got the device as evidence. The Militia is very interested.

bribe.speaker: Militia Officer
bribe.text: The officer pockets the credits with a sigh. "I didn't see you. You didn't see me." They warp away. The real spoofer is still out there.

start.speaker: Navigator
start.text: Something went wrong during the jump. We're... somewhere. Every star is the same brightness, same color. No planets, no asteroids. Position: undefined. The void is perfectly silent. The crew says they feel 'watched from all directions.'

recal.speaker: Engineer
recal.text: Recalibration burn -- heavy fuel cost, but we punched through. We're back in normal space, 2 kilometers from our destination. Ship logs say we were here the whole time. They're wrong.

wait.text: Three hours of drifting in impossible space. The silence was the worst part -- absolute, oppressive silence. Systems self-corrected eventually. We're back. Nobody wants to talk about what they felt.

start.speaker: Professor
start.text: An elderly Castellan academic in a barely-spaceworthy vessel hails you. "I was a university professor for forty years. Now I'm giving one last lecture to anyone who'll listen. Topic: the mathematical underpinnings of warp travel. Interested?"

listen.speaker: Professor
listen.text: The lecture is genuinely fascinating -- elegant mathematics, practical insights, delivered with the passion of someone who's spent a lifetime in love with their subject. Your crew is smarter for having heard it. She has six months to live and knows it. She doesn't mention it.

donate.speaker: Professor
donate.text: "You're too kind." She gifts you her research notes -- decades of work, meticulously documented. "Make good use of them. I won't be needing them where I'm going."

thanks.speaker: Professor
thanks.text: "Thank you for listening. That's all any teacher really wants." She smiles, waves, and her little ship putters away toward the next system.

decline.speaker: Professor
decline.text: "Of course, of course. Everyone's busy these days. Safe travels." Her little ship putters onward, looking for the next willing ear.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: That 'ship' broadcasting the distress signal -- Captain, it has a metabolic signature. It's not a ship in distress. It's an organism MIMICKING a ship. The distress signal is a lure. I count six destroyed ships around it. We detected the trap early.

fight.speaker: Weapons Officer
fight.text: Tentacle appendages -- hull-piercing! It's fast for its size! Laying down sustained fire -- hitting vital organs -- it's dying. Bio-materials spilling into space. Bulwark has a standing bounty on these things.

flee.text: You pull away at maximum speed. The mimic doesn't pursue -- it's an ambush predator, not a chaser. The wreckage of six less fortunate ships grows smaller behind you.

start.speaker: Grieving Captain
start.text: "My daughter's ship disappeared here. No wreckage, no signal, nothing. She's just gone. I've been waiting for weeks. I'm running low on supplies but I can't leave. Not yet."

choices.label: Carry the vigil forward. We'll watch for her.

donate.speaker: Grieving Captain
donate.text: "Thank you. I know what people think -- that I'm wasting my time out here. But she'd wait for me. I know she would." The gratitude in their voice is crushing.

choices.label: Stay as long as you need.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Deep scan complete. We found microscopic debris consistent with a warp malfunction -- a catastrophic one. There's no way anyone survived. But at least the parent knows what happened now. Closure is something.

vigil.speaker: Grieving Captain
vigil.text: "You'd do that? Here -- take this." They hand you a pendant. "Leave it at the spot if you... if you find anything. She'd have wanted someone to remember." Your crew is moved.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a derelict science vessel ahead. Hull's intact but the interior is... glowing. Bioluminescent fractals covering every surface. Something is broadcasting through its comms: "I dream of movement. Carry me."

sample.speaker: Medic
sample.text: Sample secured, but containment had a micro-breach. I'm monitoring for contamination -- so far so good. Xenoculture will pay handsomely for this.

choices.label: Seal it tight and move on.

leave.text: You pull away from the derelict. The bioluminescent glow fades behind you. The voice on the comms whispers one last time: "I will dream of you instead."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the asteroids here are arranged in impossible formations -- arches, spirals, a perfect helix of stones rotating in sync. Something invisible is sculpting gravitational fields. No ship, no station, nothing on scanners. But the art keeps being made.

observe.speaker: Engineer
observe.text: We watched for ten minutes. The gravitational precision is beyond anything known. I learned something just from watching the field patterns shift. The crew is in awe.

mine.text: As you approach with mining lasers, a gentle gravitational pulse nudges your ship away. Not hostile -- just a firm "please don't touch." The artist protects its work.

record.text: You log the coordinates and capture what footage you can. The crew watches in silence as the invisible sculptor places another stone. Nobody wants to leave.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Priority message from a Castellan legal firm: a distant relative of one of your crew has died and left them a small outpost on a remote moon. The will requires a personal visit to claim it -- and the outpost is deep in Fringe territory.

choices.label: Set a course. That outpost is ours.

claim.speaker: Engineer
claim.text: We made it to the moon. The outpost is a single habitat module with a small mining rig. Some Fringe pirates were using it as a cache -- we chased them off. It's not much, but it's ours. The mining rig still works.

decline.text: Your crew member takes the news stoically, but you can see the disappointment. The legal firm notes the outpost will revert to local Fringe authorities.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, something's wrong. Weapons are firing backwards. Engines are pushing us the wrong way. The medical scanner just diagnosed me with the captain's headache. Cause and effect are inverted here.

choices.label: Calculate an inverted course -- do everything backwards.

invert.speaker: Engineer
invert.text: We ran the calculations in reverse -- steer left to go right, brake to accelerate. It worked. There's a clock floating at the center of the zone, running backwards. We grabbed it on the way out.

stumble.text: An hour of blind stumbling through inverted physics. Systems misfired, hull took hits from our own engines. We're clear now, but the ship is bruised.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three Castellan military vessels with disabled transponders hail you. Their lead captain speaks: "We were ordered to bombard a civilian settlement. We refused. Now we're fugitives. We need supplies and a heading -- somewhere outside Castellan space."

choices.label: Help them with supplies and a route.
Turn them in for the bounty.
This isn't your problem. Move on.

help.text: You transfer fuel and food, and chart them a course through Fringe space. The captain salutes: "We won't forget this." Your crew approves -- they did the right thing, even if Castellan wouldn't see it that way.

betray.text: You transmit their coordinates to Castellan command. Within the hour, warships arrive. The deserters don't resist. The bounty hits your account. Your crew won't look you in the eye for days.

ignore.text: You cut the channel and fly on. The three ships hang in the void behind you, their futures uncertain.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain -- during the warp jump, something paced us. Organic. Cruiser-sized. Translucent, filled with swirling light. It looked at us, then accelerated past at a speed our instruments couldn't measure. A creature that lives in warp space. That shouldn't be possible.

choices.label: Follow the trail it left behind.

follow.text: The creature's wake left a faint trail through warp space. Following it, your engines find an easier path -- like swimming in a current. Fuel savings are significant. The crew is still speechless with wonder.

log.text: You record everything your instruments captured. It won't be enough to prove what you saw, but your crew knows. They saw something that lives between dimensions. Nobody speaks for a long time.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict ahead, Captain. Interior is covered in a perfectly reflective material -- every surface is a mirror. Infinite reflections in every direction. Boarding party reports the reflections occasionally move... differently. A half-second delay. A hand rising when theirs doesn't.

choices.label: Collect a sample of the material and get out.
Pull the boarding party out immediately.

sample.speaker: Engineer
sample.text: Got a sample of the reflective material -- exotic component, worth good credits. We kept the visit short. Everyone came back. Everyone is pretty sure everyone came back.

deeper.speaker: Medic
deeper.text: One crew member spent too long inside. They're convinced they left themselves behind in the mirrors. I'm treating them for acute paranoia. The reflective material sample is valuable, at least.

choices.label: Get us away from that thing.

leave.text: The boarding party scrambles back. Through the airlock window, infinite reflections watch them leave. One reflection waves. Nobody on your crew was waving.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Ambush! Pirates emerging from behind protostellar clouds -- they've been using the EM radiation to mask their signatures. Their leader hails: "Drop cargo and we drop you gently." But Captain -- their weapons are running hot. Coolant systems are strained from waiting.

choices.label: Target their engines -- exploit the overheating.
Drop some cargo as a distraction and run.

exploit.text: You target their engine housings. The overheated systems cascade into full thermal failure. Two ships dead in space, one limping away. Salvage is good, and you find a data chip showing other ambush locations.

choices.label: Sell the chip to Union Militia.

fight.text: A brutal firefight in the nursery clouds. You take hits but give worse. The pirates scatter when their flagship breaks apart. The salvage is decent.

run.text: You jettison some cargo and burn hard through the nebula. The pirates go for the easy score instead of chasing. Smart, if expensive.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's an alien ruin on this asteroid with a functioning stasis field. Inside -- a garden. Alien plants from a species extinct for millions of years, perfectly preserved, still alive in their bubble of stopped time. It was purpose-built to keep this garden alive forever.

choices.label: Leave it intact. Some things should endure.

harvest.text: The stasis field collapses as you extract the specimens. For a moment, millions of years of frozen time resume -- and the last living remnant of an entire world's biosphere withers to dust in your hands. The genetic data is scientifically priceless.

preserve.text: You seal the chamber and mark it on your charts. The garden will continue its eternal vigil -- the last dream of a dead world, preserved by builders who knew their civilization would end but wanted something to outlast them.

choices.label: Some things matter more than credits.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the internal cameras are showing footage from two minutes in the future. We're watching ourselves on the monitors, doing things we haven't done yet. The future footage shows the crew getting agitated -- which is exactly what's happening right now, watching it.

choices.label: Break the loop -- do something the footage doesn't show.

break.text: Your entertainment officer starts dancing in the middle of the bridge. Badly. The footage didn't predict that. Static floods every monitor as the causal loop collapses. The crew applauds. Reality reasserts itself.

destroy.speaker: Engineer
destroy.text: I've pulled every camera in the ship. Loop's broken, but we're blind on internal monitoring until I can replace the system. That'll cost us.

ignore.text: The loop intensifies. Audio kicks in. The screaming from the future footage is very convincing -- mostly because it's real. Your crew is now screaming because they heard themselves screaming. Paradox headaches all around.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Encrypted channel, Fringe origin. A crime boss speaks: "Simple courier work. Package goes from here to there, nobody looks inside, you get paid 3000 credits. Only rule -- you don't open the package."

accept.text: The package is surprisingly light. Your science officer detects faint life signs from inside -- but you made a deal. You deliver it, no questions asked. The credits hit your account. What was inside is someone else's problem now.

open.speaker: Medic
open.text: It's a person. A Castellan diplomat in cryo-stasis -- kidnapped. They're disoriented but grateful. Returning them to Castellan authorities won't make you friends in the Fringe.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your choice, captain. But opportunities like this don't knock twice." The encrypted channel goes dead.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, crystalline structures growing between stars -- vast reef-like networks fed by solar radiation. They're alive. Silicon-based, photosynthesizing starlight. Crystal fish swim between the branches. The crew is mesmerized.

choices.label: Mine the coral for rare crystals.
Transplant a small cutting to our hull.

mine.text: Mining yields beautiful rare crystals. But the crystal fish swarm defensively -- a few crack against the hull before dispersing. The reef network dims slightly where you harvested.

transplant.speaker: Engineer
transplant.text: We grafted a small coral cutting onto the outer hull. It's already starting to photosynthesize. Give it time and it might actually contribute to our power grid. The crew loves watching it grow.

choices.label: A living ship. I like it.

report.text: Xenoculture is thrilled with the data. A living silicon-based photosynthetic reef ecosystem -- this will keep their researchers busy for decades.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: There's a tiny automated station out here shaped like a religious confessional booth. No power source we can detect. Inside: a seat, a screen, and a prompt -- 'SPEAK.' It contains thousands of recordings from spacers across centuries.

listen.text: A crew member listens. The recording is from a freighter captain, two hundred years dead, confessing to a hidden cache in the Fringe systems. The coordinates still check out on modern charts. Could be worth investigating.

confess.text: One by one, crew members take a turn in the booth. Nobody shares what they said. But everyone seems lighter afterward, like they set down a weight they'd been carrying.

leave.text: You leave the booth drifting in the dark, its patient prompt still glowing. It's been listening to the void for centuries. It can wait a little longer.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, a small vessel has latched onto our hull like a remora. It's not attacking -- it's feeding. Power output is dropping and getting worse. The thing is alive -- a biomechanical parasite with anchoring tendrils embedded in our plating.

choices.label: EVA team -- pry it off manually.
Target it with point defense weapons.
Leave it for now. Monitor the situation.

eva.speaker: Engineer
eva.text: The tendrils fought back, tore up some hull plating on the way out. But we got it -- and its crystallized energy core is worth serious credits. Ugly thing, beautiful core.

choices.label: Patch the hull and sell the core.

shoot.text: Point defense guns shred the parasite at close range. Some hull scorching from the proximity fire, but much cleaner than pulling it off by hand. The crystallized core survived intact.

ignore.speaker: Engineer
ignore.text: Captain, it's reproducing. Three smaller parasites just appeared on the hull. Power drain is critical. We need to act NOW or we're dead in space.

choices.label: All hands -- get those things off my ship!

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: We're picking up a civilian entertainment broadcast -- a comedy show, laughter, applause. Checking the origin... it's from a system destroyed by stellar collapse forty years ago. This signal has been traveling through the void ever since. Those people are all gone.

choices.label: Listen for a while in silence.

archive.text: You record every minute. The ISD historical archive pays for the data -- a cultural record of a dead civilization, preserved in lightspeed amber. The laughter echoes in the corridors long after you turn it off.

listen.text: The crew gathers around the comms. A comedian tells jokes that aren't very funny. The audience laughs anyway. Forty years of laughter, still traveling outward, reaching no one. Until now.

off.text: The laughter cuts out. Silence fills the bridge. Some things are easier not to think about.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, something just appeared in the cargo bay. Small, vaguely feline, visibly terrified. It's partially transparent and flickers in and out of phase. Science says it's from another dimension -- accidentally displaced. It's harmless.

choices.label: Keep it. Every ship needs a cat.

keep.text: The creature settles in quickly, bonding with a crew member and curling up in the warmest spots on the ship. It occasionally stares at empty corners and hisses at nothing. Your warpsmithing officer notes it seems to perceive threats you can't see.

return.text: Your science officer attempts to reverse the dimensional displacement. There's a flash -- and the creature is gone. Or rather, it's moved two meters to the left and looks annoyed. It's staying whether you like it or not.

contain.text: You seal it in a cargo container. It phases through the wall and reappears on a crew member's bunk, purring. Containment is not an option when your guest ignores solid matter.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: An enormous automated factory orbiting a dead world. It's running -- forges glowing, conveyors moving, building ship components in a design nobody recognizes. Estimated operational time: three thousand years. The output dock is empty. Something collects what it builds.

choices.label: Interface with controls and redirect production.

redirect.speaker: Engineer
redirect.text: I've rerouted the assembly line. It's building components we can actually use -- hull plating, power cells. This will take a couple hours. Of course, we just interrupted a 3000-year production run. Whatever usually collects the output might have opinions about that.

choices.label: Take what we can and go.

observe.text: You watch the factory work for an hour. The engineering is millennia beyond anything you know. Your crew takes detailed notes -- the design principles alone are worth publishing.

leave.text: You leave the ancient factory to its endless work. Whatever it serves, it's been faithful for three thousand years. Some arrangements shouldn't be disturbed.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Captain, one of the crew has developed a neurological condition -- they're feeling everyone's emotions amplified tenfold. Another crew member's mild annoyance becomes their rage. It's a parasitic infection, and it spreads through proximity.

choices.label: We can't afford treatment. Carry on.

treat.speaker: Medic
treat.text: Isolation and medication did the trick. The parasite's gone, but it left a mark -- the affected crew member has permanently heightened empathy. They're actually better with people now.

manage.text: Your entertainment officer works overtime keeping spirits up. The infected crew member is functional but struggling -- every bad mood on the ship hits them like a sledgehammer. It's manageable. Barely.

choices.label: Keep managing until we reach a station.

ignore.speaker: Medic
ignore.text: It's spreading. Three crew members now, weeping and raging in sympathy with each other's weeping and rage. It's a feedback loop of emotional agony. We need treatment, Captain.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We've recovered a black box from a destroyed military vessel. Standard procedure is to return it for credits and rep. But Captain -- there's a faint secondary signal on an encrypted frequency. Someone hid data in this box that wasn't meant to be found.

choices.label: Sell it to the highest bidder.

decrypt.speaker: Engineer
decrypt.text: The ship wasn't destroyed by enemies. It was executed by its own faction for discovering a secret research facility -- illegal experiments on warp-space entities. The hidden data includes facility coordinates and rival factions would pay a fortune for this.

choices.label: Sell the conspiracy data to their rivals.

return.text: You hand over the black box through proper channels. Standard recovery fee, standard reputation boost. Whatever secrets it held stay buried.

sell.text: Military black boxes fetch good prices on the grey market. No questions asked, credits transferred.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, gravitational lensing from a binary star system is bending distant starlight into a sweeping arc of color. But there are extra colors -- hues that shouldn't exist, wavelengths between the familiar spectrum. Some crew members say they can taste them. Others hear them.

choices.label: Linger and let the crew experience it.

linger.text: You drift in the impossible rainbow for an hour. The synesthesia fades when you leave, but the memory doesn't. Your science officer theorizes the binary stars bend light from another dimension. Recordings show only a normal rainbow. You had to be there.

choices.label: The crew will talk about this for weeks.

record.text: The recording captures a perfectly ordinary rainbow. Whatever extra-dimensional wavelengths were present, instruments can't reproduce them. The crew is quietly awed anyway.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A massive Bulwark warship blocks the corridor ahead. "This corridor is under Bulwark protection. Toll is 500 credits or equivalent cargo. No exceptions."

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Credits received. Safe passage granted. Travel well, captain." The warship moves aside with practiced efficiency. Protection money, but at least the corridor is genuinely safe.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: "You've got nerve, I'll give you that. Tell you what -- 200 credits and you spread the word that Bulwark corridors are the safest in the sector. Deal?"

detour.text: You reroute through unpatrolled space. Two extra jumps, burning fuel, but your credits stay in your pocket. The Bulwark captain watches you go without comment.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A chunk of matter just fell out of warp space into normal space -- right in front of us. Physics says that's impossible. It's a spherical rock with fossilized remains of something that lived in warp space. Looking at it from different angles reveals different shapes. It sometimes moves when nobody's watching.

choices.label: Auction it to the highest bidder.
Push it back into warp space.

auction.text: ISD, Xenoculture, and the Castellan Academy bid furiously. Proof that warp space has its own ecology is priceless to any scientific institution. The final price is staggering.

study.speaker: Engineer
study.text: We're keeping the fossil aboard for study. Your warpsmithing officer is overwhelmed -- the dimensional compression patterns are teaching us things about warp space we never knew. It still moves when we're not looking.

return.text: You nudge it back toward a warp anomaly. It falls through and vanishes. Your warpsmithing officer looks heartbroken -- that was the discovery of a lifetime. But some things belong where they came from.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the ship's logs show maintenance entries made by crew members at times when they were confirmed asleep. Camera footage shows empty corridors. But the work is real -- systems checked, repairs done, adjustments made correctly. Something is crewing our ship during the night cycle.

monitor.text: The experiment confirms it: an invisible entity performs work equal to one extra crew member's output every night. No hostile activity detected. The logs continue. Your crew is uneasy, but the ship has never run smoother.

patrol.text: Night patrols find nothing. But the maintenance entries stop while patrols are active -- and resume the moment they're cancelled. Whatever it is, it's shy. The crew sleeps poorly.

accept.text: You mention it casually at the next crew briefing. "We have a night shift volunteer. Don't bother them." Half the crew laughs nervously. The other half doesn't sleep for a week. But the work keeps getting done.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A badly damaged pirate ship drifts into view. Their captain hails, voice strained: "We raided a medical transport. Got hit harder than expected. We have wounded -- kids among us, believe it or not. Can't pay. Can't threaten. I'm asking for mercy."

choices.label: Board and take their stolen cargo.

help.speaker: Medic
help.text: We stabilized their wounded and transferred food supplies. The pirate captain grips your hand through the airlock: "I won't forget this. None of us will." Your crew is quiet on the way back -- the good kind of quiet.

board.text: The pirates barely resist. You strip their cargo hold of stolen medical supplies. The children watch from behind a bulkhead. Your crew won't meet your eyes for days.

militia.text: Union Militia arrives within the hour. Pirates arrested, children placed in state custody. The informant reward hits your account. Clean, legal, efficient. Your crew has opinions they keep to themselves.

leave.text: You fly on. The pirate captain doesn't hail again. Your crew stares at the drifting wreck until it's out of visual range.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the science team has found something disturbing. A number -- the same number -- keeps recurring across every anomaly we've encountered. Different formats each time, but always the same value. Frequencies, coordinates, timestamps. And it's changing. Getting larger. Slowly.

meaning.speaker: Sensor Officer
meaning.text: Your science officer goes quiet for a long time. Then, very carefully: "I think it's a countdown. Running in reverse. Something is being measured. Something is approaching a threshold. I don't know what happens when it gets there."

log.text: You file the data. The number sits in your logs, quietly incrementing. Your science officer checks it every morning. They never say what they're looking for.

start.text: In the deepest void between galactic arms, further from anything than you've ever been, your comms array picks up something. Not a distress call. Not a beacon. A single, sustained note -- a vibration in spacetime itself. The universe, humming to itself. Out here, in the absolute silence, you can finally hear it.

listen.text: Every crew member stops what they're doing. No one speaks. The note holds for one full minute, then fades as you drift back toward the populated galaxy. No one on your crew can ever quite describe what they heard. But none of them forget it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, this emerald nebula is pulsing -- expanding and contracting every twelve seconds like breathing. Scans show organic molecules and plasma circulatory channels. If we fly deeper, the breathing syncs with our crew's heart rates.

deeper.text: The deeper you go, the more the crew feels it. Heart rates synchronize with the nebula's rhythm. Some crew members report feeling homesick for somewhere they've never been. It's hauntingly beautiful and deeply unsettling.

choices.label: Pull back before we lose ourselves.

observe.text: From a distance, the breathing nebula is mesmerizing. Your science team collects valuable data on its organic structure. The crew watches in quiet fascination.

leave.text: You pull away. The nebula pulses on behind you, breathing in the dark. Some of the crew glance back with an expression that's hard to read.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A metallic slab the size of a frigate, covered in script from at least nine different languages. Our computer can partially translate three of them. One passage reads: "WE BUILT THE ROADS BETWEEN STARS. WE FORGOT TO BUILD THE DOORS HOME."

choices.label: Attempt a full translation and sell the data.
Share the discovery openly with Xenoculture.

translate.text: Your science team works for hours, piecing together fragments across nine dead languages. The full translation is haunting -- a warning from an ancient civilization that connected the stars but lost their homeworld in the process.

share.text: Xenoculture is ecstatic. Nine languages on one slab -- the linguistic implications alone could take decades to unravel. They transfer a research stipend as thanks.

sell.text: ISD pays well for exclusive data rights. The slab's secrets will be locked in their archives, studied in classified silence.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Billions of bioluminescent organisms ahead -- a shimmering river of pale blue light. They're clogging our intake vents, cutting engine efficiency. A farming crew member says they're edible. Science says their migration pattern leads toward something massive.

harvest.text: Your farming specialist directs the harvest. Void krill, it turns out, taste faintly of shrimp and ozone. The crew doesn't complain. Food stores replenished nicely.

follow.text: You follow the krill migration deeper into the void, burning fuel to keep pace. The swarm funnels toward something ahead -- something enormous. Your sensors are picking up a truly massive biological signature.

clear.text: You push through the swarm at reduced speed. The pale blue light fades behind you. Your intakes need cleaning, but no lasting damage.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- a creature the size of a space station. Translucent, bell-shaped, trailing tendrils hundreds of kilometers long. The void krill swarm funnels directly into its maw. And inside its body... thousands of metallic objects. Ships. It's been feeding here for centuries.

choices.label: Scan it and keep your distance.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: We got close and cut samples from a tendril. Rich in exotic organics -- valuable stuff. But the creature's bioluminescence just shifted to deep red. It's turning toward us. Slowly. Very slowly. We should go.

scan.text: Detailed scans reveal an organism of staggering complexity -- a filter feeder that has turned this region of space into its personal ocean. The data alone is worth publishing. Your crew watches in awed silence.

flee.text: You don't need to be told twice. Full burn away from the leviathan. It doesn't pursue -- you're too small to bother with. This time.

505.title: The Last Broadcast of Station Errant-7

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Looping distress signal detected. A woman's voice, calm: "This is Administrator Voss. The station is functioning normally. All 2,300 residents are alive and well. Please do not send rescue. Please do not approach. We are functioning normally." COTAC records show this station was decommissioned forty years ago.

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: The signal originates from empty space. Or rather -- from a point that our sensors insist does not exist. There's nothing there. But the signal is definitely coming from that nothing. The hair on the back of my neck won't lie down.

hail.speaker: Comm Channel
hail.text: No response to your hail. The message loops again, identical. "We are functioning normally." Then -- just for a moment, between loops -- a different voice, barely a whisper: "Help us." Then the loop resumes.

leave.text: You mark the coordinates and leave. The signal fades behind you, still looping. Forty years of normalcy, broadcast into the void.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the hydroponics bay has a cascading blight -- aggressive fungal bloom consuming our oxygen plants. Food production is down and O2 is dropping. We need to act fast.

choices.label: Salvage what we can from the contaminated crop.

quarantine.speaker: Engineer
quarantine.text: Quarantine established. We burned the infected sections and replanted from seed stock. It cost us food reserves, but O2 levels are stabilizing. We'll be back to full production within the day.

counter.speaker: Medic
counter.text: Counter-agent synthesized and deployed. The fungal bloom is dying back. Faster than replanting, and we saved most of the crop. Textbook response.

salvage.text: Your cook works miracles with the contaminated crop, salvaging what's safe to eat. It's not much, but it buys time. The blight continues spreading in the sections you didn't address.

507.title: Ghost Fleet of the Founding War

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We've dropped out of warp into a graveyard -- hundreds of ancient warships, perfectly preserved. They predate every known faction by centuries. Captain... lights are flickering on some of the bridges.

board.speaker: Engineer
board.text: One ship's computer is still running a tactical simulation of a battle that never ended. I've downloaded the historical data -- any faction would pay for this. But Captain, the automated defense grid just lit up. We have thirty seconds to disengage.

scan.text: Long-range scans reveal incredible detail about pre-faction warship design. The data is historically significant but you wisely keep your distance from those flickering bridge lights.

leave.text: You drift past the ancient fleet in silence. The bridge lights flicker as you pass, as if watching. Your crew is glad to leave.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An elderly Fringe explorer in a battered ship hails you. "Been mapping the deep void for sixty years. I'm dying. My maps are worth a fortune -- routes, resource deposits, hidden stations. I'll sell them for 500 credits. Or... if you can spare food or medicine, I'd trade for that instead."

buy.text: The maps are extraordinary -- sixty years of meticulous charting. Hidden routes, resource caches, stations that don't appear on any official chart. Worth every credit.

offer.speaker: Comm Channel
offer.text: Her eyes light up. "Kindness is rare out here." She transfers the maps -- all of them, plus a personal warning: "Don't go past the Stillness. What's out there doesn't want to be found." She refuses to elaborate.

decline.text: "Your loss, captain. Sixty years of work, and it'll die with me." She cuts the channel. Her ship drifts away into the void.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, three crew members are on the bridge and they're not happy. "We've been eating half-portions for a week. Some of us think the officers are skimming." They're looking at you for an answer.

choices.label: Assert authority. Rations stay as they are.

inspect.text: You open every locker, every crate. Nothing hidden, nothing skimmed. The accusers are ashamed. Morale rebounds -- but everyone eats their fill to celebrate the transparency, burning through reserves.

choices.label: Honesty costs, but it's worth it.

authority.text: "I decide rations on this ship. Anyone with a problem can take it up at the next station." The crew backs down, but the grumbling continues below decks. You've won the argument, not the trust.

cook.text: Your cook rolls up their sleeves. "Give me an hour and whatever's in the back of the freezer." An hour later, the whole crew is eating something that tastes remarkably like a real meal. The tension dissolves over hot food.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Enormous crystals orbiting a dead star, each emitting a distinct harmonic tone. Together they produce a mathematically perfect chord -- base-12 counting system encoded in music. Someone built an instrument the size of a solar system.

choices.label: Mine the crystals for rare minerals.
Leave them intact and share coordinates.

mine.text: The mining yield is excellent -- rare crystalline minerals in abundance. But as each crystal shatters, the chord loses a voice. By the time you're done, the music is gone. Your entertainment officer hasn't spoken since the last note died.

preserve.text: You share the coordinates with Xenoculture. They're overwhelmed -- an alien musical instrument on a stellar scale. The research stipend is generous, and the choir sings on.

choices.label: Some things are worth more than cargo.

listen.text: You drift among the crystals and let the chord wash over the ship. The vibrations resonate through the hull. Nobody moves. Nobody needs to.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, wet footprints in corridor seven leading to a sealed cargo bay. Inside -- a gaunt figure behind the crates. Claims they boarded at our last station. "Please, I'm running from the ISD. They'll kill me." Medical scan shows human, but unusual neural activity.

choices.label: Drop them at the next station.

shelter.text: You give them a bunk and a meal. They're grateful, quiet, and stay out of the way. Whether they're a genuine refugee or something else remains to be seen. Your crew has mixed feelings, but compassion won out.

turnin.text: ISD responds quickly. An agent arrives at the next station to collect them. The stowaway doesn't struggle, just looks at you with empty eyes. ISD transfers a small reward. Some crew members won't meet your gaze.

drop.text: You leave them at a neutral station with enough credits for a meal. "Thank you, captain. For not turning me in." They disappear into the station crowd. Whatever their story, it's no longer yours.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Space is shimmering like heat haze. Captain -- our clock just jumped forward 72 hours. Food stores dropped, crew needs ticked. We've hit a natural time-dilation pocket.

choices.label: Harvest chronon particles from the anomaly.
Analyze the anomaly and move on.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: Residual chronon particles collected -- exotic stuff, worth real credits. But the time loss stings. We're three days behind on everything.

choices.label: At least we got something for our trouble.

analyze.text: Science team maps the eddy's boundaries. Valuable data for future navigation -- now we know what to look for. But those 72 hours are gone forever.

flee.text: You burn hard away from the shimmer. The time loss already happened -- nothing to do but accept it and keep moving.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: The hull is vibrating at an audible frequency -- a hum throughout the ship. No mechanical cause. The patterns are almost like language. Sleep is becoming impossible. Science says microorganisms have colonized our hull plating and are communicating.

scrape.speaker: Engineer
scrape.text: EVA teams scraped the hull clean. The silence that follows is almost jarring after days of constant humming. Crew sleeps soundly for the first time in a while.

harmonize.text: Your entertainment officer starts humming along. The vibration shifts -- it harmonizes. The noise becomes almost pleasant, a deep chord that settles into the background. The organisms seem... happy? The hull feels stronger.

leave.text: The humming continues. And continues. Crew morale deteriorates as nobody can sleep through the constant vibration. The organisms are getting louder.

choices.label: Should have dealt with this sooner.

514.title: Derelict Generation Ship: COVENANT OF DAWN

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- a generation ship. Twelve kilometers long, tumbling slowly. Launched 800 years ago, never arrived. Interior scans show forests, rivers, weather systems. But no people. Billions of personal belongings. Meals half-eaten. One journal entry: "The Outside looked in. We looked back. Now we understand why we were never meant to arrive."

choices.label: Board and salvage what we can.
Leave it. Something is wrong here.

board.speaker: Engineer
board.text: We found artifacts, supplies, technology eight centuries old. But captain -- the deeper we went, the more crew reported movement in their peripheral vision. One refused to come back. We pulled out with what we could carry.

scan.text: External scans yield incredible data about generation ship engineering. The internal ecosystem readings are beautiful -- a world in a bottle, still running after 800 years. The absence of any human life signs is deeply disturbing.

leave.text: You give the COVENANT OF DAWN a wide berth. Twelve kilometers of emptiness, tumbling in the dark. Whatever happened on that ship, it happened to everyone at once. Your crew is very quiet.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A drifting vessel broadcasts on repeat: "DO NOT BOARD. BIOLOGICAL CONTAMINATION. ALL HANDS LOST." The ship's cargo hold shows salvageable goods on scan. But that warning is there for a reason.

choices.label: Board and grab what we can, fast.

board.speaker: Medic
board.text: Full hazmat protocols. We recovered salvage and, more importantly, pathogen samples. I've synthesized a counter-agent. Sharing this data with Union Militia could save lives across the sector.

rush.speaker: Medic
rush.text: We got in and out fast, but not fast enough. One crew member is showing symptoms -- fever, disorientation. I can treat it, but they'll be bedridden for days. The salvage better be worth it.

leave.text: You leave the plague ship to its eternal quarantine broadcast. Sometimes the warning label is all you need to read.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A brilliant point of light ahead -- impossibly bright, like a tiny star. Wait -- it's a lure. Something enormous is unfolding from the darkness behind it. Bioluminescent bulb on a stalk, metallic teeth evolved to bite through hull plating. It's charging!

fight.text: A brutal close-range engagement. The creature is fast and aggressive, slamming into your hull before your guns tear it apart. The carcass yields exotic organics and a trophy tooth the size of a person.

flee.text: You bank hard and burn full thrust. The creature clips your stern with those metallic teeth before you pull away -- hull breach, quickly sealed. It doesn't pursue far. Anglers are ambush predators, not chasers.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Broadband signal -- thousands of overlapping voice recordings. Confessions. People admitting crimes, regrets, secrets. Some mundane, some horrifying. Source: a small automated satellite, collecting and rebroadcasting for decades. A Xenoculture experiment in "collective conscience."

study.text: The behavioral data is fascinating -- decades of raw human honesty, captured in the void. Your science officer compiles a paper's worth of analysis. The recordings are haunting, but illuminating.

confess.text: One by one, crew members speak into the satellite's receiver. What they say is private. But afterward, the ship feels lighter. Everyone walks a little taller.

destroy.text: A single shot and the satellite goes dark. Thousands of confessions, silenced. Xenoculture won't be pleased, but some experiments shouldn't run forever.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Distress beacon from a Fringe colony on a barren moon: "Three hundred souls. Crops failed. Supply ship two months late. Children are dying." They're begging anyone who can hear.

choices.label: Donate generously -- everything we can spare.

donate.text: You transfer food to the colony. The relief is immediate -- children eat for the first time in days. The colony administrator weeps openly on comms. "You saved us. We won't forget." Your crew stands a little straighter.

generous.text: You give until your own stores ache. The colony has enough to survive until a proper supply run arrives. They name a street after your ship. Your crew is proud, even as their own rations thin.

ignore.text: You fly on. The beacon continues behind you, fading with distance. Your crew says nothing, but their silence speaks volumes. Nobody makes eye contact at dinner.

choices.label: We have our own mouths to feed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- there's a ship ahead. It's... ours. Same hull, same modules, same damage patterns. An exact copy. It's hailing us with your voice: "Don't trust the next star you see. It's not a star." Then it jumps to warp.

choices.label: Analyze the warp signature it left behind.

follow.text: You follow the warp trail into empty space. Nothing. No ship, no trace, no explanation. Just void. The trail ends as if the ship ceased to exist. Your crew is deeply unsettled.

analyze.speaker: Engineer
analyze.text: The warp signature came from a direction where no inhabited systems exist. The quantum profile is identical to our own engines -- impossibly so. This wasn't a copy. It was us. From somewhere else.

ignore.text: Nobody talks about it. But nobody forgets it either. "Don't trust the next star you see." The words sit in the back of everyone's mind like a splinter.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, fuel is draining at triple the normal rate. An invisible structure is generating a field that excites fuel molecules, causing rapid evaporation. We can power through, drift through on minimal power, or try to tune the reactor to resist it.

choices.label: Tune the reactor to resist the field.

power.text: You burn hard through the field. Fast, but expensive. The fuel gauge drops like a stone before you clear the boundary. At least you're through.

choices.label: Check what's left in the tank.

drift.text: Six hours of silent drifting on minimal power. The crew sits in the dark, listening to the hull creak. But the fuel loss is manageable.

tune.speaker: Engineer
tune.text: Two hours of careful calibration, but I matched our reactor frequency to cancel the siphon effect. We passed through with barely a drop lost. The field is an ancient weapon -- designed to strand entire fleets. Ingenious and terrible.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Inside this dense nebula -- hundreds of pod-like organic structures, each containing a developing creature. Bioluminescent jellyfish, shelled behemoths, things with too many eyes. All in embryonic stasis. A breeding ground for void fauna. They'll hatch in about fifty years.

choices.label: Log coordinates and sell the data.
Report to Bulwark for preemptive action.

log.text: You publish the coordinates openly. Multiple factions express interest. The science community is thrilled -- a window into void fauna reproduction, undisturbed for observation.

xeno.text: Xenoculture pays a premium for exclusive access. They'll establish a research station here within the year. The embryos will be studied, protected, and left to develop naturally.

bulwark.text: Bulwark dispatches a sterilization team. "Unknown void fauna? Hundreds of them? We'll handle it." Xenoculture will be furious if they find out. But Bulwark sleeps easier.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Captain, one of the crew -- the one pulling long watches on the observation deck -- has started talking to someone who isn't there. Drawing geometric patterns on every surface. Muttering about "the shape behind the stars." It's escalating fast.

choices.label: Let it play out. Maybe they see something we don't.

sedate.speaker: Medic
sedate.text: Sedated and resting in medical. They'll be groggy for a day but safe. Curiously, the patterns they drew -- when our science officer analyzed them -- encode a valid star chart to an uncharted system.

choices.label: Log the coordinates. Keep them sedated.

talk.text: Your entertainment officer sits with them for two hours, talking softly. Slowly, the agitation fades. They can't explain what they saw, but they're calm now. The geometric patterns, analyzed later, contain a star chart to an unknown system.

choices.label: Give them rest. Log the chart.

wait.speaker: Engineer
wait.text: Captain, they've sabotaged the navigation system! Trying to fly us into the nearest black hole! "It's not a hole -- it's a DOOR!" We've restrained them, but nav systems need repair.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thousands of skeletal remains drifting in formation -- silicon-based, enormous, arranged in geometric patterns. A graveyard monument, two million years old. Microfractures in every bone are consistent with a single catastrophic event. They all died at once.

mine.text: The silicon yield is excellent. But your crew can't sleep afterward. Something about mining a two-million-year-old graveyard sits heavy on the soul. The bones were arranged with such care.

offering.text: You jettison a small offering of cargo into the formation. It drifts among the bones, a new addition to the monument. Your crew feels something settle -- a peace, maybe. Or just the relief of doing something decent.

scan.text: Science scans reveal the full scale of the catastrophe -- an entire species, billions of individuals, killed in a single moment two million years ago. The geometric arrangement suggests survivors placed the dead here deliberately.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan merchant vessel hails, and the captain is clearly drunk. "Listen, friend -- I've got four hundred barrels of the finest Castellan Red and my buyer just cancelled. I'll sell the lot for 100 credits. That's robbery and I know it."

choices.label: Buy the lot. 100 credits for 400 barrels?
Offer to help him find another buyer.

buy.text: Four hundred barrels of Castellan Red, loaded into your cargo hold. Your brewing specialist confirms it's actually quite good -- aged three years in Castellan oak casks. Resale value at any station is enormous. The crew has already cracked one barrel open.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss! I'll drink it myself!" His ship begins flying erratically, weaving between asteroids with surprising grace for someone three sheets to the wind.

help.text: You put him in touch with a station contact. He sobers up enough to make the deal and transfers you a finder's fee. "You're a good sort, captain. Next time we meet, first barrel's free."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the nebula ahead has an unmistakable structure -- it looks like an eye. And the pupil is tracking our movement. This thing spans light-minutes. It's a single organism.

communicate.speaker: Science Officer
communicate.text: I'm translating its electromagnetic pulses. It says: "SMALL THING. WHAT ARE YOU?" I've managed to establish a basic dialogue -- it's sharing fragments of alien knowledge. The data is incredibly valuable.

choices.label: Archive the data and move on.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: It blinked. The shockwave is -- brace for impact! The pulse threw us clear out of the nebula. Hull took serious damage.

ignore.text: You drift through the nebula quietly. The great eye watches you pass but makes no move. Safe passage through the iris of a living god.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, life support just failed -- O2 production is down to 20%. We've got hours before crew starts suffocating. I need orders.

choices.label: Fabricate replacement parts from raw materials.

seal.speaker: Engineer
seal.text: Sealed off the lower decks. We're breathing thin but stable. It'll buy us enough time to limp to the nearest station for proper repairs.

cannibalize.speaker: Engineer
cannibalize.text: Tore apart a secondary system for parts. Life support is back online. We lost a module but everyone's breathing easy again.

choices.label: Better a module than a life.

fabricate.speaker: Engineer
fabricate.text: Our smelter crew fabricated emergency replacement parts from raw stock. Took three hours of white-knuckle work, but O2 is flowing again.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a holographic projector floating in open space. It's displaying a 3D blueprint of a Dyson swarm -- habitats for trillions. The technology is beyond anything we've ever seen.

interface.speaker: Science Officer
interface.text: Our warpsmith downloaded partial schematics. This data is worth a fortune to any faction. The projector then displayed our ship, made a sound the translator rendered as "INSUFFICIENT," and powered down.

leave.text: You leave the projector undisturbed. It continues its silent display of impossible engineering -- a monument to ambitions that dwarf your own.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A pod of void whales crossing our path, Captain. Massive creatures -- translucent skin, internal fusion reactors visible. Their wake is causing minor turbulence.

choices.label: Ride the wake for a momentum boost.

ride.speaker: Sensor Officer
ride.text: Nice piloting, Captain. We caught the slipstream perfectly -- saved a good chunk of fuel riding their momentum.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Fascinating readings. Their internal fusion process is unlike anything in our databases. This data will fetch a decent price.

music.text: Your entertainment officer plays music over the external speakers. The whales change course to swim alongside your ship, their bioluminescence pulsing in time with the melody. The crew watches in awed silence for an hour.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict freighter ahead. Interior smeared with old blood. Logs say the crew ran out of food eight months ago. Last entry: "There are four of us left. We drew lots. God forgive me." One life sign still aboard.

subdue.speaker: Medic
subdue.text: The survivor attacked on sight -- skeletal, feral, barely human. We subdued them. Severe malnutrition and psychological damage, but they can recover with constant medical attention. It won't be easy on the crew.

choices.label: Take them aboard. They deserve a chance.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Cargo hold had some valuables the crew never got to trade. We pulled what we could without going too deep into that ship.

leave.text: Some horrors are best left undisturbed. You plot a course away from the derelict and try not to think about the life sign still flickering on sensors.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Space is bending visibly around an invisible mass ahead. Stars stretch into rings of light. We're drifting toward it. Inside the lensing zone, time flows differently -- it may be a collapsed megastructure.

enter.speaker: Science Officer
enter.text: Inside the zone, the crew experienced a shared vision -- a civilization building, thriving, dying, and being forgotten, compressed into minutes. Exiting was rough. The tidal forces scraped our hull, but we made it.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Long-range scans confirm it -- the mass is artificial. A collapsed megastructure of impossible age. The data alone is worth something.

leave.text: You give the anomaly a wide berth. The stars unstretch behind you as you leave the lensing effect. Some things are better observed from a distance.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A lone trader in an ancient vessel hails you. "I sell things people wish they hadn't lost." His wares are peculiar: a love letter, a star chart to a dead homeworld, a vial of soil from a planet that no longer exists.

choices.label: Buy the vial of soil (100 credits).

letter.speaker: Comm Channel
letter.text: He hands over the letter with surprising tenderness. "Someone wrote this with their whole heart. I hope it finds meaning on your ship." The crew passes it around. There are tears.

soil.speaker: Comm Channel
soil.text: "Soil from Verath Prime. Gone now -- stellar collapse. This is all that remains of a world that held four billion lives." Xenoculture scholars would treasure this.

regret.speaker: Comm Channel
regret.text: He pauses. "Becoming the kind of man who profits from sorrow." He says nothing more and powers up his warp drive.

leave.text: The ancient vessel drifts away. Its trader has more stops to make, more regrets to peddle.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Captain, multiple crew members are reporting the same nightmare simultaneously. The hull breaches, they float into space, but instead of dying they hear a voice: "YOU ARE ALMOST READY." Every dreamer described the same coordinates.

choices.label: Run medical scans on the affected crew.

scan.speaker: Medic
scan.text: Scans show nothing physically wrong. But the coordinates each crew member described independently -- they all point to the same spot in deep void. Whatever this is, it's not a medical issue.

log.text: You log the coordinates without comment. The crew's sleep improves over the next few days, but the shared experience lingers in quiet conversations.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two Fringe pirate vessels drop out of warp on either side of you -- a classic pincer maneuver. "Don't bother running, friend. Hand over your cargo and we'll let you keep your hull. Mostly."

fight.text: Two-on-one is ugly, but you come out on top. Both pirate ships are disabled, and your crew strips them for salvage. The Fringe won't forget this.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: "Smart move, friend. Credits speak louder than cannons." The pirates pocket your bribe and peel off, grumbling about easy marks.

bluff.speaker: Comm Channel
bluff.text: "Void-laced warheads? You're bluffing." A tense silence. Then: "...but what if you're not? Forget it. Not worth the risk." The pirates withdraw, muttering threats.

choices.label: Hold your poker face until they're gone.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: An abandoned research station ahead, but its exterior is encrusted with living coral -- in space. It's warm to sensors, photosynthesizing from starlight. Researcher notes describe a vacuum-adapted biology experiment that succeeded beyond expectations.

samples.speaker: Science Officer
samples.text: We've collected several kilograms of samples. The biological data alone is valuable, and the material has unusual structural properties.

cultivate.speaker: Science Officer
cultivate.text: Our farming specialist managed to cultivate a small colony in the cargo bay. It's already producing edible biomass. It'll spread across the hull cosmetically, but the food production is a real benefit.

leave.text: You leave the coral station to its slow, quiet growth. In a few months it will consume the structure entirely. Life finds a way, even in the void.

start.text: During a long stretch between systems, your entertainment crew member organizes a talent show. A gunner does impressions of faction leaders. An engineer juggles reactor components -- badly. The pilot recites terrible poetry about warp travel.

participate.text: Your performance is... debatable in quality, but the crew loves that you joined in. The cook wins first place with an elaborate meal. Laughter echoes through the corridors long after the show ends.

watch.text: The cook wins first place with an elaborate meal that draws actual applause. The whole crew is grinning. Sometimes the best thing a captain can do is let the crew be human for a night.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, a curved metal plate the size of a continent is drifting ahead -- a fragment of a partially-constructed Dyson sphere. Solar collectors on its inner surface are still generating power after millennia. But I'm reading active repair drones.

fuel.speaker: Engineer
fuel.text: Tapped into the collector grid. The energy output is incredible -- we topped off our fuel reserves easily. But the repair drones are getting curious about us. Time to go.

choices.label: Disengage before they weld us in.

mine.speaker: Engineer
mine.text: The alloys in this thing are advanced beyond anything we can manufacture. We loaded up, but the repair drones started welding our hull to the surface. Had to burn thrusters hard to break free.

leave.text: You observe the continent-sized fragment from a safe distance. The repair drones work tirelessly on a project that will never be completed. There's something melancholy about it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Warning buoys in dozens of languages, all saying the same thing: "BIOLOGICAL THREAT -- DO NOT ENTER." Spores are already infiltrating our ventilation system.

seal.speaker: Engineer
seal.text: Ventilation sealed. We caught it in time -- no contamination. The spore cloud is thinning as we move through. Those warning buoys weren't kidding.

medical.speaker: Medic
medical.text: One crew member developed growths before we could treat them. They say they feel "wonderful, connected to everything." I can remove the growths, but the crew member is resistant -- they don't want to lose the feeling.

choices.label: Remove the growths. That's an order.

flee.text: You reverse course immediately. The spores dissipate as you clear the zone. The warning buoys continue their ancient broadcast behind you.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a contact matching our exact size and heading, 500 meters behind us. Visual shows nothing. It mirrors every course change instantly. Science says it's been following us for three systems -- we just hadn't noticed.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: It vanished when we scanned -- then reappeared 100 meters closer. Analysis suggests it's a sensor echo from a higher spatial dimension. It's harmless. Probably. The crew is rattled.

ignore.text: You leave the shadow alone. It follows for 48 hours, then vanishes. When it's gone, engineering reports something strange -- a damaged module has been repaired. Nobody can explain how.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, our brewer has been experimenting with void krill extract and local fungi. The result glows faintly blue and tastes like "lightning and regret." It's mildly psychoactive. The crew loves it.

choices.label: Produce it in quantity for sale.
Shut down the still. Too risky.

produce.text: You invest food and organics into a production run. Thirty units of "Void Brew" ready for market. Stations are paying top credit for novelty beverages, and Castellan merchants are especially interested.

enjoy.text: The crew passes the brew around. One crew member temporarily believes they can see the future. They can't -- but their oddly specific predictions provide entertainment for days.

shutdown.text: The brewer is disappointed but complies. "Your loss, Captain. That was my masterpiece." The still is dismantled and the remaining brew poured out.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A generation ship, Captain -- intact and populated. Thirty generations removed from the original crew. They've developed their own language, religion, and culture. They don't believe in the "outside." The ship is their entire universe.

contact.speaker: Science Officer
contact.text: First contact was... intense. They were terrified, then fascinated. After hours of careful diplomacy, they traded unique cultural artifacts and one of their people volunteered to join us -- they want to see the "outside" for themselves.

observe.text: You watch the generation ship for an hour, cataloging its external features and electromagnetic signatures. A civilization in a bottle, unaware of the ocean outside. Scientifically priceless.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, the warp drive is emitting a harmonic whine -- our warpsmith says it's a pre-failure cascade. We need to act fast or we'll be stranded.

choices.label: Shut down the drive and drift on sublight.
Push through and hope it holds.

drift.speaker: Engineer
drift.text: Drive is shut down. We'll burn sublight fuel getting to the nearest system, but at least we won't be scattered across twelve dimensions.

push.speaker: Engineer
push.text: We pushed through -- and the drive held. Barely. The whine faded after an agonizing twenty minutes. Don't ask me to do that again, Captain.

repair.speaker: Engineer
repair.text: Our warpsmith worked miracles -- recalibrated the harmonic dampers mid-transit. Not only is the drive stable, it's actually running more efficiently than before.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, a vast bioluminescent reef ahead -- coral-like formations pulsing with colors across the visible spectrum. It spans thousands of kilometers. We can drift through safely. The crew is glued to the viewscreens.

choices.label: Drift through and enjoy the view.
Collect science data as we pass.
Mine exotic organics from the reef.

drift.text: Aurora-like displays wash across every viewscreen as you glide through the reef. Some crew members later describe this as the most beautiful thing they've ever seen.

science.speaker: Science Officer
science.text: The electromagnetic emissions are extraordinary. I've cataloged over two hundred distinct species in this reef alone. The data will sell well.

mine.speaker: Engineer
mine.text: We harvested exotic organics, but the damage to the reef is visible -- a dark scar where color used to pulse. The crew isn't happy about it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A heavily armed Bulwark corvette blocks the narrow passage ahead. "This lane is under Bulwark protection. Toll is 50 credits or equivalent cargo."

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Appreciated. Safe travels, captain." The corvette slides aside, and you pass through the lane without incident.

detour.speaker: Sensor Officer
detour.text: Alternate route plotted through the asteroid field. It'll cost us extra fuel and time, but we keep our credits.

fight.text: The Bulwark corvette opens fire. A toll collector is still a warship -- this won't be easy. You break through, but Bulwark will remember.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
