start.text: Wrecked scout ship ahead. Boarding party found a mummified captain clutching a hand-drawn star chart. It marks a location labeled "THE VAULT" with a note: "Enough wealth for ten lifetimes. The combination is my daughter's birthday. I never learned it."

choices.label: Salvage the wreck and move on.

take.speaker: Science Officer
take.text: The vault's coordinates are in a dangerous sector. We'd need to find the captain's identity and track down his daughter across multiple stations to get the combination. Or we could try brute-forcing it on site.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Standard salvage from the wreck. Nothing special beyond the map, which we left with the captain. Some things should stay buried.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: A dense cloud of luminous spores is engulfing the ship. They're alive, semi-intelligent, and looking for a host. They're infiltrating through micro-gaps in the hull plating.

choices.label: Let farming crew redirect them to a garden.

seal.speaker: Engineer
seal.text: Hull sealed. The spores are dying off without organic material to colonize. We caught it just in time -- another minute and they'd have reached food storage.

garden.text: Your farming specialist redirected the spores to a contained garden area. They're producing food rapidly -- should last about a week before the colony dies off naturally.

weaponize.speaker: Science Officer
weaponize.text: I've contained and concentrated the spores into deployable grenades. Military factions will pay well for biological area-denial weapons like these.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A tiny automated station in deep void -- antenna arrays all pointed toward intergalactic space. It's been listening for 12,000 years. Its last entry, logged yesterday, reads: "SIGNAL DETECTED. MATCHING CRITERIA. INITIATING RESPONSE PROTOCOL." Captain, something out there answered.

choices.label: Destroy the station before it transmits.

study.speaker: Science Officer
study.text: Twelve millennia of deep-space monitoring data. The technology alone is ancient and priceless. But what it called... I'm not sure we want to know.

destroy.text: The station breaks apart under weapons fire. Whatever signal it was responding to goes unanswered. Your science officer stares at the debris. "What if that was our only chance to hear back?"

choices.label: Or our only chance to stay hidden.

leave.text: You leave the station to its ancient purpose. Its antenna dish tracks toward the void between galaxies, transmitting a reply 12,000 years in the making. Strange things may follow.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Food stores are empty, Captain. The crew can survive 72 hours before the first death. Morale is already cratering. We need a solution now.

choices.label: Emergency foraging at the nearest planet.
Have the cook render emergency rations from inedible cargo.

forage.text: Your farming and mining crew scoured the nearest planetoid. Edible lichen, mineral-rich fungi, some passable tubers. It's not gourmet, but it'll keep us alive.

beacon.speaker: Comm Channel
beacon.text: A ship responded to our beacon. They have food -- but they want 200 credits for it. "Supply and demand, friend. Take it or starve."

paste.text: Your cook rendered hull sealant and lubricants into a grey nutrient paste. It's technically edible. The crew's faces as they eat it tell a story of profound suffering.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: That star is shedding luminous tears -- plasma flowing upward against gravity. Something inside the star is feeding, has been for millions of years. At the current rate, the star has 50,000 years left.

choices.label: Sell the data on the open market.

cotac.speaker: Science Officer
cotac.text: COTAC wants this suppressed. "Some knowledge serves no purpose but to frighten." They pay for our silence and the raw data.

isd.speaker: Science Officer
isd.text: ISD is fascinated. They want to study whatever is inside that star. The research potential is immense -- as is the danger.

sell.text: The data sells well on the open market. Every faction wants a look at what's eating a star from the inside.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three ships drifting in formation. All three crews respond with the same confused message: "Where are we? What day is it? Why can't any of us remember the last six months?" Logs show normal operations up to a specific date, then nothing.

choices.label: Help them with fuel and coordinates.
Leave them to figure it out.

help.speaker: Comm Channel
help.text: You share fuel and navigation data. The crews are deeply grateful. "We don't know what happened to us, but we won't forget your kindness. Well... hopefully we won't."

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: Medical scans show traces of an unknown energy signature in their neural tissue. No physical trauma. Six months of memory -- just gone. The energy signature matches readings from deep-space monitoring stations.

leave.text: You leave the confused fleet to sort themselves out. Three ships full of people with six months of missing time. Whatever did this is still out there.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict ship ahead. Interior is... Captain, it's an art installation. Hundreds of bodies preserved in resin, posed in scenes of daily life. A plaque reads: "THEY LIVED. I REMEMBER."

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: The artist is a maintenance drone -- ancient, still collecting bodies from derelicts for centuries. Trying to preserve the memory of the dead. Not hostile. Just deeply unsettling.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: The artifacts are well-preserved and valuable. Extracting them from those tableaux cost the crew their appetites for a week.

leave.text: You seal the derelict. The drone inside continues its lonely vigil, adding to its gallery whenever the void delivers another forgotten soul.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Intersecting planes of light, each kilometers wide, weaving through each other. Matter that passes through emerges reorganized at the molecular level. It's a manufacturing plant for something we can't comprehend.

feed.speaker: Science Officer
feed.text: It produced a single object of unknown purpose -- elegant, dense, warm. Xenoculture knows what it is but won't explain. They're paying handsomely.

study.speaker: Science Officer
study.text: Our warpsmith analyzed the molecular reorganization. The insights will improve our crafting efficiency significantly.

observe.text: The Loom transforms stray asteroids into perfect geometric shapes. Engineering beyond comprehension, running on autopilot for eons.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A pirate hails you with a sigh. "Look, I'm supposed to rob you, but my heart's not in it today. Morale's garbage, ship's falling apart, and I think piracy isn't my calling."

trade.speaker: Comm Channel
trade.text: "Finally, a normal transaction." He has surprisingly good stock at fair prices and seems genuinely relieved to do honest business for once.

advice.speaker: Comm Channel
advice.text: An hour of career counseling later, he's beaming. "You're right. I'm going to try trading. Thanks, Captain." He tips you before warping out.

rob.text: He barely fights back. Not much in the hold, and the crew feels guilty about kicking a man when he's down.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thousands of translucent void jellyfish, shuttle-sized, trailing electromagnetic tendrils. Peaceful unless touched -- a single sting delivers an EMP that disables a module.

navigate.text: Careful piloting threads you through without a sting. A crew member watches through the viewport: "Space is just an ocean we forgot how to swim in."

harvest.speaker: Science Officer
harvest.text: Their bodies contain superconducting compounds of extraordinary purity. Worth a fortune on any market.

around.text: You give the bloom a wide berth. Extra fuel spent, but no risk of an EMP sting frying your systems.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Reactor cascade in progress! I need to stabilize it NOW or we're looking at a full meltdown. We can try direct repair or fabricate containment rods if we have materials.

direct.speaker: Engineer
direct.text: Re-routed coolant loops and damped the cascade. Reactor's stable but at half capacity until proper repairs. That was too close.

fabricate.speaker: Engineer
fabricate.text: Emergency containment rods fabricated in record time. Cascade contained. Reactor fully operational.

evacuate.text: The crew evacuates. Reactor melts down, module destroyed. Limping on backup power to the nearest station for a replacement at 400 credits.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Kilometers long, with crystalline data-storage growths across its skin. Star charts, species encyclopedias, historical records spanning millions of years. It's a living library.

choices.label: Read a small portion of the data.

read.speaker: Science Officer
read.text: Star charts of unmapped regions. Extinct species. History compressed into crystal. Worth a fortune in science data.

catalog.speaker: Science Officer
catalog.text: Xenoculture will be thrilled. A living library of galactic history, preserved in a void whale.

observe.text: The archive whale drifts past, carrying knowledge beyond counting. You watch in silence as a living museum disappears into the void.

choices.label: Some things are bigger than credits.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Artificial gravity well activated -- pulling us toward a pirate base. "Welcome to the web, little fly. Cargo or hull -- your choice."

fight.text: Fighting in the gravity well is brutal, but you disable the pirates and find stash coordinates in the wreckage.

disrupt.speaker: Engineer
disrupt.text: Hit the generator with a feedback pulse. Gravity well collapsed, pirates scattered.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: They strip your hold and release you. Humiliating, but intact.

start.text: A station not on any chart, staffed by masked beings speaking in riddles. They sell impossible things: a jar labeled "COURAGE," a seed that grows in vacuum, a device pointing toward what you need most.

choices.label: Buy the jar of COURAGE (200 credits).

courage.text: Nothing visible comes out of the jar, but the crew feels braver. When you look back, the station is gone. The crew can't agree on what the merchants looked like.

seed.text: The seed takes root on an external hull panel and begins producing edible fruit -- in vacuum. When you look back, the station is gone.

leave.text: You leave without buying. The station vanishes behind you. Empty space. Always.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Something is eating our hull -- metallovore organisms metabolizing ship plating. Integrity dropping 2% per hour.

toxic.speaker: Engineer
toxic.text: Smelter crew cooked up a metallic toxin. Parasites died on contact. Ship's immune now.

remove.speaker: Engineer
remove.text: Four hours of EVA work. Every parasite removed, and their mineral-rich shells are actually valuable.

blast.speaker: Engineer
blast.text: Point defense cleared them, but we caught some friendly fire. Hull's worse for wear.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Life pod beacon. Inside: a Castellan noble with evidence of ISD illegal weapons testing. "Get me to a Castellan embassy and I'll make you rich."

castellan.speaker: Comm Channel
castellan.text: Castellan intelligence pays handsomely on delivery. But ISD will be sending hunters.

isd.speaker: Comm Channel
isd.text: ISD agents take the noble without a word. Payment arrives. The noble's face as they're led away stays with you.

neutral.text: You drop them at a neutral station. They press personal funds into your hands. "Not what I hoped for, but I'm alive."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: All emissions ceased. No radio, no scanners, no comms. Stars vanished from viewports. Total sensory blackout. Crew is panicking.

gradient.speaker: Engineer
gradient.text: Warpsmith found the field boundary. Three hours of blind flying, but we emerged. Stars never looked so good.

random.text: Hours in total darkness before stars reappear. The crew is deeply shaken.

wait.text: Hours of absolute silence. The field dissipates on its own. Crew is rattled but intact.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A spiral staircase of solid neutronium, each step city-block sized, ascending into higher dimensions. At step 30 the crew perceives four spatial dimensions and calls it "horrible."

ascend.speaker: Science Officer
ascend.text: Reached step 40. A chamber with a perfectly preserved alien corpse in a chair, dead 3 billion years. What was it waiting for? The data from each level is priceless.

base.speaker: Science Officer
base.text: Base readings alone are extraordinary. Neutronium defying material science. Solid data without the existential horror.

leave.text: The stairway spirals into dimensions you can't perceive. You leave it and the dead thing waiting at the top.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Your cook has rebelled. "I refuse to cook until we get proper ingredients. I'm an artist, Captain, not a paste dispenser."

buy.text: With proper ingredients, the cook prepares a feast. Morale soars. Sometimes the crew just needs a good meal.

order.text: The cook returns to duty but makes displeasure known through aggressively bland meals. Technically edible. Spiritually devastating.

fire.text: "You fired the cook?!" echoes through the ship. In hindsight, firing the person who feeds everyone was not your finest moment.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Magnetar burst incoming! Shields absorbing 70% but the rest is getting through. Hull's taking thermal damage.

medical.speaker: Medic
medical.text: Crew sealed in shelters. Minor symptoms only. Hull took a beating from thermal, though.

shields.speaker: Engineer
shields.text: Boosted shields to 90% absorption. Crew exposure minimal. Hull still took some thermal damage.

brace.speaker: Medic
brace.text: Two crew with radiation sickness. Hull took heavy damage. We weren't prepared.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A derelict containing a model of itself, inside a larger version of itself. "We're inside the model." The recursion goes deeper than I can measure.

navigate.speaker: Science Officer
navigate.text: Warpsmith found the outermost layer. Cargo hold full of salvage. We extracted it and ejected. I need a drink.

leave.text: Six hours of confused navigation and wasted fuel before ejecting into normal space. Ontological distress all around.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A medical frigate. "The void doesn't care about your politics. Neither do I." Free treatment, supplies at cost. She asks nothing in return.

heal.speaker: Comm Channel
heal.text: She patches up your crew with practiced efficiency. "Take care of yourselves out there."

donate.speaker: Comm Channel
donate.text: She takes the donation with quiet gratitude and shares intelligence about a nearby medical emergency worth pursuing.

leave.text: The medical frigate continues its rounds. A rare light in the void.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A massive automated factory ship -- still operational, still producing the same component for centuries. The output has formed a debris field of trillions of identical parts.

choices.label: Shut it down and reclaim materials.

shutdown.speaker: Engineer
shutdown.text: Production halted. Our smelting crew is reclaiming raw materials from the debris field. Centuries of output makes for a rich haul.

assemble.speaker: Science Officer
assemble.text: After collecting a hundred components and assembling them, our warpsmith identified the completed device -- it boosts shield efficiency. Incredible find.

leave.text: The factory ship continues its eternal task, producing components for a purpose long forgotten. The debris field grows imperceptibly larger.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Entire crew lost consciousness for exactly 4.7 seconds simultaneously. Everyone remembers being examined by something vast. One crew member now speaks sentences in an unknown language -- describing our position in real time.

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: The language is mathematical, describing our ship's position with impossible precision. Something is tracking us through this crew member. It seems harmless, but deeply unsettling.

xeno.text: Xenoculture contacts perform a disconnection ritual. The crew member stops speaking the strange language and remembers nothing. The trackers, whatever they were, have lost your signal.

monitor.text: You note the phenomenon and carry on. The affected crew member occasionally mutters coordinates in their sleep. Harmless, probably. The crew gives them a wide berth.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Union Militia broadcast: a frontier colony needs emergency supplies. 200 credits and rep for delivering 30 food and 20 fuel within 48 hours. Route passes through Fringe territory.

accept.text: You deliver the supplies through Fringe-contested space. The colony governor thanks you personally. A grateful colonist volunteers to join your crew.

decline.text: You pass on the run. Crew who overheard the broadcast exchange uncomfortable glances. A colony goes without.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Bioluminescent organisms creating false star patterns -- our navigation can't tell real stars from biological mimics. We're flying blind.

instruments.speaker: Sensor Officer
instruments.text: Backup instruments got us through. The organisms are following our engine emissions now -- a trail of light marking our position visible from vast distances. It'll fade in 12 hours.

filter.speaker: Science Officer
filter.text: Filtered the bioluminescence from our sensor feeds. Navigation restored. We can see the real stars again.

push.text: We flew in circles for six hours, wasting fuel, before stumbling out of the field. The organisms are trailing us now, lit up like a beacon.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A solo engineer in a ship that's more modification than hull hails you. "I've created a perpetual motion engine! Well, almost. It runs for 11 minutes and 7 seconds, then explodes. But those 11 minutes are magnificent!"

choices.label: Buy a burst drive module (100 credits).
Have your engineer assess his mods.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Excellent! Remember: 11 minutes of glory, then get clear. The explosion is... energetic." He hands over the module with manic glee.

assess.speaker: Engineer
assess.text: Most of his modifications are insane. But his turbo thruster design is actually sound -- I can adapt it for a small efficiency gain with minimal risk.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss! Those 11 minutes could change your life!" He warps away in a shower of sparks. His ship looks like it shouldn't fly, yet somehow it does.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A reef of crystalline coral in a nebula. Each branch contains frozen experiential memories from beings who touched it. It's been collecting for millions of years.

touch.text: A rush of alien experience floods your mind -- an alien watching a sunset on a world with three moons. The beauty of it lingers. Each crew member who touches it gains a fragment of alien knowledge.

sample.speaker: Science Officer
sample.text: The sample contains thousands of preserved memories. Xenoculture will pay generously for this -- it's a window into civilizations long gone.

observe.text: The coral pulses with faint light, each flicker a preserved moment from a life long ended. You watch, but don't touch. Some memories should stay where they are.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Reactor coolant system ruptured! Temperature rising fast. I can try to patch it, or we can fabricate emergency coolant from raw materials.

patch.speaker: Engineer
patch.text: Patch is holding. Temperature dropping. That was a close one -- another few minutes and we'd have been running on batteries.

fabricate.speaker: Engineer
fabricate.text: Emergency coolant fabricated from raw stock. Not only is the system restored, the recalibrated mixture is actually more efficient than the original.

scram.speaker: Engineer
scram.text: Reactor scrammed. We're on emergency battery -- no weapons, no shields, no warp for 8 hours while coolant is restored. We're vulnerable.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Hundreds of life pods in formation -- all empty, hatches opened from inside. Logs say the entire crew of 400 evacuated and then opened their pods to the void. Simultaneously. One pod isn't empty -- a child in cryosleep.

choices.label: Wake the child and take them aboard.
Deliver the pod to the nearest station.

wake.speaker: Medic
wake.text: The child remembers nothing. They're scared and confused. The crew's protective instincts kick in immediately -- everyone wants to help.

deliver.text: You deliver the cryopod to the nearest station. Relatives are found within days. The reward is modest, but the crew feels good about it.

leave.text: You leave the child in cryo among the empty pods. The crew is quiet for days afterward.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Aggressive fungus has colonized our food storage, spreading fast. We've lost a significant portion of our food stores. Hallucinogenic spores are affecting crew without medical treatment.

choices.label: Cook the contaminated food into safe rations.

contain.text: Your farming specialist identified the strain and contained the bloom before it reached hydroponics. Remaining food stores are safe.

cook.text: Your cook processed the contaminated food into safe rations. Not pleasant, but edible. Better than starvation.

purge.speaker: Engineer
purge.text: Sections purged. The fungus is dead, but so is most of our food supply. The hallucinogenic spores affected three crew members before we sealed the area.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A visible tear in space -- reality damaged, showing impossible colors. Ships nearby experience random module activations. A warp drive detonated here and cracked the fabric of space. It's healing, but centuries more.

fly.speaker: Engineer
fly.text: Energy leaked from the scar as we passed through -- topped off our fuel reserves. Lucky break. Could have gone the other way.

extract.speaker: Science Officer
extract.text: Our warpsmith carefully extracted scar matter -- reality-warped material with extraordinary properties. This will fetch an incredible price.

data.speaker: Science Officer
data.text: Detailed scans from safe distance. The data on spatial damage and healing is worth good credits to any science faction.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A station of 200 people -- all with amnesia. They know how to run their systems but nobody remembers their name or history. Medical scans show artificial memory suppression. Someone did this deliberately.

choices.label: Help them with supplies and move on.

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: ISD records show this was a witness protection program gone wrong -- an entire station wiped to protect one person. The administrator. Restoring their memory reveals the location of an ISD black site.

help.text: You provide supplies and basic navigational data. The colonists are grateful, even if they don't know who they are. It's the least you can do.

leave.text: Two hundred people with no memory, running a station on muscle memory alone. You leave them to their strange, nameless existence.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: An organism attached to our hull is secreting a compound that reinforces our plating. Engineering confirms it's beneficial -- but it's growing, covering viewports and sensors. It's trying to protect us. From what?

keep.speaker: Science Officer
keep.text: The hull bonus is significant. We'll need to clear viewports periodically, but the organism pulses warnings when danger approaches. A living early-warning system.

remove.speaker: Engineer
remove.text: Removed cleanly. Simple enough. But I can't shake the feeling it was trying to protect us from something specific, and now we're exposed.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan merchant consortium is holding a deep-space auction. Items include a shield generator, rare spices, navigational data, and a mysterious alien artifact that nobody else is bidding on.

choices.label: Bid on the alien artifact (50 credits).

spices.speaker: Comm Channel
spices.text: You win the spice cache. Exotic flavors from across the sector -- your cook is thrilled. Equivalent to a significant food boost.

artifact.speaker: Science Officer
artifact.text: Nobody else bid. The artifact glows in proximity to void creatures -- it's a universal translator for bioluminescent communication. Invaluable for future void fauna encounters.

navdata.speaker: Sensor Officer
navdata.text: Three uncharted systems now on our star map. Who knows what's out there waiting to be discovered.

watch.text: You watch the auction play out. The artifact goes unsold. The auctioneer shrugs and tosses it in a bin. A missed opportunity, perhaps.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A crew member confesses they're wanted by COTAC for a crime they didn't commit -- falsified evidence of smuggling. A COTAC patrol in the next system is looking for them.

hide.speaker: Engineer
hide.text: Modified the crew manifest and tucked them in a maintenance shaft during the inspection. COTAC didn't find them. But if they ever check their records against ours...

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: Cross-referencing station records and comms data, we traced the frame job to a Fringe smuggler. COTAC was embarrassed but grateful for the truth. Our crew member is cleared.

turnin.text: COTAC takes them. The bounty appears in your account. The rest of your crew watches in silence. Trust erodes visibly.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Stars going dark ahead. Our lights are dimming -- something is absorbing photons. Total darkness outside, emergency lighting only inside. "It's not alive. It's a region where light goes to die."

push.text: Eight hours of total darkness. Emergency lighting. Shields partially drained. The crew held together, barely. You emerge into starlight again, rattled but intact.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Detailed scans of the Light Eater phenomenon. Bulwark patrols will pay well for this -- they need to know where the dark zones are expanding.

back.text: You reverse course before the darkness swallows you completely. The long way around costs fuel, but at least you can see where you're going.

581.title: Megastructure: The Gate That Goes Nowhere

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A ring structure 500 meters across with power readings off the charts. It's a gate, but dormant. Our warpsmith thinks they can activate it.

activate.speaker: Science Officer
activate.text: The gate opens onto folded space -- a pristine world. Breathable atmosphere, liquid water, no life. A time capsule. We have one hour before it closes. Resources everywhere.

study.speaker: Science Officer
study.text: The gate's technology is extraordinary -- folded-space engineering we can barely comprehend. The study data alone is valuable.

leave.text: The gate sits dormant, a portal to somewhere unknown. You leave it to wait for the next curious traveler.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three ISD vessels have gone AWOL. "We were ordered to shell a civilian outpost. We refused. Now we're running." They need fuel and a recommendation to any non-ISD faction.

help.speaker: Comm Channel
help.text: You provide fuel and coordinates to friendly space. In gratitude, they hand over military-grade weapon modules. One of them -- an exceptional engineer -- asks to join your crew.

turnin.text: ISD sends a retrieval squad. The bounty is generous. Your crew knows what happens to deserters who refused immoral orders. Morale tanks.

leave.text: You wish them luck and move on. Three ships full of people who chose conscience over orders, adrift in hostile space.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Our comms array detected embedded data in the cosmic microwave background -- a message in the oldest light in the universe. I've spent 12 hours decoding it. It's a star chart of every galaxy, with one location circled. That location is 10 million years away at maximum warp.

choices.label: Sell the chart as a scientific curiosity.

sell.speaker: Science Officer
sell.text: The chart sells for a premium. Every scientist in the sector wants a look. But that circled location haunts my dreams. What if that's where it all started?

choices.label: Some answers are beyond our reach.

archive.speaker: Science Officer
archive.text: Archived in our databanks. A message from the beginning of time, pointing to a place we'll never reach. The crew finds it humbling rather than frustrating.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "I am Korrath the Undying. You're in my territory. Beat my champion in single combat and I'll give you free passage through the Fringe for life. Lose, and your cargo is mine."

accept.text: The champion's corvette is fast and well-armed, but you outfly them. Korrath roars with approval over comms. "A worthy warrior! Free passage is yours, and prize money besides."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: Korrath laughs. "A coward, but an honest one. I respect that more than false bravado. Go in peace." No penalty, and a grudging nod of respect.

choices.label: Discretion is the better part of valor.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A planet broadcasting coherent thought patterns. Everyone in range is dreaming its dreams -- crystal forests, liquid metal oceans, a civilization that became the planet itself. The dreams are addictive. 4.7 billion minds dreaming together for 100,000 years.

choices.label: Leave before the dreams take hold.

leave.text: You pull away before the dreams sink too deep. The crew is wistful but clearheaded. A few look back at the planet with longing.

data.speaker: Science Officer
data.text: Recorded the thought patterns and neural mapping data. Fascinating -- a civilization that chose transcendence over expansion. The data is valuable.

linger.speaker: Medic
linger.text: We stayed too long. One crew member tried to land, claiming they were being called home. Had to sedate them. The rest of us feel a lingering pull even after we left.

start.speaker: Medic
start.text: Crew member critically injured -- a hull panel fell during turbulence. Without surgery within 2 hours, they die. I can attempt the operation, but it's high-risk.

choices.label: Put them in cryosleep and rush to station.

surgery.speaker: Medic
surgery.text: Surgery successful. Full recovery expected. The crew is visibly relieved -- they were watching your decisions closely.

cryo.speaker: Medic
cryo.text: Patient stabilized in cryosleep. We'll need to reach a station quickly for proper surgery, but they'll survive the trip.

nothing.text: The crew member dies within the hour. The ship is silent. Their friends on the crew stare at you with something between grief and accusation.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A ship caught in a temporal loop -- it explodes, reappears intact, explodes again, every 47 seconds. The crew inside is aware. They've lived those 47 seconds for what they perceive as years.

board.text: Your warpsmith disrupted the temporal loop. The crew -- haggard, weeping with relief -- embrace your boarding party. "You freed us. We've experienced eternity in 47-second increments."

observe.speaker: Science Officer
observe.text: Temporal loop data recorded. Extraordinary readings. The crew inside presses their hands against the viewport each cycle, mouths forming the word "please."

leave.text: You leave. The ship continues its cycle -- explode, reform, explode. Forty-seven seconds of hope, forty-seven seconds of death, forever.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: This station sells "exotic proteins" at great prices. The food is delicious. But Captain... I ran an analysis. The amino acid profile -- this isn't animal protein. It's from sapient species.

free.text: You found a holding area with captive aliens. Station guards fought back, but you overpowered them. The freed captives are traumatized but alive.

confront.speaker: Comm Channel
confront.text: They deny everything. "You're imagining things, Captain." But the science doesn't lie. Without proof of captives, there's nothing you can do officially.

leave.text: You leave without buying. Your science officer stares at you. The knowledge sits heavy between you like a stone.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: Twenty-seven stars in this region are moving in perfect synchronization, rearranging into a geometric pattern. Something is moving stars. The pattern will complete in 800 years -- a three-dimensional warning written in stellar positions.

choices.label: Share with COTAC (they want it classified).

sell.speaker: Science Officer
sell.text: Every faction wants this data. A warning written in stars over 800 years -- from whom, to whom, about what? The mystery alone drives the price up.

cotac.speaker: Comm Channel
cotac.text: COTAC classifies the data immediately. "Some warnings are best left unread by the public." They pay well for compliance.

log.text: You log the phenomenon for your own records. Someone is rearranging stars to spell a warning. In 800 years, the message will be readable. You wonder who it's meant for.

start.text: Weeks of hard travel have broken your crew's spirit. Morale is critical. Fights are breaking out. Two crew members want to leave at the next station. Something has to change now.

choices.label: Address the crew with a speech.

celebrate.text: Your entertainment officer pulls together a proper celebration. Music, food, games. The crew remembers why they signed on. Spirits lift dramatically.

drink.text: The alcohol flows. Tension dissolves. One crew member gets drunk and damages a module, but the rest of the crew is laughing for the first time in weeks.

speech.text: You address the crew directly. Honest, raw, from the heart. You acknowledge the hardship and promise better days. They listen. They believe you. For now.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark warden approaches. "A war criminal is hiding in the asteroid field ahead. My ship's too large to pursue. 400 credits alive, 200 dead." The target is a former COTAC admiral who bombed civilians.

hunt.text: You corner the admiral in the asteroid field. They surrender after a brief exchange of fire. The Bulwark warden pays the full bounty. COTAC won't be pleased.

letgo.speaker: Comm Channel
letgo.text: The admiral offers 300 credits and intel on Bulwark patrol routes for safe passage. Profitable, but morally ambiguous -- they did bomb civilians.

decline.text: You decline the bounty. The warden nods curtly and moves on to find another hunter. Not your fight.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, our crew roster shows one more person than we actually have. Unfamiliar name. Records show they've been aboard for months -- duty logs, meal tickets, bunk assignment. But nobody's ever seen them.

choices.label: Delete the entry and move on.

investigate.speaker: Science Officer
investigate.text: Their bunk has belongings that don't match any known species. A journal in unknown script describing our journey from the perspective of someone watching from "outside the hull, from the thin space." Worth something to Xenoculture.

delete.text: You delete the phantom entry. It reappears the next morning. You delete it again. It stays gone this time. The belongings in the empty bunk remain. Nobody claims them.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A massive tanker parks at the crossroads and sells fuel at 150% markup. "Supply and demand, friend. Nearest station's 18 hours away."

choices.label: Point out his cracked seal for a discount.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Pleasure doing business." Expensive, but you're fueled up and back on your way.

discount.speaker: Comm Channel
discount.text: His eyes widen. "A cracked seal? Where?!" Your hauling crew spotted the leak. "You just saved me a fortune in lost cargo. 30% discount -- take what you need, friend."

leave.text: You pass on the overpriced fuel. 18 hours to the nearest station it is.

start.speaker: Science Officer
start.text: A hollowed asteroid filled with millions of seeds -- every plant species from a world that no longer exists. Perfectly preserved for millennia. A plaque reads: "For whoever comes after. Grow well."

choices.label: Take seed samples for our ship.

take.text: Your farming crew weeps as they carefully select samples. "This is priceless. Someone saved their whole world's ecosystem." Crop starts and farming knowledge secured.

xeno.speaker: Science Officer
xeno.text: Xenoculture is ecstatic. They dispatch a preservation team immediately and pay generously for the find.

leave.text: You leave the seed vault undisturbed, a memorial to a dead world's hope. Someone will find it who needs it more.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: COTAC and Castellan fleets massing near the border. A Castellan officer hails: "Civilian vessel, this sector is about to become a warzone. Choose a side or leave."

choices.label: Offer medical aid to both sides.

castellan.speaker: Comm Channel
castellan.text: You escort Castellan scouts against COTAC vanguard patrols. The fighting is intense but brief. Castellan command is grateful.

neutral.text: You treat wounded from both sides, faction irrelevant. Both commands respect your neutrality and pay for medical services.

leave.text: You clear the sector before the shooting starts. Behind you, weapons fire lights up the void. Not your war.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Encrypted channel from a stealth ship. "War's coming. Everyone knows it. I've got weapons, shields, armor plating -- and prices go up tomorrow."

hull.speaker: Comm Channel
hull.text: "Smart choice. You'll want that extra plating where we're all headed." The hull reinforcement kit is military-grade. Quality stuff.

shields.speaker: Comm Channel
shields.text: "Advanced shield modules, fresh from the Castellan production line. Don't ask how I got them." They're legitimate military hardware.

pass.speaker: Comm Channel
pass.text: "Your funeral, friend. When the shooting starts, don't say I didn't offer." The stealth ship cloaks and vanishes.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Twelve civilian ships fleeing the coming conflict. Dented hulls, failing engines, children visible through portholes. "Please, Captain. There are children on these ships. We need an escort to neutral space."

escort.text: Twelve hours and three raider attacks later, the convoy reaches neutral space. Exhausting, dangerous, and absolutely worth it. Two grateful refugees volunteer to join your crew.

choices.label: It was the right thing to do.

donate.text: You share what you can spare. The convoy spokeswoman thanks you with tears in her eyes. They push on without escort.

decline.text: You decline. The convoy moves on without protection. Your crew is quiet. Some won't meet your eyes.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A scarred mercenary in a kill-tallied gunship hails you. "Name's Drake. Factions are hiring killers for the war. I've got a contract list -- 10 targets, 100 credits each. Split the work?"

accept.speaker: Comm Channel
accept.text: "Now we're talking. I'll take the hard targets, you take the easy ones. Meet back here when it's done." Drake transmits coordinates and target profiles. This will be bloody work.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: Drake shrugs. "More for me." His gunship cloaks and vanishes. You suspect you'll see him again -- as ally or competitor remains to be seen.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark fortress station on contested space is preparing for siege. They're buying everything at inflated prices: food, fuel, weapons. Enormously profitable to sell here, but those supplies won't be available to you later.

choices.label: Use their free repairs and move on.

sell.speaker: Comm Channel
sell.text: The station quartermaster pays triple for everything. Your hold is empty but your wallet is full. Bulwark appreciates the support.

contract.speaker: Comm Channel
contract.text: "Deliver supplies regularly and we guarantee 100 credits per run plus safe harbor." A steady income during wartime, but being associated with Bulwark marks you.

repairs.speaker: Engineer
repairs.text: Free repairs from Bulwark engineering crews. They're skilled and efficient -- our ship hasn't been in this good shape in weeks.

start.text: The night before everything changes. Your crew gathers in the mess hall, unusually quiet. The cook makes the best meal they can. Someone plays music. Your pilot stares out the viewport: "I've got a bad feeling about what's coming."

choices.label: Share a moment with the crew.

share.text: Each crew member shares something personal -- a hope, a fear, a memory. The bonding is genuine. Whatever comes next, you face it together.

science.speaker: Science Officer
science.text: "Captain, I've been analyzing fleet movements. This isn't a border skirmish. This is full-scale war. Every system we know will be affected." In the distance, weapons fire lights the horizon like lightning. The war has begun.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A makeshift barricade of welded ship hulls blocks the lane. "Fifty credits or you float home in pieces. Fringe Collective doesn't do charity." Three corvettes power up behind the barricade.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Smart. Move along." The barricade slides open just enough for your ship. Quick and painless.

talk.speaker: Comm Channel
talk.text: You spin a tale about carrying medical supplies for a Fringe outpost. They buy it -- barely. "Fine, pass through. But next time, bring proof."

blast.text: You punch through the barricade at full throttle. The corvettes give chase but you outrun them. Hull took some hits from the debris.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Fresh wreckage -- a cargo hauler torn apart minutes ago. Three pirate ships still looting the remains. They've spotted us. "Another gift from the void! Lock 'em up, boys."

fight.text: Three-on-one is bad odds, but the pirates are spread thin from looting. You pick them off one by one. The hauler's cargo containers float free -- yours for the taking.

run.text: You burn hard and outpace them. They don't pursue far -- too busy with the hauler's cargo. You escape with your hull intact but nothing to show for it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Halt for inspection. Castellan Naval Authority, Sector Patrol 77. Prepare to be boarded." A Castellan military frigate locks weapons and waits.

comply.speaker: Comm Channel
comply.text: Inspection is thorough but professional. "Everything checks out. Move along, civilian." A minor delay, but no trouble.

run.text: The frigate opens fire immediately. Lance batteries and military shields -- running from Castellan Navy was a mistake. You escape but take serious damage.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: "We're on a medical emergency run, officer." They verify your story is plausible enough to let you through with a warning. "Next time, have proper documentation."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Every frequency screaming the same message: "STELLAR COLLAPSE IMMINENT -- EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY." A nearby star is swelling, light shifting deep red. Ninety seconds before the shockwave. Civilian ships ahead are struggling to spin up warp drives.

flee.text: You punch warp with seconds to spare. The shockwave clips your aft section but you're alive. Behind you, the star dies in a bloom of light. You don't look back.

guide.text: You broadcast warp coordinates and buy the civilians time by running interference. Every ship makes it out. The shockwave hits your shields hard as you're the last to jump.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A converted cargo platform surrounded by spectator ships broadcasts: "WELCOME TO THE RING! 500 credits and a rare weapon module if you survive three rounds against increasingly dangerous fighters!"

fight.text: Round one: a junker, easy. Round two: a veteran pirate, tough. Round three: a Bulwark deserter in a heavy gunship with railguns. You survive all three. The crowd goes wild.

watch.text: You watch the current challenger get demolished in round two. Entertaining, but you're glad it's not you in there. The crew enjoys the spectacle.

leave.text: You pass on the bloodsport and continue on your way.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Forty-plus ships limping through the void -- dented hulls, failing engines, children's faces through portholes. "We're fleeing the Exclusion Zone. COTAC purged our colony. We need fuel, food, anything."

donate.text: You share what you can spare. The spokeswoman clutches your hands through the airlock. "Thank you. We won't forget this."

escort.text: You guide forty ships through hostile space. Raiders test you twice but back off when they see an armed escort. The convoy reaches safe harbor. Exhausting but meaningful.

leave.text: You pass the convoy without stopping. Forty ships full of refugees watch you go. Your crew is quiet afterward.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A sleek black ship decloaks 200 meters off port. "I've been tracking you for six systems. Someone wants you brought in -- alive, preferably. Dead works too."

fight.text: The hunter uses missile racks and ECM jammers. Tough fight, but you disable their ship. Their contract data reveals who hired them -- useful intelligence.

bribe.speaker: Comm Channel
bribe.text: "Double? That's... reasonable." Credits change hands. "I'll tell my client you're dead. Don't make me regret this." They cloak and vanish.

run.text: Their ship is fast but you know the local terrain better. You lose them in an asteroid field after a tense chase. They'll be back eventually.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A massive pirate carrier flanked by six escorts blocks your path. "I am Void Warlord Kessix. I rule this corridor. Every ship pays tribute: 200 credits, 20 fuel, or a crew member."

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Wise. You may pass." Kessix gives you a token that prevents future encounters with his ships. Expensive, but a long-term investment.

fight.text: A carrier and six escorts. This is a war, not a skirmish. You manage to break through with heavy damage, but Kessix will remember your defiance.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: Kessix raises an eyebrow. Your reputation precedes you. "Perhaps an alliance serves us both better than tribute. Pass freely -- and remember who your friends are."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Proximity mines everywhere! A synthesized voice: "You have entered ISD Containment Zone 14. Remain stationary for retrieval, or attempt exit at your own risk." ISD patrol incoming in 30 seconds.

wait.speaker: Comm Channel
wait.text: ISD agents board and inspect. Tense questioning, but they find nothing actionable. "Move along. Don't enter restricted zones." They escort you out.

navigate.text: Inch by inch, your pilot threads through the mines. Sweat-inducing precision flying. You clear the field just as the ISD patrol arrives.

brute.text: Multiple detonations rock your ship as you blast through at full speed. Hull takes heavy damage but you're clear before ISD arrives.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict freighter with flickering lights mimicking a distress signal. Interior smeared with blood, scratched tallies on walls -- hundreds. One survivor, feral and armed. Behind a sealed bulkhead: a cargo hold of rare minerals.

board.speaker: Medic
board.text: The survivor attacked our boarding party. We subdued them. Sealed suits protected us from whatever's in the air recycler that caused the psychotic breaks. The mineral cargo is secure.

external.speaker: Engineer
external.text: We pulled what we could from the exterior without breaching the hull. Not as much as going inside, but no risk of whatever drove that crew mad.

leave.text: You leave the cannibal ship to drift. The flickering lights continue their false distress call, luring the next curious traveler.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Two pirate factions in a vicious firefight -- eight ships total, beams and missiles crisscrossing the void. We've warped directly into the crossfire. Stray fire already hitting shields.

slip.text: Careful piloting threads you between the battling ships. A few stray hits but nothing critical. You clear the warzone intact.

wait.text: You hang back and wait. The battle ends with three ships limping away and five destroyed. The wreckage yields solid salvage.

engage.text: You wade into the fight guns blazing. Both sides turn on you briefly before returning to killing each other. Chaotic, brutal, profitable.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: That mineral-rich asteroid is moving. Crystalline tentacles unfurling from its surface. A deep vibration through our hull. It's a void leviathan in dormant phase -- station-sized -- and we just woke it.

choices.label: Scan it from a safe distance.

grab.speaker: Engineer
grab.text: Fast passes, quick grabs. We snagged crystal fragments worth a fortune before it fully woke. One tentacle grazed our hull on the last pass. Time to go.

flee.text: You burn engines and get clear before the leviathan fully awakens. Smart move -- those tentacles could crush a station.

scan.speaker: Science Officer
scan.text: Remarkable readings. A silicon-based mega-organism using crystalline structures for neural processing. The data is scientifically priceless.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You slowed for the escape pod and four pirate ships decloaked around you. "Works every time," their leader laughs. The pod is empty -- just a transmitter. They're jamming your warp drive.

fight.text: Surrounded and outgunned, but you fight like cornered wolves. Two pirates go down, the other two break off. Your hull is battered but you kept your cargo.

surrender.speaker: Comm Channel
surrender.text: "Smart move. Dump it all." They strip your cargo hold and vanish, leaving you alive but humiliated.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan military shuttle hails frantically. "Please, I'm not going back. They were going to execute me for what I saw." Lieutenant Mira Voss, deserter. Classified data and a price on her head.

take.speaker: Comm Channel
take.text: Voss comes aboard -- skilled pilot, decent fighter, haunted eyes. "Thank you, Captain. I'll earn my keep, I promise." Castellan will be looking for her.

turnin.speaker: Comm Channel
turnin.text: Castellan command is pleased. The bounty and reputation are worth it. Voss's face as she's led away -- she knew this might happen.

leave.text: You leave Voss in her shuttle. She'll find another ship, or Castellan will find her first. Not your concern.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Twenty-plus pirate vessels in formation ahead. A converted dreadnought flagship broadcasts: "All non-affiliated vessels: leave or be incorporated." This is not a fight we can win.

flee.text: You reverse course at maximum burn. The armada doesn't pursue -- they have bigger targets in mind. You live to fight another day.

hide.text: You cut engines and drift into a debris field, running silent. The armada passes without spotting you. Heart-stopping minutes of silence.

hail.speaker: Comm Channel
hail.text: The flagship responds. Your reputation with the Fringe earns you a hearing. They let you pass -- and offer a job. "We can always use more guns. Think about it."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive solar flare erupting -- wall of charged plasma heading our way. We can angle to minimize exposure, ride the edge for a speed boost, or take it head-on.

angle.speaker: Engineer
angle.text: Good call. Angled the ship to present minimum cross-section. Shields absorbed most of it. Minor exterior module damage only.

ride.text: Riding the flare's edge is terrifying and exhilarating -- the plasma wall propels you at incredible speed. Useful if someone was chasing you.

hit.speaker: Engineer
hit.text: Full flare impact. Shields dropped to zero. Exterior modules scorched. Not recommended.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Merchant ships clustered for an impromptu auction. The prize: a salvaged alien artifact. Bidding starts at 200 credits. Other bidders include a COTAC rep, a Xenoculture scholar, and a suspiciously wealthy pirate.

bid.text: Bidding war drives the price up, but you win. The artifact turns out to be a navigation module revealing hidden jump points. Incredibly useful.

bluff.text: You talk up fake defects in the artifact. The other bidders get cold feet and drop out. You win at base price.

watch.text: The Xenoculture scholar wins. She seems thrilled. You wonder what secrets the artifact held.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Something enormous in the darkness -- kilometers long, bioluminescent tendrils pulsing with predatory intent. A void kraken, thought to be myth. A tendril lashes toward us with terrifying speed.

choices.label: Go dark and hope it loses interest.

sever.text: Weapons sever the tendril. The kraken screams -- a sound that resonates through the hull. You grab the severed tissue and run. Xenoculture will pay a fortune for this.

evade.text: Maximum burn, weaving between tendrils. Your pilot earns their pay today. You clear the kraken's reach and don't slow down for an hour.

dark.text: Systems cut. Drifting in darkness. The tendrils probe around you, seeking. Minutes pass like hours. Finally, the kraken moves on. Your crew remembers how to breathe.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A pirate corvette latched onto a passenger liner. "1000 credits and safe passage, or we vent the passenger deck. Five minutes." 200 civilians at stake.

choices.label: Precision strike on the corvette's engines.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Pleasure doing business." The pirate detaches and warps away. 200 lives saved for a thousand credits. The liner's captain thanks you profusely.

strike.text: Precision gunnery disables the corvette's engines without hitting the liner. The pirates surrender. The liner's passengers cheer through their portholes.

board.text: Your combat crew breaches the corvette and secures it in minutes. The pirates are subdued. The hostages are safe. Your boarding team is bruised but proud.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Union Militia warships stretched across the space lane. "This sector is under martial law. Submit to full cargo inspection and crew manifest review."

submit.speaker: Comm Channel
submit.text: Inspection is thorough. They find nothing objectionable. "Clear to proceed. Stay safe out there, civilian."

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: You explain you're on an urgent medical run. The officer hesitates, then waves you through. "Go. But if I find out you lied..."

run.text: Concentrated beam fire from five warships. Running a Militia blockade is suicide in anything less than a cruiser. You take massive damage breaking through.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A gaudy pleasure yacht covered in flashing lights hails you. "Welcome, traveler! I am Fortuno the Magnificent! Care to test your luck? Stakes from 50 to 500 credits!"

choices.label: Enter the asteroid slalom race (100 credits).

cards.speaker: Comm Channel
cards.text: Pure luck -- and luck is with you today. Fortuno grumbles as he pays out. "Beginner's luck! Double or nothing?" You wisely walk away with your winnings.

race.text: Your pilot tears through the asteroid slalom while Fortuno's ship clips two rocks. "Impossible! My course, my rules, and you STILL won!" He pays up, pouting magnificently.

riddle.speaker: Comm Channel
riddle.text: Your science officer answers every riddle correctly. Fortuno is speechless. "You... you brought a SCIENTIST to a riddle contest?! That's cheating!" He pays anyway.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss, traveler! Fortuno the Magnificent awaits your return!" His yacht zips away in a shower of sparkles and bad taste.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A Castellan battlecruiser, dead in space. No power, no transponder, no life signs. Crew of 600, all gone. Boarding reveals everything intact but abandoned mid-meal, mid-conversation. The ship's log ends with: "They're already inside."

investigate.text: Deep in engineering, your crew hears movement in the walls. Something living has colonized the ship's infrastructure. You retreat with partial data -- enough to sell, not enough to explain what happened to 600 people.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Quick salvage from accessible areas. Military-grade components, personal effects. We didn't stay long enough to find out what happened. Probably for the best.

leave.text: You leave the battlecruiser to drift. 600 people vanished without a trace. "They're already inside" echoes in your mind. Inside what?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Fringe pirate on private channel: "COTAC supply convoy incoming -- four haulers, two frigates. Help me hit it and we split cargo 60/40. I draw the escorts, you crack the haulers."

raid.text: The pirate draws the frigates while you breach the haulers. Military cargo -- weapons, supplies, electronics. Your 40% share is substantial. COTAC won't be happy.

warn.speaker: Comm Channel
warn.text: You tip off the convoy. The escort frigates are waiting when the pirate attacks. COTAC command sends a thank-you and a reward.

leave.text: You watch from a distance as the pirate attacks alone. The frigates make short work of him. Not your problem.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A lone ship stops at weapons range. "I am Commander Thale of the Burning Wake. I challenge you to single combat -- ship to ship, no allies, no running. Winner takes the loser's cargo and one module."

accept.text: Thale's corvette is fast and well-armed -- lance batteries and point defense. A brutal, honest fight. You emerge victorious. Thale transmits respect: "Well fought. I'll remember this."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "A coward's choice. I'll let every channel know." Thale mocks you on open comms as they warp away. No real penalty, but your reputation takes a minor dent.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three alien ships of unfamiliar design surround you, their hulls covered in bioluminescent patterns. A translated message arrives: "You violate the boundary. Leave or be consumed."

diplomacy.speaker: Sensor Officer
diplomacy.text: They respond to our peaceful signals. The lead ship transmits coordinates for safe passage and a container of rare alien trade goods -- a sign of respect.

fight.speaker: Engineer
fight.text: Their weapons fire organic acid -- it ate through our hull plating! We drove them off but took serious damage.

retreat.text: You power up engines and leave their territory. The alien ships watch you go but do not pursue.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, we found someone hiding in the cargo hold -- a teenager, no ID, terrified. "Please don't send me back. The ISD took my family."

choices.label: Drop them at the next station.
Ask about the ISD black site.

keep.text: The kid is grateful but clearly traumatized. Another mouth to feed, but your crew respects the decision.

station.text: The teenager goes quietly, eyes hollow. Your crew is uncomfortable but understands.

intel.speaker: Comm Channel
intel.text: The kid's eyes light up. "I can show you where they took my family -- an unmarked station in the Drift." They hand over coordinates scratched on metal.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A massive explosion rips through a prison transport. Escape pods scatter as turrets fire indiscriminately. "This is Dax Morenni -- COTAC framed me. I need extraction NOW!"

rescue.speaker: Sensor Officer
rescue.text: Morenni is aboard -- bruised but functional, and his engineering credentials are real. COTAC is broadcasting our ID as accomplices.

recapture.speaker: Comm Channel
recapture.text: COTAC security acknowledges your assistance. Bounty credits transfer as each pod is recovered.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Grabbed what we could from the debris before COTAC reinforcements arrived. Good haul.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, that same unregistered signature is back -- edge of detection range, matching our heading exactly. Third time in as many jumps. It never approaches, never hails. It just follows.

confront.speaker: Sensor Officer
confront.text: The signature vanished the moment we turned. Like it was never there. Whatever this is, it does not want to be caught.

hail.text: Static on every channel. Your comms officer swears there is a pattern buried in the noise -- like breathing. Then the signal fades.

ignore.text: Your crew exchanges nervous glances. Nobody sleeps well. The signature remains at the edge of sensors, patient and silent.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Civilian vessel, you are in a restricted fire zone! However -- we could use an opposition force for our drill. 200 credits plus a Bulwark commendation. What say you?"

accept.speaker: Comm Channel
accept.text: The drill is intense -- simulated weapons still sting. Your crew dodges fire and nails drone targets. The commander sounds impressed.

leave.text: You clear the fire zone without incident. The Bulwark fleet resumes exercises behind you.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Four armored transports with six combat escorts -- a slaver convoy moving human cargo to a Fringe labor camp. Muffled distress signals leak from the transports.

choices.label: Attack the convoy and free the captives.
Follow at a distance to locate the camp.

attack.text: A brutal fight, but the transports crack open and dozens of captives float free. Word spreads fast.

follow.speaker: Sensor Officer
follow.text: We tracked them to their destination. This intel could fuel a much larger rescue operation.

ignore.text: You change course. The muffled cries fade from your comms. Your crew is quiet for a long time.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cluster of ships sit dead in space -- engines cold, reserves empty. "We've been here nine days. If you have fuel to spare, name your price. One of us has a rare star map to trade."

choices.label: Sell fuel at a steep markup.
Trade fuel for the star map.

sell.text: They pay through the nose but they are moving again. Desperate people pay desperate prices.

donate.speaker: Comm Channel
donate.text: "You're a saint, captain. We won't forget this." The stranded captains spread word of your generosity.

trade.speaker: Comm Channel
trade.text: The captain with the star map hands it over. "Routes the cartographers missed -- shortcuts, hidden depots. Worth more than fuel."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thousands of metallic micro-drones on sensors -- remnants of an ancient defense system. They are treating us as a target. Individual drones are harmless but the swarm corrodes hull plating.

choices.label: Activate point defense and sweep them.

defense.speaker: Engineer
defense.text: Point defense chews through them and beam sweeps clear whole clusters. Some hull corrosion but we are through. Salvageable drone components everywhere.

flee.speaker: Engineer
flee.text: Engines straining but we pulled ahead. Some drones latched on -- they did a number on the hull before we scraped them off.

endure.speaker: Engineer
endure.text: That was ugly. They ate through hull plating like acid. Venting atmosphere in two sections. But we are through.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two voices argue over the same channel. The captain screams for help. A mutineer responds: "This bastard hasn't paid us in three months! Stay out of it -- or don't."

captain.speaker: Comm Channel
captain.text: With your help, the captain regains control. "I owe you, friend. My home station will give you preferred rates."

mutiny.speaker: Comm Channel
mutiny.text: The mutineers win. Their leader offers her hand: "You stood with working people. Let me join your crew."

leave.text: You pull away as the argument escalates into weapons fire. Not your problem.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: A hidden micro-singularity has us in its grip! Engines at full burn just to hold position. Fuel draining at triple rate. Crushed debris rings ahead. We have maybe two minutes.

choices.label: Angle thrust carefully to conserve fuel.

burn.speaker: Engineer
burn.text: Engines screaming, fuel gauges plummeting -- but we are pulling free. That cost us dearly.

jettison.speaker: Engineer
jettison.text: Cargo away! The mass reduction gives us just enough thrust to crawl out. Lost supplies but kept the ship.

angle.speaker: Engineer
angle.text: Engineering calculates a slingshot trajectory using the singularity's own pull. Brilliant work, but the hull groans under tidal stress.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Looking for firepower? I've got hardware that'll make a Castellan admiral blush. Railguns, prototype lance batteries, experimental missiles. Steep prices but top-tier gear."

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Pleasure doing business. ISD monitors these transactions so you might notice a little heat. Worth it for the firepower, eh?"

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss, friend. I'll be around."

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Magnetic grapples in the hull! They are cutting through the airlock! This is deck-by-deck fighting -- our crew against theirs.

choices.label: Vent the compromised sections to space.

fight.text: Close-quarters fighting through corridors. Your crew holds the line and drives them back. You counter-board their crippled ship.

vent.speaker: Engineer
vent.text: Atmosphere vents hard -- boarders flushed into space along with anything loose. Brutal but effective.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three pilots in souped-up racers wave you over. "Settle this -- race to that beacon and back through the asteroid belt. No weapons. Loser buys drinks!"

race.speaker: Comm Channel
race.text: Heart-pounding stuff weaving through asteroids. You cross the finish line first! "Quicksilver" Rei is impressed: "You fly like you were born in a cockpit."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Suit yourself! More glory for us!" They blast off laughing.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Ambassador K'thali, a towering crystalline alien, appears on screen: "We seek understanding of human music, food, and social ritual. Allow our observer aboard your ship for ten systems."

choices.label: Not set up for that right now.

accept.speaker: Comm Channel
accept.text: The observer boards -- curious, polite, fascinated by everything. Your crew finds them endearing despite occasional awkward questions.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "We understand. Perhaps another time." The ambassador inclines graciously and departs.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Cargo container floating in the void -- sealed, unmarked. Scans show refined platinum worth a fortune. But it is broadcasting a faint tracking signal.

choices.label: Take it and deal with consequences.
Disable the tracker, then take it.

take.speaker: Engineer
take.text: Platinum secured. That tracker is still pinging -- whoever lost this will know where we are.

disable.speaker: Engineer
disable.text: Tracker disabled. They will know it was picked up but cannot trace it to us.

leave.text: You mark the coordinates and move on. Some treasure is not worth the heat.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We warped into an active warzone! A Castellan dreadnought trading broadsides with a Fringe carrier group. Fighters everywhere. We are an ant between giants.

navigate.text: Threading between lance beams and torpedo volleys, you somehow make it through. A few stray shots clip your hull.

scavenge.speaker: Engineer
scavenge.text: Insane but profitable -- military-grade components grabbed between explosions. A nearby torpedo detonation rattles the hull hard.

flee.text: Emergency warp! A lance beam passes close enough to superheat the hull. You escape -- barely.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A scarred woman in a gunship hails: "Putting together a crew for a high-risk op on a pirate fortress. 800 credits per head, upfront. Need pilots, gunners, and people not afraid to bleed."

choices.label: Hire out some crew for the mission.
Sell intel about the fortress instead.

hire.speaker: Comm Channel
hire.text: Your crew ships out with the mercenaries. It will be dangerous but the pay is real. They will return hardened.

intel.speaker: Comm Channel
intel.text: "Good intel is worth as much as a gunner. Here's your cut." She transfers credits and departs.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your call. If you change your mind, ask around for Captain Voss."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive electromagnetic storm front sweeping through the sector -- a crackling wall of blue-white energy. It kills electronics. Thirty seconds before it hits.

choices.label: Power down non-essentials and ride it out.
Brace for impact with shields up.

ride.speaker: Engineer
ride.text: Systems dark, crew holding their breath. The storm passes through -- some circuits fried but nothing critical. Good call powering down.

outrun.text: Full burn ahead of the storm front. Your pilot threads the needle between the leading edge and an asteroid cluster. Just barely made it.

shields.speaker: Engineer
shields.text: Bad idea -- the storm amplified shield frequencies into hull-damaging resonance! Major electrical damage across the ship.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "I'm bored. Bring me a fight worth having and I'll give you my weight in platinum. Bore me and I'll eat your ship." The pirate king Voraxis commands a heavily modified battlecruiser.

fight.text: The most brutal fight of your career. Voraxis fights like a demon, but your crew prevails. The pirate king laughs as his ship burns: "Finally! Worth it!"

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Coward. But a living coward. Go, before I change my mind about letting you leave."

flee.text: You burn hard away from the battlecruiser. Voraxis does not pursue -- you are not worth the chase.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A ship that should not exist -- its registration belongs to a vessel destroyed fifteen years ago. Running lights on, no signals. Pristine condition.

board.text: The crew is at their stations, perfectly preserved but dead -- no wounds, no decomposition. The chronometer shows a date three centuries in the future. You grab what you can and get out.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Readings make no sense. Temporal signatures, impossible energy states. Our instruments are giving contradictory data. I recommend we leave.

leave.text: Smart choice. Some mysteries are better left alone. The ghost ship drifts on, its running lights fading behind you.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An ISD corvette pulls alongside. Agent Kova speaks: "We're not here for you. We're here about someone you met three systems back. Tell us everything and you'll never see us again."

cooperate.speaker: Comm Channel
cooperate.text: "Appreciated. Your compliance has been noted." The corvette peels away without another word.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Interesting choice. We will remember your lack of cooperation." The corvette departs, but you feel watched.

lie.speaker: Comm Channel
lie.text: Kova studies your face for a long moment, then nods. "Very well." They depart. You are fairly sure they bought it.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A hauntingly beautiful melody plays across all frequencies -- not a recording, something live. The helmsman is steering toward the source without orders. Dozens of wrecks surround a bioluminescent entity ahead.

choices.label: Try to resist and study the signal.
Give in and approach the source.

shutdown.speaker: Engineer
shutdown.text: Comms killed. The helmsman snaps out of it, confused and shaken. We are pulling away from the graveyard. Close call.

study.speaker: Sensor Officer
study.text: Science team identifies it as a psychoactive waveform. We have mapped its frequency patterns -- valuable data. But the crew is rattled.

approach.text: The entity's pull grows stronger. Hull scrapes against the wrecks of other victims. At the last moment, engineering cuts the engines and breaks the spell.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Six pirate ships converging from the asteroid field -- coordinated ambush! They have disabled the navigation beacon to prevent escape jumps.

choices.label: Make for the beacon and reactivate it.

fight.text: A vicious brawl. You break enough ships to scatter the rest. The jump point is clear.

beacon.speaker: Engineer
beacon.text: EVA team reaches the beacon under fire and gets it back online. Warp drive spooling -- we can jump!

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Do not approach. Crew infected with Stellaris Pox. Contagious. Fatal." They are begging for medical supplies to synthesize a cure.

choices.label: Stay back but offer advice over comms.

deliver.speaker: Medic
deliver.text: Supplies delivered using full decontamination protocols. The medical officer aboard is overwhelmed with gratitude and offers to join our crew.

advise.speaker: Comm Channel
advise.text: You walk their medic through synthesis steps over comms. Slower, but it works. They are grateful.

leave.text: You maintain quarantine distance and move on. Their desperate pleas fade on the comms.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An eccentric billionaire in an absurdly ornate yacht hails: "I collect curiosities! Alien artifacts, strange specimens, unusual stories. Show me something I haven't seen and I'll pay handsomely."

choices.label: Offer rare resources from our hold.
Tell him about our strangest encounter.

sell.speaker: Comm Channel
sell.text: "Magnificent! I haven't seen crystalline formations like these in decades. Triple market value, as promised."

story.speaker: Comm Channel
story.text: "Extraordinary! A ghost ship with a chronometer from the future? Here -- stories like that deserve compensation."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "A pity! I'll be around -- the universe always provides curiosities to those who look."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Space itself is tearing -- a warp storm. Fractures of impossible color ripping through the void. Ships caught in the distortion are scattered across light-years.

choices.label: Navigate safe corridors through the storm.
Ride the storm's edge for faster travel.

navigate.speaker: Engineer
navigate.text: Warpsmithing reads the pattern. We thread through safe corridors -- harrowing but effective. Barely a scratch.

detour.text: The long way around. Burns fuel but keeps the ship in one piece.

ride.speaker: Engineer
ride.text: Riding the edge -- incredible speed! But the storm bucks and we take a beating before breaking free in an unexpected location.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Two mercenary companies with bounties on each other -- twelve ships total, weapons hot, no one firing. Both sides want us as a tiebreaker.

choices.label: Fight for the Iron Talons (400 credits).
Fight for the Void Reapers (500 credits).

talons.speaker: Comm Channel
talons.text: The Iron Talons cheer as you open fire on the Reapers. A fierce battle, but with your help, the Talons prevail.

reapers.speaker: Comm Channel
reapers.text: The Void Reapers welcome your firepower. Together you break the Iron Talons. The Reapers pay well.

peace.speaker: Comm Channel
peace.text: After an hour of tense negotiation, both sides agree to split the sector. Both captains grudgingly thank you.

leave.text: You burn away before the first shots are fired. Behind you, the void lights up.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A binary star system creates a narrow gravity corridor. If navigated precisely, it could slingshot us at incredible speed. The corridor is littered with debris from ships that failed.

choices.label: Harvest exotic particles at the center.

attempt.text: Perfect trajectory! The gravitational forces hurl your ship forward at incredible velocity. Travel time cut dramatically.

harvest.speaker: Sensor Officer
harvest.text: At the corridor center, gravitational forces create brief windows for exotic particle collection. We grab what we can before the forces become dangerous.

around.text: The safe route. Takes longer but no risk to the ship.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A shaky voice on comms: "L-look, I don't want to do this, but if I don't bring back your cargo, they'll kill me." A young pirate recruit in a barely-functional junker.

choices.label: Let them take a token amount.

talk.speaker: Comm Channel
talk.text: The kid breaks down. "I never wanted this life." They are talented despite everything -- offer to join your crew if you will have them.

token.text: You jettison a small crate. The kid grabs it and runs. Maybe it is enough to keep them alive.

destroy.text: The junker comes apart in seconds. Your crew watches in uncomfortable silence. Just a kid.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Four COTAC gunships pound a mining station. The administrator broadcasts: "They want our mineral rights! We've operated here for thirty years!"

miners.text: A hard fight against COTAC hardware, but the station stands. The miners are deeply grateful.

cotac.speaker: Comm Channel
cotac.text: "Efficient work. COTAC appreciates contractors who understand the value of decisive action."

leave.text: You pull away as the station's shields flicker and fail. Not your problem. Your crew disagrees silently.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Ancient escape pod, decades old. Cryo-system still functioning against all odds. One occupant, frozen in time.

thaw.speaker: Medic
thaw.text: The old spacer wakes confused and grateful. "What year is it? What happened to the Meridian?" Their crew is long gone, but they have knowledge of forgotten locations -- including a legendary treasure ship crash site.

leave.text: You leave the pod drifting. Whoever is inside will sleep on, perhaps forever.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Militia revenue cutter demands 300 credits in "transit taxes." Your science officer notes this does not match any known tax code. Either a corrupt officer or an outright scam.

choices.label: Pay the tax to avoid trouble.

pay.text: Credits transferred. Safe but wasteful. That money went straight into someone's pocket.

challenge.speaker: Comm Channel
challenge.text: You cite specific Militia tax regulations. The officer sputters, then backs down. "Fine. Move along." They power away quickly.

refuse.text: The cutter powers weapons. "Wrong answer." It is well-armed and the crew is clearly experienced at this shakedown.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Vast membranes of biological material stretched between asteroids, pulsing with light. An alien breeding ground. Small bio-drones are investigating our ship.

choices.label: Study the organisms from a distance.

harvest.speaker: Sensor Officer
