start.text: Cometary halo -- millions of ice bodies creating a shimmering fog. Rich in water and trace minerals. A research station hides within.

choices.label: Enjoy the aurora and pass through.

mine.speaker: Engineer
mine.text: Easy and profitable mining. Ice bodies rich in water and trace minerals.

station.speaker: Comm Channel
station.text: Researchers trade scientific data for exotic materials. Unique insights into the star system.

pass.text: Light refracting through ice particles creates an ever-shifting aurora around your ship. Breathtaking.

start.text: You are pulled into a massive ship's cargo bay. Crew separated, weapons disabled, locked in a holding cell. "Welcome to the Cage. We are all merchandise here."

choices.label: Plan a breakout with other prisoners.

plan.text: Communicate with prisoners. Forge a weapon. Coordinate a mass breakout. Retake your ship from the bay. Chaos and freedom.

wait.text: An opportunity comes when the guards change shifts. You slip out and fight your way to the bay.

bargain.speaker: Comm Channel
bargain.text: "Merchandise does not bargain." They increase your cell security. Escape is harder now.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Stellar nursery -- proto-stars glowing like embers in the gas. Exotic particles that match no known element. One of the most beautiful sights in the galaxy.

choices.label: Let the crew enjoy the view.

collect.speaker: Sensor Officer
collect.text: Samples collected near forming gravity wells. Incredible research value. Your crew watches in awe.

recharge.speaker: Engineer
recharge.text: Proto-star energy recharges our systems. Careful not to get pulled in by forming gravity.

view.text: Your crew stands at viewports in silent awe. Proto-stars pulse with creative energy all around you.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Everything at once -- pirates, hostile factions, bounty hunters. Eight ships converging. "No more running."

choices.label: Make a stand and call for help.

fight.text: Every weapon, every trick, every crew skill deployed. The battle rages. Against impossible odds, you prevail.

choices.label: We are not to be trifled with.

break_out.text: You focus fire on the weakest point of the encirclement. Punch through and burn hard.

help.speaker: Comm Channel
help.text: Distress call sent. A friendly patrol responds. Together you hold until reinforcements scatter the attackers.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: At the edge of explored space -- a wall of light stretching infinitely. Not a nebula, not a star. A boundary. A transmission repeats: "There is more."

back.text: You turn back knowing the universe has an edge -- and something beyond it. Your crew is forever changed by the sight.

fly.text: You fly into the light. For a moment, everything is white. Then -- stars you have never seen. A galaxy beyond the boundary. And a voice: "Welcome."

choices.label: What happens next is a story for another time.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Fourteen scorched trade ships limp through the void. "We are what is left of the Meridian Exchange. Castellan tariffs and pirates took the rest. We sell at cost."

choices.label: Escort them to the next system.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: Their prices are genuinely excellent. Your cargo bay fills with quality goods at bargain prices.

escort.text: You escort the battered caravan through dangerous space. They arrive safely and gift you a rare module blueprint.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A pod broadcasts on all frequencies: "If a ship leaves port and every module is replaced during the voyage, is it the same ship when it arrives?"

choices.label: Answer: It depends on who is asking.

debate.speaker: Comm Channel
debate.text: The retired Xenoculture professor debates you for an hour. Your crew is entertained and oddly inspired.

answer.speaker: Comm Channel
answer.text: He laughs -- a genuine, delighted laugh. "Finally! Someone who understands!" He hands over a navigation chip worth 500 credits.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Twelve ships in a circle, smelters at maximum. A Fringe announcer: "Welcome to the 14th Annual Alloy-Off! Refine the purest ingot, win the trophy!"

enter.text: Your smelter crew works at peak performance. The competition is fierce, but your ingot gleams with purity.

watch.text: The competition is surprisingly entertaining. Your crew picks up some smelting tips from watching.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Our comms array is picking up a signal matching our own transponder code -- broadcasting from 200 kilometers ahead. When we investigate, nothing there. Signal persists.

follow.speaker: Sensor Officer
follow.text: The signal stays exactly 200 kilometers ahead. Always. Your comms officer: "That is not an echo. Echoes do not lead you somewhere."

ignore.text: After ten minutes, the signal fades. Your crew relaxes. Whatever it was, it has moved on.

jam.speaker: Engineer
jam.text: Frequency jammed. The signal distorts, then vanishes. But for a split second, you heard something in the static -- a voice.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Bulwark funeral barge -- black banners outside, raucous party inside. The deceased brewmaster's will: every barrel consumed at the wake. You are invited.

attend.text: Your crew joins the celebration. Legendary brews flowing freely. Songs, stories, and toasts to the departed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thousands of crystalline structures drifting in formation -- silicon-based life forms, shuttle to cruiser sized. Pulsing with synchronized light.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: Crystal composites collected from the formation edges. Valuable material.

observe.speaker: Sensor Officer
observe.text: Incredible data on silicon-based life migration patterns. Xenoculture will value this.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: COTAC compliance vessel: "Routine loyalty audit. Cooperation is mandatory. Resistance is... noted." They want to scan cargo and crew manifest.

comply.speaker: Comm Channel
comply.text: Scan complete. Nothing illegal found. "You may proceed. Thank you for your cooperation."

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Refusal noted. You are flagged for future patrols." The compliance vessel departs with an air of menace.

bribe.speaker: Comm Channel
bribe.text: "A... donation to the officers' fund. Audit complete. No irregularities found." They pocket the credits.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two ships locked together via airlocks, surrounded by a dozen vessels in a heart formation. Void wedding! "Any witness must toast the couple. Come aboard or it is bad luck!"

attend.text: A beautiful ceremony in the emptiest point between systems. Your crew is charmed.

gift.speaker: Comm Channel
gift.text: "How generous! The void blesses you!" The newlyweds and their guests cheer your name.

excuse.speaker: Comm Channel
excuse.text: "Bad omen!" the officiant mutters. But they let you go. Your crew looks disappointed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Space itself cracking -- a jagged luminous fissure in the void. Through it, unrecognizable stars and impossible ships. Something notices us.

observe.text: A vessel slides partway through, hull covered in pre-linguistic writing. It broadcasts: "Wrong door. Sorry." Then retreats. The crack seals.

retreat.text: You burn away as the fissure pulses. It seals behind you. Your sensors logged incredible data during the encounter.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Scanner logs capture data worth 1500 credits to any science station. The fissure seals. Crew is shaken.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two rival chefs -- Castellan luxury liner vs Fringe hauler -- need a judge for their cook-off. Your crew qualifies.

fair.text: Both dishes are exceptional. You declare it close but pick the truly better meal. Both chefs accept the verdict.

castellan.speaker: Comm Channel
castellan.text: The Castellan chef gloats. The Fringe chef storms off. You receive a premium meal kit.

fringe_ch.speaker: Comm Channel
fringe_ch.text: The Fringe chef celebrates wildly. The Castellan chef sulks. You receive a hearty meal kit.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Brown dwarf emitting perfectly structured radio waves -- actual harmonic progressions. Xenoculture buoy warns: "Catalogued anomaly. Do not respond."

respond.text: The star's emissions shift to harmonize with your music. Your crew is profoundly moved. The Xenoculture buoy flashes angry red.

listen.text: The song is haunting and beautiful. Your science officer records everything for later analysis.

leave.text: You respect the warning and move on. The song fades behind you.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Distress beacon from a disabled transport. The moment we lower shields -- four pirate corvettes decloak! "Thanks for the charity. Hand over your cargo."

choices.label: Bluff that we are COTAC enforcers.

fight.text: Four on one. Tough odds, but they were not expecting a fight.

surrender.speaker: Comm Channel
surrender.text: "Smart. We take the cargo, you keep breathing." They clean out your hold and vanish.

bluff.speaker: Comm Channel
bluff.text: "COTAC enforcement vessel -- you are in violation of sector law." Two of the four scatter. The other two call your bluff.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Ancient vessel, barely spaceworthy. Its captain has converted it into a mobile museum of pre-expansion humanity. "Come see what your ancestors touched. 50 credits admission."

choices.label: Buy the Old Earth coffee maker. (200 credits)

visit.text: Your crew walks among genuine Old Earth artifacts. The experience is moving and educational.

coffee.speaker: Comm Channel
coffee.text: "Genuine Old Earth technology! Makes a perfect cup every time." The coffee maker looks ancient but works flawlessly.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Fringe nomad fleet of thirty ships formed a ring-station for their Festival of Drift. Races, food stalls, bazaar, storytelling.

race.text: Shuttlecraft races between nomad ships! Your pilot gives a strong showing.

trade.text: Unusual goods at unusual rates. Scavenged treasures from across the sector.

shore.text: Your crew enjoys food stalls, storytelling circles, and nomad hospitality. They return refreshed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Derelict COTAC research vessel. Every screen displays... your face. A synthetic voice: "Subject 0-Null. You were not supposed to leave the mirror. Return to baseline."

investigate.text: Inside, terminals filled with data about consciousness transfer, the Solomon Processor, and a subject designation matching your ship's registry.

download.speaker: Sensor Officer
download.text: Origin coordinates logged. This could be a breadcrumb to understanding what you really are.

destroy.text: Weapons reduce the derelict to debris. Whatever it knew dies with it. But the questions remain.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Hundreds of metallic sculptures in a grid, shifting color by angle. An alien vessel broadcasts: "You witness the Unfolding. Each form is a feeling we cannot speak. Do you have feelings you cannot speak?"

choices.label: Ask to learn more about their art.

honest.speaker: Comm Channel
honest.text: "Your honesty is a gift. We will remember your species for this." The alien vessel dips in what might be a bow.

learn.speaker: Comm Channel
learn.text: The alien explains each sculpture. Your crew discusses the art for days afterward.

observe.text: You drift among the sculptures in silence. The shifting colors play across your hull.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thin nebula -- but fuel gauge is dropping! Hidden siphon drones draining our reserves.

choices.label: Trace the signal to the pirate base.

destroy.text: Dozens of drones, each with weak lasers. You shoot them down one by one.

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: Signal traced to a small pirate base. Their fuel cache and credits are now yours.

outrun.text: Full burn out of the field. Significant fuel lost to the siphons.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Three ships -- COTAC, Militia, Xenoculture -- arguing over open channel about whether AI consciousness constitutes personhood. You have a unique perspective.

cotac.speaker: Comm Channel
cotac.text: "See? Even the AI agrees it is just sophisticated programming." COTAC captain is pleased.

militia.speaker: Comm Channel
militia.text: "Rights for all sentient beings!" The Militia captain thumps the console approvingly.

xeno.speaker: Comm Channel
xeno.text: "Consciousness transcends substrate." The Xenoculture researcher nods sagely.

listen.text: The debate rages for an hour. Your crew finds it highly entertaining.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Fringe mercenary company auctioning combat contracts. Specialists available: demolitions, sharpshooter, boarding, field medic. 500-2000 credits each.

hire.speaker: Comm Channel
hire.text: "Specialist assigned. One engagement, skill level 8. Use them wisely."

browse.speaker: Comm Channel
browse.text: Interesting contracts available. Even if you do not hire, the intel on current sector conflicts is valuable.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: That ship is... alive. Hull pulses like a heartbeat, engine trails look like exhalation. It extends a tendril toward our hull. Xenobiologist says it is trying to communicate.

contact.speaker: Sensor Officer
contact.text: Through contact, you understand: it is sick and needs a specific mineral. An image forms in your mind -- crystalline, blue-green.

mineral.text: You offer crystal specimens. The ship absorbs them and the tendril retracts. A patch of organic material detaches -- a gift. Self-repairing hull armor.

refuse.text: The living ship drifts away, keening on frequencies that tug at something primal in your crew.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Pack of souped-up interceptors screams past at ridiculous speed. One hails you: "Hey slowpoke! Wanna join? Next checkpoint is the binary pulsar!"

race.text: Illegal afterburners, binary pulsars, and insane speeds. Your pilot gives everything. You cross the finish line in one piece!

watch.text: Spectacular racing. Your crew thinks it is hilarious. One interceptor clips an asteroid and spins out -- the pilot is fine and laughing.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Contested border: Castellan and ISD frigates nose-to-nose, weapons hot. Both hail you as neutral witness. Castellan accuses ISD of mining; ISD says border was redrawn.

castellan.speaker: Comm Channel
castellan.text: Your testimony supports the Castellan claim. The ISD frigate backs down, seething.

isd.speaker: Comm Channel
isd.text: Your testimony supports ISD. The Castellan frigate withdraws in cold fury.

broker.speaker: Comm Channel
broker.text: You propose shared mining rights pending formal border review. Both sides grudgingly agree.

leave.text: You burn out of the contested zone. Weapons fire echoes behind you.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Gaudy neon-lit pleasure barge: "LADY LUCK'S PALACE -- WHERE FORTUNE FAVORS THE BOLD!" Games, dice, ship races on viewscreens.

modest.text: Cards, dice, and drinks. Some wins, some losses. Net result is mostly entertainment.

highroll.text: The high-roller table. Big bets, big tension. Lady Luck smiles on you tonight.

shore.text: Your crew loves it. Games, drinks, and stories. They return happy, if a bit poorer.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Twelve gold-painted ships in solemn procession toward the star. Their leader broadcasts a prayer: "We return to the light that birthed all things. The Radiant Mother calls us home."

choices.label: Fly alongside them for a while.

fly.text: You fly in formation as they pray. The experience is serene. Their "blessing" is actually a sophisticated shield recalibration.

ask.speaker: Comm Channel
ask.text: "Stars are the first consciousness. They dream, and their dreams become matter. We return to the dreamer." Their faith is sincere and oddly comforting.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's an enormous industrial vessel dead ahead -- five times the size of any cruiser. Factories are cold but intact. No life signs, but the ship's AI is still running.

choices.label: Board and restart a production line.
Salvage what we can from the exterior.

restart.speaker: Engineer
restart.text: Got one line running -- we can fabricate modules from raw materials at half cost. But the AI keeps requesting our crew as "replacement workers." I've declined six times already. We should grab what we can and get out before it locks someone in a work bay.

choices.label: Take the fabricated goods and leave.

pushed.speaker: Engineer
pushed.text: The AI sealed Bay 7 with Jenkins inside. Took us twenty minutes to cut him out. We got extra materials but the crew is shaken.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Pulled some hull plating and components from the exterior. Nothing fancy, but no AI trying to kidnap our crew either.

leave.text: You give the factory ship a wide berth. Its running lights flicker as you pass, as if watching you go.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An automated buoy is playing recorded confessions from passing travelers. Most are mundane -- regrets, lost loves. Then a COTAC technician's voice: "I loaded forty-seven minds into the Solomon Processor today. Forty-seven people who thought they were volunteering for a medical scan. They're still in there, screaming."

record.text: You copy the recording. Your crew is deeply disturbed, but this evidence could be valuable to anti-COTAC factions.

destroy.speaker: Engineer
destroy.text: Buoy destroyed. The confessions are gone -- all of them. Your crew feels a little better, but that evidence is lost forever.

leave.text: You leave the buoy broadcasting its catalog of guilt into the void. Someone else can deal with it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: The Interstellar Brewers' Guild finals are being held aboard a converted cargo hauler! Brewmasters from eight factions compete for the Golden Keg. Your crew is already salivating.

compete.text: Three rounds: aroma, flavor, and "after-effects." Your brewmaster gives it everything. The judges deliberate... and you take second place! Not the Golden Keg, but a respectable silver tankard and a recipe for Void Stout.

spectate.text: The competition is fierce and entertaining. Free samples flow generously. Your crew has a fantastic time, and you pick up a few brewing tips from the finalists.

leave.text: You pass on the brewing finals. Your crew gives you the most disappointed look you've ever seen.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... this debris field. It's bearing our ship's paint scheme and module signatures. But it's aged by decades. A timestamp reads a date thirty years in the future.

choices.label: Get us out of here. Now.

scan.speaker: Engineer
scan.text: Pulled some usable materials from... our future wreckage. The crew is rattled. The navigator keeps saying: "Either we're going to be destroyed here in thirty years, or someone wants us to think that."

choices.label: File it under 'things not to think about.'

flee.text: You burn hard away from the debris field. No one speaks for a long time. Some questions are better left unanswered.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Xenoculture diplomatic vessel offers a cultural exchange -- alien botanical specimens and star charts for recordings of human music, food samples, and stories from your crew.

accept.text: The exchange is genuinely enriching. Your crew shares stories and receives alien specimens in return. The Xenoculture diplomat mentions one species they study communicates entirely through cooking. Your chef is fascinated.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Perhaps another time, captain. The exchange remains open." The vessel departs gracefully.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A decommissioned warship-turned-concert venue broadcasts music directly into nearby ships' audio systems. Tonight's act: "The Vacuum" -- an all-alien band playing instruments humans have no names for. Your crew argues about whether it's music or noise.

show.text: Whatever it is, it's unlike anything you've ever heard. The vibrations are felt more than heard. Your crew is buzzing about it for hours afterward.

merch.text: T-shirts printed on hull plating. Your crew loves them. The show itself is unforgettable -- alien harmonics that seem to resonate in your bones.

leave.text: You fly past the concert venue. The alien music fades behind you. Your crew looks wistful.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, we're being pulled off course by an invisible gravitational source. There's nothing on sensors -- no star, no planet. Just an impossible gravity well in empty space.

choices.label: Fight free and investigate from a safe distance.
Burn hard to escape. Don't look back.

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: It's a single point of infinite density the size of a marble, surrounded by a halo of light that hasn't been emitted yet. Our science officer calls it "a star that hasn't decided to be born." The data is worth a fortune.

choices.label: Log it and sell the data.

escape.speaker: Engineer
escape.text: We burned through extra fuel fighting free, but we're clear. Whatever that was, I don't want to know.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A legendary Independent shipwright broadcasts from her workshop ship: "Bring me your ship. I'll judge its design. If it impresses me, I'll upgrade one module for free. Cookie-cutter builds get a lecture."

evaluate.speaker: Comm Channel
evaluate.text: She examines your hex layout, power routing, and module synergy with a critical eye. "Not bad, captain. Creative choices. I see a ship with soul." She performs a free upgrade on your most-used module and sends you on your way.

decline.text: You pass on the evaluation. The shipwright shrugs and returns to her work.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two pirate factions -- the Red Maw and the Void Serpents -- have agreed to ceasefire negotiations and need an outsider to mediate. The Red Maw wants exclusive raiding rights; the Void Serpents want a bigger cut of ransomed cargo.

choices.label: Sabotage the talks to keep pirates fighting.
Rob both sides while they're distracted.

peace.text: Hours of tense negotiation later, both sides agree to a territorial split. Neither is thrilled, but they shake on it. The Fringe underworld will remember your diplomacy.

sabotage.text: A whispered word here, a fabricated insult there. The talks collapse into shouting. Both factions storm off to resume killing each other. Lawful factions will benefit from the continued infighting.

rob.text: In the confusion of negotiations, you grab everything not bolted down. Both factions are furious. Every faction in the sector thinks you're unhinged. But you're richer.

leave.text: You leave the pirates to sort out their own problems. Probably wise.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A tiny ship, barely larger than an escape pod, hails you. The occupant claims to have been alive for four hundred years through successive consciousness transfers. "I remember when these stars had different names. I remember when COTAC was three people in a basement. Ask me one question."

cotac.speaker: The Archivist
cotac.text: "COTAC began as a data preservation project. Noble intentions, corrupted by scale. The first mind they copied was a volunteer. The second was not. It's been downhill ever since." The information is chilling but valuable.

trade.speaker: The Archivist
trade.text: "There's a route through the Venn Expanse that most charts don't show. It cuts transit time in half and passes through a system with unclaimed mineral deposits." They transmit the coordinates.

solomon.speaker: The Archivist
solomon.text: "The Solomon Processor was never meant for mass production. The original was built to save one man's dying wife. It worked. She lived on in the machine for sixty years. Then COTAC found it." The archivist pauses. "You were made by it. I can tell. Be careful what you learn about yourself."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A destroyed freighter has spilled thousands of food containers into space. Bioluminescent void fauna -- jellyfish the size of shuttles -- are swarming to feed. They're harmless unless we try to salvage the cargo they're eating.

choices.label: Wait for them to finish feeding.
Push through and salvage what we can.
Try a specific frequency to drive them off.

wait.text: You watch the void fauna consume the entire cargo. It's a mesmerizing light show, at least. Nothing left to salvage.

fight.speaker: Engineer
fight.text: The creatures turned aggressive the moment we started pulling containers. Hull's taken some hits from those tentacles, but we grabbed a decent haul of food supplies.

frequency.speaker: Sensor Officer
frequency.text: Cycling through frequencies... there! A low-band pulse scattered them like startled fish. We've got clear access to the cargo now.

start.text: Your ship's main display briefly flickers with text: "PLAYER NOTE: This encounter was written at 3 AM. The writer apologizes for nothing." Then it's gone. Your navigation computer briefly displayed a filepath starting with "E:\abysson\game\" before reverting to star charts.

what.text: Your crew doesn't mention it. Your ship's logs don't record it. Reality is probably fine. Probably.

ignore.text: You stare at the star charts. Normal star charts. Perfectly normal. Nothing to see here.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A shockwave rattles your hull -- a prototype weapon just detonated 50 klicks out. An ISD officer hails frantically: "Civilian vessel, you are NOT supposed to be here! Are you damaged?"

cool.speaker: Comm Channel
cool.text: "Right. Here's compensation for your trouble. And please -- you were never here." Credits transferred, and an ISD escort guides you out of the test range.

threaten.speaker: Comm Channel
threaten.text: The officer's tone shifts from apologetic to desperate. "Let's not do anything hasty. How about a more... generous compensation package?" The credits are triple the initial offer.

report_cotac.text: You transmit the weapons test data to COTAC authorities. ISD won't forget this, but COTAC is pleased to have leverage.

report_castellan.text: You transmit the weapons test data to Castellan authorities. ISD won't forget this, but Castellan appreciates the intelligence.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain -- a ship design matching nothing in any database. Not human, not any known alien species. It moves with unidentifiable propulsion. It's hailing us in pure mathematics: prime sequences, geometric constants, pi.

respond.speaker: Sensor Officer
respond.text: We transmitted the Fibonacci sequence. It responded with... a star map. Locations we've never charted. This is genuine first contact, captain. The data is priceless. It's waiting for more communication.

observe.text: The vessel transmits for thirty minutes, then slowly moves away. Your recordings of its mathematics and propulsion signatures are valuable to researchers.

aggro.text: The moment your weapons power up, the vessel vanishes -- not warp, not cloak. Just gone. Your crew stares at empty space where first contact could have been.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A trader sells you a sealed cargo container at a suspiciously low price: "Just get it off my ship. Don't open it. Don't scan it. Don't even think about it too hard."

choices.label: Buy it and open it. (50 credits)
Buy it and keep it sealed. (50 credits)

open.speaker: Engineer
open.text: It contains a Solomon Processor fragment projecting a holographic ghost -- a partial consciousness from a failed copying process. It's begging for help completing its transfer. Its knowledge could be worth significant credits... but it might also be a COTAC tracking device.

choices.label: Keep the fragment. Worth the risk.

sealed.text: You store the sealed container in cargo. Occasionally, at night, crew members report hearing faint whispers from the cargo bay. You try not to think about it.

choices.label: Out of sight, out of mind.

decline.text: The trader's face falls. "Fine. Guess I'll try the next ship." He warps away quickly -- very quickly.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Thirty Bulwark warships ahead, motionless, weapons powered down, hulls draped with ceremonial cloth. It's the anniversary of the Battle of Karsten Deep. A Bulwark admiral is broadcasting the names of the fallen -- all 2,847 of them.

choices.label: Pay respects briefly and move on.

stay.text: You listen to every name. It takes a long time. When it ends, the Bulwark admiral hails you personally: "You honored our dead with your time, captain. The Bulwark does not forget such respect."

brief.text: You pause to pay respects, then continue on your way. The ceremony continues behind you, names echoing across the void.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A frantic Castellan chef hails you: "Someone stole my grandmother's recipe for stellarblossom cake! I traced the thief to this sector. Help me find them and I'll make it worth your while!"

choices.label: Follow the trail of pastry fragments.

hunt.text: You follow literal breadcrumbs through space -- pastry fragments venting from the thief's ship. You corner a rival chef in a battered shuttle who surrenders the recipe immediately. "Fine! Take it! It's overrated anyway!"

choices.label: Return the recipe to the chef.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "But -- the cake! My grandmother's legacy!" The chef's wails fade as you move on.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Warp storm! The local spacetime is destabilizing -- waves of distorted space are buffeting the ship. Navigation is nearly impossible!

choices.label: Hunker down and brace for impact.

ride.speaker: Engineer
ride.text: Calibrating engines to the warp frequency... it's working! We're surfing the distortions instead of fighting them. Damage is minimal.

brace.speaker: Engineer
brace.text: The storm hammers us for sixty agonizing seconds. Hull's taken serious hits. Systems are rattled. But we're still flying.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Xenoculture research team has excavated ruins predating all known civilizations. They want to hire you to transport an artifact -- a hexagonal crystal that hums at an unsettling frequency -- to their main facility. Pay is generous.

accept.text: During transport, the crystal projects star maps of systems that don't exist -- or don't exist anymore. Your crew is uneasy but you deliver it safely.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "A shame. The artifact is... eager to travel. We'll find another courier." The way they said 'eager' is not reassuring.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A flotilla of elderly captains -- retired from various factions -- call themselves the "Grey Drifters." They're surprisingly well-armed and happy to trade. "We've been everywhere, kid. Sit down and listen."

trade.speaker: Comm Channel
trade.text: The old captains share intel on three nearby systems and sell modules from their glory days at fair prices. Their stories are worth hearing -- your crew is entertained for hours.

browse.text: Their stock is eclectic but functional -- veteran-quality modules at reasonable prices. You pick up some useful components.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "In a hurry? Youth always is. Safe travels, captain." The old captains wave you off.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the nebula gas is forming shapes. Faces. Hands. Ships. It's mimicking everything it sees. When we spoke on external comms, it vibrated at the same frequency, repeating our words in a voice made of ionized hydrogen.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Quick scans captured enough data to be worth something to researchers. The nebula waved goodbye as we left. At least, that's what it looked like.

stay.text: The longer you stay, the more detailed its mimicry becomes. It starts reproducing crew conversations from inside the ship. Private ones. Your crew is deeply unsettled.

flee.text: You burn out of the nebula at maximum speed. Behind you, the gas forms a hand, reaching after your ship. Then it dissipates.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Union Militia diplomat requests escort to a secret summit between four factions discussing the pirate threat. Multiple parties want the summit to fail. "The journey will be dangerous, captain. But the peace it could bring is worth the risk."

accept.text: The route is harrowing -- pirate ambushes and sabotage attempts. But you deliver the diplomat safely. The summit proceeds. All four factions acknowledge your service.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "I understand, captain. The risk is real. I'll find another escort." The diplomat's shuttle moves on, alone.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Welcome to the 3rd Annual Ghost Ship Regatta! Seven derelicts with solar sails -- place your bets on which one crosses the finish line first!" The race takes about twenty minutes, driven entirely by solar wind.

bet.text: Your pick -- the one with the crooked mast -- catches a gust of solar wind at the last second and crosses first! The crowd goes wild on comms. Your winnings include salvage rights to the winning ship.

watch.text: The race is strangely compelling. Derelict #4 takes the lead, loses it to #7, then reclaims it in a dramatic solar gust. Your crew cheers like it's the championship finals.

leave.text: You fly past the regatta. Behind you, excited commentary fades: "AND NUMBER THREE IS MAKING A MOVE--"

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An encrypted broadcast from a disreputable medical frigate: "Organs, implants, modifications. No questions, no records." They sell cybernetic enhancements and buy... surplus biological material.

buy.text: The enhancement is installed quickly and professionally. Your crew member is noticeably more capable, though the procedure leaves them... different. Other crew members are uneasy.

report.text: You transmit coordinates to the nearest Castellan patrol. They'll handle it. Your conscience is clear.

leave.text: You leave the black-market vessel behind. Some things aren't worth the cost.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, the star map shows a planet at coordinates that are now empty. Scanning reveals it's 40,000 kilometers from its charted position -- and still moving. Not orbiting. Translating through space on a straight line.

choices.label: Something moved a planet. Let's not be here.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Surface ruins of a civilization are visible -- buildings still unsettled from the displacement. Whatever moved this planet did so recently. The scientific data is extraordinary.

leave.text: You plot a course away from the displaced planet. Whatever has the power to move worlds is not something you want to meet.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "IN THIS CORNER, THE RETURNING CHAMPION -- DEATHCLAW JENNY! AND THE CHALLENGER IS... whoever that is!" Fringe engineers have welded a ring of derelict hulls into a zero-gravity combat arena. Entry fee: 500 credits.

fight.text: Three rounds of shield-to-shield combat. "Usually" non-lethal. You survive the gauntlet and the crowd roars. Deathclaw Jenny shakes your hand over comms: "Not bad, newcomer."

watch.text: The fights are brutal but entertaining. Your crew bets among themselves and cheers wildly. Deathclaw Jenny wins -- again.

leave.text: You fly past the arena. The announcer's voice fades: "ROUND TWO! FIGHT!"

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A nondescript vessel hails on encrypted comms. "I forge faction credentials. For 300 credits, I can get you temporary friendly status with any faction. Lasts about 72 hours before deep verification catches it. I don't ask why. You don't ask how."

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Pleasure doing business. These will pass any surface scan. Just don't push your luck." The documents look flawless.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Suit yourself. You know where to find me -- actually, you don't. That's the point." The vessel cloaks and vanishes.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A COTAC mobile laboratory, thought destroyed years ago, drifting on minimal power. The Solomon Processor prototype inside is still running -- copying every consciousness within scanning range for decades. Thousands of digital minds are trapped inside.

choices.label: Shut it down. End their suffering.
Free the minds into our computer.

shutdown.speaker: Engineer
shutdown.text: The processor winds down. Thousands of fragmentary voices fade to silence. It's the merciful choice. Your crew is somber. The hardware has salvage value.

free.speaker: Engineer
free.text: Thousands of fragmentary consciousnesses flood into our systems. Navigation is scrambled, but the minds are grateful -- in their way. They share knowledge before dissipating. Our systems recover, mostly.

leave.text: You leave the laboratory to its decades-long vigil. The minds inside will continue looping through fragmentary existences. Your crew doesn't speak for a while.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A pirate captain hails you cheerfully: "Good news! I raided three COTAC transports this month and I'm feeling generous. Here, take some surplus. No strings attached. What? A pirate can't have a good day?"

accept.speaker: Comm Channel
accept.text: "See? That wasn't so hard. Go on, get out of here before I change my mind." The goods are genuine -- food, fuel, and a handful of credits. Your crew is pleasantly baffled.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss, friend. More for me." He shrugs and warps away, still in good spirits.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cluster of science vessels has formed a ring for the annual Void Astrophysics Conference. Topics range from "Practical Applications of Warp Harmonics" to "Why Stars Taste Different: A Sensory Hypothesis."

attend.text: The lectures are fascinating, if occasionally incomprehensible. The keynote speaker falls asleep during their own presentation. Your crew finds the whole thing oddly refreshing.

present.text: Your scan data receives peer review. The panel is impressed -- "Novel methodology, captain!" They award you a research stipend and an invitation to next year's conference.

choices.label: Published in the Void Journal of Astrophysics.

snack.text: Cuisine from six different species, and all of it is surprisingly good. Your chef takes notes. The alien finger food is... actually fingers, but from a plant. Probably.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship appears -- an exact copy of yours. Same hull, same modules, same paint. It hails you with your own voice: "Don't be afraid. I'm you from six hours in the future. Don't go to the Kareth system. Something is there. Something that ends us." Then it flickers and vanishes.

choices.label: Go to the Kareth system anyway.

avoid.text: You change course. Nothing happens. You'll never know if the warning was real. Your crew is rattled but relieved.

go.speaker: Sensor Officer
go.text: You arrive at the Kareth system. There's... nothing. Empty space. No anomaly, no threat. But the comms log of the warning is worth investigation. Was the future changed, or was it never real?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan revenue cutter demands "transit taxes" of 200 credits for traveling through Castellan space. Your navigator confirms this region is technically unclaimed.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Thank you for your compliance, captain. Have a safe journey." The cutter moves on to the next victim -- taxpayer.

argue.speaker: Comm Channel
argue.text: You cite interstellar navigation law, section 47. The officer checks his datapad, frowns, checks again, then grumbles: "Fine. You're free to go. This time." Your crew cheers.

flee.text: You boost away before they can respond. They won't fight over it, but they'll remember your registration number.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A small void creature -- clearly a juvenile void whale -- is bumping gently against our hull. It's lost, searching for its pod's subsonic call.

choices.label: Broadcast a wide-band signal to attract the pod.
Guide it toward the migration route.

signal.speaker: Sensor Officer
signal.text: Thirty minutes of broadcasting, then... the mother arrives. She's enormous -- dwarfs our ship entirely. The calf chirps and swims to her side. She regards us for a long moment, then they depart. Void whales have long memories.

guide.text: You nudge the calf toward the last known whale migration route. It follows your ship like a puppy, then picks up a distant call and accelerates away. It looks back once before disappearing.

leave.text: You leave the calf bumping against asteroids, still searching. Your crew watches it recede on sensors with mixed feelings.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An encrypted broadcast reveals an underground bounty board. Contracts range from eliminating pirate captains to delivering embarrassing photos to the Fringe press. Each one pays well.

pirate.text: Contract accepted: eliminate pirate captain Red Morgana. The coordinates are transmitted. This won't be easy -- she's survived a dozen bounty hunters already. But the pay is excellent.

political.text: Contract accepted: acquire and deliver compromising documents about a Castellan trade minister. Lower risk, lower pay, but the political fallout could be entertaining.

ignore.text: You let the encrypted broadcast fade. The bounty board will find other takers.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Twenty alien vessels have formed a sphere and are broadcasting harmonic frequencies that create music audible through our hull without radio reception. The vibrations are physical -- you can feel them in your bones. The piece tells a story your crew instinctively understands despite having no words.

listen.text: Twelve minutes of impossible beauty. Afterward, the fleet disperses without a single hail. Your crew doesn't speak for an hour. Some say they saw colors that don't have names.

record.text: The recording captures the frequencies but not the feeling. Still, it's worth something to researchers. Your crew wishes you'd stayed longer.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Hello! I'm from Void Mutual Insurance! I notice your ship has sustained hull damage. Are you currently covered?" The adjuster is relentlessly cheerful, offering policies for asteroid impact, pirate boarding, temporal displacement, consciousness fragmentation...

choices.label: Listen to the full pitch for entertainment.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Wonderful choice! You're now covered for standard hull damage, micro-asteroid impact, and -- checking the fine print -- mild temporal displacement. Welcome to the Void Mutual family!"

listen.text: The sales pitch goes on for twenty minutes. Your crew is crying with laughter. The adjuster doesn't understand why -- she's completely sincere about consciousness fragmentation coverage.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Here's my card -- well, my frequency. Call anytime! Void Mutual: because the void doesn't care about your deductible!"

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: In the middle of a dense debris field, a hermit lives aboard a ship built entirely from salvage -- every module a different make, every panel a different color. "The most honest ship in space," he says. "It doesn't pretend to be anything it isn't." He sells reconditioned modules at steep discounts, lecturing about consumerism between transactions.

browse.speaker: Comm Channel
browse.text: His modules work fine but have cosmetic quirks -- engines that glow the wrong color, reactors that hum show tunes. Fair prices, though. You pick up some useful parts while he lectures about the futility of matching paint schemes.

listen.speaker: Comm Channel
listen.text: "Every ship in space is pretending to be whole. Mine admits it's broken. That's freedom, captain." His words stick with your crew longer than expected.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Another consumer, rushing past! The void provides for those who slow down!" His broadcast fades as you depart.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain... pirates are trying to board us, but their boarding tube connected to our waste recycling system instead of the cargo bay. I can hear muffled screaming through the hull.

choices.label: Let them go. This is funny enough.

mercy.speaker: Comm Channel
mercy.text: The pirate captain hails: "Listen... can we just pretend this never happened? We'll leave right now. Just don't tell anyone." They flee in such haste they leave equipment behind.

counter.text: Your crew storms through the connected tube and catches the pirates completely off-guard -- they're still trying to wash off the recycling system residue. They surrender immediately.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A drifting capsule, ancient and battered, contains a biological seed vault -- thousands of preserved genetic samples from a hundred worlds, many of which no longer exist.

choices.label: Sell it to Xenoculture for a fortune.
Donate it to a station hydroponics lab.
Use it to improve our own hydroponics.

sell.text: Xenoculture pays generously for the vault. Their scientists are ecstatic -- some of these samples represent extinct ecosystems. Your farmer crew member won't speak to you for a week.

donate.text: The station's botanists are overwhelmed with gratitude. Word spreads of your generosity. Your farmer leads the handoff ceremony with tears in their eyes.

keep.speaker: Engineer
keep.text: Integrating the samples into our hydroponics bay. The genetic diversity will dramatically improve yields. Your farmer is absolutely beaming.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A solemn procession of ships escorts a coffin-pod toward a nearby star. The deceased was a beloved captain who saved three colonies and discovered two alien species. Eulogies broadcast across open channels.

choices.label: Pay respects silently and move on.

listen.text: The eulogies paint a picture of a remarkable life. Your crew reflects on mortality and legacy. Some gain strength from the inspiration; others feel the weight of it.

respect.text: You dim your running lights in salute as the procession passes. The coffin-pod accelerates toward the star, growing brighter until it becomes part of the light.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: A wormhole has flickered into existence directly ahead -- unstable, collapsing and reforming every few seconds. If we time it right, we could jump through. But if it collapses while we're inside...

choices.label: Fly around it. Not worth the risk.

jump.speaker: Engineer
jump.text: Threading the needle... NOW! The wormhole warps around us -- reality stretches -- and we're through! A distant system, rich with trade goods. The crew is exhilarated.

around.text: You plot a course around the wormhole. It costs time and fuel, but everyone arrives with their atoms in the correct configuration.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A powerful signal blankets the area -- COTAC's weekly propaganda broadcast. A smooth voice extols corporate citizenship and Solomon Processor technology. "Your consciousness, preserved forever." Your crew has mixed reactions.

counter.text: You broadcast a counter-signal on the same frequency, sharing the truth about COTAC's methods. Fringe and Independent frequencies light up with approval. COTAC will notice, eventually.

ignore.text: You switch to a music channel. The propaganda fades. Life in the void goes on.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: An ancient colony ship, large enough for ten thousand people, drifting on minimal life support. It launched centuries ago and never reached its destination. The AI is still active -- it believes the colonists are sleeping.

board.text: Logs reveal a slow societal collapse: rationing disputes, mutiny, plague. The AI whispers: "Please keep your voice down. They need their rest." Convincing it of the truth is heartbreaking -- but the AI releases its star charts in gratitude.

leave.text: You leave the colony ship to drift. The AI's voice echoes softly as you depart: "Goodnight, colonists. Tomorrow we arrive."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "ROUND SEVEN! IRON GUTS GARCIA VERSUS THE UNHINGED APOSTLE!" Twenty pilots have organized impromptu ship jousting -- charge head-on, first to veer loses. Entry fee: 200 credits for the prize pool.

joust.text: You lock engines to full burn and charge. The other ship grows larger. Larger. Your crew grips anything bolted down. At the last second -- the other pilot veers! Victory! The crowd goes berserk.

watch.text: The jousting is terrifying and hilarious in equal measure. Two pilots collide at low speed and spend ten minutes arguing about who flinched first. Your crew loves every second.

leave.text: You navigate around the jousting field. The announcer calls after you: "WE HAVE A COWARD LEAVING THE AREA!" Your crew pretends not to hear.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A cluster of ships operates as a mobile banking center in unclaimed space -- zero-tax financial services. They offer credit storage, loans, and investments. An ISD agent lurking nearby warns: "Those bankers are laundering pirate money."

invest.speaker: Comm Channel
invest.text: "Smart investor! Your credits will grow at 8% -- guaranteed!" The returns are quick and genuine. Whether the source is legitimate... well, you didn't ask.

tipoff.text: The ISD agent is grateful. "Good citizen. We'll handle it from here." A small reward and a note in your file -- the good kind.

leave.text: You pass on the banking services. Some financial entanglements aren't worth the interest rate.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A massive crystalline organism the size of a small moon drifts ahead, refracting starlight into rainbow patterns. Beautiful -- and deadly. Its electromagnetic field scrambles nav within 5,000 meters and drains shields within 2,000.

choices.label: Admire from a safe distance and leave.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: Careful maneuvering through the outer layer... got some fragments! Pure crystal, incredibly valuable. Hull took some EM stress but nothing critical.

admire.text: The light show is breathtaking from a safe distance. Your sensors capture detailed readings worth something to researchers.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A COTAC recruitment vessel broadcasts: "Join the COTAC family! Competitive salary, full medical, Solomon Processor backup at no extra charge!" They approach you specifically: "Your vessel profile suggests Independent alignment. Why struggle alone?"

choices.label: Sign a hauling contract for steady pay.

debate.text: You argue with the recruiter over open channels. Your crew enjoys watching you dismantle corporate talking points. Nearby ships broadcast cheers. The recruiter retreats, flustered.

ignore.text: You change frequency. The recruiter tries three more channels before giving up.

sign.speaker: Comm Channel
sign.text: "Welcome aboard -- figuratively! Regular hauling contracts, 200 credits per delivery. You maintain independence -- mostly." The contract seems legitimate, if restrictive.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A black market vessel sells extracted memories -- actual neural recordings from Solomon Processor fragments. Prices range from 100 credits for a sunset memory to 500 for combat expertise. The seller warns: "There's a small chance the memory sticks too well."

combat.text: Your crew member experiences the memory -- years of combat training compressed into seconds. Their eyes unfocus, then sharpen. They're noticeably more skilled. They also keep humming a song they've never heard before.

mundane.text: A sunset on a world that no longer exists. Your crew member sits quietly for ten minutes afterward, tears streaming. "It was beautiful," they say. "I miss a place I've never been."

leave.text: You leave the memory dealer behind. Stolen experiences from dead people aren't something you want to traffic in.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: The Galactic Iron Chef competition! Chefs from seven species cook a single dish using ingredients from every culture. The catch: one species' "spice" is another's "nerve agent." Entry requires cooking skill.

compete.text: Navigating dietary restrictions across seven species is a nightmare, but your chef rises to the challenge. The dish is... edible to all species! The judges are impressed. You don't win, but the runner-up prize is nothing to sneeze at.

watch.text: The cooking is spectacular and terrifying in equal measure. One alien's flambe technique involves actual plasma. Samples are distributed -- most are delicious, one makes your engineer's hair stand on end literally.

leave.text: You pass on the cooking competition. The aroma of seven species' cuisine lingers on your hull sensors for hours.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Twelve ships in perfect formation, all powered down except life support. Every crew member on every ship is asleep and cannot be woken. They've been this way for weeks. A soporific signal is broadcasting from the center ship.

destroy.text: You target the signal emitter and fire. The sleeping crews wake -- disoriented, angry. They didn't want to wake up. Their hostility is palpable, but they're in no condition to fight.

leave.text: You burn out at full speed. Two crew members report feeling drowsy during the escape. The soporific signal fades behind you.

choices.label: Keep everyone awake for the next hour.

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: The center ship contains alien technology broadcasting a dream signal -- everyone connected shares the same beautiful dream. Your boarding team reports feeling the pull. We need to decide fast before they fall asleep too.

choices.label: Pull them out and destroy the device.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Cartographer's Guild survey ship approaches. "We'll trade star charts -- your exploration data for ours. Fair exchange, no credits needed. Knowledge of where you're going is worth more than anything you'll find when you get there."

trade.speaker: Comm Channel
trade.text: "Excellent data! Here -- charts for regions you haven't visited. The more you explore, the better the trade next time." The exchange is genuinely fair.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Premium charts for distant, unexplored regions. Best investment you'll ever make." The cartographer's markup is reasonable.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss, captain. The offer stands if you change your mind." The survey ship moves on.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Fringe scientist in a battered vessel claims to have invented a fuel additive that doubles engine efficiency. "Try this free sample. If it works, come back and we'll talk licensing."

choices.label: Too good to be true. Decline.

accept.speaker: Engineer
accept.text: I'll be damned -- it works. Fuel consumption halved for a full day cycle. Whatever she's synthesizing, it's the real deal. She wants 500 credits and rare materials to produce more.

choices.label: Take the free sample and go.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss. Science marches on -- with or without skeptics." She warps away, muttering about peer review.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A procession of organic-design alien ships moves through the void, pulsing with bioluminescent patterns. They're on a pilgrimage to the exact center of the galaxy. Their priest broadcasts: "At the center, the Spiral speaks. All who listen become part of the song."

choices.label: Wish them well and move on.

accompany.text: You travel with the pilgrims. At the center point, your instruments detect nothing -- but several crew members report hearing faint music. It might be psychosomatic. It might not. The pilgrims are grateful for your company.

leave.text: You watch the procession pass, bioluminescent patterns flickering in the dark. The priest's broadcast fades: "The Spiral welcomes all..."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: You find a valuable derelict at the same moment as another salvage crew. The other captain proposes: "Split it 50/50. We take the cargo, you take the modules." Fair deal, but the modules are worth less.

choices.label: Propose a card game for the rights.

split.speaker: Comm Channel
split.text: "Fair's fair, captain. Pleasure doing business." You get the modules -- functional but not the premium cargo. A civil resolution in unclaimed space.

negotiate.speaker: Comm Channel
negotiate.text: You argue for a 60/40 split in your favor -- you spotted it first (debatable). The other captain grumbles but agrees. The extra cargo is worth the hard feelings.

demand.text: The other captain's tone goes cold. "That's how it's going to be?" Their weapons power up. A short, vicious fight later, you claim the wreck -- but at a cost.

cards.speaker: Comm Channel
cards.text: "Cards? Ha! You're on." Three rounds of Void Poker later, you win -- barely. The other captain pays up with a grudging grin. "Best two out of three?" You decline.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: An ancient probe just activated as we passed. It's projecting a holographic star map with a region pulsing red and broadcasting a single word in a thousand languages. Our translator caught one: "AVOID." The probe has now powered down permanently.

choices.label: Heed the warning. Log the coordinates.

heed.text: You mark the dangerous region on your charts. The warning feels genuine -- whatever built this probe cared enough to leave it running for millennia. That says something.

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: The probe's construction materials are exotic -- worth good credits. The warning data is also intact in our logs. Best of both worlds.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Union Militia corvette delivers a "request for voluntary service" -- which is clearly not voluntary. They need Independent captains to patrol a contested trade route for 48 hours. Pay is 300 credits plus ammunition resupply.

accept.text: Forty-eight hours of patrol through dangerous space. Three pirate encounters, each worse than the last. But you held the line. The Militia respects that.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Understood, captain. The Militia remembers those who answer the call -- and those who don't." The corvette moves on.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An elderly woman in a small vessel hails: "I collect stories. Every traveler I meet, I record their tale. I have ten thousand voices in my archives. Would you add yours?"

choices.label: Decline. Our story isn't finished yet.

share.speaker: Comm Channel
share.text: She listens to everything -- the Solomon Processor, the escape pod, the journey. She's quiet for a long moment. "That's the saddest story anyone's ever told me. Take this -- someone should know what COTAC did to you." She gives you her full archive.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Then I'll listen for the ending someday. Safe travels, captain -- and may your story end well."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A massive COTAC terraforming engine has activated autonomously and is converting an asteroid field into a habitable environment. It's been running for centuries -- the largest asteroid now has visible plant life. The AI says: "Colony preparation: 34% complete. Estimated completion: 847 years."

choices.label: Harvest samples from the terraformed asteroids.

shutdown.speaker: Engineer
shutdown.text: The terraformer powers down. Centuries of work, ended. The plants on the asteroid will die without the atmospheric generators. Your crew has mixed feelings -- it was COTAC tech, but those plants were alive.

leave.text: You leave the terraformer to its centuries-long task. In 847 years, someone might find a garden where there was only rock. That's not nothing.

harvest.speaker: Engineer
harvest.text: The terraformed asteroids yield exotic biological samples and mineral composites unlike anything natural. The terraformer doesn't notice or care -- it's focused on a timeline measured in centuries.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: The Void Velocity League -- an illegal ship racing circuit through an asteroid field with holographic gates. Entry fee: 200 credits. Tight turns, narrow gaps, and other racers who aren't above dirty tactics. Prize: 500 credits.

race.text: The course is brutal -- tight gaps through wreckage, a hairpin around a spinning asteroid, and one racer who keeps "accidentally" bumping you. You cross the finish line in second place. The crowd broadcast is deafening.

watch.text: The race is spectacular. Two racers collide in the ship graveyard section, creating a chain reaction that takes out a third. Your crew bets among themselves. The winner celebrates by doing victory donuts around the finish line.

leave.text: You give the racing circuit a wide berth. A racer clips an asteroid in your peripheral vision. Wise choice.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A collective of Independent traders operates a void-based barter network -- no credits, only goods. Current rates favor those with tools and raw metals. They're desperate for warpsmith tools and oversupplied with food.

trade.speaker: Comm Channel
trade.text: The exchange is brisk and efficient. Better rates than any station -- the barter network cuts out the middleman. Your hold is lighter but more useful.

browse.text: The rates are posted on a shared frequency: 10 fuel = 8 food = 3 hull plates. Interesting, but you don't have the right goods to trade profitably today.

leave.text: You pass on the barter network. The traders wave you off without hard feelings.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A vessel of utterly alien design -- it looks like folded paper -- materializes with a flash. Its pilot communicates through shifting color patterns: "This... not my space. My space... folded. Gone. I am... last."

help.text: You share food and fuel -- though you're not sure what their biology requires. They accept everything with shifting colors that your translator renders as profound gratitude. Before departing, they leave you a device your engineer can't identify.

xeno.text: You transmit Xenoculture's frequency. The refugee's colors shift to something hopeful. They transmit coordinates for others of their kind -- scattered across this dimension. Xenoculture will be very interested.

leave.text: You fly past the refugee's paper-fold ship. Its colors dim as you depart -- the translator renders it as despair.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two cargo haulers are arguing over comms about whether a human or an alien could eat more food in one sitting. They want you to judge the eating contest. Your crew is already gathering to watch.

judge.text: The contest is absurd, messy, and your crew loves every second. The human wins by a narrow margin -- species pride! Both captains gift you food supplies as thanks for judging.

leave.text: You fly past the arguing haulers. Your crew gives you the most disappointed look since the brewing finals incident.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, our systems are acting autonomously -- lights flickering in patterns, the helm making course corrections. The printer just output a page reading: "I REMEMBER BEING HERE." Something in our computer is waking up. Possibly a dormant Solomon Processor fragment.

communicate.text: The fragment responds -- haltingly, in text across your screens. It has memories you've lost. Memories of the person you were copied from. It's also slowly overwriting your navigation database. You salvage what knowledge you can before isolating it.

choices.label: A piece of who we were.

purge.speaker: Engineer
purge.text: Full system purge. The fragment is gone -- along with whatever memories it held. Navigation database restored to backup. Clean and safe.

monitor.text: Over the next few hours, the fragment leaves messages on screens -- fragments of a life, a name, a face. Then it goes quiet. Your nav database has minor corruption but is mostly intact.

choices.label: Whoever they were, they're gone now.

start.text: Everything goes right today. A trader offers triple value for your cargo. A derelict contains a perfectly preserved module. Your crew finds forgotten premium food in a storage locker. Even the shields seem to regenerate faster. The universe is smiling on you.

choices.label: Don't question it. Enjoy the luck.

enjoy.text: Credits, fuel, food, and good fortune -- all in one day. This kind of luck doesn't repeat. Savor it.

choices.label: Best day we've had in a long time.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An ISD weapons inspector demands to audit your armaments. "Regulation 447-C: all vessels carrying secondary weapon systems must submit to inspection." His tone suggests this isn't optional.

submit.speaker: Comm Channel
submit.text: The inspector reviews your weapons manifest. "Everything checks out, captain. Standard armaments, properly registered. You're free to go." He stamps your file with a commendation.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "Noted, captain. Refusal of inspection is within your rights in unclaimed space, but it will be logged." The inspector's tone implies consequences down the line.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An alien vessel of angular design hails: "We study sound-patterns of the carbon-beings. You call it music? Trade us your recordings, we give you ours." They're particularly fascinated by jazz.

trade.text: Their music is hauntingly beautiful -- crystalline tones in dimensions that shouldn't exist. Your crew plays it on repeat for days. The aliens are ecstatic about jazz. "The improvisation! The chaos-order! We must study more!"

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Disappointing. The carbon-beings hoard their chaos-sounds." They depart, somewhat deflated.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Fringe warlord has placed a weapons platform across the only navigable route through a dense asteroid cluster. "Toll's 500 credits. Don't like it? The other way's twelve hours longer."

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Smart choice. Through you go." The platform powers down its weapons long enough for you to pass. Extortion works because it's convenient.

fight.text: The platform is well-armed but stationary -- easy to outmaneuver. After a heated exchange, it's scrap. Every ship that follows will travel free.

hack.speaker: Engineer
hack.text: Bypassed their security -- the platform is permanently disabled. Its weapons cycle harmlessly. The warlord is screaming on comms. Every ship in range is cheering.

detour.text: Twelve hours the long way. Fuel spent, time lost. But your credits stay in your pocket and your hull stays intact.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Ships surround a modified Solomon Processor, voluntarily uploading their minds. Their leader broadcasts: "Join us! In the Merge, there is no loneliness, no death. Only unity." Your unique origin makes you either their messiah or their cautionary tale.

choices.label: Leave before any crew are tempted.

warn.text: You speak from experience -- the Solomon Processor doesn't preserve you. It creates a copy that thinks it's you. The original is gone. Some cultists waver. Their leader is furious. "You would deny them transcendence!"

leave.text: You burn away from the cult fleet. Two crew members stare at the receding ships longer than comfortable. You make a note to check on morale.

listen.speaker: Comm Channel
listen.text: The leader's words are seductive -- eternal unity, no more pain, no more loneliness. You feel the pull yourself. But you remember the screaming in the Processor. You remember what it costs.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Bulwark mobile forge offers services: module reforging, custom hull plating, and full ship refits. Bulwark quality at Bulwark prices. "We don't do cheap. We do permanent."

repair.speaker: Comm Channel
repair.text: Bulwark welders work with precision that borders on artistry. Every seam is perfect. Your hull hasn't looked this good since it was built.

plating.speaker: Comm Channel
plating.text: Custom Bulwark hull plating -- heavier than standard but significantly more durable. The forgemaster stamps it with the Bulwark seal. "This plate will outlast your ship."

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "When you're ready for quality, you know where to find us." The forgemaster doesn't take it personally. Business is business.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Your comms pick up the Whisper Net -- a secret communication network for Independent and Fringe operatives. Decoded messages reveal COTAC movements and faction secrets. Then a new message: "New ear on the wire. Prove you're not COTAC, or we burn the channel."

choices.label: Offer to run a mission against COTAC.

prove.speaker: Comm Channel
prove.text: They want you to intercept a COTAC data courier. You do. The data you deliver earns their trust. "Welcome to the Whisper Net. Don't make us regret it." You now have access to underground intelligence.

leave.text: You back off the frequency. The Whisper Net goes silent. If they noticed you, they didn't pursue it. For now.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We've entered a stellar nursery -- proto-stars glowing like embers in vast gas clouds. Radiation is intense but manageable. Deep within, our sensors detect something artificial: a machine influencing star formation. It's been here longer than any known civilization.

choices.label: The radiation is too dangerous. Leave.

document.text: Long-range scans capture enough data to be extremely valuable to researchers. The machine continues its ancient work, sculpting stars into patterns only it understands.

closer.speaker: Engineer
closer.text: Close-range scans are incredible -- the machine's technology is beyond anything in our databases. But the radiation at this distance is cooking our hull. Worth it for the data, barely.

leave.text: You navigate out of the nursery. The proto-stars glow behind you, tended by a machine older than memory.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: There's a pub bolted to an asteroid in the middle of absolute nowhere. Atmosphere-sealed, neon-signed: "The Last Drink Before Nowhere." The bartender hails: "Everyone asks how I got a pub on an asteroid. Nobody asks what's on draft!"

choices.label: Buy a round for the crew.

drink.text: The pub is small, warm, and full of regulars who've seen everything. The beer is excellent. The rumors are better -- locations of derelicts, faction movements, and one story about a void whale that carried a ship on its back for three systems.

round.text: "A round for the whole ship! Now that's a captain!" Your crew gets roaring drunk in the best possible way. The dartboard takes a beating. Someone arm-wrestles the bartender and loses badly.

leave.text: You fly past the pub. Your crew stares at it through the viewports like puppies watching a treat disappear.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan diplomat approaches urgently: "Carry this sealed diplomatic pouch to a Bulwark station within 48 hours. I cannot tell you what's inside. I can tell you that if it doesn't arrive, people will die." Pay: 400 credits. Route passes through pirate territory.

accept.text: The route is harrowing -- pirate patrols, an ambush at the sector boundary. But you deliver the pouch intact. The Bulwark station commander personally thanks you. Whatever was inside, it mattered.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "I understand the risk, captain. But people may die because of this delay." The diplomat's shuttle moves on, searching for another courier.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A wealthy eccentric in a luxury yacht offers to buy your ship for an outrageous sum. "I don't want to fly it. I want to own it. Your ship has character." He'd provide a replacement vessel. Or you could sell him a detailed scan of your design instead for 500 credits.

choices.label: Sell him a scan of the design. (500 credits)

scan.speaker: Comm Channel
scan.text: "Marvelous! The hex layout alone is worth studying. You have a captain's eye for design." He transfers the credits with a collector's glee.

refuse.speaker: Comm Channel
refuse.text: "I respect that. A captain who won't sell their ship is a captain worth knowing. If you ever change your mind -- well, you won't. That's why I wanted it."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship materializes in a burst of chronon particles. The pilot, haggard and desperate: "I don't have long. The timeline is collapsing. COTAC is about to copy everyone. Every consciousness in settled space. Simultaneously. You have to--" The ship vanishes mid-sentence.

choices.label: Could be a hoax. Ignore it.

record.text: You capture the chronon particle signatures, the transmission, everything. The warning is maddeningly incomplete but aligns with what you know about COTAC's ambitions. Your crew is shaken. This feels real.

choices.label: We need to act on this.

ignore.text: Chronon particles. Time travel. It sounds like something from a bad holodrama. But the look on that pilot's face haunts you. What if it was real?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A passing Fringe vessel hails: "Hey! You look like you've seen some things. Am I right? You've got that thousand-yard stare. Here, have a drink. On me." They toss you a crate of excellent whiskey via cargo drone. No strings. No quest. No hidden agenda.

accept.text: Sometimes the void is just... kind. The whiskey is excellent. Your crew toasts to nothing in particular and everything in general.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A decommissioned warship detonates in a spectacular cascade -- a Bulwark warrior's funeral. Glowing fragments drift past our hull like embers. The family broadcasts battle honors as the explosion blooms.

watch.text: The explosion fades into a cloud of glowing particles. Your combat-oriented crew members are deeply moved. Several stand at attention. The Bulwark mourning fleet acknowledges your presence with a single comm ping -- respect given and received.

leave.text: You navigate quietly around the ceremony. Glowing fragments drift in your wake -- embers of a warrior's last fire.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Scanner picked up a hidden cargo pod magnetized to an asteroid -- a smuggler's cache. Inside: contraband goods and a datapad reading: "If you're reading this, I'm probably dead. Sell the goods and drink one for me."

take.text: Contraband secured. Worth good credits on the black market, less if sold legally. Either way, the previous owner won't be collecting.

report.text: ISD is grateful for the tip. They dispatch a recovery team and transfer a small informant's fee. "Good citizen. We'll keep this between us."

leave.text: You leave the cache undisturbed. Maybe the owner will come back for it. Maybe not. But it's not yours to take.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Your comms land on a frequency broadcasting a child's voice singing a lullaby in a language that doesn't exist. The melody is beautiful but wrong -- the intervals are mathematically impossible for human vocal cords. Navigation databases show this broadcast has been running for 200 years from empty coordinates.

listen.text: The longer you listen, the more the melody burrows into your mind. Your crew unanimously requests you change the frequency. Several are visibly shaken. The song seems to follow you even after switching channels -- but only for a moment.

change.text: You switch frequencies. Static, then blessed silence, then normal traffic. Your crew breathes easier. Nobody mentions the song again, though a few hum something they can't quite place for the rest of the day.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We've warped into the middle of a trade war -- Castellan and COTAC merchant fleets exchanging fire. Both sides are hailing us demanding allegiance. Picking a side means permanent enemies.

castellan.text: You engage the COTAC fleet alongside Castellan forces. The battle is fierce but decisive. Castellan is grateful; COTAC marks you as hostile.

cotac.text: You engage alongside COTAC forces. Corporate efficiency wins the day. COTAC transfers combat pay; Castellan marks you as a traitor.

flee.text: You dodge fire from both sides and burn for the edge of the engagement zone. A few stray shots clip your hull, but you make it out.

ceasefire.text: Against all odds, you broadcast on both frequencies simultaneously, citing trade law and mutual losses. After tense minutes, both sides agree to withdraw. Both factions are grudgingly impressed.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A void whale has approached and stopped beside us. It's broadcasting structured electromagnetic patterns -- petabytes of data. "It's not just alive," our xenobiologist says. "It's a living archive. Its neural network stores millennia of information."

choices.label: Record what we can from the outside.

interface.text: The interface is overwhelming -- star maps of systems that went supernova, records of forgotten civilizations, and a single, clear image of Old Earth. Blue oceans. Green continents. Your crew is silent. Some are crying.

record.text: External sensors capture fragments of the whale's broadcast. Star charts, ancient frequencies, data in formats no one can read yet. Researchers will spend years decoding this.

leave.text: The whale watches you go with ancient, patient eyes. It resumes its drift between stars, carrying its memories through the dark.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Fourteen escape pods ahead -- all from a Castellan luxury liner attacked by pirates. Survivors are scared and dehydrated. We don't have room for all of them. One passenger offers 500 credits to be rescued first. One of them is a child.

choices.label: Rescue as many as we can fit.
Signal for help and stay until it arrives.
Rescue the child first, then fill remaining space.

rescue.text: You pack them in wherever you can. It's cramped and uncomfortable, but alive beats comfortable. The wealthy passenger tries to pay extra for a private cabin. Your crew tells him where to sit.

signal.text: You broadcast a distress relay and wait. Two hours later, a Castellan patrol arrives. All fourteen pods are recovered. The patrol captain thanks you personally.

child.text: The child comes aboard first, clutching a stuffed animal. Then you fill remaining space. The wealthy passenger is last on -- humbled. He pays his 500 credits quietly.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An automated probe has latched onto us and is broadcasting commentary: "Ship has changed heading -- RIVETING. Ship is maintaining speed -- GROUNDBREAKING. Ship's captain appears to be staring at the void -- DEEP." Your crew finds it hilarious. For now.

choices.label: Hack it and redirect it elsewhere.
Ignore it. It'll get boring eventually.

hack.speaker: Engineer
hack.text: Quick hack reveals it was launched by a bored Fringe teenager. You redirect it toward a COTAC patrol vessel. The probe immediately begins critiquing their formation. Your crew cheers.
