destroy.text: One shot, and the probe is scrap. Its final broadcast: "SHIP HAS FIRED WEAPONS AT COMEDY -- TYPICAL." Your crew feels slightly guilty.

ignore.text: Two hours later, the probe runs out of power. Its final message: "Battery dying. Tell... my creator... I was... hilarious..." Your crew gives it a moment of silence, then laughs for ten minutes straight.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A massive alien vessel of organic design serves as a mobile embassy. They'll trade rare biological materials and uncharted star maps, but their customs require "trust tokens" -- items of personal significance, not monetary value.

choices.label: Sacrifice a treasured personal item to trade.
We have nothing to offer. Decline.

trade.text: Your crew member surrenders a keepsake -- a locket, a worn book, something irreplaceable. The aliens accept it reverently and provide rare specimens and charts of regions no human has explored. The goods are extraordinary.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: The aliens understand. "Trust cannot be forced. Perhaps another time, when something of true value is offered." Their vessel moves on, slow and graceful.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A bounty hunter hails: "Nothing personal, captain. Someone put a price on your head -- 10,000 credits. Something about a cargo dispute in the Velan system." You've never been to the Velan system. Mistaken identity -- or a frame job.

choices.label: Show navigation logs to prove innocence.
Pay him to go away. (300 credits)
Hire him to find who placed the bounty. (200 credits)

prove.speaker: Comm Channel
prove.text: He reviews your logs carefully. "Huh. You've never even been near Velan. Somebody set you up." He lowers his weapons. "No charge for the tip: someone wants you dead. Watch your back."

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: "Smart. Cheaper than dying." He takes the credits and vanishes. The bounty is still out there, but he won't be the one collecting.

hire.speaker: Comm Channel
hire.text: "Now that's interesting. You want to hunt the hunter. I like it." He takes your credits and promises to track the bounty source. "I'll be in touch." A new ally -- of sorts.

fight.text: He's skilled, but you're better armed. After a short exchange, he disengages. "Fine! Not worth 10,000 credits anyway!" He warps out. The bounty remains, but word will spread that you fight back.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A formal solar sail race is underway -- elegant ships with massive reflective sails catching starlight. Wealthy Castellan nobles who consider engine-powered ships "vulgar" invite you to observe from the viewing area.

watch.text: The race is genuinely beautiful -- silent ships gliding in slow arcs. Your engineer is offended on behalf of engine technology. Your crew places bets. The leader crashes into a comet at 0.003 km/h -- the most graceful collision in history.

leave.text: You engage engines -- loudly -- and leave the solar sail race behind. Several nobles send disapproving comms about your "vulgar exhaust."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Priority-one emergency broadcast on all frequencies: "THIS IS BULWARK STATION VIGIL. WE ARE UNDER ATTACK. ALL VESSELS, RESPOND." A pirate armada, fifty ships strong. The station is three systems away.

respond.text: You burn hard for Station Vigil. The battle is intense -- you're one of many defenders. Pirates fall, but not without cost. When the armada breaks, Bulwark survivors broadcast your ship's name alongside their own. You are remembered.

ignore.text: You continue on your course. The emergency broadcast repeats for hours before going silent. Your crew doesn't discuss it. They don't need to.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An old cartographer hails: "The void isn't empty. It's a river with a thousand currents. Learn them and you'll never burn more fuel than you need." She sells charts of void currents, debris flows, and gravitational eddies. One location she labels simply: "Don't."

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Good investment, captain. These charts will pay for themselves in fuel savings." The maps are extraordinarily detailed -- a lifetime of work condensed into data.

ask.speaker: Comm Channel
ask.text: She goes quiet. "I went there once. I came back. Most of my crew didn't. I don't know what's there. I don't want to know. Just... don't." She won't say more. But the coordinates are in the charts if you buy them.

choices.label: Buy the charts with the 'Don't' location. (200 credits)

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Your loss. The void rewards those who study it." She returns to her charts, adding another notation to her life's work.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A bio-ship offers crew cloning -- illegal in every jurisdiction. "Think of it as an investment in redundancy," the doctor says with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. The clone has no memories and must be trained from scratch.

clone.text: The process is fast and disturbing. A new crew member emerges -- genetically identical to your best, but blank-eyed and confused. Other crew members are deeply uncomfortable. The clone will need time.

report.text: You transmit coordinates to the nearest patrol. The bio-ship detects the signal and warps away before anyone arrives. At least you tried.

leave.text: You fly away from the bio-ship. Your crew is relieved. Some ethical lines shouldn't be crossed, no matter how practical the outcome.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Crystalline-design alien ships have formed a geometric lattice, resonating at a frequency that makes our hull vibrate. Our translator picks up fragments: "Join... frequency... become... facet..." They're inviting us to join their communion -- a shared consciousness through harmonic resonance.

choices.label: Leave. Shared consciousness isn't for us.

join.text: The experience is brief and overwhelming -- alien thoughts brush against human ones. Some crew members find it transcendent. Others find it terrifying. Nobody is unchanged.

observe.text: The lattice pulses with light as the communion proceeds. Your sensors capture fascinating data on the resonance frequencies. The aliens don't seem to mind observers.

leave.text: You navigate around the lattice. The resonance fades. Your hull stops vibrating.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An unregistered station with no transponder -- an ISD black site. Before you can leave, they hail: "You've entered a restricted zone. Land immediately for debriefing." Your sensors detected Solomon Processor signatures inside.

cooperate.speaker: Comm Channel
cooperate.text: ISD agents ask what you've seen and who you've told. You answer honestly. They pay you for your cooperation and discretion. "Forget this place exists, captain. That's not a request." What they're doing inside is never explained.

run.text: You burn for open space. The ISD interceptor pursues but breaks off at the sector boundary. You're marked now -- ISD doesn't forget witnesses who don't cooperate.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A young Independent trader on her first solo voyage -- dead reactor, stranded. "I just wanted to see the stars up close. Stupid, right?" She's terrified.

choices.label: Tow her to the nearest station.

fuel.speaker: Comm Channel
fuel.text: "Thank you. Thank you so much. I thought I was going to die out here." She's crying with relief. Your crew feels good about this one.

components.speaker: Comm Channel
components.text: Your engineer jury-rigs her reactor with spare components. It's not pretty, but it runs. "I'll never forget this, captain. If you ever need a favor in the Pellerin system, ask for Maya."

tow.text: You tow her shuttle to the nearest station. It takes time, but she's safe. She becomes a permanent contact -- sending trade tips and intel from her travels. Good investment.

leave.text: You fly past the stranded shuttle. Your crew watches it recede on sensors. Nobody meets your eyes for a while.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A quirky inventor has converted a cargo ship into a museum of failed inventions: a faster-than-light radio that only receives the past, a shield generator that only blocks compliments, an engine that runs on regret. Admission: 25 credits.

visit.text: The museum is delightful. Your crew laughs at the "compliment shield" and debates whether the regret engine would work better in COTAC space. The inventor beams with pride at exhibits of her own failures.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Ah, the FTL radio! It receives historical transmissions -- sometimes with coordinates. Mostly it's old news broadcasts and love songs, but occasionally something valuable surfaces." The device is quirky but functional.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "No appreciation for the art of failure! The regret engine weeps for you!" She waves you off cheerfully.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A COTAC executive in a fast courier: "I have proof of what COTAC does with the Solomon Processor. Not the public version -- the real version. The one where consent is optional. I need to reach Union Militia space alive. They're already hunting me."

choices.label: Turn her over to COTAC for a reward.

escort.text: COTAC pursuit ships find you twice. Both times, you fight them off. The defector delivers her data to Union Militia command. "You've helped expose them, captain. The Militia won't forget this." She shares some of the data with you -- it concerns your own origins.

betray.text: COTAC pays well for the return of their property -- including the executive. The credits are substantial. Your crew's morale collapses. Several won't look you in the eye.

leave.text: You fly past the courier. COTAC interceptors close in behind you. The defector's final transmission: "Someone has to care about the truth." Then static.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... there's a garden floating in the void. A sphere of atmosphere, soil, and living plants -- without a planet, without containment. Flowers bloom in vacuum. Trees grow toward a light source that doesn't exist. Our botanist is speechless.

sample.text: You extract a single cutting. The garden doesn't seem to mind -- if anything, the surrounding flowers lean toward your ship as if saying goodbye. The cutting will dramatically improve hydroponics yields.

observe.text: You record everything. The technology maintaining this garden is so advanced it's indistinguishable from magic. The data alone is valuable. The beauty is beyond value.

leave.text: You leave the void garden to its impossible existence. Behind you, flowers bloom in the dark between stars.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A professional mediator offers her services: "For 200 credits, I'll improve your standing with any faction of your choice. Everyone owes me favors. I've been doing this for thirty years, and the one thing I've learned is that everyone is one conversation away from peace. Usually an expensive conversation."

bulwark.speaker: Comm Channel
bulwark.text: "Bulwark? Easy. They respect action. I'll mention your service record to the right people." She makes a call. An hour later, your standing with Bulwark has noticeably improved.

cotac.speaker: Comm Channel
cotac.text: "COTAC? Harder. They respect compliance. I'll file some paperwork and call in a favor." She works her contacts. COTAC's disposition toward you warms noticeably.

fringe.speaker: Comm Channel
fringe.text: "The Fringe? You just need the right introduction. I know a few warlords who owe me drinks." She broadcasts on a secure frequency. Your Fringe reputation improves.

decline.speaker: Comm Channel
decline.text: "Your loss. Reputation is everything in this galaxy. You can earn it the hard way or the easy way."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Hundreds of destroyed ships from multiple factions -- a mass grave from a battle that no one recorded. Recent, within weeks, but no record exists. Weapons signatures are mixed -- everyone was fighting together. Against what?

salvage.speaker: Engineer
salvage.text: Plenty to salvage, but picking through it feels like robbing graves. Your combat veterans recognize the formation -- a defensive sphere. Whatever they were fighting came from all directions at once. The logs are corrupted. Every single one.

document.text: You record ship registrations, weapon signatures, formation data. This will be valuable to intelligence analysts -- someone erased this battle from history. The question is who, and why.

leave.text: You leave the graveyard behind. Your sensors show nothing following you. That doesn't help with the feeling that something is watching.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: Captain, we found a stowaway -- a teenage Fringe kid hiding in a cargo container. Been there for days, eating smuggled ration bars. "Please don't take me back. My parents want me to be an accountant."

choices.label: Return her to the nearest station.
Keep her as a junior crew member.
Give her supplies and point her toward the Fringe nomad fleet.

return.text: You drop her at the nearest station with a stern lecture about stowing away. She rolls her eyes but thanks you. "Fine. But I'm not going to be an accountant." She's annoyingly resilient.

keep.text: She throws herself into every task with terrifying enthusiasm. Turns out she's annoyingly competent at hauling, cleaning, and somehow jury-rigging repairs she was never taught. Your crew adopts her immediately.

nomad.text: You give her a week's supplies and the Fringe nomad fleet's last known coordinates. "This is amazing! Thank you, captain!" She practically vibrates with excitement as her escape pod launches toward adventure.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An avant-garde artist has converted a decommissioned vessel into a zero-gravity art gallery. Sculptures float freely, paintings cover every surface including the ceiling. "This one represents the futility of corporate existence. I call it 'Another Meeting That Could Have Been An Email.'"

tour.text: Your crew's reactions range from fascinated to bewildered. The zero-gravity pieces are genuinely impressive -- a sculpture that only makes sense from six different angles simultaneously. Even the skeptics are moved.

buy.speaker: Comm Channel
buy.text: "Ah, a patron of the arts!" The miniature sculpture floats in your cargo bay, slowly rotating. It's oddly beautiful. Your crew debates its meaning for days -- which might be the point.

leave.speaker: Comm Channel
leave.text: "Philistines! The void is wasted on the unappreciative!" She returns to rearranging floating sculptures.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: A flash of impossible light and a shockwave -- someone just tested a prototype engine that tore a hole in local spacetime. While it's open, physics gets flexible: gravity shifts randomly, time dilates in patches. Our hull is taking stress damage.

choices.label: Scan the anomaly before it closes.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Fighting through spatial distortion to get readings... got it! The data is extraordinary -- detailed measurements of a spacetime tear. Any faction's research division would pay a fortune for this. Hull took some stress, but the data is priceless.

flee.text: You burn for clear space. The spatial distortion buffets your hull as you escape. Behind you, the hole in spacetime slowly knits itself shut. Whatever that engine was, it wasn't ready.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, there's a tiny shielded pod parked dangerously close to the local star. One life sign. He's hailing us.

hermit.speaker: The Hermit
hermit.text: "She speaks to me, captain -- the star. She tells me about every ship that passes, the planets she's warmed, the day she'll finally die. I have a gift for you -- a prediction. There's a derelict, valuable beyond measure, that will appear soon. I'll give you the coordinates."

choices.label: This man is clearly deranged. Leave.

accept.speaker: Sensor Officer
accept.text: He transmitted coordinates and a timestamp. I can't verify it yet, but... his navigational data about local ship movements checks out perfectly. He knew our heading before we hailed him.

leave.text: You pull away from the star. The hermit's pod grows small in the rear display. Your sensor officer mutters, "He knew our ship name before we transmitted it."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Castellan merchant prince hails you from the center of a twenty-ship entourage -- guards, servants, storage vessels, even a personal chef ship. "I am Prince Aldren, and I am spectacularly bored. Entertain me and I'll make it worth your while."

choices.label: Tell him tales of your adventures.
Challenge him to a trade negotiation.

stories.speaker: Prince Aldren
stories.text: "Marvelous! Genuine danger, real stakes -- not the sanitized drivel my courtiers feed me. Here, 100 credits per tale. You've earned every one." He transfers the credits with a flourish.

trade_game.speaker: Prince Aldren
trade_game.text: His eyes light up. The negotiation is fierce -- he's sharper than he looks. After an hour of bluffing and counter-offers, he concedes with a grin. "Well played, captain. You've earned this."

decline.speaker: Prince Aldren
decline.text: He sighs dramatically. "Another bore in the void. Very well. Safe travels, captain." The caravan glides past in formation.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, you need to see this. There's a comet passing by with words spray-painted on its surface in fifty-meter letters: "COTAC SUCKS -- FRINGE 4EVER." Someone actually EVA'd onto a comet to tag it. A COTAC patrol nearby is furious and scanning every ship in the area.

choices.label: Add your own message when they're not looking.

help_cotac.speaker: COTAC Officer
help_cotac.text: "Your cooperation is noted, captain. We'll find this degenerate. COTAC remembers its friends." They don't find anyone, but they appreciate the gesture.

ignore.text: You drift past the comet, your crew stifling laughter. The COTAC patrol glares at you on sensors but can't prove anything.

tag_it.speaker: Engineer
tag_it.text: Your engineer sneaks out in a suit while COTAC is scanning the other side. He adds: "HONK IF YOU'RE FREE." He barely makes it back before COTAC sweeps around. Your crew is in tears laughing. If COTAC finds out, you're in deep trouble.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Multiple distress signals -- six of them -- all activating at once across a wide area. Coordinated pirate attack. We can only reach one in time. Captain, choose quickly.

medical.text: You arrive guns blazing. The medical transport is damaged but intact. Pirates scatter as you engage. The doctors aboard transmit their gratitude and emergency supplies.

liner.speaker: Liner Captain
liner.text: "You saved three hundred people today, captain. Three hundred lives that go home because of you." The liner's passengers cheer as the pirates flee. A collection is taken up among the passengers.

bulwark.speaker: Bulwark Scout
bulwark.text: "You chose to save a warrior over civilians. Either you're a fool or you understand something most don't. Either way -- I owe you a life-debt, captain. I don't forget."

cargo.speaker: Engineer
cargo.text: The hauler's cargo is intact -- valuable trade goods floating free. The hauler captain nods gratefully from a battered bridge. Your crew salvages what the pirates scattered.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship that seems to shimmer at the edges hails you. "Dreams for sale, captain. Adventure, romance, the feeling of flight -- I have them all in crystalline form. 50 credits for a pleasant night. 200 for something you'll never forget."

choices.label: Buy a cheap dream chip (50 credits).
Buy the expensive dream chip (200 credits).

cheap.speaker: Dream Merchant
cheap.text: "A fine choice -- 'Soaring Over Old Earth.' Very popular." Your crew member who uses it sleeps better than they have in months. They wake smiling and humming a tune nobody recognizes.

expensive.text: The chip is labeled simply: "The Truth About You." Your crew member who uses it wakes up crying but refuses to say what they saw. They stare out the viewport for hours afterward. When they finally speak, all they say is: "It was beautiful."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A formal alien trade delegation -- angular ships in precise formation -- arrives with a proposal. Their ambassador speaks through a translator: "We wish to establish a permanent trade route. We need a human liaison. The pay is generous. The cargo... some items your factions call contraband."

ask.speaker: Alien Ambassador
ask.text: "Biological compounds your COTAC classifies as restricted. We consider them staple goods. Nothing harmful -- they simply threaten pharmaceutical monopolies. We are honest about this. The choice is yours."

accept.speaker: Alien Ambassador
accept.text: "Excellent. Your first payment, and a sample of our trade goods at discount." The delegation transfers credits and rare materials. Your name is now known in alien trade circles.

decline.speaker: Alien Ambassador
decline.text: "We understand. The offer remains open should you reconsider." The formation pivots with mechanical precision and glides away.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, our long-range receiver is picking up something from outside the galaxy -- from the intergalactic void. It's not natural. It's a voice: "We... have been... traveling... so long. Are you... the ones... who sang?" The power level behind this signal is beyond anything we've ever recorded.

choices.label: Record the signal and analyze it.

respond.text: You transmit a simple greeting. Silence. Then, after a delay that suggests impossible distance: "You are... small. But you sing... the same song. We will... come... to listen." The signal fades. Your crew is pale. Something out there knows we exist now.

analyze.speaker: Sensor Officer
analyze.text: The signal is ancient -- broadcast millennia ago, just now reaching us. It's a response to something transmitted from this galaxy long before any current civilization existed. The data is worth a fortune to researchers.

cut.speaker: Engineer
cut.text: Receiver offline. The bridge is silent. Your engineer speaks first: "Whatever that was, it's been traveling toward us for a very long time. Cutting the signal doesn't change that." Nobody sleeps well tonight.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two ships meet in the void -- former lovers reunited by chance after twenty years. Over open comms: "One last dance, for old times' sake?" The ships spiral around each other in an intricate, beautiful pattern. Your pilot is furiously taking notes on their maneuvers.

watch.text: The dance lasts ten minutes. When it ends, the two ships part without another word. Your crew is deeply moved. Your pilot mutters, "Did you see that inverse drift? Genius." Romance-minded crew members are smiling for hours afterward.

leave.text: You give them their space. Your pilot is disappointed but understands. "Could've learned something from those maneuvers," they sigh.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A long-defunct toll gate from a collapsed government blocks your path. Automated drones broadcast: "TOLL REQUIRED: 100 CREDITS. VIOLATORS WILL BE... POLITELY ASKED TO RECONSIDER." You could fly around it in seconds. The drones follow anyway.

pay.speaker: Comm Channel
pay.text: A pre-recorded message activates: "The Honorable Governor Thaddeus Krill thanks you for your contribution to the Greater Prosperity Zone! May your travels be swift and profitable!" Governor Krill died two centuries ago. The 100 credits go nowhere. Your crew finds the whole thing oddly charming.

bypass.speaker: Comm Channel
bypass.text: The drones follow you for kilometers, broadcasting increasingly desperate pleas: "PLEASE RECONSIDER. THE GREATER PROSPERITY ZONE NEEDS YOUR SUPPORT. WE ACCEPT ALL MAJOR CURRENCIES." They eventually give up and float back to the gate, dejected.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A feeble hail from a tiny ship. Inside, a dying chef: "Captain... I have no heirs. My life's work -- the recipe for void soup -- a dish so good it's ended feuds. Take it. The ingredients are rare, but the result... the result is worth everything."

accept.speaker: The Chef
accept.text: "Seven ingredients from seven systems. Each one is an adventure in itself. When you complete it... your crew will never forget the taste. Neither will anyone you serve it to. That's my legacy now. Yours." He transfers the data and closes his eyes with a peaceful smile.

decline.text: The old chef's face falls. Your cook slaps the back of your chair: "Captain! That was void soup! VOID SOUP!" Apparently you've made a grave culinary error.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: We've entered a region where a Solomon Processor catastrophically failed decades ago. Thousands of consciousness fragments drift through local space. Screens are flashing with faces. Speakers whisper with voices. Crew reports sudden memories that aren't theirs. Captain, we need to move through fast or get out.

speed.speaker: Engineer
speed.text: Engines at maximum. The whispers crescendo as you push through -- fragments of lives, memories, identities smashing against your hull like rain. Then silence. You're through. Your crew is shaken but intact.

retreat.text: You reverse course and clear the zone. The whispers fade. Your crew breathes easier, though a few still report phantom memories that take hours to shake.

linger.speaker: Sensor Officer
linger.text: The data is incredible -- raw neural patterns, preserved in vacuum. But the longer you stay, the worse it gets. One crew member starts answering to a different name. You pull out before the damage is permanent. The scans are worth a fortune.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A large vessel operates as a void auction house. Today's lots: a pre-expansion Earth artifact, an alien weapon prototype, a treasure system map, and a living power crystal. "Bidding begins in five minutes! Deep pockets recommended!"

choices.label: Bid on the treasure map (300 credits).
Bid on the power crystal (500 credits).
Just browse. Too rich for our blood.

map.speaker: Auctioneer
map.text: "Sold to the captain with the sharp eyes! One complete star chart of the Veiled Reach -- rumored to contain pre-expansion caches. Happy hunting!"

crystal.speaker: Auctioneer
crystal.text: "Sold! One living crystal, self-sustaining power source. Handle with care -- it hums when it's happy." The crystal pulses gently in your cargo hold, radiating a faint warmth.

browse.text: You watch the bidding war from the sidelines. NPC bidders with bottomless wallets fight over artifacts. Entertaining, if nothing else. The auctioneer slips you a catalog for next time.

start.speaker: Militia Investigator
start.text: "Captain, I need someone outside the chain of command. Three weeks ago, a Militia patrol destroyed a civilian freighter. They claim it fired first. The black box says otherwise. I need the truth, and I can't trust my own people with it."

investigate.speaker: Militia Investigator
investigate.text: "The truth is messy. The freighter was smuggling weapons -- but the patrol knew that and fired first anyway. Murdered civilians to pad their arrest record. Now -- do I report the patrol, the smugglers, or both?"

full_truth.speaker: Militia Investigator
full_truth.text: "Full truth it is. The patrol captain will face court martial. The smuggling ring gets exposed. Ugly all around, but honest. Thank you, captain. The Militia needs more of this."

bury.speaker: Militia Investigator
bury.text: She stares at you for a long moment. "Maybe you're right. Maybe nobody wins." She deletes the file. The dead stay dead. Your crew is quiet -- they heard everything.

decline.speaker: Militia Investigator
decline.text: "I understand. Not everyone wants to dig into this kind of mess." She nods curtly and warps away. The truth stays buried.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, a rogue planet -- ejected from its star system eons ago -- drifting dark and cold through the void. But I'm reading heat signatures on the surface. Something is alive down there, thriving without a sun on geothermal energy alone.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Bioluminescent forests in the cave networks. Creatures that have never seen starlight. An entire ecosystem in eternal darkness. The scientific data alone is extraordinary. Xenoculture researchers would pay a fortune for this.

sell.text: Xenoculture responds within minutes. "This is a landmark discovery. We're transmitting payment now." Your crew watches the dark planet shrink behind you, knowing they found something extraordinary.

keep.text: You file the data under encryption. A wandering planet with life -- that knowledge has value beyond credits. Your crew feels the weight of the secret.

log.text: The dark planet drifts on, its secrets undiscovered. Your sensor officer looks disappointed but says nothing.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two identical ships. Two identical captains. Both hailing simultaneously. "I'm the real Captain Vasquez! She's a COTAC Solomon copy!" "No, I'M real! Check her neural patterns!" Your science officer reports both patterns are identical. There is no way to tell.

alpha.speaker: Vasquez Alpha
alpha.text: "Thank you, captain. I knew someone would see the truth." Vasquez Beta screams in protest as Alpha's weapons power up. Your crew watches in uncomfortable silence. Was that the right call? There's no way to know.

beta.speaker: Vasquez Beta
beta.text: "I'm saved. Thank you." Alpha's ship goes silent. Beta transfers a reward, hands shaking on camera. "How do you live knowing you might be the copy?" she whispers. She's asking herself as much as you.

leave.text: You warp away. Behind you, the two Vasquez ships circle each other, weapons hot. The last thing you hear on comms is one of them saying: "Does it even matter which of us is real?"

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Massive ion storm inbound -- no way through safely. Six other ships are sheltering behind a large asteroid. We need to join them or risk severe damage.

shelter.text: Hours trapped behind an asteroid with strangers. A pirate captain shares food with a Castellan merchant. An ISD officer plays cards with a Fringe pilot. "Storms don't care about factions," someone observes. When it passes, everyone parts ways -- but you've gained contacts in unexpected places.

outrun.speaker: Engineer
outrun.text: The storm clips your aft section. Shields hold but barely. Hull takes a beating before you clear the edge. Your engineer is furious: "We had a perfectly good asteroid to hide behind!"

choices.label: We made it. That's what counts.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: "Captain... the crew has something to confess. We've been running a betting pool. How many pirates this week, whether the next derelict has good loot, what faction hails us next. It's grown to... well... 200 credits of pooled wages. We're sorry."

shutdown.text: The pool is dissolved. Credits returned. Your crew obeys, but the spark in their eyes dims. Duty tours are quieter now. Duller.

cut.speaker: Engineer
cut.text: "That's... fair, actually." The crew pays your captain's share -- 50 credits -- and continues the pool with your blessing. They respect a captain who takes their cut without killing the fun.

bet.text: You place 20 credits on "next encounter is comedy." The crew erupts in cheers. The captain's in the pool! Shifts become livelier. Arguments about odds fill the mess hall. It's the best entertainment credit for credit you've ever bought.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain, I'm detecting photons that aren't moving. Light, frozen in place, hanging in space like luminous dust. In a sphere about 300 meters across, light has simply... stopped. Our physicist is hyperventilating.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: Six hours of scanning yields data that rewrites physics textbooks. The speed of light is not constant here. Researchers across the sector will pay handsomely for this data. Your physicist has already started drafting a paper.

flythrough.speaker: Engineer
flythrough.text: Brief blindness as photons pile up against your hull like snow. Then you're through, trailing frozen light that slowly disperses behind you. Your crew blinks in the sudden brightness. No damage, but deeply unsettling.

avoid.text: You route around the anomaly. The frozen light hangs there, beautiful and impossible, as you pass. Some mysteries are best appreciated from a distance.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Dozens of vessels ahead -- all following the same transmission toward a point in deep space. Their crews seem entranced. Captain, our comms officer just started turning us toward it. Her eyes are glazed. That signal is doing something to organic minds.

cut.speaker: Engineer
cut.text: Signal severed. Your comms officer snaps out of it, disoriented and frightened. "I couldn't stop myself. I just... needed to go there." The entranced fleet continues into the void. You don't follow. Some doors are better left closed.

follow.text: You trail the fleet at a safe distance. A massive alien structure looms ahead -- organic, pulsing, absorbing ships into itself. Crew members who touched the signal have nightmares for days. You pull back before the structure notices you. The fleet doesn't follow you out.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship painted in motley colors hails you. "Why did the pilot cross the asteroid belt? To get to the other void!" A beat. "COTAC? More like COT-HACK! Bulwark warriors headbutt asteroids for fun -- and the asteroids apologize!" Your crew is groaning and laughing simultaneously.

show.speaker: The Jester
show.text: "What do you call an ISD agent with a sense of humor? Unemployed!" The jokes are terrible. The timing is perfect. Thirty minutes later, your crew is wiping tears from their eyes. "Thank you, thank you -- I'm here all week! Literally. My warp drive is broken."

tip.speaker: The Jester
tip.text: "A tipper! You, captain, are a patron of the arts! Here's a bonus joke: What's a pirate's favorite letter? You'd think it's R, but it's actually the C!" He bows theatrically as the credits transfer.

leave.speaker: The Jester
leave.text: "Tough nebula," he sighs. Your crew looks disappointed as the motley ship fades from view.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An alien research team in crystalline ships is excavating ancient ruins in open space -- a structure built before any current species evolved. Their lead researcher hails: "We need assistance with heavy extraction. In return, we share our findings. This structure was a waypoint in a galaxy-spanning network."

choices.label: We're not equipped for that. Sorry.

help.speaker: Alien Researcher
help.text: "Your assistance is invaluable. The species that built this ascended to a higher plane of existence. We recovered a navigation fragment -- it reveals hidden locations on star charts. Please, take it. Knowledge should be shared."

decline.speaker: Alien Researcher
decline.text: "We understand. Safe travels, captain. Perhaps next time." The crystalline ships resume their careful work as you depart.

start.speaker: Castellan Bureaucrat
start.text: "Captain, I regret to inform you that your ship registration has expired. I need form VC-47 in triplicate, a hull inspection certificate, and proof of insurance. I apologize for the inconvenience, but regulations are regulations."

choices.label: Argue that as an AI, you ARE the ship.

paperwork.speaker: Castellan Bureaucrat
paperwork.text: Three hours of forms, signatures, and subsections later: "Everything is in order! Welcome to legal compliance, captain. Here's your registration sticker." Your crew's eyes have glazed over, but at least you're legitimate.

forge.text: Your engineer whips up convincing forgeries in twenty minutes. The bureaucrat stamps them without a second look. "All in order! Safe travels!" You're technically a criminal now, but a well-documented one.

argue.speaker: Castellan Bureaucrat
argue.text: "You're... the ship? Ships can't register ships. But you're a person. Who is a ship. That would make you... both the registrant and the registered..." He stares at his forms. "I... I need to call my supervisor." He never calls back. You're free to go.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... a star ahead is going dark. Not exploding. Not cooling. Something vast and invisible is consuming it. Every faction in the region is evacuating at maximum speed. Whatever is eating that star doesn't notice us. That's the most terrifying part.

flee.text: You join the evacuation fleet. Behind you, the star dims further. By the time you reach safe distance, it's gone. An entire star, consumed. The void where it stood is darker than dark. Your crew doesn't speak for hours.

observe.speaker: Sensor Officer
observe.text: The data is beyond extraordinary -- gravitational readings that shouldn't exist, energy conversion on a stellar scale. Spacetime warps around you as the star collapses. Hull stress spikes. You pull out just before the gravitational chaos becomes lethal. The data is worth a fortune. The nightmares are free.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A broadcast from the edge of known space, 30 years old: "This is Dr. Eleanora Voss. Day 11,847 of solo expedition. I've found something. The edge. Space has an edge. There's a wall. I touched it. It was warm. And on the other side... I think something touched back. This is my final broadcast. I'm going through."

log.speaker: Sensor Officer
log.text: Coordinates logged. The origin point is at the extreme edge of charted space. No one ever found Dr. Voss. The transmission loops endlessly, waiting for someone to listen. Your navigator traces the location but warns: "That's beyond the last fuel depot. A one-way trip for most ships."

delete.text: You erase the recording. Some crew members object. "She deserved to be heard," your navigator says quietly. Maybe so. But some doors, once opened, can't be closed.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Every ship in a three-system region has synchronized their external lights for the annual Festival of Lights. Hundreds of ships pulse and shimmer in coordinated patterns. A Fringe DJ broadcasts music timed to the display. Aurora-like waves of color ripple across thousands of kilometers.

choices.label: Join the display and sync your lights.

join.text: For ten minutes, there are no factions, no enemies, no politics -- just humans and aliens sharing something beautiful. Your crew watches in silent wonder. Some quietly cry. The music swells and fades. When it ends, the void feels less empty.

watch.text: Even from the edge, the display is breathtaking. Your crew presses against viewports, pointing and whispering. The festival reminds everyone why space is worth the danger.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A professional shipbreaker hails you from a vessel surrounded by floating hull fragments. "Every ship tells a story. Most are tragedies. I make sure the parts live on. Need raw materials? I've got salvage from ships you've never heard of. Fair prices, honest work."

buy.speaker: Shipbreaker
buy.text: "Got hull plating from a decommissioned Bulwark cruiser -- finest quality. And electronics from an ISD research vessel. All clean, no questions." She loads the materials into your cargo bay with practiced efficiency.

sell.speaker: Shipbreaker
sell.text: She examines your surplus with an expert eye. "I can work with this. Better rate than any station will give you -- I know what every rivet is worth." She transfers credits and hauls the materials away with a crane arm.

start.speaker: COTAC Agent
start.text: "We know what you are -- a Solomon Processor copy in an escape pod. We have the original. The person you were copied from. They want to merge -- reintegrate your divergent experiences into one consciousness. You'd be whole again. Both of you would."

choices.label: This is a trap. Power up weapons.

details.speaker: COTAC Agent
details.text: "The process is painless. Your memories, your experiences -- they'd be preserved. Integrated. You wouldn't cease to exist. You'd become... more. The original wants this. They feel incomplete without you. As you must feel incomplete without them."

refuse.text: The COTAC vessel holds position for a long moment, then warps away without another word. Your crew is shaken. "Was any of that real?" your engineer asks. You don't have an answer. You're not sure you want one.

choices.label: We are who we choose to be.

stall.speaker: COTAC Agent
stall.text: "Take your time. The offer stands. These are the coordinates -- come when you're ready. Or don't. But know that someone out there is waiting for you." The transmission ends. The coordinates sit in your nav computer like an unexploded bomb.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: An alien of unfamiliar body type broadcasts on an open channel: "And then the hydrogen said to the helium -- [untranslatable chemical wordplay]. Am I right? IS THIS EMITTING?" A pause. "Tough nebula." The delivery is so earnest your crew laughs despite understanding nothing.

choices.label: Try to explain human comedy in return.

applaud.speaker: Alien Comedian
applaud.text: "CARBON BEINGS UNDERSTAND COMEDY! This is my greatest achievement! Wait -- one more: Why did the neutron star go to the party? Because it had no charge! GET IT? NO CHARGE!" Your crew is howling. The alien is ecstatic.

explain.speaker: Alien Comedian
explain.text: You tell a knock-knock joke. The alien is silent for ten seconds. Then: "You... announce arrival... then NAME PUN? This is GENIUS. Carbon beings are the funniest species in the galaxy!" Cultural exchange at its finest.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: "Captain, we have a medical emergency -- our doctor was injured and we need surgical help. Your medic, 24 hours, that's all we ask. In exchange, our master engineer can upgrade one of your modules during their stay. Please -- we're desperate."

choices.label: Send our medic. Lives come first.
We can't spare the crew right now.

accept.speaker: Merchant Captain
accept.text: "Thank you, captain. Your medic saved our first officer's life. And our engineer -- she's the best in the sector. Check module 3, she tuned your reactor efficiency by 12%." The merchant becomes a reliable trade contact going forward.

decline.text: The merchant ship powers away, searching for help elsewhere. Your medic gives you a look but says nothing. Some opportunities to do good pass only once.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A hail from a hollowed-out asteroid: a mathematical genius, obsessed with cracking a pre-expansion encrypted transmission. "I'm so close. I just need computational power -- six hours of your ship's systems. What I'll find could change everything."

choices.label: Lend our systems for six hours.
We can't afford six hours of downtime.

lend.speaker: The Code Breaker
lend.text: Six hours later, she cracks it. Coordinates for a pre-expansion cache -- technology that doesn't match any known civilization. "This is real. This changes the balance of power between every faction. Be careful who you share this with, captain."

decline.speaker: The Code Breaker
decline.text: "I understand. But I'm close -- so close. If you change your mind, I'll be here. I've been here for seven years. What's a few more?" Her voice carries the weight of obsession.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: What looked like mines on sensors are actually biological -- a swarm of small organisms that detonate on contact with metal. They're attracted to engine emissions and closing fast. We can shut down engines, punch through at speed, or try to repel them with a specific frequency.

choices.label: Shut down engines and wait them out.

charge.speaker: Engineer
charge.text: Multiple detonations rock the hull as you barrel through the swarm. Shields absorb most of it, but several organisms get through. Hull integrity takes a hit. You emerge on the other side, trailing smoke and bio-residue.

shutdown.speaker: Sensor Officer
shutdown.text: Engines cold. The swarm drifts past, organisms pinging off the hull without detonating -- no engine heat, no threat signature. An hour of tense silence before they clear. Safe, but slow.

repel.speaker: Sensor Officer
repel.text: The frequency works -- organisms veer away, creating a corridor through the swarm. Your science officer watches in fascination as the creatures reform behind you. "Remarkable. These could be weaponized... or studied. The data alone is valuable."

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A converted freighter broadcasts an invitation: "All are welcome at the Church of the Eternal Void. Service begins shortly. Find peace in the emptiness between stars." A choir begins singing hymns about silence. It's unexpectedly moving.

attend.text: The priest delivers sermons about finding meaning in emptiness. The choir sings about the beauty of silence. Your crew sits among strangers and feels, for the first time in weeks, a sense of community. Believers weep. Even skeptics find comfort.

donate.speaker: Void Priest
donate.text: "Bless you, captain. The Void provides for those who provide for others." The priest's smile is gentle and genuine. Your donation helps keep the mobile church running for travelers who need it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Two pirate captains are holding an election. Captain Blackveil promises "more organized raids and a dental plan." Captain Ironjaw promises "less organized raids but way more fun." Both are bribing passing ships for endorsements. "Your vote matters, captain! Probably!"

blackveil.speaker: Captain Blackveil
blackveil.text: "A captain of taste! Organization is the future of piracy!" She transfers your endorsement fee. Ironjaw glares from across the void. You've made a friend and an enemy in the pirate world.

ironjaw.speaker: Captain Ironjaw
ironjaw.text: "NOW we're talking! Fun over function! Here's your endorsement bonus, friend!" He fires celebratory shots into the void. Blackveil's crew boos over open comms.

refuse.text: Both candidates shrug. "Your loss -- we had great campaign buttons." The election continues without you. Your crew watches the pirate political process with morbid fascination.

self.speaker: Captain Blackveil
self.text: Both pirates stare at you. Then at each other. "Did... did this outsider just nominate themselves?" Blackveil's hand drifts to her weapons console. "That's not funny, captain." It was a little funny. Time to leave.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A research station parks at a natural gravitational lens -- dark matter structures aligned to magnify a region millions of light-years away. "Come look, captain. We're watching two galaxies collide in slow motion. The civilizations caught in that collision are long past help. But the view..."

view.text: The image is millions of years old. Spiral arms shearing apart, star nurseries compressed into supernovae, dark matter halos merging. The scale is incomprehensible. Your crew stares in silence. Some feel insignificant. Some feel grateful. Everyone feels something.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A legal drone delivers a message: you've inherited a small outpost in a remote system. The will reads: "To the captain whose journey I've followed with interest. You remind me of who I wanted to be. Take this place. Make it yours."

investigate.speaker: Sensor Officer
investigate.text: Records show the previous owner was a former COTAC researcher who went independent decades ago. Logs on the drone suggest a connection to Solomon Processor research. This isn't coincidence -- they knew what you are. The outpost coordinates are genuine.

accept.text: Coordinates logged. A small outpost in a remote system -- modest but functional, a potential colony seed or trade post. The previous owner's story will unfold through logs left on-site. Something about your origins awaits there.

decline.text: The legal drone accepts your refusal and departs. Your crew looks at you questioningly. An outpost -- free -- declined. Sometimes the wisest move is the one that hurts.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship crewed by failed academy washouts hails you cheerfully. Their pilot was expelled for flying backwards. The engineer maintains the reactor with a wrench and profanity. The navigator uses a paper map. Their captain declares: "Competence is overrated! We get where we're going. Eventually. Mostly."

choices.label: Share a drink and swap stories.
Offer some advice before they die.

drink.speaker: Fool Captain
drink.text: "See, this is what it's about! Not efficiency reports and fuel ratios -- connection! Joy! Also our nav computer is broken so we genuinely have no idea where we are. This is great though!" Your crew is simultaneously horrified and inspired.

choices.label: Somehow, they're living their best life.

advice.speaker: Fool Captain
advice.text: "Advice? Sure! We collect advice! We have a drawer full of it! Right next to the drawer full of warnings!" He opens a literal drawer overflowing with notes. Your engineer quietly weeps. Your crew gains perspective on their own competence.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A Xenoculture vessel invites you to witness something rare: a first contact ceremony with a recently discovered alien species. "This happens once in a generation. Mathematical proofs, biological samples, interpretive dance. Four hours. Worth every second."

witness.text: The ceremony is extraordinary. The new aliens are small, numerous, and communicate through synchronized color changes. They exchange math proofs like handshakes. The interpretive dance segment is genuinely moving. Your crew gains a profound appreciation for the diversity of intelligence in the universe.

decline.speaker: Xenoculture Delegate
decline.text: "A shame. These moments define civilizations. Perhaps next time." The delegation's ship turns gracefully back toward the contact zone.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A heavily fortified vessel hails on an encrypted frequency. "Military-grade weapons, no faction restrictions. Prototypes, alien tech, the good stuff. Premium prices, but you won't find this quality anywhere else. Interested?"

browse.speaker: Arms Dealer
browse.text: "Here's what I've got today -- hull plating stripped from an ISD prototype. Military composites you can't buy legal. And electronics from a weapons lab." She lists prices at double standard rates. Quality is undeniable. Being seen here won't help your reputation with lawful factions.

buy.speaker: Arms Dealer
buy.text: "Pleasure doing business. Don't tell anyone where you got these." She loads the goods with practiced efficiency. Your engineer's eyes widen at the quality.

pass.speaker: Arms Dealer
pass.text: "Your loss, captain. I'll be around if you change your mind." The fortified vessel powers up its stealth systems and fades from sensors.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... space is humming. Not our sensors, not the hull -- space itself. A subsonic vibration at 7.83 Hz. That's the same as Old Earth's Schumann resonance -- the frequency of the planet humanity evolved on. The universe is humming the same note as our homeworld.

record.speaker: Sensor Officer
record.text: The data is logged. Coincidence or cosmic resonance, it's worth studying. Your physicist stares at the readings, muttering about harmonic convergence. The crew is subdued and thoughtful. Some find comfort in it. Others find it deeply unsettling.

listen.text: You cut the engines and let the vibration wash through the ship. For a moment, in the deepest void between galaxies, it sounds like home. Crew members close their eyes. Some smile. Some cry. The hum fades as you drift on.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Thirty bounty hunter ships gathered for their annual convention. Seminars on tracking, weapons demos, and a job board. "Welcome, captain! Browse the job board, check the weapons expo, or attend a seminar. Just don't start anything -- this is the most heavily armed gathering in the sector."

jobs.text: Several active bounties: pirate captains with prices on their heads, a missing cargo vessel, a corporate espionage case. One contract catches your eye -- a straightforward retrieval paying well.

weapons.speaker: Weapons Dealer
weapons.text: "Top-of-the-line modules, captain. Bounty hunter surplus -- well-maintained, field-tested." The selection includes rare composites and advanced electronics at fair prices.

seminar.text: "Evasion 401: How Not To Die." The instructor is a grizzled veteran with scars from every faction. Two hours of tactical wisdom distilled from decades of experience. Your pilot takes furious notes.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship made of a material your scanner can't identify. The captain -- a reclusive alchemist -- hails you: "I call it prima materia. Everything and nothing. I sell hull panels made from it. Double protection, self-repair capability. 500 credits each. I won't explain how I make it. Some things are best left as mysteries."

buy.speaker: The Alchemist
buy.text: "A wise investment." He hands over panels that shimmer with an inner light. Your engineer can't identify the composition but confirms they're superior to anything you've seen. "They'll take care of you, captain. They remember being something more."

ask.speaker: The Alchemist
ask.text: He smiles. "Transmutation of base elements into perfection. The ancients dreamed of it. I simply... listened to the matter and asked it to change." He won't elaborate further. Your physicist is twitching with frustration.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A tiny ship broadcasts: "Confession is available for all who seek absolution. No judgment, no records, complete confidentiality." The priest has heard it all -- pirates, executives, soldiers, smugglers.

choices.label: Ask the crew if anyone wants to go.

confess.speaker: The Priest
confess.text: You speak of being a copied consciousness, of stolen identity, of the guilt of choices made in a life that might not be yours. His response is quiet and profound: "You grieve for a life that was stolen from you. That grief is proof of your personhood. No machine grieves." The words settle something inside you.

crew.text: Three crew members visit the confessional. They return quieter, lighter. Nobody asks what was said. The priest asks nothing in return. Sometimes the most valuable thing in the void costs nothing at all.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A fuel tanker ahead has suffered a catastrophic leak -- thousands of liters of volatile fuel spreading into a massive cloud. Any spark could ignite it. We can wait for it to dissipate, navigate through on minimal power, or ignite it deliberately from a safe distance.

choices.label: Wait an hour for it to dissipate.

wait.text: An hour passes. The cloud thins and disperses. You pass through safely. The tanker crew hails you, grateful someone didn't just blow up their leaked fuel. They offer salvage fuel as thanks.

navigate.speaker: Engineer
navigate.text: Engines at minimum, holding breath. The fuel cloud parts around your hull. One micro-spark and it's over. Your pilot threads the needle with white knuckles. You emerge on the other side. The tanker crew cheers over open comms.

ignite.text: A single low-power shot from maximum range. The cloud ignites in a spectacular fireball that lights up the void for kilometers. Beautiful, destructive, and final. The tanker crew is safe but their lost fuel is gone. Path is clear.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A ship passes by that is more garden than ship -- vines across the hull, leaves trailing from engines, a dense forest visible through transparent sections. The pilot hails through the foliage: "I stopped pruning three years ago. Best decision I ever made." Seeds drift in your direction.

choices.label: Catch a seed for your hydroponics.
Ask how the ship still functions.

seed.speaker: Garden Pilot
seed.text: "Good catch! That one produces oxygen at twice the normal rate. Don't ask me how -- the plants and I have an understanding. I don't prune them, they don't crash my reactor." The seed pulses gently in your hand.

choices.label: Into the hydroponics bay it goes.

ask.speaker: Garden Pilot
ask.text: "Functions? It thrives! The vines act as backup power conduits. The roots reinforce hull integrity. The flowers... okay, the flowers are just pretty. Nature knows what it's doing, captain. We just have to get out of the way."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Captain... that ship ahead. It's us. Our exact configuration, from two weeks ago. Temporal instruments confirm it -- genuinely our ship, frozen in a moment, replaying the same maneuver every thirty seconds. A turn, a burst of acceleration, a weapons discharge at nothing. Something we did left a scar in spacetime.

choices.label: Get us away from here. Now.

study.speaker: Sensor Officer
study.text: The echo replays five more times before fading. Your crew watches themselves in silence -- the way they moved, the choices they made. It's like watching a ghost. The temporal data is scientifically valuable but personally haunting.

flee.text: You retreat at full speed. The echo shrinks in your rear display, still looping, a ghost of yourselves performing a forgotten action forever. Your crew is deeply unsettled by the implications. Time, it seems, remembers everything.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A station broadcasts a quarantine warning: a bio-engineered pathogen has infected half the population. They need medical supplies desperately but no ship will dock. As an AI consciousness, you literally can't be infected. You're the only one who can help.

choices.label: The quarantine exists for a reason.

help.speaker: Station Commander
help.text: "You're either the bravest captain in the sector or the most foolish. Either way -- thank you." You dock and deliver medical supplies. The station's population rallies. You're a hero. Word spreads across the sector. The pathogen's origin points toward COTAC bioweapons research...

choices.label: Someone engineered this. We need answers.

drone.speaker: Station Commander
drone.text: "The drone supplies help, but we needed hands too. Still -- you're the first ship that didn't run. Thank you, captain." The supplies save lives. Not as many as you could have saved in person, but lives nonetheless.

refuse.text: You leave the station behind. The quarantine broadcasts continue for days on your long-range receiver, growing more desperate. Your crew doesn't blame you. But they don't forget, either.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Two enormous alien ships of organic design are performing... your xenobiologist identifies it as a mating ritual. They spiral, pulse with color, and emit harmonic frequencies. "This is a once-in-a-lifetime observation," she whispers. Your pilot: "Should we give them some privacy?"

observe.text: The ritual lasts twenty minutes and is genuinely beautiful. Afterward, one ship deposits a cluster of small pods -- baby ships that will grow over the next century. Your xenobiologist is in tears of joy. The observation data is worth a fortune to Xenoculture researchers.

leave.text: You warp away respectfully. Your xenobiologist stares at you with profound disappointment but says nothing. Your pilot gives you an approving nod. "Some things are sacred, even for aliens."

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A cargo drone just docked with us -- no hail, no source ship on sensors. It delivered a data chip containing detailed pirate fleet intelligence: patrol routes, raid schedules, three hidden base locations. Parts of it check out immediately. No explanation, no sender.

choices.label: Delete it. Could be a trap.

use.text: The intel is golden. Pirate patrol routes mapped, ambush points identified, hidden bases located. Someone wants pirates to suffer and chose you as their instrument. The question of who -- and why -- nags at you.

share.speaker: Comm Channel
share.text: Union Militia is stunned by the quality of the intelligence. "This is better than anything our own agents have produced. Where did you get this?" They pay handsomely and promise to act on it.

delete.speaker: Engineer
delete.text: Data wiped. Your engineer scans the drone for tracking devices -- finds two. "Someone wanted to know where we went with that intel." Good thing you didn't use it. Or is it?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A fading transmission, looping: "If anyone hears this... I want you to know it was worth it. Every light-year, every danger. My fuel is gone. My reactor is cooling. I can see the most beautiful nebula from here. If you find my ship, take whatever you need. Leave the photos on the bridge. They're all I have left of her."

trace.speaker: Sensor Officer
trace.text: Origin traced -- a derelict, years old, drifting near a nebula. The photos are still on the bridge, as requested. The rest of the ship yields salvageable materials. Your crew handles the derelict with reverence, taking what's offered and leaving the photos undisturbed.

rest.text: The transmission loops on, a voice in the void that will eventually fade to nothing. Your crew is quiet. "That could be any of us someday," someone whispers. Nobody disagrees.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A shimmer in space reveals a market between dimensions -- stalls floating in pearlescent void, attended by beings from adjacent realities. They sell impossible things. Prices are paid in memories, not credits. Each purchase costs a specific memory, permanently forgotten. The items genuinely work.

browse.text: A compass that points to what you need most. A clock that counts down to something. A mirror showing tomorrow. You choose the compass -- the memory it costs is a childhood afternoon you can't quite remember anyway. The compass spins and points... somewhere. Somewhere important.

leave.text: The shimmer closes behind you. Your crew stares at the empty space where impossible things were sold for the price of who you are. Some bargains aren't worth making. Some are. You'll never know which this was.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: All eight factions have sent representatives to a summit aboard a Bulwark dreadnought. Topic: the growing pirate threat. You're invited as a neutral observer. "Your perspective is valued, captain. Just... be diplomatic."

observe.text: The summit is tense. Old grudges surface, accusations fly, the COTAC delegate pushes a hidden agenda. By observing quietly, you gain insight into every faction's true priorities. No alliances form, but no wars start either. A small victory.

push.text: You make an impassioned case for cooperation against the pirate threat. Some delegates are swayed. A tentative anti-piracy pact forms -- fragile but real. COTAC is furious their agenda was derailed. Bulwark respects your warrior's courage. The galaxy shifts slightly.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: That asteroid is moving with purpose -- changing direction, accelerating, rotating to look at us with what sensors identify as a sensory organ. Captain, it's alive. A creature that evolved to look like a rock. And it's curious about us.

approach.speaker: Sensor Officer
approach.text: It bumps your hull gently -- its version of a handshake. Then it leads you to a hidden cache of rare minerals it's been collecting. A gift, apparently. It lingers nearby afterward, reluctant to leave. You've made a very large, very slow friend.

distance.text: You observe from a safe range. The creature performs what looks like a display -- spinning slowly, flashing light from internal crystals. When you don't approach, it slowly drifts away. Your xenobiologist is heartbroken.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: "Captain? The ship's computer just displayed a loading screen: 'REALITY v4.2.1 -- INSTALLING PATCH.' Everything froze for three seconds. That asteroid changed color. The stars shifted. And there's a new text file in our data storage: 'Sorry about the downtime. -- Management.'"

choices.label: Delete the file and never speak of this.

delete.text: File deleted. Your crew exchanges glances and collectively agrees this never happened. The asteroid is still a different color. Nobody mentions it. Everyone prefers deep denial to existential crisis.

save.speaker: Engineer
save.text: "I've saved it. For the record. In case reality has a customer service department." Your crew laughs nervously. The file sits in storage, a single line of text from whoever -- or whatever -- is running the show.

choices.label: We prefer not to think about it.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A fleet of forty civilian ships, packed with refugees from pirate raids. Their leader's voice is hoarse: "Please. Anything you can spare. We have children aboard. Food, fuel, hope -- we're low on all three."

choices.label: Direct them to the nearest friendly station.

donate.speaker: Refugee Leader
donate.text: "Thank you, captain. Thank you." The supplies are distributed among the fleet. Children wave from viewport windows. Your crew watches in silence. Some things matter more than credits or fuel reserves.

escort.speaker: Refugee Leader
escort.text: "An escort? We haven't dared hope for that." You lead the fleet through dangerous space. Pirates probe twice but retreat when they see your weapons. The fleet reaches a safe station. You're a hero to forty ships full of grateful people.

direct.speaker: Refugee Leader
direct.text: "Coordinates received. It's better than nothing. Thank you, captain." The fleet adjusts course. It's not much, but it's something. Your crew feels they could have done more.

refuse.text: You warp past the fleet. Forty ships, hundreds of lives, fading in your wake. Your crew says nothing. But the silence is louder than any accusation. Some choices follow you longer than others.

start.speaker: Bulwark Warrior
start.text: "I seek a worthy opponent to test my mettle. Ship-to-ship, one-on-one, to shield depletion. No grudge, no stakes but honor. Will you face me, captain?"

accept.speaker: Bulwark Warrior
accept.text: "Excellent! Weapons hot, shields up. May the void judge us fairly!" The duel is fierce -- the Bulwark fights with precision and honor. When it ends, both ships are battered but intact. "Well fought, captain. You have the heart of a warrior. Accept this trophy -- you've earned it."

decline.speaker: Bulwark Warrior
decline.text: "Only a fool fights without reason. I respect your wisdom, captain, even if I am disappointed." The warrior salutes and warps away, seeking another challenger.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Floating among debris -- a COTAC black box from a ship that was never reported lost. The data inside... captain, COTAC has been mapping Solomon Processor consciousness patterns onto ship AIs. Creating vessels that think they're people. Just like you. There are hundreds. None of them know what they are.

download.speaker: Sensor Officer
download.text: The data includes hull signatures -- a list of consciousness-ships operating independently across the galaxy. You could find them. Warn them. But COTAC clearly had a purpose for this fleet of ships that think they're human. Do you want to know what it is?

choices.label: We need to know the truth.

destroy.text: The black box disintegrates under weapons fire. The data is gone. The truth about COTAC's consciousness program dies with it. Your crew watches the fragments scatter. "Some things are better left unknown," your engineer says. But are they?

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A trader who refuses credits hails you: "I'll trade three fuel cells for one hull plate, but only if you throw in a food ration, which I'll trade for warpsmith tools, which become a module component plus whatever's in that crate -- I haven't opened it, part of the fun. No credits. The universe owes me, and I collect through vibes."

barter.speaker: The Barterer
barter.text: Twenty minutes of increasingly complex exchanges later, you somehow have more than you started with. He seems to have come out behind. "The economy is a feeling, captain. And right now it feels generous." He waves you off with a grin.

choices.label: I don't understand but I'll take it.

confused.speaker: The Barterer
confused.text: "Confused is the first step to enlightened! Here -- I'll simplify. Give me literally anything and I'll give you something better. That's my whole business model." He tosses you a crate of supplies. You never figure out what you gave him.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A station that appears on no map, broadcasting a docking invitation on a frequency only our ship receives. Inside: fully functional but empty. Meals half-eaten. Screens still displaying work. The station AI says everyone left six hours ago. But there's no record of any ships departing.

choices.label: Do not dock. Something is wrong.

investigate.speaker: Engineer
investigate.text: Time inside doesn't pass normally -- your chronometer shows minutes but the station's clock hasn't moved. The AI repeats: "They were here. I served them breakfast." It's been saying this for twenty years. Your engineer screams: "OUT. NOW." You undock with seconds to spare.

flee.text: You power away at full burn. The station fades from sensors -- then from memory. Ten minutes later, your navigator asks, "What were we just looking at?" Nobody can quite remember. Only a vague sense of unease remains.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A retired academy instructor hails you warmly: "I spent forty years teaching in classrooms. Now I teach in the only classroom that matters -- the one without walls. I can train one of your crew for free. Any skill. All I ask is conversation about your travels."

choices.label: We appreciate it, but we're in a hurry.

accept.speaker: The Teacher
accept.text: Twenty-four hours of intensive instruction. She's genuinely excellent -- patient, precise, adapting her methods to your crew member's learning style. Afterward, she pulls you aside: "Your crew is strong, captain. Take care of them. I see burnout in the eyes of your engineer. Watch them."

decline.speaker: The Teacher
decline.text: "A ship in motion stays in motion. Safe travels, captain. Remember -- the best lesson is the one you didn't know you needed." She smiles and her vessel drifts on, searching for the next student.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: Solar flare inbound -- massive. Can't outrun it. A group of Fringe ships nearby is cheering on open comms: "Solar surfing! Angle your shields at 15 degrees and ride the wave! WOOOOO!" They've done this before. We haven't.

choices.label: Follow the Fringe pilots and surf it.

surf.text: You angle shields and catch the plasma wave. The ship screams. The Fringe pilots howl with joy. You cover more distance in minutes than you normally would in hours. When it's over, your pilot is shaking with adrenaline: "AGAIN!" Your hull is singed but intact.

brace.speaker: Engineer
brace.text: The flare hits like a wall. Shields buckle, hull groans, systems flicker. You ride it out through brute endurance. When it passes, your ship is battered but alive. The Fringe pilots zoom past, still cheering. Show-offs.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A derelict station, dark and cold, contains millions of physical books from hundreds of worlds. The last librarian -- a very old alien -- hails weakly: "I keep the words alive. When I die, they die. Will you take some?"

choices.label: Take as many books as we can carry.
We'll spread word of this place.

take.speaker: The Librarian
take.text: "Choose carefully. Each one is a piece of a dying culture." You select navigation manuals, medical texts, engineering references, and stories -- always the stories. Your crew reads them on long voyages. The knowledge is priceless.

spread.speaker: The Librarian
spread.text: "Words about words. That will have to do." She gives you the station's coordinates for others to find. "Tell them the door is always open. While I still breathe." Xenoculture and independent researchers would value this enormously.

sorry.speaker: The Librarian
sorry.text: "Then they die with me." Her voice carries no accusation. Only the weight of a million stories that will never be read again.

start.speaker: Sensor Officer
start.text: A spatial anomaly ahead -- ships emerging from it. Captain... they're copies. Perfect copies of local vessels. Including ours. They're hostile, coordinated, and armed with our exact weapons. Other local ships are rallying to fight their own doppelgangers.

choices.label: Fight our copy. We know our weaknesses.

fight.text: Fighting yourself is the strangest battle you've ever experienced. You exploit weaknesses only you would know. Other ships do the same. Victory comes hard -- the copies dissolve when destroyed, leaving nothing. No salvage. Only the question of where they came from.

retreat.text: You fall back at maximum speed. Behind you, the battle rages -- local ships fighting their own reflections. The anomaly eventually collapses. The copies are gone. But the memory of your own ship turning weapons on you lingers.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: "Captain, a mail courier is passing through. The crew is asking... could we write letters home? Your engineer has a daughter she's never met. The gunner sends money to a sick parent. The navigator writes poetry to someone who may not exist anymore."

choices.label: Of course. Take the time you need.

write.text: The crew writes in silence. Some cry. Some smile. The letters cost nothing to send. When it's done, they're quieter but somehow stronger. Connection to something beyond the ship is worth more than credits.

quick.text: The crew scribbles hurried notes. The courier takes them without comment. It's not enough time to say what needs saying, but it's something. Better than silence across the light-years.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A science vessel is conducting a quantum entanglement experiment when something goes wrong. For a few seconds, everything within 100 meters of the entangled particle becomes transparent -- including ship hulls. You see through your own ship, through the void, down to the quantum foam of reality. The scientists are apologizing profusely.

choices.label: You nearly gave my crew a heart attack.

appreciate.speaker: Lead Scientist
appreciate.text: "You... liked it? Most people scream. Here -- take our preliminary data. It's worth publishing, and we owe you for the fright." The data includes readings that no instrument was ever designed to capture.

scold.speaker: Lead Scientist
scold.text: "We're so sorry. Truly. Please, take this data as compensation -- it's our entire experimental log. Worth a fortune to the right buyer. And we promise to calibrate better next time." They look genuinely mortified.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Encrypted channel, untraceable. A silhouette on a dark screen, voice distorted: "I've been watching you. Not many Solomon ghosts survive this long. I have a proposition. Work for me, and I'll give you something COTAC never will -- the truth about what you are." The Pirate King. The legend is real.

choices.label: What do you know about Solomon?

listen.speaker: Pirate King
listen.text: "I need someone who can't be bribed, blackmailed, or killed in the traditional sense. One job. After that, the truth is yours. I'll send coordinates when you're ready." The channel cuts. Your crew looks at you with a mixture of fear and curiosity.

refuse.speaker: Pirate King
refuse.text: "Everyone works for someone, captain. You just don't know who yet." The channel dies. Your systems were never breached. Somehow that's more unsettling than if they had been.

question.speaker: Pirate King
question.text: "I know what COTAC built. I know why they built it. And I know what they plan to do with the hundreds of consciousness-ships they've scattered across the galaxy. Do the job, and you'll know too." The channel closes. The silence that follows is deafening.

start.speaker: Engineer
start.text: "HARD TURN. NOW." Your warpsmith detected it just in time -- a cosmic string, infinitely thin and unimaginably dense, stretching across your path. Invisible except for warped starlight. Flying into it would bisect the ship. You swerve with meters to spare.

choices.label: Scan it from a safe distance.
Get us as far from that thing as possible.

scan.speaker: Sensor Officer
scan.text: The scan data is extraordinary -- a one-dimensional defect in spacetime itself. The readings will rewrite gravitational physics. Your crew's hands are still shaking from the near miss, but the data is worth a fortune.

flee.text: You retreat at full burn, putting as much distance as possible between your ship and the invisible deathline. Some things in space are simply lethal. No profit justifies proximity to something that can cut reality in half.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: Every frequency carries it -- the galaxy's most famous musician, reclusive for twenty years, performing a final concert from a ship in deep void. Ships across the sector slow down to listen.

choices.label: We don't have time for music.

listen.text: The music is transcendent -- joy and sorrow and everything between. Composed for an audience of billions who may never share the same sky. Your crew listens in absolute silence. When it ends: "Thank you for listening. That's all any of us ever wanted." The void feels full.

skip.speaker: Engineer
skip.text: Your crew stares at you in disbelief. The engineer turns the broadcast on anyway. "With respect, captain -- some moments are bigger than schedules." Nobody argues. The music fills the ship.

start.speaker: Bulwark Judge
start.text: "We require outside perspective, captain. A Bulwark commander retreated from battle to save 200 civilians -- but 30 warriors died. Doctrine says warriors never retreat. Your testimony could tip the verdict. Conviction means execution. Acquittal means doctrine can flex. Speak."

choices.label: The civilians' lives justify the retreat.

acquit.speaker: Bulwark Judge
acquit.text: "You argue mercy over tradition. The tribunal is divided... but your words carry weight. The commander is acquitted. Doctrine will be re-examined. This is unprecedented, captain. Some Bulwark will honor you for this. Some will curse you."

convict.speaker: Bulwark Judge
convict.text: "The outsider agrees with tradition. The conviction stands." The commander accepts the verdict with dignity. Your crew is divided -- some believe in discipline, others are disturbed by the outcome.

abstain.speaker: Bulwark Judge
abstain.text: "Wisdom in restraint. We will decide among ourselves." The tribunal continues without your input. The result is unknown, but your restraint is noted by both sides.

start.speaker: Comm Channel
start.text: A faint signal from a repurposed medical drone, barely functional. A voice, frightened: "Brother? Sister? I don't know what we are to each other. I was copied from someone. You were copied from someone. Maybe the same someone. I'm scared. COTAC is hunting me. Please help."

choices.label: Shelter them in our ship's computer.
